path: /Products & Services/Dubu - Dubu3/4. Tools/5.1 Updating the XSD
content:
## Download XSD

1. Delete all files in 001_dsa_dubu3\src\PowerShell\xsd\ (just normal delete, not svn delete)
2. Download the newest release metadata from https://dok.kombit.dk/boern-kultur-social-og-sundhed/digitalisering-udsatte-boern-og-unge-dubu#datamodel
3. Unzip the file
4. Copy all the xsd files from zipfile\Lis_Vx.y.z - Skemafiler_YYYYMMDD to 001_dsa_dubu3\src\PowerShell\xsd\
5. Open 001_dsa_dubu3\src\PowerShell\XSD_Prepare.ps1 and ensure that the variable $filepath is set to the correct path.
6. Run the 001_dsa_dubu3\src\PowerShell\XSD_Prepare.ps1 powershell script
7. Browse to the 001_dsa_dubu3\src\PowerShell\xsd\ folder
8. Review each XSD

There are a few cases you want to check for when reviewing the XSD's.
Because we would like to deploy the DSA before the new fields are added to the dataset, we have to be able to handle the xml files with and without the new fields. Therefore all new fields should have minOccurs="0"
If a field is removed then we need to manually add it again such that in can run until the the fields is removed from the xml.

Deploy the new DSA in a development envoriment and run the extract job. If the job succeeded then it is ready to be deployed in production.

content:
**PROBLEM: The query processor is unable to produce a plan because the index on table or view is disabled.**


I had a problem during the load to DM, for tables which have clustered index(in my case it was clustered columnstore index). I was getting an error:
	
Executing the query "[system].[DMReplicateOneTable]" failed with the following error: 
The query processor is unable to produce a plan because the index 'Fact_PersonerOgFuldtidspersoner_CIDX' on table or view 'Fact_PersonerOgFuldtidspersoner' is disabled.  

I needed to add extra code in sp: [system].[DMTableUpdate], where I am updateing a column CreateIndexOnDestTable on table system.DMTable with value 2 (defualt is 1). That say the table have clustered index and it will not be disabled. Important thing is that this sp is executed during the deploy/installation. It is not executed during the load.

path: /Teams/3. PDT5/3.11 Moving Data further from EDW (IQ, DataOut, DM etc)
content:
# Moving Data further from EDW (IQ, DataOut, DM etc) - possible scenarios and things to consider
### Load Jobs types:
- **Load** (eg. 580_BI_KP_LOAD)- uses the datatransfer tool that takes configuration from the param file (used as parameter in the execution) and exports data to SAP IQ Database on top of which Business Object operates. **Most of BO customers use IQ db and this kind of setup**, the exception is Esbjerg which is a BO customer but has its own BO and we load its data using Dataout job.  
- **Load_MS** (eg. 580_BI_KP_LOAD_MS) - loads data to the Data Mart Databese XXX_03_DM located on KMD ETL server - the same one where XXX_Area_02_EDW and XXX_Area_01_DSA are located. As this is the same sever, instead of using the datatransfer tool, dedicated SSIS and stored procedures are used, **most of Targit clients use this type of setup.**
- **Dataout** (eg. 580_BI_KP_DATAOUT) moves data to different, other than SAP IQ servers (usually outside KMD network). It uses the datatransfer tool that takes configuration from the param file. Depending on DataOut customer type we apply different filtering policy for objects sent to them that reflects in /SourceEntityList param in param file, details below.
### Filtering policies for Data Out customers.
As dataout customers can reach databases by themselves, we are particularly careful in what we send them
- **Full Dataout** we send all objects to customers for which we are responsible for frontend. This is usually a special setup on Targit and a special setup for BO (currently only Esbjerg), no special filtering policy here, **Area_DATAOUT.param** should be used. 
- **Limited Dataout** - we use this configuration when we are not responsible for reports, we just sell data. To avoid questions from the customer developers we are very careful here, in order not to transfer any objects that are new and still under development. 
If time aggregation takes place on facts in the given solution ( Day/Dag, Month/Maaned, week/uge, facts are present in a solution), we only transfer core facts with periods on top of which these time aggregated facts are built; time aggregated facts should not be transferred. **Area_LIMITED_DATAOUT.param** param file should be created and used, exemplary entity list:
```
/SourceEntityList:dimension.*,fact.*,-fact.*Maaned*,-dimension.Dato,-dimension.Aldersinterval,-dimension.*KMFMAF*,-fact.*KMFMAF*
```
Here we remove monthly facts: _-fact.*Maaned*_ and objects under development:_-dimension.*KMFMAF*,-fact.*KMFMAF*_

path: /Teams/3. PDT5/3.10 Creating and executing jobs after migration to PIM
content:
_**TIP**: When starting using SSMS on PIM server and connecting to database engine put as a server name this with ip address. Like **172.31.112.142\DEVELOP**  not **KMDDBS0029\DEVELOP**, as it was by default suggested and use Windows Authentication. That should help to resolve some issues which appeared after migration to PIM._

After our data warehouse server was moved from 172.31.112.142 to new PIM (KMDAPP0140) at the beginning of June some things works now differently than before.

For instance when you want to create a job by using one, which someone else already has created, you need to do the following steps.
Firstly you need to open script for creating job as shown below:

![jobs_1.png](/.attachments/jobs_1-7aa54db4-392d-4f67-8548-883c94c4bfd3.png =470x200)

Then you need to do few adjustments in code (shown example is for KY solution and customer 615):

![jobs_2_2.png](/.attachments/jobs_2_2-036cd71e-7523-475d-83b2-2b59dc3d6cf0.png =720x800)

First of all you need to **put your own user data** (replace old one to your own new one). In above example we need to replace z6mpc to **pimadm_dom_nr_dima_XX_**, where _XX_ is your number in user.
Then you need to **delete parameter** with its value (remove this part of code in example: "**@owner_login_name=N'kmdpfosap\z6mpc',**".
Moreover make sure that parameter @command has proper value. Then you're ready to create a job.

Once it has ended successfully last step is to right-click on just created your own job and go to:
_Properties->Steps->Edit->Run as_
and **choose** here **proper user**. 
For instace for LOAD job you need to select the only one possible option, which is _service_sqlagent_.

![jobs_3.png](/.attachments/jobs_3-3bc979c8-db45-436c-9c18-a142dbfad3c3.png =570x200)

Now, you're free to run your job :)

The Nexus KL Gateway solution delivers Nexus (FSIII) data to KL on behalf of our customers (the municipalities) on a daily basis. A delivery is a JSON report for each citizen with Nexus (FSIII) data. Each day changes in data is recorded and sent to KL Gateway. 

The solution has been sending reports to KL Gateway since June 2022. In August 2022 we deliver in total around 15.000 reports pr. day shared among 58 customers. 

On top of the solution we also share the delivered data with the customers trough standard reports in SAP BO - both free and extended reports. 

The solution therefore consist of three elements:

1. JSON reports delivered to KL Gateway (main solution)
2. Free standard reports in SAP BO showing current data delivered to KL Gateway
3. Extended standard reports in SAP BO showing the differences between the delivery to KL Gateway and current registrations in Nexus (e.g. interventions registered in Nexus but not delivered to KL Gateway because the registered data is not compliant with the KL Gateway requirements).

The purpose of the solution is to generate JSON reports with Nexus data and sent it to the KL Gateway. Therefore the solution consists of two core elements. First the dataarea on MS SQL Server which handles the data and generates the (pre) JSON reports and second the Azure setup which sent JSON reports to the KL Gateway. Furthermore the solution also enables the customer to get an insight in their data trough SAP BO - this is the third element.

The overall architecture is shown below. Elements in the project are colored orange. 

![image.png](/.attachments/image-abe54297-bdfb-4c14-a9ea-1fb383ea3de2.png)

## KL Gatway JSON Report

A JSON report covers one citizen and changes in data regarding registrations for the citizen since the last update. Each report contain data for 8 areas (4 main and 4 sub)

Main:
- Completed intervention (besøg uden forudgående bestilling)
- Planned intervention (indsatser)
- Condition (tilstande)
- Matter of Interest Observations (potentielle tilstande)

Sub:
- Goal (mål/forventet niveau)
- Citizens Own Observation (borgervurdering)
- Encounter (opfølgning)
- Follow Up Observation (opfølgning med resultat)

A change in data in a "sub area" requires the related main area to be covered in the report as well. 

The datamodel from KL can be found at [http://build.fhir.org/ig/hl7dk/kl-gateway/]()

![image.png](/.attachments/image-472eb844-7b57-4108-a507-1d2e5d1da02b.png)


## Jobs

The three jobs can be executed when the 001_dsa_nexus2 has run for the customer. 

Job 1: 001_BI_NEXUSKL_Transform
Job 2: 001_BI_NEXUSKL_Gateway
Job 3: 001_BI_NEXUSKL_Load


## Element 1: NEXUSKL dataarea

The NEXUSKL dataarea (001_dataarea_nexuskl) is build as a standard dataarea module ("fælleskommunal" / 001_dataarea_template) and is installed on each customers (e.g. 219_nexuskl_02_edw). The main end point for the dataarea is to genereate JSON reports for citizen with updates on the KL Gateway relevant data. A step by step recap is covered beneath. 

Job: 001_BI_NEXUSKL_Transform 

1. Each of the 8 areas consist of three tables (schema: mapping, workdelta, work). Keys (mapping) and content (work tables) are extracted and transformed from the source (001_dsa_nexus2). Each work table (e.g. "work.Condition") has a delta variant (schema "workdelta") where potential changes are covered. Data from the workdelta are then compared and transfered to the final work table (e.g. "work.Condition"). 

2. When new/changed data are recorded and inserted in a work table, the id (e.g. "condition_id") is inserted in the table gateway.ChangedRecords. This happens in the final section of each work stored procedure. 

3. The last procedure to be executed is [stage].[Insert_WorkDeliveryReport]. It selects citizens with changes (from gateway.ChangedRecords) and generate a JSON report with the changes based on id's from gateway.ChangedRecords. The JSON report is inserted in the table gateway.DeliveryReports and contains all the data that is going to be delivered to the KL Gateway. 



## Element 2: KMD KL Gateway Azure setup

The azure setup element consist of three micro services with the purpose of sending reports to the KL Gateway. They are triggered by a PowerShell script (step 1 in the Gateway job on MS) telling which customer to send and from which server ip address. 

Job: 001_BI_NEXUSKL_Gateway

The setup is fully documented at https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_git/KMD.DIMA.LG.NexusKLGateway. In short it consist of:

1. Kommune Ready Publisher: This microservices as a single HTTP POST endpoint /ready. When it receives a call it posts this message over to the KommuneReadyToSend Queue. That is the extent of this microservice

2. KommuneDataAccess.ReportLoader: This is the microservice that does most of the heavy lifting. It handles all of the database connections. It must be configured properly for every kommuneNumber that we will be using.

3. CareReportsSender. This is the microservice's job is to convert a Nexus care report into something that the KL gateway can understand. Then it sends it to the gateway and waits for a response.

![KMD Nexus to KL Gateway v1 (1).png](/.attachments/KMD%20Nexus%20to%20KL%20Gateway%20v1%20(1)-e8f686cf-efb4-4344-aa83-8f14856098c9.png)

## Element 3: SAP BO Universe and standard reports

Job: 001_BI_NEXUSKL_Load

The universe (NEXUS - KL Gateway) is build upon views from the dataarea. Each work table and the table gateway.DeliveryReports is full loaded to the IQ server trough views. In the universe they are combined with the Nexus2 solution trought an outer join in derived tables. Hereby we are able to match the work tables with the "brutto" registrations in Nexus. 

From the universe there are created five free of charge standard reports to the customers. One report to get an overview of the number of reports sent to the KL Gateway and four reports (one for each main area) with a detailed insight to the current data that has been sent. 

Furthermore the customer can get access to four extended standard reports (one for each main area). Trough the derived tables in the universe the reports show the difference between sent ("netto") registrations to the KL Gateway and all ("brutto") relevant registrations in Nexus. Hereby they are able to examine the registrations and their compliance to KL.

# MISC

content:
This section describes essential aspects of the KL Gateway application. An architecture overview is given in Section  https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.LG.wiki/2755/Architecture?anchor=element-2%3A-kmd-kl-gateway-azure-setup.


# 1 Application
The KL Gateway application consumes reports with healthcare data and converts it to the Fhir standard. The resulting report is send to the service KL Gateway. The KL Gateway application is build as three microservices with an underlying Common and Model layer. Communication between the microservices happens through three RabbitMQ queues. 

## 1.1 Services 
The application consists of three application services and a RabbitMQ with three queues, see the Architecture page. The flow starts with Pub getting notified via a rest API, this means the daily set of report from a given municipality is ready to be processed and send. The Load service fetches the data, from the NexusKl database and sends it to the Send service. Send handles converting the data to a Fhir report, authentication to the KL Gateway, sending the report, and receive the reply. The reply is then send back to loader who writes the reply back to the database. 

### 1.1.1 KommuneReadyPublisher (Pub)
This service is the start point of the other two microservices. This service hots a rest API that that listens for a POST message to 'https://pub.sco-dev.dima.kmd.dk/ready' (Test) / 'https://pub.sco.dima.kmd.dk/ready' (Prod).
Here is an example of the powershell code that invokes the REST endpoint:

```
$Uri = 'https://pub.sco-dev.dima.kmd.dk/ready'
$body = @{"customerNumber"="219"; "dataSource"="KMDDBS0106,1433"; "database"="219_NEXUSKL_02_EDW"} | ConvertTo-Json
$header = @{
    "Accept"="application/json"
    "Content-Type"="application/json"
}
Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $Uri -Method 'Post' -Body $body -Headers $header
```
The code the receives the request is found here
`Src\Servies\KommuneReadyPublisher\Controllers\ReadyController.cs`

The body message contains the databasename and hostname that loader will use to fetch data and write the report status.
The message is published to the queue KommunaReadyToSend ready where Load is subscribed.

### 1.1.2 Report Loader (Load)
The Loader has two responsibilities (yes, it properly should have been two different microservices) and is split into two sections. The first responsibility is loading all the reports from the designated database (this section) and later write back the response from KL Gateway to the database (Section 1.1.4).
The connection string is partially supplies by the message from Pub, where hostname and database is given, and azure secrets (more on that later).
The database table `gateway.DeliveryReport` contains the JSON reports that are ready to be send to the KL Gateway, a query is construncted and all report matching the following criteria are fetched.
* Anything that has not run `([QueueDate] is null) `
* Anything that has failed response `([ResponseOK] = 0)`
* Anything that has been queued more that 60 minutes ago but does not have a response `([ResponseDate] is null and DATEDIFF(minute,[QueueDate],GETDATE()) > 60)`

The report contains healthcare data for a citizen formatted as Json. Three things happens when the report has been loaded:
1. An update query is send to the database, it sets the `[QueueDate]` column with the current timestamp, this signals that the report has not been added to the queue.
2. Loader desterilizes the json report to ensure that it is well structured. The code is located in `\src\Models\NexusKLModel\Model\NexusCareDeliverReport.cs` in the `QueueReport` method.  
3. The report is added to the CareReportReadyForSend queue. It is important that the report is well structed before it can be added to the queue.

The Loader has a role to play again later, see Section 1.1.4.

### 1.1.3 Care Report Sender (Send)
The Sender converts the Json report to the Fhir standard and handles the communication with KL Gateway including the authentication.
Care Report Sender is subscribed to the queue CareReportReadyForSend, when a new report appears it is desterilized and converted to a `NexusCareDeliverReport` object, the mapping logic is found in Model folder. The report is then serialized to Json and send to KL Gateway.

However, before a report can be send, a secure connection to KL Gateway need to be established. A technical description of this can be found here https://ehealth-dk.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/EDTW/pages/2187362305/SAML+Assertion+to+JWT+Exchange#Obtaining-the-kid-from-a-Public-key. A short description of how the authentication is implemented can be found in Section 1.1.3.1.



Convert to Fhir

#### 1.1.3.1 Authorization
`This section is incomplete`
The authentication processes is called "JWT client authentication“ and use “OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange".
Here is how it implemented in the application.

0) By signing a service agreement in the "service portal", we get a certificate and a clientId.
1) At application startup the certificate PEM file is loaded, converted to a pfx file and added to the http client as a client certificate, see `KombitTokenHelper.ExtractPublicKeyFromP12`. 
2) The next step is getting an Access Token. The Access Token has to be send along the report to KL Gateway as proof of authenticity. To get an Access Token we need to create an SAML Assertion Token and send it to the authentication service (Sundhed.dk). 
The SAML Assertion Token (also called a subject token some places) is created using the certificates private key, the clientID and an Audience (this is the purpose of the request, it comes from our appsetting files and never changes).



 Next a SAML assertion is created  Subject token or SAML assertion token

##### Authorization to sundehed.dk 

The [IDP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Identity_provider) we are connecting to in order to request an access token that can be used to send requests to the Gateway is owned by sundhed.dk.

The authorization method is called [token-exchange](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8693)

Security token exchange allows us to identify ourselves to KL and very that we not only have permission to access their system but that we have the permission of a customer to send data on their behalf.

Addional infromation can be found \\pfosap2016\IM-p\NEXUS KL Gateway





##### SAML Assertion from Kombit STS
We are using an undocumented method of retreiving a SAML assertion token from Kombit STS. This is due to the fact that we can not use their SOAP web service with .Net 5.

They are allowing us to use a rest api end point instead.

# 2 Environment
This section introduce the services and environments to give an overview of the setup.
This project use docker pods running in a kubernetes Azure cluster. 
We have three environments.  The Production and Test environments are hosted on Azure and Development is run the developers local pc.

## 2.1 Tools and services
Here is a short description of the tools and services used in the environment.
We also use several Azure and Kubenetis tools but we will not describe them all here.

### Argo CD 
Argo is a GitOps continuous delivery tool for Kubernetes. We use it to deploy pods to the Kubenetes cluster and view status on secret and environment configuration. This is the first place to start debugging at it also can be used to see the logs for the pods, health check status, and more.

### Log analytics
This is a query interface that allows us to search log logfiles.
Here is an example query:

```
let appName = "send";
let logSearchString = "Exception";
let startTime = ago(24h);
let endTime = now();
//below gets the latest Image & ImageTag for every containerID, during the time window
let ContainerInv = ContainerInventory  | where TimeGenerated >= startTime and TimeGenerated < endTime | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by ContainerID, Image, ImageTag | project-away TimeGenerated | project ContainerID1=ContainerID, Image1=Image;
//below gets the latest Name for every containerID, during the time window
let KubePodInv = KubePodInventory | where ContainerID != "" | where TimeGenerated >= startTime | where TimeGenerated < endTime | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by ContainerID2 = ContainerID, Name1=Name | project ContainerID2 , Name1;
//now join the above 2 to get a 'jointed table' that has name, image & imagetag. Outer left is safer in-case there are no kubepod records are if they are latent
let ContainerData = ContainerInv  | join kind=leftouter (KubePodInv) on $left.ContainerID1 == $right.ContainerID2;
//now join ContainerLog table with the 'jointed table' above and project-away redundant fields/columns and rename columns that were re-written
//Outer left is safer so you dont lose logs even if we cannot find container metadata for loglines (due to latency, time skew between data types etc...)
ContainerLog
| where TimeGenerated >= startTime and TimeGenerated < endTime
| join kind= leftouter (
ContainerData
) on $left.ContainerID == $right.ContainerID2 | project-away ImageTag, Name, Image, Name1, ContainerID1, ContainerID2, LogEntrySource, Computer, ContainerID, Repository, _ResourceId, SourceSystem, TimeOfCommand, Type | project-rename Image=Image1
| filter Image contains appName
| filter (LogEntry contains  logSearchString)
```

### Grafana
Grafana is a data visualation tool that we use to see CPR, RAM and Disk consumption for the Pods and RabbitMQ.


### Promethious
Promethious is a systems monitoring and alerting toolkit that collect timeseries data. 
This data can be used by other tools to do health checks and performance reporting.


## 2.2 Deploying code
In order to deploy code to Production or Test the flow is as follows.

### 2.2.1 Code in Development
Details about the Development environment and how to setup the environment are described in Section 2.3.3.
A new feature or bugfix should be developed in a new branch. Remember to run test and perform local test. When a new feature or bugfix is done the branch should be merged into the Test branch. 
To run the app in development, follow these steps:

1) Open project in visual studio

2) Run project as <Multi startup project> (see 2.3.3)
3) A swagger page opens. (URL http://localhost:5000/swagger/index.html)
![image.png](/.attachments/image-c0937e15-7c8d-423b-9b1a-cf541596a489.png)
Press Try it Now and enter the following JSON message:
```
{
  "customerNumber": "001",
  "dataSource": "localhost",
  "database": "001_NEXUSKL",
  "count": 1
}
```
A test report will be processed and passed through Load and Send via the local Rabbit MQ.

####Querying local sql database
To manipulate the kind of report that is processed you powershell or a database manager to manipulate the data. 
```
$SqlAuthLogin = "SA"
$SqlAuthPw  = "password123!"
$SqlServer = "localhost"

$query = "select * from [001_nexuskl].[dbo].[DeliveryReport]"
Invoke-Sqlcmd  -ConnectionString "TrustServerCertificate=True; Data Source=$SqlServer; User Id=$SqlAuthLogin; Password =$SqlAuthPw" -Query "$Query" | Format-Table
```

### 2.2.2 Code in Test
Details about the Test environment are described in Section 2.3.2.
When a branch is merged into the Test branch the relevant pipelines run, they build the project and make the pods. To deploy the pods the tool Argo is used. 
To sync the newly build pods with the pods on the environment press the Sync button. I recommend to run with the -prune -force and -replace flags.
![image.png](/.attachments/image-b5b9036a-7eb4-4c34-a055-2721863d9782.png)
After manual tests on the test environment have been conducted a pull request to prod can be made.

### 2.2.3 Code in Production
Details about the Prod environment are described in Section 2.3.1.
When a branch is merged into the Prod branch the relevant pipelines run, they build the project and make the pods. To deploy the pods the tool Argo is used. 
To sync the newly build pods with the pods on the environment press the Sync button. I recommend to run with the -prune -force and -replace flags.
The changes a now live.

Naming convention: <customerno><service><#service>
- <customerno>: Municipality code for municipalities and CVR numbers for other organisations
- <service>: What is the intended service for the given created data bank. Ex:
 1. SDO: SAP BO data out - data extration from SAP BO to data bank.
 2. CD: Customerdata - data delivery from customer to KMD for Customerdata solution.
 3. DO: Data out - data out delivery from LG DWH ex. datamart, for customer to access.
- <#service>: No of service, ex if customer like multiple data banks with different storage configurations and security settings.

One customer can have multiple ressource groups, and mulptible versions of the same service/ressourcegroup. This is done to make a modular setup, and keep clear structures around each service. Also done for storage configurations (hot/cold/archive), security configurations and tracebility of costs/billing.

Følgende ressource grupper bliver etablere:

- 376CD1 (Customer data 1 - bliver nummereret hvis der skal etableres flere)

- 37723223SDO1 (SAP BO Data Out 1 - bliver også nummereret, hvis der skal etableres flere)

- 000SDO1 (test kunde SAP BO Data Out 1 - også nummereret. Kommer jeg til at lege med i forhold til at eksportere data ud og senere ind i PBI)

- 000DO1 (test kunde data out leverance fra on prem datamart, til evt. lege med SQL adgang ovenpå)

path: /Technology & Software/2. Targit/2.1 Introduction/2.1.1 What is Targit in KMD/Targit Decision suite
content:
#Targit Windows client

In this documentation, the TARGIT Designer client refers to the Windows application by TARGIT that works as the end-user interface for designing analyses, reports, dashboards, slideshows etc. upon data from an established data warehouse.

The TARGIT Designer client is an extremely rich and powerful tool with many options for designing your Business Intelligence Experience the way you want it.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-4414127b-777d-4e6a-90f7-7b95301abcdf.png)


#Targit Anywhere

The TARGIT Anywhere client is what is known as a zero footprint application. I.e. the end user does not need to install anything on the client machine. All the necessary installations are done on the server and the end user will just need to know the correct URL address to type into the Internet Explorer browser.

The address to type in is http://localhost/anywhere

This will bring up the TARGIT anywhere client as displayed below:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-bee95a35-35e7-4ba4-9304-c926bbfe9425.png)





#Targit Management

![image.png](/.attachments/image-4bda34e0-7639-4a37-82e2-49ce51fcffe8.png)

#ETL Studio
TARGIT ETL Studio is for both basic and advanced data modeling. The ETL toolset allows for easy drag-and-drop connections to a wide range of data sources as well as the full power for complex data abstraction with TARGIT’s easy-to-learn scripting language. Users with SQL skills already have everything they need to master TARGIT’s advanced scripting options.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-c699aab1-a833-47a8-8c06-dea66edf2f43.png)

#Scheduler Management
The InMemory Scheduler Management is responsible for executing your ETL scripts. The jobs can be set up to run automatically and keep your databases content up to date according to a pre-defined schedule. You can administrate your combined scheduled jobs from here, see logging statistics etc. Among other things, this is also where you set up deployment folders for your InMemory databases.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-457500b2-5387-4c0a-b3e7-52d37ca509be.png)

#Query tool
If you know how to write SQL queries, you also know how to use the InMemory Query Tool. It is a simple equivalent to the query tool you may know from Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio. You will often use it during the development process of your ETL packages for checking whether executing the ETL scripts produce the expected results in the database.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-3492746e-6a0c-405a-98d3-886640d19b0c.png)

#Data model editor
The Data Model Editor is run through the TARGIT Management Client. In the TARGIT Management Client, once you have created a connection to your InMemory database, you can start up the Data Model Editor on that connection in order to define relations between tables, dimensions, hierarchies, measures, calculations etc. – and eventually one or more cubes, which is the basis for the data you get access to through the TARGIT Designer client.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-be7536c5-6d7a-48f9-a56a-8969fb815354.png)

#Data Discovery
TARGIT Data Discovery enables an end-user to consume data from a wide variety of data sources and combine them with other data without knowing about data types and complicated query languages. We call these combinations for cubes. 

TARGIT Data Discovery is not meant to be a replacement for a traditional BI solution, but rather be the add-on that gives business analysts and other user types with basic understanding of data structures a tool to instantly deploy company-wide solutions in a collaborative spirit.

 

The engine of the TARGIT Data Discovery module is a service called TARGIT Data Service. The TARGIT Data Service is an in memory engine designed to work with datasets of millions of rows and must be installed on the same server hosting the TARGIT Server component.

 

TARGIT Data Service will work with up to two million rows of data out of the box, but with the addition of the Data Discovery license module to the TARGIT solution, it can exceed the two million rows limit – limited only by memory.

path: /Technology & Software/2. Targit/2.1 Introduction/2.1.1 What is Targit in KMD/Architecture Overview
content:
The architecture of a TARGIT solution is best illustrated as a structure with multiple levels or tiers.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-e5ad5e01-8d76-4f37-85da-0e7ab2c7bc6c.png)

Starting from the leftmost tier, a typical solution will contain these tiers:

#The Data Sources tier
A company’s source systems are located in this tier. Examples of source systems might be NAVISION, AXAPTA, CRM systems, Excel sheets and log files. Source data are retrieved from the ERP tier.

Data Warehouses, suitable for analytical and reporting purposes, are designed and built for this tier. The purpose is to collect, to uniform and to store data from the ERP tier.

Most often, you will find multiple Data Warehouses in this tier: Multiple relational Data Warehouses and one or more multidimensional Data Warehouses.

The TARGIT Server (in the Server tier) is capable of communicating with all common Data Warehouse platforms. However, most TARGIT solutions have been implemented in a MS SQL Server environment on top of a MS SQL Server Analysis Services multidimensional Data Warehouse or in an environment with TARGIT’s native InMemory Data Warehouse.

#The Server tier
This is a central tier in a TARGIT solution. The TARGIT Server is located in the Server tier. The TARGIT Server handles all communication and distribution of data between the Data Warehouse tier and the Client tier.

A Microsoft Internet Information Services must be running on the server tier as well to enable TARGIT Anywhere Server functionality. TARGIT Anywhere Server functionality includes working with the browser based TARGIT Anywhere client and Mobile clients.

TARGIT Anywhere Server is also a requirement for so-called deep integrations with various ERP systems.

TARGIT Data Discoverer is a component running on the TARGIT server that enable end-users to work with ad-hoc data sources, e.g. data in Excel documents or online data sources.

#The Client tier
The Client tier is the top most tier in a TARGIT Solution. The standard end-user will be working with the analytical and reporting clients of this tier. The administrative client, the TARGIT Management client, is also part of this tier.

The TARGIT Windows client is the tool you need if your role is to design analyses and reports for yourself or for others to use. While the TARGIT Windows client is mainly a Designer tool, it can also be used for standard Consumer purposes.

The browser based client, the Anywhere client, and the mobile platform clients are purely Consumer clients. An end-user with a Consumer client will take full advantage of the power of stored analyses and reports, but will lack the ability to design new TARGIT documents.

To change the service account for the 'TARGIT Server' open "Services" on the targeted machine.

Locate and right click the 'TARGIT Server'-service to open 'Properties'.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-b6bbe673-db23-43f9-8508-19f0f201d558.png)

Go to "Log On" tab and press 'This account' and 'Browse...'.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-2475b5a5-dd62-43eb-aa19-6e06e9c2783e.png)


Depending on whether the service account is created on the server or in the Active Directory (AD), you'll have to "Check Names" in order to connect to the right account. ![image.png](/.attachments/image-eceb7eef-535d-45be-9bd5-454820665305.png)

If you have to enter your credentials in order to change "Location", you can simply log on with the service account, which can be found in passwords.kmd.dk (if someone has created the secret). This is because the account is created as an admin on the server.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-9dd6e7a3-ab90-4d40-81d3-bcd147c35ec0.png)

Afterwards we can change to "Entire Directory". 

![image.png](/.attachments/image-2c8b8c8f-05a2-4d22-aa1c-cba75bcd8ee4.png)
Proceed by inserting the service account as seen below and pressing "Check Names".
Proceed with pressing "OK", and "Apply".


![image.png](/.attachments/image-23305a10-4a28-4e9d-8291-67f648129a72.png)

You might have to restart the machine before the changes are put into effect.

path: /Technology & Software/2. Targit/2.10 TARGIT Analysis and Reports/2.10.2 Guidelines for Designing TARGIT Analysis and Reports
content:
# Introduction

In this guide we will describe the basic principles and guidelines for creating TARGIT inspirational analyses and reports for KMD Insight solutions. The key aspects when designing these analyses and reports are:

- Presentation: Present a good overview of what the KMD Insight solution can provide to the customer
- Transparency: It should be fairly easy for trained TARGIT designers to recreate or build similar analyses to the inspirational reports we deliver
- Portability: The analyses and reports should be portable, hence no adjustments are required to ensure analysis and report consistency, despite different customer setups

Just to elaborate a bit on the last one, the analyses and reports should work and look exactly the same on all customer servers, we don't want to use time and effort to post-distribution adjustments, since it would cause too much maintenance and we will loose standardized analysis and report consistency in no time. This might also require that customers have been upgraded to specific TARGIT versions for certain functionality to be available, but it will also require that report designers use the specific functionality in certain way for the analyses to be portable.

But first a short introduction to the structure of the inspirational analyses portal framework and how it covers our main business areas.

# Inspirational Analyses Portal Framework

We have two folder structures when working with inspirational analyses and reports (highlighted):

![image.png](/.attachments/image-6ba34e38-6c80-4254-9c4c-8c9e44903e4d.png)

The first folder structure "KMD Insight" is the folder structure for finalized analyses and reports, and it is also the folder structure we deploy to customers, because it resembles the structure established on their TARGIT servers.

The second folder structure "KMD Insight - Udvikling" has the same structure as the first one, but also contains analyses and reports currently being worked on, and they remain here until they are finished. When this happen, they are copied to the same location in the first structure and are the for deploy.

In these folder structures, the portal framework resides; to provide easy navigation between our inspirational analyses and reports, the analyses are designed to be a part of a general portal framework, which consists of a main frontpage, that leads to frontpages of each of our main areas of business:

![portal structure.png](/.attachments/portal%20structure-bebed61b-523d-41e8-88a5-41bb5868c7c5.png)

These areas are:

- Administration & Økonomistyring (Administrative, Economic Governance & HR) (PDT3)
- Social Sundhed & Uddannelse (Social, Health and Care & Education) (PDT4)
- Arbejdsmarked & Beskæftigelse (Job Market & Employment) (PDT5)
- Andre løsninger (Other solutions, eg. KMD TARGIT Log cube)

Each of these main pages have a top menu, where you can navigate to solutions within that business area:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-03bde093-b7f6-41dd-9409-249e43514c2c.png)

And if you click the menu items, you will navigate to the first analyses made for this solution (you can choose freely which analysis should be the first one, it depends on how you configure the menu item) and a submenu appears, where you can navigate between the different analyses:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-07a60385-00c3-4c94-ad84-bfefbe847b9c.png)

If analyses are not available, menu items will not be shown.

So with just 2-3 clicks, you can access any of the inspirational analyses and reports within our different business areas, and if you want to go to the main frontpage again, you can just click the KMD logo on top on any page.


# Design principles

In this section we will go through some of the basic principles when designing dashboards. Some of them might be obvious while others might be more difficult to adhere, but try to use them as a sort of reminder or checklist when designing your analyses and reports:

- **Who are your end users and what is your story?** 
How you should design your dashboards depends on your audience and what you would like to present to them, so find out who is your main audience, and consider which information is critical and relevant to present to these recipients and consider which questions the analyses should answer.

- **Overview: Ordering, relation and visualization of objects.** 
If your dashboards consists of multiple objects, you should place the simplest and most important objects on top and more detailed objects below, and take advantage of natural reading direction in ordering objects, so recipients understands the main scope and message initially and can dig into details afterwards.

- **Perception: Formatting, sorting and coloring of objects.** 
How objects are perceived relies much on how they are formatted and structured; sorted data are easier to compare, and use visualizations to show the variance in your data. Use consistent coloring (not too many variants), only relevant and short text labels, format numbers and values for easier decoding and understanding, and aligning your objects will make them visually more appealing and it will be easier for the users to get an overview of the dashboard.

- **Simplicity and Complexity.** 
Always try to keep things as simple as possible and only introduce complex objects when absolutely necessary, and consider splitting complex visualizations into smaller and simpler ones to highlight more specific messages. When keeping things simple, it also lowers the level of interpretation at the recipient, and thereby also minimizing the risk of making wrong decisions based on the data presented.

- **Consistency.** 
Analyses should be designed with consistency in mind; stick to a few different types of visualizations and use the same fonts and color scale in all objects, since it will create uniformity, increase the ability to compare and generate a more quiet expression. Being consistent will improve user confidence and adoption of the analyses being designed.

This was a quick walkthrough of some key design principles, which can be beneficial when designing analyses and reports. Other principles could be added to the list, and existing ones could be elaborated further, but let's keep things simple for applicability and transparency purposes.

# Design for presentation

Present the KMD Insight solution in the best way possible; inspirational reports is not only an analysis, it is also a presentation of our solution, so make sure that the analysis is easy to understand, is appealing and is representative in terms of what is possible with their new solution. Both customers and ourselves will benefit from having inspirational analyses that can be used to demonstrate how the solution can be used - also because we can skip the discovery phase and having to design everything from scratch.

# Design for transparency
One of the main purposes is to present how easily analyses can be made using our solutions, so keep filtering low, don't use too many hiding features or complicated calculations, because it will require a larger effort from the users to see through how the analysis is designed. This might also give the impression, that the solution is not easy to use, if you have to do complex implementations. Also refrain from using from static time and date filtering, since it requires maintenance in terms updating the filters after a period of time, since data becomes newer compared to when the analysis was made, so use TARGIT's dynamic time capabilities instead.

# Design for portability

To have the best staring point in creating portable analyses, we have made a template with portal framework elements built in, and this is available from this location:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-3d2b8bd8-8352-420f-ad0e-08b15e253996.png)

When using TARGIT you could often benefit from using stored criteria and shared user dimensions, so you don't have to create them over and over again, and you can share them with other users. But if you are creating portable analyses, you should avoid using the store and/or share part of these functions, since then the information will be written in the analysis (.xview) file itself. Otherwise it will be stored in the settings on the server, and they will be left out, if you move your analysis file to another server, where the analysis will give you an error and the respective objects will not work. The same goes for color sequences and series, only use object specific colors and not the ones that are shared.

If you would like to use non-standard fonts, you should check whether the same font is installed on both source and destination server, if this does not apply, the font use on the destination will roll back to another (standard or default) font installed on the server.

And most importantly, avoid using customer specific filters, since distribution to other customers might fail to show the content.

# Best Practices using the TARGIT client

The best practices described here is perhaps more like "shortcut to success", since it is often more efficient to reuse objects already designed and used in other analyses, and this approach also contribute to ensuring consistency among objects. 

Normally you might start designing objects by selecting dimensions and measures first and then configure afterwards how the objects should look. But if you already have finished dashboard, you can often pick (copy) objects, that already looks like objects you are about to design and then just change dimensions and measures. Since the above mentioned template and the examples below, all have been designed according to the KMD Brand Refresh from 2024, with a certain degree of freedom in design choices where the guidelines were not comprehensive, so nearly all design and formatting have already been done in existing objects, which can be seen here:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-55ee05de-0e55-425d-a289-ae59fd9797e8.png)

You can see the formatting of the object itself by clicking the "wheel", and the formatting of the frame around it can be seen by clicking the "pencil". An updated cross tab theme will also be available, so formatting of cross tabs according to guidelines can easily be applied.

In the example below we have an inspirational analysis where all design configuration has been done, and the highlighted elements are objects that are common for all analyses in the portal framework:

![analysis elements.png](/.attachments/analysis%20elements-bdb771dd-4162-4a97-9044-69f63fe10d5c.png)

The top part contains headline object and menu items for navigation, while the bottom part has an info box with common details from the dimension folder "Generel info" and the use of system variables. 

The menu is not a shared menu, since this feature has often been affected by errors in several versions of TARGIT, so the menu object has to be maintained in each analysis, but the upside is better portability and not having to remember other files than xview files when deploying. 

These are the common objects, used in all analysis, shown in the object list in the TARGIT client:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-c09414cb-79f4-4291-8bef-46bd46ecf10f.png)

All the other objects (charts, KPI's and tables etc.) have been formatted according to guidelines, so instead of writing a comprehensive guide on how to format all different kinds of objects, please refer to these tips:

- Use the template, it will save you a lot of time in doing basic configuration and formatting.
- Look at existing analysis to see how objects are designed and configured. They are kept fairly simple for better transparency.
- Please try to be consistent in terms of colors, fonts, labels, charts usage, spacing between objects and object alignment, since it will give a much better impression when navigating between the different analyses.
- Not all design decisions have been made by now, so please reach out if you need some sparring on design choices not covered anywhere else.

If you have any questions or comments to this page, please reach out to ocg@kmd.dk.

path: /Technology & Software/2. Targit/2.10 TARGIT Analysis and Reports/2.10.1 TARGIT Demo Server (no longer available)
content:
The TARGIT Demo server is an Azure server, which contains inspirational TARGIT analyses and reports based on our standard KMD Insight solutions.

The server can be reached at https://targitdemo.dima.kmd.dk (the part /anywhere/embed is added automatically):

![image.png](/.attachments/image-99c1b956-a92b-4c34-9861-448a2d92ca07.png)

Notice: The server is not online 24/7 at the moment; it has to be started manually (please contact OCG if you would like to use it) and it shuts down automatically at 5:00 p.m.

To log on, use the username "targitdemo" and password for this account can be found in https://passwords.kmd.dk 

When you log in, you will automatically reach the front page of the portal, which contains the TARGIT analyses and reports:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-1bfd52af-c4f0-45e2-af7d-3e113763a256.png)

You can use the top part of the menu to navigate between the different KMD Insight solutions, and the submenu just below will provide access to the inspirational analyses made for the respective KMD Insight solution:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-e5d0c019-d29c-4927-a925-800e2e943b35.png)

Here is an example of the "Oversigt" analysis from the Nova Byggesag solution:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-80ce0314-3a51-4257-94cd-f6e1098be404.png)

All analyses have been designed and made using the principles and guidelines described in [Guidelines for designing TARGIT analysis and reports](/Targit/TARGIT-Analysis-and-Reports/Guidelines-for-designing-TARGIT-analysis-and-reports).

The analyses and reports in this portal are identical to the analyses we provide, when we are delivering a KMD Insight solution with inspirational reports (customer name is removed from analyses on the demo server, it normally resides on the top-right corner along with the data updated date). The analyses are made for our standard solutions and will only be updated to match the content of our standard solutions accordingly. 

The content in this portal is provided "as is" and may change over time; content and new solutions will be added when ready and according to business needs. The data, which the analyses are built on, are not updated regularly, since no ETL flows are running on the server, we just copy and update the database file when needed.

If you have any questions or comments to this page, please reach out to ocg@kmd.dk.

``` The code examples below can be downloaded from svn: ..\targit\tools\DatamodelMinimize ``` #Minimize load time and database size In order to prevent long loadtimes and keep the cost of memory down, it is important that the ETL package is optimized. Each table in a Datamart contains some framework columns, that we never use in Targit. These columns should not be loaded. Furthermore is should be considered which columns is required for building the datamodel. Changing the ETL load is an easy task and there is no need to load all fields from a table, if only a few is needed. Missing fields can easily be added later. To help with the task of printing out all fields from a table, that are not framework fields, we have created a tool. 1. Get access to the customers DM database 1. Open Management Studio and select the customers DB database 1. Copy the script from below and fill out the customer db and schema in the top of the script
The procedure should result in something like this, just to be copied into your ETL project ![image.png](/.attachments/image-14c49b17-3adf-452b-b8ad-d85130bb07c3.png) ``` sql /* This procedure requires that output 'Results to text (Ctrl+T)' is chosen. This means that results will be written out as text and not as the normal 'grid' in management studio. To ensure the proper result - set 'Tools - Options - Query results - SQL Server - Results to Text - Maximum number of characters displayed in each column' to value 4000. Thereby the total scipt can be presented in one text window. After changing options a new windows must be opened to enforce new settings. When the procedure is executed the result window presents a result that can be copied directly into the Targit ETL script */ USE [XXX_03_DM] --change to appropiate DM database SET NOCOUNT ON DECLARE @SchemaName AS NVARCHAR(50) = ' XXX ' /*INPUT schema*/ DECLARE @TargitSource NVARCHAR(50) = 'SQL_DM' /*INPUT name of targitdata as used in your targit etl package*/ DECLARE @Sql AS NVARCHAR(max) DECLARE @FinalTableName nvarchar(100) DECLARE db_cursor CURSOR FOR SELECT TABLE_NAME from INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = @SchemaName ORDER BY TABLE_NAME OPEN db_cursor; FETCH NEXT FROM db_cursor INTO @FinalTableName WHILE @@FETCH_STATUS = 0 BEGIN --include the 2 lines below, only if certain tables should be included. change db with splitstring function --declare @List as nvarchar(max) = 'Dim_MedarbejderDynamisk' if 1 = 1 --and @FinalTableName IN (select Item from [XXX_02_EDW].dbo.SplitString(@List,',')) BEGIN SET @Sql = N'SELECT ''IMPORT [Viewname]=[[TargitSource]].{ select '' +REPLACE( (SELECT ''[''+COLUMN_NAME+'']'' AS ''data()'' FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_NAME=''[Viewname]'' AND TABLE_SCHEMA = ''[Schemaname]'' AND COLUMN_NAME NOT IN (''DW_ArchiveID'',''DW_ValidFrom'',''DW_ValidTo'',''DW_IsCurrent'',''DW_Audit_Insert'',''DW_Audit_Update'',''DW_Audit'',''DW_Delta'',''DW_IsDeleted'') ORDER BY ORDINAL_POSITION FOR XML PATH('''')) ,''] ['',''], ['') + '' FROM [Schemaname].[Viewname] }'' ' SET @Sql = replace(@Sql,'[Viewname]',replace(@FinalTableName,'v_','')) SET @Sql = replace(@Sql,'[SourceName]',@FinalTableName) SET @Sql = replace(@Sql,'[Schemaname]',@SchemaName) SET @Sql = replace(@Sql,'[TargitSource]',@TargitSource) EXECUTE sp_executesql @Sql END; FETCH NEXT FROM db_cursor INTO @FinalTableName; END; CLOSE db_cursor; DEALLOCATE db_cursor; ``` #Minimizing already existing models Please consider doing the above to your existing Targit projects. If you already have a finished datamodel you can minimize the consumption further by running the code belov. The code compares the fields of a dimension table with the fields from that dimension that are actually used in the datamodel. Using this code requires: 1. You need to create your own personal 'compare' database on KMDDSB0106. If you do not have you own database, you can seek access to a non-existing database, which will then be create for you. 1. Add the targit datamodel.xml file to the share mentioned. 1. Script the schema and table you are checking, from the customers DM. The procedure should result in this, showing that the attributes 'Institutionsnummer' and 'Skattekode' from the dimension table, is **not** used in the datamodel and therefore could be removed from the ETL flow. ![image.png](/.attachments/image-3d80a171-2785-4dab-a387-577037824fec.png) ``` /* Create a database on KMDDBS0106 using the portal (seek access to a database using a servername and databasename. If the database does not exsist, it will be created Deploy the table definition scripted from the customers DM database Add your datamodel.xml file to the share \\KMDDBS0106\TargitDatamodelCheck\ and modify @SourceFilename below. Do not change path, only datamodel filename */ use [z3MCC_TargitDMtest] declare @debug INT = 0 declare @SourceFilename nvarchar(4000) = 'H:\TargitDatamodelCheck\860Datamodel.xml' --CHANGE HERE declare @DimensionTable nvarchar(250) = 'Dim_OekonomiPostering' --CHANGE HERE declare @SolutionSchema nvarchar(50) = 'oes' --CHANGE HERE --Create meta data from table. The dimension table you are investigating must be deployed here. DROP TABLE IF EXISTS system.[XMLCheck|DimensionTable] select s.name as [SCHEMA_NAME] ,case T.TYPE_DESC when 'USER_TABLE' THEN 'TABLE' else T.TYPE_DESC end as OBJECT_TYPE ,T.NAME AS [OBJECT_NAME] ,C.column_id as [COLUMN_ID] ,C.NAME AS [COLUMN_NAME] ,P.NAME AS [DATA_TYPE] ,case c.system_type_id when 231 then C.MAX_LENGTH / 2 else C.MAX_LENGTH end AS [SIZE] ,isnull(c.Collation_name,'') as [COLLATION_NAME] ,case c.is_identity when 0 then 'No' else 'Yes' end as [IS_IDENTITY] ,case c.is_nullable when 0 then 'No' else 'Yes' end as [IS_NULLABLE] ,c.precision as PRECISION ,c.scale as SCALE ,c.column_id as SortOrder into system.[XMLCheck|DimensionTable] FROM SYS.OBJECTS AS T JOIN SYS.COLUMNS AS C ON T.OBJECT_ID=C.OBJECT_ID JOIN SYS.TYPES AS P ON C.SYSTEM_TYPE_ID=P.SYSTEM_TYPE_ID JOIN SYS.schemas AS S on s.schema_id = T.schema_id WHERE T.TYPE_DESC IN ('USER_TABLE','VIEW') AND p.name != 'sysname' AND s.name != 'sys' AND LEFT(c.name,3) != 'DW_' AND t.name = @DimensionTable AND s.name = @SolutionSchema if @debug = 1 select * from system.[XMLCheck|DimensionTable] --Load datamodel xml scipt to table. Your datamodel must be saved on share \\KMDDBS0106\TargitDatamodelCheck\ and variable @SourceFilename must be changed --Inspiration https://www.mssqltips.com/sqlservertip/2899/importing-and-processing-data-from-xml-files-into-sql-server-tables/ declare @SqlStr as nvarchar(max) declare @SourceFile as nvarchar(max) = ''''+@SourceFilename+'''' DROP TABLE IF EXISTS [system].[XMLCheck|DataModel]; CREATE TABLE [system].[XMLCheck|DataModel] (XmlCol xml); set @SqlStr = '' select @SqlStr = @SqlStr + 'INSERT INTO system.[XMLCheck|DataModel](XmlCol) SELECT * FROM OPENROWSET( BULK [Source], SINGLE_BLOB) AS x' set @SqlStr = replace(@SqlStr,'[Source]', @SourceFile) EXECUTE sp_executesql @SqlStr if @debug = 1 select * from [system].[XMLCheck|DataModel] --Compare Dimension structure and datamodel definition DROP TABLE IF EXISTS [system].[XMLCheck|Result]; DECLARE @XML AS XML, @hDoc AS INT, @SQL NVARCHAR (MAX) SELECT @XML = XMLCol FROM system.[XMLCheck|DataModel] EXEC sp_xml_preparedocument @hDoc OUTPUT, @XML SELECT o.COLUMN_NAME DM_field ,o.[SCHEMA_NAME]+'.'+o.[OBJECT_NAME] DM_tablename ,a.[name] model_visualname ,a.[displayfolder] model_displayfolder ,a.[levelname] model_levelname ,a.[namecolumn] model_namecolumn ,a.[keycolumn] model_keycolumn ,a.[table] model_tablename ,o.[SortOrder] sorting INTO [system].[XMLCheck|Result] --select * FROM system.[XMLCheck|DimensionTable] o LEFT JOIN OPENXML(@hDoc, 'analysisDatabase/shareddimensions/dimension/level') WITH ( --dimension [name] [varchar](50) '../@name' ,[displayfolder] [varchar](150) '../@displayfolder' ,[description] [varchar](250) '../description' ,[timedef] [varchar](250) '../timedef' --level ,[levelname] [varchar](50) '@name' ,[levelorder] [varchar](50) '@order' ,[namecolumn] [varchar](50) 'namecolumn' ,[keycolumn] [varchar](50) 'keycolumn' ,[table] [varchar](150) 'table' ) a on a.[table] = o.[OBJECT_NAME] and a.[keycolumn] = o.[COLUMN_NAME] if @debug = 1 select * from [system].[XMLCheck|Result] --Present result of compare, fields from DimensionTable but NOT represented in DataModel will not be shown select distinct r.model_tablename,'['+r.[DM_field]+'],' as 'Dim_OekonomiPostering',r.[DM_field], r.sorting, r.model_displayfolder,r.model_visualname from [system].[XMLCheck|Result] r where r.model_tablename IS NOT NULL order by r.sorting ``` #Taking it all the way The third part is not completed yet. We are working on extending the datamodel to database compare module, for customers with the KMD TargitLog solution. It is possible to run through the log and check if certain fields is used. Thereby is would be posible to rule out fields from the datamodel that the customer does not use. This is most convinient for datamodels running at one customer only.

path: /Technology & Software/2. Targit/2.5 Installation/2.5.8 Move Data Discovery setup from one server to another server
content:
This article is based on the TARGIT Community article, which can be found here:
https://community.targit.com/hc/en-us/articles/360017077998-Move-Data-Discovery-setup-from-test-server-to-production-server

# Move Data Discovery setup from one server to another server

To copy data sources and cubes from one server (source) and OVERWRITE EVERYTHING on another server (target), it can be done like this:

1. Stop **TARGIT Data Service** service in Services on target server. (IIS Application Pools)
2. Backup everything in installation folder on target server, typical: C:\Program Files\TARGIT\TARGIT Data Service
3. Copy the following data from source server to target server:
C:\Program Files\TARGIT\TARGIT Data Service\ConfigurationDB.db
C:\Program Files\TARGIT\TARGIT Data Service\Files\*.*

4. Restart **TARGIT Data Service** service in Services on target server.
The target server now runs with new setup and configuration.

 

**Note that it is not possible to copy only selected data sources and cubes. It is everything that is copied, and what is in target server is lost.** 

If data sources are located on a network share on the source server, the service account running Data Discovery on the target server should also have access to this share, otherwise the network share should perhaps be moved to the target server, with the same network share name as on the source server, hence the network share on the source server should be disabled or renamed, since two network shares cannot have same name. So moving the network share is a "one-off" operation.

Also, if moving the network share to a new location, you should check that the service account running Data Discovery on the target server also have the same folder privileges as on the previous location, since service accounts might have the same name, but have different ID's on each server.

# If Data Discovery is placed on another server - seperate from Targit Server


If you wish to run the TARGIT Data Discovery component on another computer than the TARGIT Server you must ensure the following prerequisites:

- A TARGIT Server with a valid TARGIT Data Discovery licence must be configured and running.
- Ensure that the computer you wish to install the TARGIT Data Discovery component on meets the requirements. You also need to turn off the secure browser mode for the UI to be shown.
- An accessable Windows Share must be created and provided with full write permissions for the service account that TARGIT Server is running. This share must point to the TARGIT settings folder. Default path is 'C:\ProgramData\TARGIT\ANTServer\'.

Once this is achieved, follow the steps below to perform the installation:

1. Download the Installer, continue the installation process until you reach the point where you can configure the components.
1. Select the TARGIT Data Discovery component (deselect all other components), click on the cogwheel icon to perform the configuration.
1. Customize your installation, if necessary.
1. On the 'TARGIT Server' tab, enable the 'Use remote TARGIT Server' box and set the server name and
1. port number as well as the path to the TARGIT Server.
1. The TARGIT Server name format must be [servername:port number], the default port number is 1301.
1. The path to the server is the share created earlier, in the format [\\servername\TARGIT].
1. Validate your settings.
1. Open Windows 'Services' control panel and stop the 'TARGIT Data Service' service. Change the service account credentials to an account with full permission to modify the file share created earlier, then restart TARGIT Data Service.
1. Go back to the Installer and finish the installation by clicking 'Install'.
1. Restart the 'TARGIT Server' service account on the server where it is installed.
1. Start the 'TARGIT Management' application, go to 'Rights' and give the current user permission to be 'Data Discovery Administrator'.

The installation is now completed and you can launch the Data Discovery tool from the 'Design menu' in the TARGIT client application.

path: /Technology & Software/2. Targit/2.5 Installation/2.5.7 Setting up the logging functionality
content:
This article is based on the TARGIT Community articles, which can be found here:
https://community.targit.com/hc/en-us/articles/360017096717-Setting-up-the-logging-functionality- and
https://community.targit.com/hc/en-us/articles/360016980157-Logging-Analysis-Requests-to-Auxiliary-Database

# Setting up the logging functionality

Create an empty relational database on the installed SQL Server instance. Give it a proper name i.e. TARGITLogDB.

Create an Auxiliary Relational Database connection in TARGIT Management client.

This is done using the Connections tab à right-click in the working area and add a connection à click ‘Other’ à click ‘Auxiliary Relational Database’.

![mceclip0.png](/.attachments/mceclip0-e4ec0031-ea62-4936-bcc0-a1122db88d61.png)

Specify a proper name for the connection, i.e. LogDB. – on the next screen a connection string needs to be specified. Click ‘Change connection string’.

![mceclip1.png](/.attachments/mceclip1-7c901bf7-7990-46e2-b9ae-bda615ecd11a.png)

Select the desired provider. In this case we will be using the ‘SQL Server Native 10.0’ provider to connect to the relational database we created earlier.

Now, click ‘Next’ to configure the connection and database. In our case, the database is hosted on the local installed SQL Server instance, so we simply refer to the server: ‘Localhost’.

We can connect to the server using Windows integrated security. This setting also needs to be applied. Finally, the database we will be using needs to be selected from the list. Click ‘OK’ to create the connection string.

![mceclip2.png](/.attachments/mceclip2-faa3ab19-8960-4873-aa48-0c87dbb50cbc.png)

Click ‘Create’ to finish configuration of the Auxiliary connection.

# Enabling logging
To enable logging, go to the Setup tab in TARGIT Management.

1. Click Back-end.
2. In the window, check the boxes "Log Analysis requests to auxiliary database" and "Log storyboard requests".
3. Select for how long you want to keep the log information in the database.
4. Restart the TARGIT Server to start logging.

# Targit Log database
A Targit log database is set up either on an existing SQL server or alternatively an MS SQL server 2016 express edition can be installed on the Targit server where logging in. 

Installation for SQL Server 2016 express can be found at \\kmd1p\AS-BI-EDW\Install 

A database (TARGIT_LOG) is created where the ANTserver service is used becomes a member of the dbadmin role on this database. A connection from Targit to the database is then set up to log queries.
  
History is set to 180 days.

content:
**DER MANGLER EN SEKTION OM DOTNET INSTALLATION**

[[_TOC_]]


Going forward our customers are recommended to run a two server setup. This following guide is used to install a new customer from scratch. The two server setup indicates having two separate servers who run different TARGIT components. We can boil it down to having:
- **AntServer** (Which runs Data Discovery, TARGIT Anywhere and the TARGIT Client)

- **InMemory server** (Which runs all the InMemory components (ETL Scheduler Management, ETL Studio, Query Tool, InMemory Database (tiServer))).

# **AntServer installation**

# Folder structure on the AntServer

The folder structure on the AntServer is not as excessive as on the InMemory server, due to the fact that no InMemory or ETL work needs to be saved on the AntServer. Furthermore, all KMD work regarding ETL or InMemory is located on the 'InMemory server'. Therefore folder structure needs to be as following and created manually or using the following PowerShell commands:
``` powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -path "D:\KMD\BackUp"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -path "D:\KMD\Install\Programs\TARGIT\Build [VERSION]"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -path "D:\KMD\Install\Programs\Chrome"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -path "D:\KMD\Install\Programs\dotnet"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -path "D:\KMD\Install\Programs\Notepad++"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -path "D:\KMD\Install\Programs\SSMS"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -path "D:\KMD\Install\Programs\Microsoft Edge WebView2"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -path "D:\KMDWORK\[UserInitials]"
```

path: /Technology & Software/2. Targit/2.5 Installation/2.5.4 Installing Data Discovery on a Separate Server
content:
**Prerequisites:**
1. Having atleast two servers:
   - TARGIT Client server
   - Data Discovery server
2.  The 'TARGIT Client'-server must have the TARGIT Client-component installed. You need this to generate a connection string in TARGIT Management as well as creating the 'DataService'-connection.
3. .net core must be installed on the Data Discovery server (atleast version 6). Can be found here: https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download
4. The two servers must be able to communicate because we need to make a connection between the two servers (if they are in the same network/domain, this usually is not a problem).
5. IIS must be installed on the Data Discovery server. The Data Discovery service is using the IIS. IIS configuration can be seen here: https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.LG.wiki/3419/Setting-up-a-new-server-for-a-new-customer-on-a-2-server-setup?anchor=iis-installation


To simplify the process, we split this guide up into two sections: What to do on the 'TARGIT Client'-server and what to do on the 'Data Discovery'-server.


**What to do on the 'TARGIT Client'-server:**



Run the TARGIT Decision Suite and install the components required (TARGIT Client is of course required in this example).

Go into TARGIT Management --> Opsætning --> Back-End --> Write the URL for the given 'TARGIT Client'-server as seen in the picture below. This TARGIT servers name is 'SL-TAR-APP-01' for reference.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-b95470dc-1b81-4531-93b8-6867f889ca7b.png)


Afterwards go to "Service account" under "Security". Here you right click and create a Data Discovery service account. 
![image.png](/.attachments/image-6f208a12-46b8-4404-b0c9-f9bb3e8c724e.png)
If you right click and check properties, the data discovery service account has two keys as well as a connection string.
This connection string is needed when installing Data Discovery on the dedicated 'Data Discovery'-server. 
![image.png](/.attachments/image-6a9453bc-b9b3-4c4f-82ff-3fec1f6cce06.png). 

If you use the "Key 1"-connection string, you will also have to use this 'Key 1' in the DataService-connection as seen below:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-03ef3bd3-debf-4a71-b0e7-62232a92ec20.png)

For now, paste the Connection String from the 'Data Discovery Service account' and head to the 'Data Discovery server'.


**What to do on the 'Data Discovery'-server:**

Before running the TARGIT Installation Wizard we have to run .net core (atleast version 6). The installation wizard can be found here: https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download

This is just a "Next->Next->Next"-installation without any configuration in the installation wizard.

After you have installed .net - Run the 'TARGIT Decision Suite'-setup file on the Data Discovery server.


![image.png](/.attachments/image-ebff1862-7e06-47e5-bce9-a61c948b50bf.png)
Install

![image.png](/.attachments/image-83f43ef4-af52-4acc-80a1-c5268dc59faf.png)

Press 'I accept the license agreement' --> Next

![image.png](/.attachments/image-8784bc18-2034-4bb1-9f4f-779bbe6f70e8.png)

'Continue without license' --> Next

![image.png](/.attachments/image-b47eef49-8cbb-45e5-90cd-aedca7840fbc.png)

Next

![image.png](/.attachments/image-3c89bf6c-5728-44f9-ac46-cbbf4ee1449a.png)

Deselect all components except 'TARGIT Data Discovery' --> Proceed by clicking the cogwheel next to 'TARGIT Data Discovery'



![image.png](/.attachments/image-bb67c763-11a0-4df1-962b-ace3b2c8e27b.png)

Deselect 'Use default settings', however the 'General' and 'Data Manager'-tab is just default. 'Language' and 'TARGIT Server' needs some configuration.


Language - make sure 'Danish' is above 'English (Worldwide) in the right window:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-207e5cba-6f1a-4b84-a8ef-ac529de45e20.png)


'TARGIT Server'-tab:
Press remote and copy the connection string found in TARGIT Management (Data Discovery service account):

![image.png](/.attachments/image-c73e5e16-00ed-4489-af11-4df2be088608.png)

'Test connection' and make sure the connection is OK.

Proceed by clicking Next 

Run the installation


![image.png](/.attachments/image-c5cbb92b-bfb8-4a58-9c47-89b2f0c6f62c.png)

The data discovery component has now been successfully installed. 

Go back to the 'TARGIT Client'-server to test if data discovery works properly in the TARGIT client.



## HTTP Error 500.30 - ASP.NET Core app failed to start

If you experience following error: 
![image.png](/.attachments/image-b0fc587a-d0d8-4a93-bcaf-45cf8c14ca3d.png)

An input to debugging can be to check if the connection string specified in the TARGIT installation process is correctly registered in _"Targit.DataService.Exe.Settings"_.
If the connection string is not registered correctly it will be shown as: 
![image.png](/.attachments/image-ec220710-f301-475a-895b-b940202a15cd.png)


The connection string should be as followin. **Please note that you should stop the Data Service in the IIS before changing the connection string**:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-0d723667-1f32-437d-a673-f3ac7b606eab.png)

For clarification, KOLAPP2005 is the Antserver and should be specified in Management -> Opsætning -> BackEnd.
**"<ANTserver.Url.ConnectionString>TargitServerAddress=https://KOLAPP2005:1301;ServiceAccountID=bb9677a4-97b0-4beb-9aa3-91b415c57d26;ServiceAccountKey=baj6fGS6SbeWyHgjVZNcmCzL1h/LgpSAG0KLw2CwcSzZVeTV+2U0Si55ad1PjTvi98MXWZhZM6p2Di/kMXa3dw==</ANTserver.Url.ConnectionString>"**

After this, it should work properly.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-68909725-0e74-4c5f-aee6-7b2370cb13c7.png)
