This guide provides a step-by-step process for enabling GitHub Copilot, a powerful AI-based code assistant, within your development environment. Whether you're setting it up for the first time or reviewing security protocols, this guide covers the essential steps. You will be guided through understanding security policies, obtaining a GitHub Copilot license, and enabling the tool in popular IDEs such as Azure Data Studio and Visual Studio Code.
By following these instructions, you can confidently and securely integrate GitHub Copilot into your workflow.

---
# How to enable GitHub Copilot
This is a guide on how to get started with using GitHub CoPilot. It overall requires two steps:
1. Read and understand security terms
2. Obtaining GitHub CoPilot licens
3. Enable GitHub CoPilot in IDE software

## 1. Read and understand security terms
You have to remember and accept the following points to use AI Assistance in you source code:
- you are responsible for all code you push to git - independent of whether you use AI or not
- you need to understand and test your code before you are allowed to push it to Git repository
- you are not allowed to share secrets and GDPR data with AI Assistant
- you should ensure that AI Assistant will not learn from our data (is already done on DIMA organization level in the Enterprise GitHub subscription).

Other general guidelines and policies on using AI agent in KMD can be found [here](https://kmddk.sharepoint.com/sites/SECURITYHANDBOOK/Public/Forms/AllItems.aspx?id=%2Fsites%2FSECURITYHANDBOOK%2FPublic%2FSecurity%20Policies%2FRules%20for%20AI%20chatbots%20and%20other%20third%2Dparty%20online%20available%20tools%2Epdf&parent=%2Fsites%2FSECURITYHANDBOOK%2FPublic%2FSecurity%20Policies). 

These are highlights of the current KMD policy around using source code as input to AI assistants:
- Before using any part of a source code, get prior and unequivocal approval from the 
asset owner for the specific code, and for the specific purpose of use.
- Always make sure that none of the provided code will be saved for optimizing the 
AI/LLM.
- Make sure that there are no secrets or sensitive data hardcoded into the used code.
- Make sure that you have the copyright for using the provided code/output for 
commercial use.
- Live usage of AI code assistants should not be used on production code.
- AI code assistants are not allowed to be used when processing personal data in your 
code.
- You are still fully responsible for the security and integrity of the final code.

## 2. Obtain GitHub licens
1. Contact MMP about the need/wish to have a GitHub CoPilot license.
2. Create a free GitHub account https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/start-your-journey/creating-an-account-on-github
You can either use you @kmd or own personal email. If you actively engage open source solutions using you private account could make sense.
3. Ask MMP or KZH (Group IT) to add you GitHub account to our existing KMD DIMA account/organization. 
4. Accept invite and setup two factor authentication. Once you accept the invite you can request a seat within GitHub Copilot (see image below), or you can request it manually asking MMP or KZH. Once you have been granted a GitHub Copilot seat, you will get a notification by email.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-b7b88bb8-84a3-462d-8c23-d62b97e92bab.png)

## 3. Enable GitHub CoPilot in IDE software
The supported IDE tools that allows GitHub Copilot through extensions can be found [here](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/start-your-journey/creating-an-account-on-github).

This guide only explains how to enable GitHub CoPilot inside Azure Data Studio and Visual Studio Code. If you need it inside other IDE's then please find information online.

### Azure Data Studio
..... in progress

1. Open Visual studio code
2. Go to 'Extensions' and search for github copilot and go ahead install the extension
![image.png](/.attachments/image-6b8ab4ee-76aa-44d3-a6c6-5b4bbf1be685.png)
3. Go to the Copilot on left menu and sign in using GitHub Account.
![image.png](/.attachments/image-0b941ce5-13b6-4f7e-9d84-3f38953c4585.png)
Remember to have other default browser than Internet Explore for completing the two factor authentication that is required at first login.

#Introduction 
This guide walks you through the process of retrieving usage KPIs for GitHub Copilot using the GitHub API. By following these steps, you can generate reports on how GitHub Copilot seats are being utilized within your organization. This guide includes instructions for creating a GitHub personal access token, authorizing it for your organization, and using PowerShell to fetch and process the data.
You'll learn how to securely configure the API access token and execute the script to extract and save key metrics in both JSON and CSV formats for further analysis.

---
# Get usage KPI from GitHub Copilot
On this page [here](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/copilot/copilot-usage?apiVersion=2022-11-28) you can find documentation about how to access the github API to gain data about how the seats within copilot on GitHub have been use.

Here is a guide on how it can be retrieved using powershell.

## 1. Create a access token on github
1. Log in to GitHub:
- Go to GitHub and log in to your account.

2. Navigate to Developer Settings:

- In the upper-right corner of any page, click your profile photo, then click Settings.
- In the left sidebar, click Developer settings.

3. Create a New Token:

- In the left sidebar, click Personal access tokens.
 -Click Generate new token.

4. Configure the Token:
- Give your token a descriptive name in the Note field.
- Set the Expiration for the token. You can choose from preset options or set a custom date.
- Select the Scopes or permissions you want to grant this token. in this case we only need 'read:org'

5. Generate the Token:
- Click Generate token at the bottom of the page.

6. Copy the Token:
- Once the token is generated, copy it and store it securely. This is the only time you will be able to see it. If you lose the token, you will need to generate a new one.

7. Authorize token towards GitHub organization
- Hit 'Configure SSO'
- Authorize new token against KMDDima.

## 2. Run script against API 

Use the access token from above and insert it into the script below. The script writes the output to terminal and creates to txt files with the output ass well.

- raw_response.json: contains all information and nested objects from the API.
- copilot_usage.csv: contains only data about the top level of the json hierarchy.

Please go ahead adjust the output file path so it fits your usage and developer environment. 

```
# Define the GitHub API endpoint to fetch Copilot usage
$orgName = "KMDDIMA"  # Replace with your organization name
$apiUrl = "https://api.github.com/orgs/$orgName/copilot/usage"
$outPutPath = "<insert output path>" # ex. E:\KMDWORK\z6...

# Define your GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT)
$token = "<insert generated access token>"  # Replace with your actual token

# Send a GET request to the GitHub API with authentication and headers
$response = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $apiUrl -Method Get -Headers @{
    "Accept" = "application/vnd.github+json"
    "Authorization" = "Bearer $token"
    "X-GitHub-Api-Version" = "2022-11-28"
}

# Inspect the raw response to understand its structure
$response | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 | Out-File -FilePath "$outPutPath\raw_response.json"

# Define the path to save the CSV file
$outputPath = "$outPutPath\copilot_usage.csv"  # Replace with your desired file path

# Save the response to a CSV file
$response | Export-Csv -Path $outputPath -NoTypeInformation

# Display the response
$response | Format-Table -AutoSize

# Display a message indicating the file has been saved
Write-Output "Response saved to $outputPath"

#Introduction On this page, you will find various scripts used for maintaining and automating our wiki structure, ensuring that documentation stays organized and up-to-date. These scripts are integrated into our pipelines, automating many processes to reduce manual effort and improve efficiency. Each entry includes a link to the script and a brief description of its function. Click on a headline to view or edit the script and see how it is used within our automated workflows. [[_TOC_]] --- ###Scheduling The automation pipeline is set to run automatically once every 24 hours, although most of the scripts will run everytime there is a change in any wiki page. For technical information you can check out the pipeline here [KMD.DIMA.LG.wiki - Pipelines](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_apps/hub/ms.vss-build-web.ci-designer-hub?pipelineId=5347&branch=wikiMaster) ###[Table of Subpages Manager](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_git/KMDBI.wiki?path=/updateAllParentPages.ps1) Checks all markdown files in the wiki for subpages, adding or removing a table of subpages as needed to maintain a well-structured page. Changes are automatically committed and pushed to the repository. ###[Tag Manager](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_git/KMDBI.wiki?path=/updateTags.ps1) The script scans the wiki for initiate tags and matches them with corresponding final tags, generating a table that includes links to the paired pages along with a 300-character excerpt from their introductions. Tag pairs can be viewed and managed in the [tagConfiguration](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_git/KMDBI.wiki?path=/tagConfiguration.json) file, where new pairs can easily be added. The script efficiently searches for final tags within or below the same folder as the initiate page, allowing the same tag to be utilized across multiple folders without interfering with/include pages from other subject areas. If you wish to create a tag pair that can match with pages anywhere in the wiki, include `!root!` anywhere in your initiate tag. ###[Order Structuring](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_git/KMDBI.wiki?path=/orderStructure.ps1) Script that order files in folders numerical, so users doesn't have to order files manually whenever they create a new file. The script ignores alphabetical structures, it will only reorder numerical filenames. It works by scanning the wiki repository for .order files, which lie in every folder with subfolders, and orders them numerical. ###[Repository Content Manager](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_git/KMDBI.wiki?path=/productServiceGen.ps1) This script automates the creation of folders and pages for each repository listed in the table found in Products-&-Services main file. It extracts the technical and friendly names from the table, creates corresponding folders and pages, and then searches for repositories matching the technical name in the project. If a doc.config file is found in the repository, it creates a subject folder and markdown page based on the subject, and pulls content from the repository's README.md to populate additional pages. This ensures that documentation is automatically generated and updated from repository content, improving efficiency and consistency across the wiki. The script runs whenever there is a change in Products & Services, is run manually or otherwise it will change once a day. ## Q&A
What if I dont want a README from a repository to be in the wiki? If the repo is not used anymore, disabled repos will not be put into the wiki. If you still want the repo to be available, but not shown on the wiki, simply just delete the doc.config file. At this time, you still have to manually delete the unwanted page from the wiki - but do this after you have either disabled or deleted doc.config.

When does the README content be updated? The pipelines for tagging etc. outside the products & services folder will run whenever there is a change. Updates for README files will happen if there is a change in the products & services or any of the files contained in that wiki subpage - otherwise it runs once every 24 hours.

What pages do i have to save when i use the tagging function? Whenever you tag a page with a finaltag and save the page, the pipeline will run and your indexpage will automatically update. So there is no further action needed than tagging your page and saving it.

Can I edit the README content directly on the wiki? You cannot edit the readme directly on the wiki page, because the pipeline will always fetch what is in the repository and replace the page with that content, so be sure to always edit the README file directly in the repository.

Can I edit the friendlyname for a repository in Products & Services? Yes. The friendlynames are made from our best guesses to what it should be. If a more fitting name is needed, it can be edited, just be sure to edit the name in the table and NOT edit the folder name

content:
[[_TOC_]]

##Requirements for GlobalCitizenIdentifier :
-	Can’t be cpr
-	allows joining citizens across modules in easy and efficient way across one municipality (there is no need for cross municipality analysis based on this ID) 
-	Can be used and shown on reports.
-	Performs better on joins then CPR

Nice to have if possible:
-	On customer request (rarely) it would be nice to be able to regenerate new Identifier.

##Implementation
GlobalCitizenIdentifier dimension (dbo.DimensionGlobalCitizenIdentifier) is independent of new Citizen module (it is part of ms.common.global). Can be used to join citizens across modules without using CPR. The Dimension contains only CPR and new identifier.
The identifier itself is a DW_SK_GlobalCitizenIdentifier. A standard framework key is sufficient to play this role. Dimension contains all possible CPRs generated apart from cprs of people born in 19th century. It is part of global common and located on each ETL Server. 
Since the dimension is very large and doesn’t have any information apart from the key itself it shouldn’t be transferred to IQ or Dataout (that is why it is deliberately placed in dbo schema instead of default dimension schema).Instead IF fact can be transferred further since it has only Citizens taken from source project (a project related local dim citizen key) and DW_SK_ GlobalCitizenIdentifier.
Regeneration of the DW_SK_ GlobalCitizenIdentifier on customer request is possible but to take effect on all IF facts all involved projects need to be reloaded.


##Technical details of installation and sequence regeneration – for maintenance

Module: https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_git/ms.common.global
Portal info:
![Portal.jpg](/.attachments/Portal-cd1ddad3-7adb-4feb-9db2-5ee6bf22dea6.jpg)

To keep the same combination of Citizen and its identifier on all servers, the dimension is populated on one server and table data is replicated to rest of ETL servers by @<Claus Donner>  Powershell script. 
That is why after module installation the table is empty and should be filled only on one server  **KDIPMSSDB02**. 
Dimension population is executed by running procedure:
EXECUTE  [dimension].[Insert_GlobalCitizenIdentifier];
After this step two tables are filled:
[dbo].[DimensionGlobalCitizenIdentifier]
[system].[DimensionGlobalCitizenIdentifierAudit]
both should be replicated by  @<Claus Donner>  Powershell script to the rest of ETL servers.

If sequence regeneration for GlobelCitizenIdentifier is ordered bot steps should be repeated, but the procedure should be executed with with **@RegenerateGlobalCitizenIdentifier**  = 1 parameter.

##Application to existing modules

### Creation of IF Fact - default approach
Creation on IF fact based on KP dataarea module example - first local Citizen dimension name and local cpr field should be found:
![KP.jpg](/.attachments/KP-cef0f23a-9af5-4ca1-9217-fc877ff335c6.jpg)
The easiest and safest method of creating GlobalCitizenIdentifier IF fact is using a dedicated template in module builder. Instead of full Fact name only its unknow part – local Citizen dimension name needs to be provided as a "Name of fact" parameter:
![MB_1.jpg](/.attachments/MB_1-9c9f0162-9c3a-4e46-98f2-63cbfaa953eb.jpg)

List of objects created for given example in KP project (in KP Citizen dimension is called BorgerCitizen):  
![MB_2.jpg](/.attachments/MB_2-279ec8fc-d311-4bd2-9c1e-96b1b0c54db9.jpg)
All objects can be deployed without additional changes apart from procedure in fact schema where local CPR field needs to be provided according to the comment inside the comment.
![MB_3.jpg](/.attachments/MB_3-e0a5af93-4af6-42ec-88a2-46e8cc9684ac.jpg)

### New field in local dimension Citizen

Since relation between citizen and its GlobalCitizenIdentifier is 1:1, there is nothing wrong in placing DW_SK_GlobalCitizenIdentifier directly in existing Citizen Dimension. It might save some time in its implementation to BO universes if there are many. Still it requires special attention when it comes to delta load of dimension and lack of local DW_Audit in dbo.DimensionGlobalCitizenIdentifier, this requires special attention especially in case of possible DW_SK_GlobalCitizenIdentifier regeneration, these things are handled in template for IF Fact.

# How to create a new DSA or DATAAREA module
Creating a new DSA or DATAAREA involves completing a sequence of steps like:
1. clones the template repository
2. create a new remote module repository
3. copy content from the template to the new module
4. replaces template-specific strings with the specified module name
5. and commits the changes to the remote repository.

Compared to the previous process of using the modulebuilder functionality, this has now been automated by utilizing the kmdbips library. Inside the module kmdbips.helper.global there is a function that based on some input parameters does all the above actions automatic. The function to use is New-MSModuleFromTemplate. Documentation and examples on how to use this function can be found [here](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/9106/15.2.3-New-MSModuleFromTemplate). 

Inside template.dsa.001 and template.dataarea.001 a copy_module.ps1 under the bin folder is added. This ps1 file contains some predefined parameters, to copy the content of that exact template. This ps1 file can just be executed with powershell and it will then automatic prompt you for the new module name and local path for storing the local branch.

#Introduction

This page contains information about our local/own PowerShell (PS) repository. All inhouse developed PS modules goes with the prefix name KMDBIPS (KMD BI PowerShell). All KMDBIPS modules is distributed across all servers and can be accessed by the given PS module environment paths. Each KMDBIPS solution is its own powershell module, which then contains of multiple functions, which can be utilized.

---

[[_TOC_]]

# Utilizing KMDBIPS
## Getting overview of modules and functions
All modules contains help files, containing basic information about the given module. Further each module function contains command based help keywords like .Synopsis, .Descriptions and .Parameters.

### Get information module level
To get all kmdbips modules and a brief description of their content and usage (from module manifest), use the following command:
`Get-Module -ListAvailable | Where-Object { $_.Name -like 'kmdbips*' } | Select-Object Name, Description, Moduletype, Version`


Get help text from given module:
`Get-Help kmdbips.helper.global`

### Getting information function level

Get overview of all modules and their functions
```
# Retrieve all modules matching the pattern 'kmdbips*'
$modules = Get-Module -ListAvailable | Where-Object { $_.Name -like 'kmdbips*' }

# Group the modules by their names and select the latest version
$latestModules = $modules | Group-Object -Property Name | ForEach-Object {
    $_.Group | Sort-Object -Property Version -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
}

# Initialize an array to store function information
$functionInfo = @()

# Iterate through each latest version module and its functions to retrieve help information
foreach ($module in $latestModules) {
    # Get all functions within the module
    $functions = Get-Command -Module $module.Name -CommandType Function

    # Iterate through each function in the module
    foreach ($function in $functions) {
        # Retrieve help information for the function
        $helpInfo = Get-Help -Name $function.Name -Full

        # Retrieve the description from help info
        $description = if ($helpInfo.Description) { 
            $helpInfo.Description | Out-String 
        } else { 
            "No description available" 
        }

        # Add function information to the array
        $functionInfo += [PSCustomObject]@{
            ModuleName   = $module.Name
            FunctionName = $function.Name
            Description  = $description.Trim()
            Version      = $module.Version.ToString()
        }
    }
}

# Display function information in a table
$functionInfo | Format-Table -AutoSize

```

Get help from given function
`Get-Help Set-GitSubmodule`

#Introduction

# .DESCRIPTION
The New-MSModuleFromTemplate function creates a new module by copying content from a specified template repository and making necessary replacements in the copied files. It 
1. clones the template repository
2. creates a new remote module repository
3. copies content from the template to the new module
4. replaces template-specific strings with the specified module name
5. and commits the changes to the remote repository.

## .PARAMETER organization
The organization name in Azure DevOps. Default is "kmd-dima".

## .PARAMETER project
The project name in Azure DevOps. Default is "KMD.DIMA.LG".

## .PARAMETER templateRepository
The name of the template repository to clone content from. This must be one of the supported templates: "template.dsa.001", "template.dataarea.001".

## .PARAMETER localPath
The local path where the new module will be created.

## .PARAMETER moduleName
The name of the new module to be created.

## .EXAMPLE
```
import-module kmdbips.helper.global

New-MSModuleFromTemplate -templateRepository template.dsa.001 -localPath E:\KMDWORK\z6mmp\test -moduleName "tester5.dsa.001"
```
This example creates a new module named "tester5.dsa.001" by copying content from the "template.dsa.001" template repository to the specified local path.

#Introduction
---

# .DESCRIPTION
This function creates or updates a GIT submodule. This function is automatic executed everytime you build your project, as it is executed by the bin\pull_includes.ps1 file in each product module. It also handels nested submodules.

## .PARAMETER IncludePath
String parameter, will often be default to 'include' in module root folder, but can be changed.

## .PARAMETER IncludeName
String parameter, mandatory, provides a friendly name to the submodule in your parent directory. This is needed due to some legacy paths in the old SVN modules.

## .PARAMETER Repository
String parameter, mandatory, the name of the remote repository name that should be added as submodule/include in the parent repository.

## .PARAMETER Branch
String parameter, mandatory, will often be master branch from submodule that is linked to parent directory. But can be changed to other feature branches if needed.

## .PARAMETER CommitHash
String parameter, mandatory, if you subscripte to always include the lates version of the submodule, then leave this blank. If commit hash is provided then you link you parent repository to a specefic commit from submodule. Here is a guide on how to get the commit hash from Azure Devops: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/repos/git/commit-history?view=azure-devops (Copy commit SHA)

##.EXAMPLE
```
Write-Host "Adding submodule"

# Import kmdbips.git.global module
Import-Module kmdbips.git.global

#### Get Basic Reuse 
    #---------------------------------------------
    $IncludeName = "reuse_dataarea"
    $Repository = "reuse.dataarea_ms.001"
    $Branch = "master"
    $CommitHash = ""
    #---------------------------------------------
    
    Write-Host "Pull $IncludeName"

    Set-GitSubmodule -IncludeName $IncludeName -Repository $Repository -Branch $Branch -CommitHash $CommitHash

####

# if more reuse is needed, copy above and change parameters.


# Keep terminal open to see 
Read-Host "Press enter to exit..."
```

path: /Technology & Software/15. KMDBIPS - Powershell Framework/15.3 kmdbips.git.global/15.3.3 Add-GitSvnToGitModuleArray
content:
#Introduction
---
# .DESCRIPTION
This function can be used as a wrapper around New-GitSvnToGitModule, which then allow you to convert an array of modules in the same execution. It takes an array of SVN modules and then iterates over New-GitSvnToGitModule foreach added SVN module. Further it eliminates the need for creating local folders, which has to be done if you executes New-GitSvnToGitModule directly.

## .PARAMETER localRootPath
String parameter that takes the root folder where you want to store all local git repositories. Ex. E:\KMDWORK\<username>

## .PARAMETER repository
Array parameter, that takes an array of all SVN modules you want to convert. The Array consists of the svnUrl and gitModuleName. 

Ex. 
@(
    [PSCustomObject]@{ svnUrl = 'https://internsvn.dima.kmd.dk/im/TRUNK/Produkter/001_dataarea_ia'; gitModuleName = 'ia.dataarea.001' },
    [PSCustomObject]@{ svnUrl = 'https://internsvn.dima.kmd.dk/im/TRUNK/Produkter/001_dsa_ia'; gitModuleName = 'ia.dsa.001' }
)

## .PARAMETER skipNameCheck
Bool parameter, optional, that takes true or false. By default false, but if true then it skippes the validation on the naming convention. This should not be used for DSA or Dataarea modules, but only custom modules.

## .PARAMETER skipExitInteraction
Bool parameter, optional, that takes true or false. By default false, but if true then it skippes the read-host execution interaction in New-GitSvnToGitModule. So when iterating over multiple repositories it is recommended to set this value to true.

## .EXAMPLE
```
# Import the module
Import-Module kmdbips.git.global -Force

# Set root directory, for where new git modules should be stored locally
$localRootPath = 'E:\KMDWORK\z6mmp'


# Define the list of pairs as custom objects
$repository = @(
    [PSCustomObject]@{ svnUrl = 'https://internsvn.dima.kmd.dk/im/TRUNK/Produkter/001_dataarea_ia'; gitModuleName = 'ia.dataarea.001' },
    [PSCustomObject]@{ svnUrl = 'https://internsvn.dima.kmd.dk/im/TRUNK/Produkter/001_dsa_ia'; gitModuleName = 'ia.dsa.001' }
)

# Execute function
Add-GitSvnToGitModuleArray -localRootPath $localRootPath -repository $repository -skipExitInteraction $true
```

# Introduction We have intention of utilizing open source technology in a larger extend within DMBI. Opportunities within open-source around data engineering are many, and growing over time. This page contains information about potential relevant open source application to use on our data platform, in relation to the various aspects of operating our platform. --- Find link to all open source application in above image here: https://github.com/pracdata/awesome-open-source-data-engineering Read more here: https://alirezasadeghi1.medium.com/open-source-data-engineering-landscape-2024-8a56d23b7fdb

# Introduction

TARGIT is a powerful business intelligence (BI) and analytics platform that supports key decision-making processes across organizations. This section of the wiki provides comprehensive information on how TARGIT is utilized within KMD, including details on production, development, deployment, and support.  

In this section, you’ll find documentation on topics such as:  
- **TARGIT in KMD**: Discover how TARGIT is implemented and utilized across KMD.  
- **Production**: Insights into the Operations Portal, environments, and deployment processes.  
- **Development**: Best practices for designing and rolling out new dashboards and reports.  
- **Support**: Resources and guides for troubleshooting and resolving TARGIT-related issues.  
- **Tools**: An overview of additional tools and integrations that enhance TARGIT’s functionality.  

Explore these resources to make the most of TARGIT and optimize your workflows.

---

[[_TOSP_]]

In KMD LG we use Targit software for customers, that does not want to be a part of the common municipality Business Objects platform.

The software is typically installed on KMD servers reciding in the customers own domain.

#Demo
For inspiration and for a demonstration of what Targit looks like, go to the Targit demo server: demo.targit.com or solutions.targit.com

We are currently working on a KMD Targit demo server for internal use. The server is not running 24/7 due to operation costs. Please contact OCG if you need to use the server: https://targitdemo.dima.kmd.dk/

KMD DIMA is using Targit as an internal BI tool, mostly for Operations data. Try this out here: [Operations Portal](https://targit.intranet.kmdhub.net/touchserver/#vfs://global/Portal/Portal%20Frontpage.xview)

#TARGIT Decision Suite
The core of all TARGIT installations is the TARGIT Server. The TARGIT server cannot stand alone - you will also need a couple of clients. As a bare minimum you will need these TARGIT components to get going:

##The TARGIT Server. 
This is the central service that handles all communication between the Data Warehouse and the end-users. All requests from the end-users (opening dashboards, applying filters, expanding crosstabs etc.) is forwarded through the TARGIT Server to the connected Data Warehouse. In response, all matching data from the Data Warehouse is returned to the end-user client.

##The TARGIT Management client.
This client is necessary, not least in order to create a connection to your Data Warehouse(s). In general, you can say that the TARGIT Management client is the tool you need to configure and manage your TARGIT Server. E.g., you will use the TARGIT Management client to attach a mail server to your TARGIT installation - to facilitate sending automated, scheduled reports from your TARGIT system. It is also in the TARGIT Management client that you will manage everything with regard to Data Governance - using Rights and Roles to define what users are allowed to do, and what data users are allowed to see.

##The TARGIT Designer Client.
At least one of these clients is required to start working with your data. See the Designer Client description below.
As mentioned a couple of times, you will of course also need some kind of Data Warehouse holding your data of interest. E.g., you can connect directly to a SQL Server Analysis Services database (tabular or multidimensional). You can connect to many other kinds of Data Warehouses as long as it has a well defined Data Model. If it hasn't, you can create one.

If you do a trial installation of the TARGIT Decision Suite, the TARGIT Server will automatically connect to a Demo Data Warehouse with a full Data Model. You will even get a number of pre-defined Demo dashboards and reports to go along with the trial installation.

###Client types
Your license includes a number of Designer users as well as a number of Consumer users, typically in a ratio 1:10. E.g., in a medium sized company you may have licenses for 10 Designer user clients and 100 Consumer user clients.

###The TARGIT Designer Client.
The TARGIT Designer client is a Windows application - typically it is installed directly on the Designer user's PC. This is the end-user client that you will use to design dashboards and reports from the available data. You can also use this client as a Consumer client - for opening and working with already existing dashboards and reports. However, if your role is purely a Consumer user role, then we recommend you work with the Consumer-specific Anywhere client instead.
###The TARGIT Anywhere Client - the pure Consumer client. 
The Anywhere client is a browser based client. In other words, nothing needs to be installed from an end-user's perspective to start using the Anywhere client. Just open a browser and type in the proper URL to get access to the TARGIT Anywhere client. The Anywhere client is a pure Consumer client. You can open pre-defined dashboards and reports with the Anywhere client, you can filter, slice and dice the data in these documents, and you can export results to Excel or PDF. You cannot edit the design of existing dashboards and reports, nor can you create new ones with the Anywhere client.

###Included Modules
If your TARGIT installation is running with a Subscription pricing model, then all modules in this section is included in your license. All new TARGIT installation are based on the Subscription pricing model. If you are running a legacy pricing model, a Perpetual pricing model, some of the modules in this section may require an expansion of your existing license.

###Mobility module
The Mobility module makes sure that you connect to the TARGIT Server with mobile devices and even with the browser based Anywhere client.

For the Browser based Anywhere client to work, you will first need to configure the Anywhere web site on an Internet Information Server (IIS). This is easily done with the Anywhere Configuration tool. See this guide: https://community.targit.com/hc/en-us/articles/360017096277-TARGIT-Anywhere-Installation-and-Configuration

For TARGIT's mobile application for tablets or smartphones, search for 'TARGIT' in your AppStore or in Google Play.

###Data Discovery module
The Data Discovery module enables end-users to connect to their own data sources - e.g., an Excel file or an online weather data service. The Data Discovery module offers a simple, semi-automatic data modelling tool to make such ad-hoc data available for analytical purposes in a matter of minutes, or even seconds.

###Online Data Providers module
Data Discovery and InMemory comes with a lot of built-in Online Data Providers. Examples: Weather data, European Central Bank currency rates, Statistics Denmark etc.

A few online data providers still requires an additional check in the license setting - although, these should be included for Subscription pricing models by default. These data providers are:

JIRA
SalesForce
Jobindsats
Dynamics 365 Business Central
Custom Data Provider
 

###Enterprise Reporting (legacy)
The Enterprise Reporting module is a legacy module that, as long as it exists in our licensing model, should be included for all new installations.

The Enterprise Reporting module without the Enterprise Distribution module will grant access to:

Scheduled job for Report layouts (to PDF).
Scheduled job for Slideshows (to HTML).
Distribution options: Email and Folder only.
 

Add-on Modules
The Add-on Modules are not included with the standard installation of TARGIT Decision Suite. If any of these modules are required, access must be granted by a TARGIT Account Manager, and an additional charge may be associated with it.

 

Add-on: Enterprise Distribution
The Enterprise Distribution module enables many of the advanced fetaures related to TARGIT's Scheduling offering. 

Scheduling options without the Enterprise Distribution add-on license:

Scheduled job for Report layouts (to PDF).
Scheduled job for Slideshows (to HTML).
Distribution options: Email and Folder only.
In addition, the Enterprise Distribution add-on license will enable:

Scheduled job for Dashboard layouts (to graphical format, PDF or HTML).
Scheduled job for table data (to CSV, Excel or XML).
Distribution options: Publishing and Subscription.
Batch distribution.
Furthermore, the Enterprise Distribution license includes the option for Generic Embedding. With Generic Embedding, you can embed the TARGIT Anywhere client in any of your Business Systems.

 

Add-on: TARGIT InMemory
TARGIT InMemory is TARGIT's own offering with regard to a blistering fast column stored database engine. In many respects, it is similar to Microsoft's Analysis Services Tabular database engine.

TARGIT InMemory comes with a number of tools:

The TARGIT InMemory ETL tool - for extracting, transforming and loading of data from any of your source data systems into the InMemory database.
The TARGIT InMemory Scheduler - for automation, logging etc. of the ETL projects.
The TARGIT InMemory Query tool - for ad hoc querying of data in the InMemory database.
 

Add-on: TARGIT Insights
TARGIT Insights will provide valuable information about the use and current state of your TARGIT solution.

Once you enable TARGIT Insights, you will get all of this out-of-the-box:

A cloud-based logging database.
A comprehensive Data Model that connects automatically to your TARGIT Server.
More than 30 pre-defined dashboards with relevant statistics about your TARGIT solution.

# Targit ETL

## SET PRESERVE DECIMAL TRUE
By default then decimal data is imported it is converted into Double format, to speed up 
calculations. Double types can execute up to 5 times faster, than Decimal. This can cause 
small rounding issues when dealing with large amount of records.

IF you want to disable this behaviour you can use the command 

**SET PRESERVE DECIMAL TRUE** 

To reenable Decimal to Double conversion you can then use

**SET PRESERVE DECIMAL FALSE**

If the PRESERVE clause is used, it need to be set and disabled outside a parallel grouping like below

![image.png](/.attachments/image-c3935c52-8b35-4bf0-96e7-c3d698e68c89.png)

[[_TOSP_]]

# Deployment of Targit solutions
It has long been a widespread wish, that we would be able to deploy Targit solution to external machines without logging on to various customer servers.

Due to the nature of a Targit deployment it is not a simple task to automate this completely and initial setup will have to be done manually.

But the following should represent an easier way to deploy solutions, to restart failed jobs or to retrieve a support setup on KMD servers that mirrors the customers setup.

The general idea in this project is to create a way of deploying Targit solutions (ETL + Datamodel) from a KMD development server (or local pc) to a customer server without the trouble of requiring access or logging on to the remote server.

By using the following method, it is possible to deploy a solution to a customer by adding the deployment files to a deployment folder. The deployment files in this case, means an IMPROJ file and a Datamodel.xml file.

## Prerequisites
* The “SOLUTION” in the TargitSources config file must be alike on dev and all prod/customer servers.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-e797dec7-57a0-4d4c-992a-3d09cfc3c24d.png)
 
Prefix customer numbers suchs as "860OES" will be changed to "OES" and "DEV" will be changed to "PROD" when using the "DeployTool".

* The dev machine should be a lower than newest edition of Targit. ETL scripts and reports developed on a newer version will not always work on customer servers with lower versions. If you use our Targit Development server, you should be on safe ground.

## Reach out for initial installation.
TARGIT Platform will help with the initial installation. To ensure a good implementation, please provide the following:

* Impd and datamodel.xml file.
* Name of the connection used in the impd package and the TargitSources file.
* Information on what solution name should be checked in the IsAreaReady functionality.

TARGIT Platform will ensure that

* Deployment of the impd file to ..customerserver..PublishedFolders\KMDProduction.
* Execution of IMPD file when data is ready
* Entering connection information to the TargitSources file.
* Creation of a Connection on the customers server. The connection id from the Connections.xml should be reported in the TargitDeployDistribution table.
* Deployment of datamodel file (Not for the following customers: Jammerbugt, Thisted, Holstebro or Herning)

path: /Technology & Software/2. Targit/2.6 Development/2.6.5 SAP BO Solution conversion to TARGIT
content: #Prerequisites 1. Business layer text file You need a text file of the business layer. This can be gathered if you have access to SAP BO by saving the business layer as a text file. ![image.png](/.attachments/image-5d810f40-bbc3-4653-a35e-710a59f1d97e.png) ![image.png](/.attachments/image-9262157b-3878-4f05-af90-fb67f12bfb9e.png) ![image.png](/.attachments/image-4e43723d-1c6a-41b2-9819-9526c352ec8d.png) If you don't have access to SAP BO then ask @ for a business layer text file. 2. Business layer join text file You need a file with all joins between fact tables and dimension tables to assist in creating the data model. It can be gathered by saving the .dfx file in SAP BO as a text file or you can ask @ for the file. 3. SQL database with all relevant tables (facts and dimensions) Ask @ for a database that can be used to develop the solution. 4. PowerShell Script to convert BL text file to excel. The script can be found on SVN at Interne/targit/tools/DatamodelDocumentation/MakeDocFromBL.ps1 This script converts the step 1 text file to an excel file that can be used to create the Targit data model. #Step By step implementation ##PowerShell Script Make sure you have the BL text file and powershell script on you own system as it needs Excel installed to run. Run MakeDocFromBL.ps1 Enter locatation of Business layer text file in the shell. enter "y" for developer info. This gives you xml code that can be used to add dimensions to data model. Then the script will create an excel file with all measures and dimensions. ##Targit ETL Studio On KMDDBS0108 1. Create a copy of StandardETL.improj from SVN: Interne/targit/standard 2. Change name of file and Database name ![image.png](/.attachments/image-f4dff906-b726-4d3b-ba58-d2e9b77561c5.png) 3. Change version to 1.0.0, add release data and author >4. Add connection to SQL data catalog to TargitSources Located at: D:\KMD\Config\Targit\TargitSources.csv 5. Change "Set configurations" to select the connection just added to TargitSources 6. Use ***SelectOnlyCertainFields*** SQL script to get IMPORT lines. Found on SVN at Interne/targit/tools/DatamodelMinimize Description here: [Data minimizing](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.LG.wiki/3403/Data-minimizing) Copy output with “results to text” into a text file and remove line dividers. 7. Use Import CDIM_Dato in "Date" Use filters on date to prevent excessive load Example using all fact tables to find oldest date of all date dimensions where the main date dimension is maximum 5 years ago. ``` sql where case when da.DW_SK_Dato <= 19000101 then 99990101 else da.DW_SK_Dato end >= ( Select left(min(Dato),4)+'0101' From ( Select min(DW_SK_Dato) as Dato FROM sdloen.Fact_Forbrug where (DW_SK_Dato >= cast(DATEPART(YYYY,dateadd(YYYY,-5,getdate())) as varchar) +'0101') and DW_SK_Dato>0 union Select min(DW_SK_Dato_Optjeningsaar) as Dato FROM opuskvote.Fact_Beregninger where (DW_SK_Dato >= cast(DATEPART(YYYY,dateadd(YYYY,-5,getdate())) as varchar) +'0101' or DW_SK_Dato<0) and DW_SK_Dato_Optjeningsaar>0 union Select min(DW_SK_Dato_Afviklingsaar) as Dato FROM opuskvote.Fact_Beregninger where (DW_SK_Dato >= cast(DATEPART(YYYY,dateadd(YYYY,-5,getdate())) as varchar) +'0101' or DW_SK_Dato<0) and DW_SK_Dato_Afviklingsaar>0 union Select min(DW_SK_Dato_Optjeningsaar) as Dato FROM opuskvote.Fact_Feriesaldi where (DW_SK_Dato >= cast(DATEPART(YYYY,dateadd(YYYY,-5,getdate())) as varchar) +'0101' or DW_SK_Dato<0) and DW_SK_Dato_Optjeningsaar>0 union Select min(DW_SK_Dato_Afviklingsaar) as Dato FROM opuskvote.Fact_Feriesaldi where (DW_SK_Dato >= cast(DATEPART(YYYY,dateadd(YYYY,-5,getdate())) as varchar) +'0101' or DW_SK_Dato<0) and DW_SK_Dato_Afviklingsaar>0 union select cast(DATEPART(YYYY,dateadd(YYYY,-5,getdate())) as varchar) +'0101' ) Dato ) -- ADDING A YEAR TO MAX DATE and da.DW_SK_Dato <= ( Select max(Dato)+10000 From ( Select max(DW_SK_Dato) as Dato FROM opuskvote.Fact_Beregninger union Select max(DW_SK_Dato_Optjeningsaar) as Dato FROM opuskvote.Fact_Beregninger union Select max(DW_SK_Dato_Afviklingsaar) as Dato FROM opuskvote.Fact_Beregninger union Select max(DW_SK_Dato) as Dato FROM opuskvote.Fact_Feriesaldi union Select max(DW_SK_Dato_Optjeningsaar) as Dato FROM opuskvote.Fact_Feriesaldi union Select max(DW_SK_Dato_Afviklingsaar) as Dato FROM opuskvote.Fact_Feriesaldi union select cast(DATEPART(YYYY,getdate()) as varchar) +'1231' ) Dato ) ``` 8. Add Imports to "Load dimensions and facts"¨ Cross reference output from SelectOnlyCertainFields with table names from excel file from PowerShell script and copy in lines that exists in the Excel File - Copy table names from excel file into a new excel file and remove duplicates to make it easier. Limit date range on fact tables if limited in Date dimension Example: ``` sql select [fields] FROM opusloen.Fact_Loenkontering as LK Where LK.[DW_SK_Dato_Bogfoering] >=cast(DATEPART(YYYY,dateadd(YYYY,-5,getdate())) as varchar) +'0101' or LK.DW_SK_Dato_Bogfoering<0 ``` 9. Add roleplay dimensions If multiple date dimensions are used then (multiple datekeys) then add to roleplay dimension. This needs to be done for all dimensions used more than once. example: ``` sql IMPORT [Dim_Udbetalingsdato] = ME.[CDim_Dato] IMPORT [Dim_Aldersinterval_Anciennitet] = ME.[CDim_Aldersinterval] ``` >If for some reason a table exists in the excel file that doesn't exist in the database and it is not a roleplay dimension. Then you need to investigate directly in SAP BO or ask @ for clarification. 10. Run ETL package ##Targit Data Model Editor Once the ETL package has run you can begin designing the data model. 1. Add new connection in Targit Management to the newly created database. 2. Create designer tabs for each tab in the business layer. This can be one tab per fact table or multiple if related. But it doesn't matter much as long as all necessary joins are made. ![image.png](/.attachments/image-79a9bdc6-709a-435f-8736-ff4d238a444f.png) 3. Create all joins Using the join text file create all joins between fact tables and dimensions tables using the same keys. 4. Copy time dimension Find a NORM Cube data model in C:\ProgramData\TARGIT\ANTServer\Settings\Connections and copy the time dimensions into the data model you have created also somewhere in C:\ProgramData\TARGIT\ANTServer\Settings\Connections. ![image.png](/.attachments/image-29fa927e-caf0-4f8b-955a-f50771f4286e.png) If multiple date dimensions are needed in the new data model then copy the dimensions to a new window in notepadd++ and search replace the following lines before copying into the new data model. replace ``` " displayfolder ``` with ``` ([date dimension name])" displayfolder ``` replace ``` displayfolder="01 Tid\ ``` with folder used in excel sheet for other time dimensions: ``` displayfolder="01 Tid\[specific folder]\ ``` replace ``` schema="">CDim_Dato< ``` with ``` schema="">[dimension name]< ``` Then paste it into the data model as well. Do this for all date dimensions. 5. Create cubes and add measures Filter the excel sheet documentation to show only measures: The definition of the measures should then be in the select in column K: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-7c65bb44-0e74-4e50-89a0-64db087af6a3.png) Start adding all SUM and regular COUNT measures by creating a cube: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-9d11c19c-4cff-4114-ae74-c33a89127412.png) ![image.png](/.attachments/image-00387dc3-6080-4cde-b83a-0977f2a58180.png) ![image.png](/.attachments/image-10505035-005b-4724-bd76-bddd90af2fd1.png) and then right click the measure in the fact table and add as measure: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-17eb39b0-ac95-4be2-a531-52b1d1279d8e.png) Then add name, description and formatting to the measure: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-376c10b7-49bb-4d63-89f7-c78b7f7278aa.png) If there are measures like distinct count on a dimension member then you need to add that dimension to fact table in the ETL package by joining the fact and dimension tables. ``` sql select isnull(P.CPRnummer,-1) as measureCPRnummer , isnull(M.Medarbejder,-1) as measureMedarbejder FROM opusloen.Fact_Loenkontering as LK left join opuscommon.Dim_Person as P on P.DW_SK_Person = LK.DW_SK_Person left join opuscommon.Dim_Medarbejder as M on M.DW_SK_Medarbejder = LK.DW_SK_Medarbejder ``` If it is not good enough to have all unique occurrences of something based on one fact table then you need to create a new alias fact table based on the dimension and join this one to all relevant fact tables (which then join on underlying dimensions) example: ``` sql IMPORT [Fact_Medarbejder] = ME.{ select M.[DW_SK_Medarbejder], [Medarbejder] FROM Dim_Medarbejder as M join Fact_FuldtidsansatteMaaned as FM on FM.DW_SK_Medarbejder = M.DW_SK_Medarbejder union select M.[DW_SK_Medarbejder], [Medarbejder] FROM Dim_Medarbejder as M join Fact_Loenkontering as LK on LK.DW_SK_Medarbejder = M.DW_SK_Medarbejder } ``` Then you create relationships between this fact table and the other fact tables in the Targit Data model editor. Finally you add the measure from the Fact table to a new cube and add all shared dimensions. 6. Test that the model works by opening the Targit Client and creating tables using the measures and time dimensions. 7. Clean excel sheet - Duplicates - Alias tables Now that all measures and time dimensions are working it is time to add other dimensions to the data model but first the excel documentation needs to be cleaned. ###Handle duplicates Targit does not allow two dimensions to have the same name unlike SAP BO. So each dimension needs to have its own unique name. to make editing the names easier you can create a new dynamic column in excel. Here inserted as column M: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-4ce4cbef-4551-4878-813f-c5a7846e979f.png) ``` excel [Danish] =" Make sure you look at the top and buttom of names ![image.png](/.attachments/image-fa2bcdbe-ae3a-40a9-8a33-b2e3c8258c55.png) ####Sort by name Sort by name to make it easier to see duplicates ![image.png](/.attachments/image-0e3418a1-cec8-4371-9201-1bea79fa4d41.png) ####Color duplicates Select all rows in column C from row 5 and down and add conditional formatting on duplicates. (Found under Home tab) ![image.png](/.attachments/image-ab4c5d0c-2a72-4618-8ed9-14b390092785.png) ####Filter for duplicates Add a color filter to "Navn" column ![image.png](/.attachments/image-2e0bed20-14fa-454c-ae57-8966501f2fa4.png) ####Rename duplicates For each duplicate you need to rename dimensions such that they are unique. You could add a parenthesis at the end for hierarchies as such: ``` Dimension name (H) ``` Otherwise use your own judgement or ask for help. ###Alias names In the ETL package you might have added some alias tables you need to make sure these are referenced correctly by the XML in the Excel sheet. ####Filter Table column for alias tables Remove filters on color from "Navn" and then filter Table column (L) The table names should be easy to spot otherwise refer to the excel sheet you made in step 8. ![image.png](/.attachments/image-314ad474-1d3a-4db3-8096-48271f19629d.png) ####Replace with Targit InMemory table name. Look at the last part of the XML in column N: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-32a59d6c-15f2-4f25-bd41-bedeff543a0d.png) You need to replace the name in "schema" to match the name of the table in InMemory. In the shown example replace ```schema="">CDim_Aldersinterval (anciennitet)"<``` with ```schema="">CDim_Aldersinterval_Anciennitet<``` ![image.png](/.attachments/image-5ff4d414-d03c-498b-bd1f-b96b52c01a07.png) Do this for each different table. Now the excel file should be cleaned so you can go ahead and remove filter on table such that you only have filters on "Mappe" (B) Finally sort the table by "Mappe" (B) 8. Add dimensions to data model You can now start adding dimensions to your data model. >You may want to back up your data model at various points so that you can return to a working version if something goes wrong. You could start by taking dimensions one prefix at a time (eg. "02 Filtre") or all of them at once. Just copy the rows into the datamodel.xml under shared dimensions: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-2a049229-bf5c-4d98-b4eb-520590778519.png) Then open the data model editor and add the dimensions to your cubes. Right click shared dimensions for each cube and click add dimensions: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-ce72f69f-7c82-498b-b2d5-3a51ffbf273e.png) Click "Select all" and press OK: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-bd1831de-797d-42c1-a97b-89afc4365839.png) Do this for each cube. Test in the Targit client that the dimensions are working during this process. > You can refresh the data model in the client by right clicking the cube and pressing "Opdater" ![image.png](/.attachments/image-550b9304-7473-402f-b2c3-c64a4ed77688.png) 9. Create virtual cube and hide other cubes With all dimensions working and tested you can finalize the data model by creating a virtual cube containing all cubes, measures and dimensions. ![image.png](/.attachments/image-49dc063b-25c6-42c2-b178-0b8f430547bc.png) Select all cubes: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-2d55fcf2-decc-4579-8519-91cb7075730e.png) Select all dimensions: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-42e6a245-65f1-4c76-9a11-72f0f48516be.png) Select all measures: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-2079a54f-42b0-4aae-af2b-63f69bd27a93.png) Finally hide all the underlying cubes: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-de00d407-e112-424b-9c2a-f51e0e97e9b8.png) Save the data model. 10. Test the finished data model Open the new virtual cube in Targit client and test that all measures and dimensions are working as expected. If something looks wrong you may want to contact the person responsible for delivering the backend data. 11. Add datamodel version to data model To add datamodel version to the datamodel. Right click "AreaID" from CDIM_MartInfo in the datamodel editor and add as shared dimension ![image.png](/.attachments/image-07f8cb7b-7a47-4a14-a376-431fe6143736.png) Then format it as such: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-75c66230-d843-453e-9f6b-9d67682652f2.png) With name ``` Datamodel version ``` and the relevant version in the Description turn off visibility 12. Deploy to SVN You want to deploy the following to SVN. - Datamodel.xml - ETL package - Bus matrix - Excel documentation ###Datamodel This is the datamodel that is found in C:\ProgramData\TARGIT\ANTServer\Settings\Connections it needs to be deployed to 001_dataarea_XXX\src\targit\model ###ETL package This is the ETL package that was used to create the InMemory Database. This needs to be deployed to 001_dataarea_XXX\src\targit\etl ###Bus matrix You create the Bus matrix from TARGIT Data Model Editor. Select the Virtual cube and group by display folders: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-75f471fd-afa8-48dd-bb0a-31f7cfa751fe.png) Then just export the result and deploy it to 001_dataarea_XXX\src\targit\model ###Excel documentation To create the excel documentation you need MakeDocFromBL.ps1 from SVN found at Interne/targit/tools/DatamodelDocumentation/ Copy the datamodel.xml to your own system as well as the MakeDocFromBL script. > Excel needs to be installed to run it Run the script and enter the location of the datamodel when prompted. You will then get an Excel documentation that you need to deploy to SVN at 001_dataarea_XXX\src\targit\model

path: /Technology & Software/5. GIT/5.2 GIT - What, when and how?
content:
#Introduction --- [[_TOC_]] ## Convert from SVN to GIT ## It has for some time been requested and prioritized to change version control system (VCS), from SVN to GIT. Some of the reasons for this request are: - Linking work items with commits - Improve UI around our version control - Improve efficiency and ease around collaboration and distributed development. Including: - Branching - Pull requests - Extend the usage of the capabilities within Azure DevOps - Being able to automate process around our CI/CD pipelines - Use the capabilities within GIT - Access to a larger community also in regard of open source projects ## General differences between SVN and GIT The differences between SVN and GIT are many. This section covers some of the central differences in working with GIT instead of SVN as version control technology. | **Parameter** | **SVN** | **GIT** | |--|--|--| | **Interface/UI for accessing and managing VCS** | In DIMA LG we have used Windows/SVN dialog boxes to access and managing our SVN server. | Azure DevOps Repos will be used for accessing and managing our GIT projects. | | **Interface/UI for interacting with VCS** | Many DIMA LG developers are familier with TotoiseSVN, which is a Windows Explore extension, making it easy to do SVN commands in the Windows Explore. Besides Windows Explore support command lines can also be used, but is not commonly used inside DIMA LG.| Based on tests carried out in DIMA LG, we have chosen to recommend the usage og SourceTree instead of Totoise, because of easy of usage and visualization capabilities. SourceTree is a free client GIT GUI tool, that offers a visual representation of your repositories. Find documentation how to use SourceTree [here](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.LG.wiki/4869/Sourcetree). Command line and Visual Studio Code extensions can also be used, and usage is based on the individuel developers preferences.| | **Checkout/Upgrade/Commit** | To interact with SVN DIMA developers have often utilized **Checkout**, **Update** and **Commit** actions. | Git is a distributed version control system, where SVN is centralized. Therefor compared to SVN, GIT have a local repository that is a full clone of a central repository. This brings some changes on how to interact and contribute to the VCS.

Instead of using **Checkout** commands, **Clone** commands is used in GIT.

Instead of using **Update**, **Pull** command is used in GIT.

Instead of using **Commit**, **Commit(add)** and **Push** commands are used in GIT.

GIT have a lot of other command options in interacting with the VCS, an illustration of this is shown in the figure below. | | **Externals/reuse** | In our framework we have a lot of external modules that is linked to the given solution model each developer are working on. These are all place in the include folder as an external library. | Externals is a SVN element, where in GIT there are some other ways of handling external modules. Currently we do not utilize any GIT native service for this, as all the reuse component still is stored on SVN. Therefor we have create a Pull_Include.ps1 script which pulls the relevant external modules into include folder. This Pull_Include.ps1 file can be configured based on the needs within the given project, but templates for DSA and DATAAREA modules is provided. All scripts within include folder is then removed from source control by adding them to the .gitignore file. | | **Ignore list** | In SVN we use Windows/SVN dialog box to add folders, paths and files to ignore list, which is then excluded for versioning control within the given solution module. | In GIT we use a .gitignore file placed in the root folder | |**Naming convention** | We have had a naming convention around i product modules for many years. This naming convention have focused around DSA and DATAAREA modules. | We have changed the naming convention doing the transition to GIT. The reason is to cover other modules types than DSA and DATAAREA. Also it is aligned with the display options in Azure DevOps Repos. The naming conventions can be found [here](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.LG.wiki/4526/Naming-conventions). | ![image.png](/.attachments/image-b741ef0f-8e02-4369-8e58-0ed21bf62466.png) _Workflow/commands for interacting with GIT_ ## Available tooling, documentation and guidelines To smooth and assist the transition from SVN to GIT, some tooling, documentation and guidelines have been created and made available for everyone inside DIMA LG. These artifacts have been created not only to assist the transition, but also to give the teams/developers some agility to plan the conversion. The general rollout is planned in Q2 2024, but tools, documentation and guidelines is already in place, if you wish to convert to GIT before Q2 2024. This decision can be made by the individual product teams. The documentation that is available are: - Naming conventions and module types on GIT can be found here: https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.LG.wiki/4526/Naming-conventions - Creation of DSA modules: To be done... - Creation of DATAAREA modules: To be done... The tooling and guidelines of usage that is available are: - Automation script for converting SVN module to GIT and preserving all commit history. Find documentation on usage here: [Convert From SVN to GIT - Overview](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/9140/Convert-From-SVN-to-GIT) - SourceTree for interacting with GIT is installed on below listed development servers. Find documentation on usage here: [Sourcetree - Overview](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/9146/Sourcetree) ## Implementation plan and activities As mentioned general roll-out of usage of GIT in DIMA LG will be done in Q2 (planned for medio April). But if teams or developers decides to convert to GIT before, that is just fine. The actual conversion of modules from SVN to GIT will not involve all developers inside DIMA LG. One representative from each PDT will be responsible for converting all modules owned by the given PDT. The reason for this, is to have knowledge persons and contact persons within each team to ease-, speed-, streamline- and anchor the implementation of GIT. The roll out plan is as illustrated below: ::: mermaid gantt title Implementation GIT, starting 1. April 2024 dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD section Preparation T1 - Assessment of module ownership :t1, 2024-04-01, 30d T2 - Implement changes to pull_includes.ps1 script :t3, after t8, 3d T3 - Test of changes to pull_includes.ps1 script :t4, after t2, 3d section Onboarding T4 - Introduction of conversion to GIT - 45 min :crit, t5, 2024-04-17, 1d T5 - Session on how to use GIT - 1 hour :crit, t6, 2024-04-22, 1d T6 - Advanced - Session on how to use GIT - 1 hour :crit, t6, 2024-05-02, 1d Q&A - GIT Q&A - 15 min :done, crit, t20, 2024-06-03, 1d Q&A - GIT Q&A - 15 min :done, crit, t21, 2024-06-10, 1d section Conversion T8 - Conversion of all reuse (SVN modules on freeze) :t8, 2024-04-23, 3d T9 - Conversion of all in house tools (SVN modules on freeze) :t9, after t8, 3d T10 - Conversion of individuel solution modules :active, crit, t10, 2024-05-13, 18d T11 - Evaluation :t11, 2024-06-11, 3d section Operation T12 - Hypercare :t12, 2024-05-13, 28d ::: _Tasks/boxes of color blue only involves DIMA AO._ _Tasks/boxes of color red involves all developers inside DIMA LG._ _Tasks/boxes of color light blue with red boarder involves one selected developer from each PDT team_ _Tasks/boxes of color light grey with red boarder is optional for all developers inside DIMA LG_ _'T7 - Session on how to convert from SVN to GIT' is removed from general plan, and introduction is planned based on individual PDT request._ This plan indicates that the conversion of our module will start beginning of week 17, and will be done latest by the end of this week. ## Roadmap for feature requests around existing tools This section covers the by now known feature request to our tools to secure a smooth transition and use of GIT. If you experience any difficulties or have other wishes on our current tools for utilizing GIT, then please reach out to DIMA AO. By now the current feature request are: - Change request to ModuleCoreTool: To be able to automatic call pull_includes.ps1 file when building projects. This will secure an automatic incorporation of wanted external libraries. - Change request to ModuleCoreTool: To automatic rename patches to relevant release version. ## Responsibilities and roles - Owner: DIMA AO is the owner of the usage and processes of using GIT inside DIMA LG. Contact MMP if any questions. - Knowledge persons: - KAM Questions related to the conversion or usage of GIT within Q1 in 2024, should be directed to KAM, due to MMP being on leave. [#ADGuideline]()

##Guideline on how to migrate from SVN to git with preserved commit history
The guideline consists of of powershell scripts for automation of as much of the migration as possible. This guideline uses 001_dataarea_ia module as an example. Note that this guideline only consider migration of SVN revisions to git and not branches. 

###1. Find the wanted SVN module to convert
- First find the wanted module on SVN to convert to git. Browse TotoiseSVN (repo browser) and find the wanted URL:
![Screenshot 2023-10-12 202020.png](/.attachments/Screenshot%202023-10-12%20202020-8fa4d458-2aa7-4805-9a9a-a76014b1414d.png)
In this example https://internsvn.dima.kmd.dk/im/TRUNK/Produkter/001_dataarea_ia is used.

###2. Create a local folder from where you want to store your new git module
- Create a new empty local folder in you user path, remember to follow the naming conventions. These conventions can be found here: https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.LG.wiki/4526/Naming-conventions

- Example:
![Screenshot 2023-10-12 204709.png](/.attachments/Screenshot%202023-10-12%20204709-63c2dfcb-dab7-47a5-b890-881ee1862bf1.png)

###4. Clone the SVN repository into a new Git repository folder
- Check out the svn module to you newly created git folder. In this example 'KMD.DIMA.LG.ia.dataarea.001'. This can not be checked out by the TotoiseSVN interface, as tags, revisions, etc. have to be checked out as well and converted to a git structure. To do so utilize below powershell script, as it cannot be done manual.

```
cd [Newly created git folder path]

git svn clone ["SVN repo URL"] --authors-file=["Authors file path"] .

. = it is possible to ad a dest path to above command.

example:

cd "E:\KMDWORK\z6mmp\git_projects\KMD.DIMA.LG.ia.dataarea.001"

git svn clone https://internsvn.dima.kmd.dk/im/TRUNK/Produkter/001_dataarea_ia --authors-file=authors.txt .

```
- NOTE: this command can take some time to complete due to the number of revisions on our current SVN server.

- Now validate that .git folder is created and all script files and folders is cloned to the git folder. Note that externals (usually elements within include folder is not cloned to new svn module):
![image.png](/.attachments/image-a9a22d91-2eb9-4e30-b604-daeaae7c00f6.png)

###5. Delete authors.txt file
- No need for versioning the author files, as that wast just just for the migration from SVN to git folder/structure.

###6. Create bin folder and add Pull_Includes.ps1 file
- Git does not use external/include elements like SVN does. There are multiple ways of handling external repos in GIT. For now we have chosen to include these elements by running a .ps1 script. The reason for this is, that we have also can include SVN modules as external modules. Some framework components like config will still be maintained from SVN, until the ownership of this component have been decided.

- Depending on which module you are converting go copy Pull_Include.ps1 file from the related template module. An example of a template module could be:
  - KMD.DIMA.LG.template.dsa.001
  - KMD.DIMA.LG.template.dataarea.001

- You could also create you own pull_include.ps1 script, if you have other external modules used in your solution.
![image.png](/.attachments/image-2a2c5af0-9fac-4d54-b7cf-64fc87a987b8.png)

###7. Add .gitignore file
- To prevent pushing reuse/external repos to you solution repo remember to add a .gitignore file. This file tells GIT on which files, folders and paths to exclude from commit and pushes to remote repo.

- Depending on which module you are converting go copy .gitignore file from the related template module. An example of a template module could be:
  - KMD.DIMA.LG.template.dsa.001
  - KMD.DIMA.LG.template.dataarea.001

- You could also edit the file from template module or create you own .gitignore script, if you have other things in you solution to exclude from source control.
![image.png](/.attachments/image-04e0f315-8bc4-42d9-9096-2063d275716a.png)

###8. Create a new empty repository on Azure DevOps
- Go to KMD.DIMA.LG project on Azure DevOps https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_git/001_custom_carbonkey_tenant
- Crete new git repository. Use the same name as in step 2, which also is compliant with the [naming conventions](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.LG.wiki/4526/Naming-conventions). **Do not have the server auto-generate any files such as .gitignore or README.md.**
![image.png](/.attachments/image-a7310325-ac7c-4ac2-893a-d0bffdc6524e.png)

###9. Push new locale git module to new remote repo
- Commit the newly added files (pull_include and .gitingore). Using this powershell command:
```
cd [Newly created git folder path]

git add .

git commit --message "Added .gitignore and pull_include to module and converted to GIT."

Example:

cd "E:\KMDWORK\z6mmp\git_projects\KMD.DIMA.LG.ia.dataarea.001"

git commit -a --message "Added .gitignore and pull_include to module and converted to GIT."

```
- Set the Git repository on your computer to use the remote repository run this powershell command. The https address can be found after creation of remote repo:
```
cd [Newly created git folder path]

git remote add origin http://git.example.com/my-reopsitory

Example:

cd "E:\KMDWORK\z6mmp\git_projects\KMD.DIMA.LG.ia.dataarea.001"

git remote add origin https://kmd-dima@dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_git/KMD.DIMA.LG.ia.dataarea.001

```
- Mirror you local git project with remote project. Run this powershell command:
```
cd [Newly created git folder path]

git push --mirror

Example:

cd "E:\KMDWORK\z6mmp\git_projects\KMD.DIMA.LG.ia.dataarea.001"

git push --mirror

```

 
Migration is now done!


##Inspiration from
This guideline was inspired by KIP guideline. Elements that is added to the guideline compared to the KIP guideline is the stuff around migrating history on versioned folder. Also documentation from Microsoft can be found here: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/repos/git/perform-migration-from-svn-to-git?view=azure-devops

content: #Introduction This guide provides a detailed walkthrough for converting an SVN module into a Git module, guiding you through each step of the migration process. Whether you're converting one module at a time or handling multiple modules, this guide offers both manual instructions and an automated approach using a PowerShell function. By following the steps outlined here, you will learn how to securely authenticate, prepare your environment, and successfully migrate your SVN modules to Git, ensuring a smooth transition to modern version control practices. --- [[_TOC_]] # About This guide walks you through the steps of converting an SVN module into a Git module. I provides you with guidance on how to convert one module at a time, and gives you an insight into the steps that required to migrate a module from SVN to GIT. ### Migrate multiple modules at once If you are comfortable with these steps, you can skip all manual steps and utilize the powershell function Add-GitSvnToGitModuleArray from KMDBI local ps repository. This function takes a few input parameter, and an array of all the modules you want to convert, and then it iterates through all the provided modules and convert one module at a time in a sequence. Documentation on this function, and examples on how to utilize it can be found here: [15.3.3 Add-GitSvnToGitModuleArray - Overview](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/9110/15.3.3-Add-GitSvnToGitModuleArray) # Prerequisite ## 1. Set credentials and connect to Azure DevOps _Can be skipped if you already have authenticated to Azure DevOps once from given instance._ The remote GIT repository is located on Azure DevOps. Before you can connect to that from you environment, you have to make sure, that you have establish a connection with your credential. Open a powershell and execute the following command to authenticate to Azure DevOps: ``` az login ``` Then use you '@kmd.dk account and provide password. ## 2. Secure authentication to SVN _Can be skipped if you already have authenticated to SVN lately from given instance._ Make sure that you have authenticated towards the SVN server. 1. Right click and repo browser 2. Provide username/password if needed 3. Accept certificate permanently ![image.png](/.attachments/image-4df1648d-b6ff-4dfd-9a5c-bccc86aacf06.png) ### 2.1 Authentication realm - Error If you doing your execution of the conversion script experience an error like, 'Authentication realm: DIMA SVN Repository'. ![image.png](/.attachments/image-e8a220f2-fd93-425e-81a6-ef897245e3a7.png) Then please provide the SVN password when prompt. If it by default utilize a username that does not match you SVN account (svn username != kmdpfosap username), then it will prompt you again where it ask for both username and password. When prompt for password please provide you SVN password. Then the authentication should be saved on you account. # Start conversion of module ##1. Make sure you have committed all your updates to SVN ![image.png](/.attachments/image-0ea421d9-bb79-4590-aa2a-50d78d2da882.png) ##2. Create a local folder from where you want to store your new git module - Create a new empty local folder in your workfolder (fx aula.dsa.001), remember to follow the naming conventions. These conventions can be found here: https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.LG.wiki/4526/Naming-conventions An overview of all SVN modules and their new module name can be found here: https://kmddk.sharepoint.com/:x:/s/DIMALG-365/EVv8c1p0tyVKrQ_9Xv96h74Bki_FnXfteQh-SWxHDIFNhg?e=dpVegm - Browse to the folder ![image.png](/.attachments/image-9f8c2bce-23bc-4c33-bd2f-531a85c73eba.png) ##3. Make a powershell script files - Create a new text file - Rename the file to "ConvertToGit.ps1" ![image.png](/.attachments/image-838a8497-2563-4e3e-b3b4-e7643a5ebea8.png) - Paste the following code into the powershell file - Save and close the file ``` # Import kmdbips.git.global module Import-Module kmdbips.git.global # Call the New-GitSvnToGitModule.ps1 function to convert module from SVN to GIT New-GitSvnToGitModule #* # Keep terminal open to see actions Read-Host "Press enter to exit..." #*it is possible to add the SVN url as a input parameter instead of being promt for it in the pipeline (ex.: New-GitSvnToGitModule https://internsvn.dima.kmd.dk/im/TRUNK/Produkter/001_dataarea_ia) ``` ##4. Running the script - Right click the file and press "Run with PowerShell" - The script prompts you to enter the URL of the SVN repository, open the SVN repo browser and find the path of the repository you want to migrate. ![image.png](/.attachments/image-5ba24045-2df8-468e-b902-d1935ca84668.png) - If the SVN repository URL is not valid or the folder does not conform to the naming convention, it will display an error. - Otherwise it will start converting each SVN commit to a Git commit. It will take a while, depleting on the number of commits in the project, and will output a lot of text. You will be told when it is done, then press enter to exit. - In your workfolder the project "template.svntogit.001" will be cloned, you can delete the folder when it is done. - Once the conversion of the module is completed, please go to the following file and mark the module as converted in the column 'Is migrated to git'. The file can be found here: https://kmddk.sharepoint.com/:x:/s/DIMALG-365/EVv8c1p0tyVKrQ_9Xv96h74Bki_FnXfteQh-SWxHDIFNhg?e=dpVegm ## 5. Start using Git and Sourcetree https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.LG.wiki/4869/Sourcetree [[_TOSP_]] [#Guideline]()

##Guideline on how to migrate from SVN to git with preserved commit history
The guideline consists of of powershell scripts for automation of as much of the migration as possible. This guideline uses 001_dataarea_ia module as an example. Note that this guideline only consider migration of SVN revisions to git and not branches. As DIMA LG not have used branches in SVN, this must be sufficient for must solutions.

_Prerequisite_
Git have to be updated to new version on development environment ex. git version 2.42.0.windows.2. The current  git version 2.33.0.windows.2 on developer environment is missing git svn commands. If not passible to upgrade on developer environment, then this migration guideline can also be done from local pc. If it is done form local PC, then you need a TotoiseSVN, GIT installation and PowerShell installation. Also username/password is needed to authenticate towards SVN server.


###1. Find the wanted SVN module to convert
- First find the wanted module on SVN to convert to git. Browse TotoiseSVN (repo browser) and find the wanted URL:
![Screenshot 2023-10-12 202020.png](/.attachments/Screenshot%202023-10-12%20202020-8fa4d458-2aa7-4805-9a9a-a76014b1414d.png)
In this example https://internsvn.dima.kmd.dk/im/TRUNK/Produkter/001_dataarea_ia is used.

###2. Create a local folder from where you want to store your new git module
