![Screenshot 2023-10-12 204709.png](/.attachments/Screenshot%202023-10-12%20204709-63c2dfcb-dab7-47a5-b890-881ee1862bf1.png)

###3. Map SVN authors to GIT authors
- SVN just uses the username for each commit, while Git stores both a real name and an email address. By default, the git-svn tool will list the SVN username in the author and email fields. However, you can create a mapping file for SVN users along with their corresponding Git names and emails. The real name is your full name and email is your kmd email ex. xxx@kmd.dk. These name is also the once you should use when you configure you git environment and commit towards Azure DevOps. In case the revision is made by someone not in KMD anymore, just fill out the mapped name/email with the given 'z' user and a corresponding @kmd.dk email. Like the exsample below:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-a03a5e83-af40-43a9-9e52-de20df3b3317.png) 

- Run this powershell command to populate a text file containing all users who have made commits to this module:
```
cd [Newly created git folder path]

svn log ["SVN repo URL"] --quiet | ? { $_ -notlike '-*' } | % { "{0} = {0} <{0}>" -f ($_ -split ' \| ')[1] } | Select-Object -Unique | Out-File ["Authors file path"]

example:

cd "E:\KMDWORK\z6mmp\git_projects\KMD.DIMA.LG.ia.dataarea.001"

svn log https://internsvn.dima.kmd.dk/im/TRUNK/Produkter/001_dataarea_ia --quiet | ? { $_ -notlike '-*' } | % { "{0} = {0} <{0}>" -f ($_ -split ' \| ')[1] } | Select-Object -Unique | Out-File 'authors.txt'

```
- ![image.png](/.attachments/image-a7788b2b-61cd-45b5-a755-206871fae961.png)

###4. Clone the SVN repository into a new Git repository folder
- Check out the svn module to you newly created git folder. In this example 'KMD.DIMA.LG.ia.dataarea.001'. This can not be checked out by the TotoiseSVN interface, as tags, revisions, etc. have to be checked out as well and converted to a git structure. To do so utilize below powershell script, as it cannot be done manual.

```
cd [Newly created git folder path]

git svn clone ["SVN repo URL"] --authors-file=["Authors file path"] .

. = it is possible to ad a dest path to above command.

example:

cd "E:\KMDWORK\z6mmp\git_projects\KMD.DIMA.LG.ia.dataarea.001"

git svn clone https://internsvn.dima.kmd.dk/im/TRUNK/Produkter/001_dataarea_ia --authors-file=authors.txt .

```
- NOTE: this command can take some time to complete due to the number of revisions on our current SVN server.

- Now validate that .git folder is created and all script files and folders is cloned to the git folder. Note that externals (usually elements within include folder is not cloned to new svn module):
![image.png](/.attachments/image-a9a22d91-2eb9-4e30-b604-daeaae7c00f6.png)

###5. Delete authors.txt file
- No need for versioning the author files, as that wast just just for the migration from SVN to git folder/structure.

###6. Create bin folder and add Pull_Includes.ps1 file
- Git does not use external/include elements like SVN does. There are multiple ways of handling external repos in GIT. For now we have chosen to include these elements by running a .ps1 script. The reason for this is, that we have also can include SVN modules as external modules. Some framework components like config will still be maintained from SVN, until the ownership of this component have been decided.

- Depending on which module you are converting go copy Pull_Include.ps1 file from the related template module. An example of a template module could be:
  - KMD.DIMA.LG.template.dsa.001
  - KMD.DIMA.LG.template.dataarea.001

- You could also create you own pull_include.ps1 script, if you have other external modules used in your solution.
![image.png](/.attachments/image-2a2c5af0-9fac-4d54-b7cf-64fc87a987b8.png)

###7. Add .gitignore file
- To prevent pushing reuse/external repos to you solution repo remember to add a .gitignore file. This file tells GIT on which files, folders and paths to exclude from commit and pushes to remote repo.

- Depending on which module you are converting go copy .gitignore file from the related template module. An example of a template module could be:
  - KMD.DIMA.LG.template.dsa.001
  - KMD.DIMA.LG.template.dataarea.001

- You could also edit the file from template module or create you own .gitignore script, if you have other things in you solution to exclude from source control.
![image.png](/.attachments/image-04e0f315-8bc4-42d9-9096-2063d275716a.png)

###8. Create a new empty repository on Azure DevOps
- Go to KMD.DIMA.LG project on Azure DevOps https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_git/001_custom_carbonkey_tenant
- Crete new git repository. Use the same name as in step 2, which also is compliant with the [naming conventions](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.LG.wiki/4526/Naming-conventions). **Do not have the server auto-generate any files such as .gitignore or README.md.**
![image.png](/.attachments/image-a7310325-ac7c-4ac2-893a-d0bffdc6524e.png)

###9. Change in Module builder
Open the build.proj file and insert VersionServerType under the PropertyGroup
```
<PropertyGroup>
...
    <VersionServerType>GIT</VersionServerType>
...
</PropertyGroup>
```
After the change Module builder will ask again for PAT, the old one can be used (if you have it stored). Otherwise just regenerate it please. 

###10. Push new locale git module to new remote repo
- Commit the newly added files (pull_include and .gitingore). Using this powershell command:
```
cd [Newly created git folder path]

git add .

git commit --message "Added .gitignore and pull_include to module and converted to GIT."

Example:

cd "E:\KMDWORK\z6mmp\git_projects\KMD.DIMA.LG.ia.dataarea.001"

git add .

git commit --message "Added .gitignore and pull_include to module and converted to GIT."

```
- Set the Git repository on your computer to use the remote repository run this powershell command. The https address can be found after creation of remote repo:
```
cd [Newly created git folder path]

git remote add origin http://git.example.com/my-reopsitory

Example:

cd "E:\KMDWORK\z6mmp\git_projects\KMD.DIMA.LG.ia.dataarea.001"

git remote add origin https://kmd-dima@dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_git/KMD.DIMA.LG.ia.dataarea.001

```
- Mirror you local git project with remote project. Run this powershell command:
```
cd [Newly created git folder path]

git push --mirror

Example:

cd "E:\KMDWORK\z6mmp\git_projects\KMD.DIMA.LG.ia.dataarea.001"

git push --mirror

```

 
Migration is now done!

#Introduction

[[_TOC_]]


# About GIT submodules
Git submodules are a way to include and manage repositories within another Git repository. This is particularly useful when you want to incorporate external projects or dependencies into your own project while keeping them separate and maintaining their own version control.

## How to add a submodule

There are some basic commands to ad a git submodule to your parent project. To add a submodule to your repository, you can use the git submodule add command:

```
git submodule add <repository-url> <path>
```

Anther relevant git submodule command is:
```
git submodule update --init --recursive
```
This command initialize and update any added submodules. On the remote git branch submodules is not added to the source code, instead it references the submodule. So in some situations when working with the repository locally, the submodule have to be initialized for the reuse library to materialized inside your parent repository.

### Set-GitSubModule
To keep it simpel in handling the right naming convention, that is aligned with the structure of our BI framework, a function is added to kmdbips modules. This function is called Set-GitSubmodule and is part of the kmdbips.git.global module. Therefor this function can be utilized by importing the kmdbips.git.global module on all development servers. Documentation about this module/function can be found [here](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.LG.wiki/6102/Set-GitSubmodule), where it also describes the relevant input parameters to use.

By running either the native git submodule add cmd or the Set-GitSubmodule function all relevant nested submodules from the targeted submodule will be added.

### pull_includes.ps1
Inside all modules and template module for both DSA and DATAAREA, there is added a bin folder ind the root folder. This bin folder contains a pull_includes.ps1 file. Inside this file there are preconfigured parameters for including the default reuse libraries like reuse_dsa and reuse_dataarea. These pull_includes files utilizes the Set-GitSubmodule function. An example of pull_includes.ps1 file that includes reuse_dataarea looks like this:

```
Write-Host "Adding submodule"

# Import kmdbips.git.global module
Import-Module kmdbips.git.global

#### Get Basic Reuse 
    #---------------------------------------------
    $IncludeName = "reuse_dataarea"
    $Repository = "reuse.dataarea_ms.001"
    $Branch = "master"
    $CommitHash = ""
    #---------------------------------------------
    
    Write-Host "Pull $IncludeName"

    Set-GitSubmodule -IncludeName $IncludeName -Repository $Repository -Branch $Branch -CommitHash $CommitHash

####

# if more reuse is needed, copy above and change parameters.


# Keep terminal open to see 
Read-Host "Press enter to exit..."
```
As default the latest commit of a reuse library is included. If you with to include a specific commit from any reuse library, then use the CommitHash parameter. The commit hash key can be found in the commit history of a relevant repo. More information on this [here](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.LG.wiki/6102/Set-GitSubmodule?anchor=.parameter-commithash).

The location for the pull_includes.ps1 inside your module is important, as this particular file is called every time you build your project using the modulebuilder. Read more about this [here](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.LG.wiki/6121/GIT-Submodules?anchor=modulebuilder).

## .gitmodules
When adding a git submodule some meta data is added to both the projects .git folder and a file called .gitmodules will be added. This .gitmodules file contain information about the added submodule. An example of a .gitmodules file is:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-9d97d488-0901-4362-a69a-e499408ad566.png)

## Modulebuilder
To make sure that relevant submodules always is included in deployment and releases, execution of pull_includes.ps1 is part of the build process when using the modulebuilder. It is part of the Copy_dependencies task in the modulebuilder, and can be seen in the terminal when running relevant build operations:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-b7bd272e-2c3b-4dcd-b1ce-7def063bfbf0.png)

## SourceTree
In SourceTree a git submodule is not by default included when cloning a repository. Either doing the clone operation, a checkmark on 'Recurse submodules' have to be added. 

![image.png](/.attachments/image-10c0b7dc-6411-4bf0-b392-68bc56fdacd1.png)

This can also be set as default behavior when cloning repositories, go to Tools -> Options -> Git and add a checkmark in 'Perform submodule actions recursively'.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-dc34b20d-cbd9-484a-a3aa-56835c7eeee3.png)

The submodules can be seen in the left menu of any given repo. From the left side menu you can navigate to the given submodule.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-ccbb01b6-9989-43d9-b0f1-0b29a5bf567f.png)

## Azure DevOps repos
Adding a git submodule to your repository is just a reference to given sub module. Name of the submodule and other meta data can be found in the .gitmodules file in the root folder. Where information about the given commit can be found in the reuse folder when browsing the repository remotely like on Azure DevOps Repos:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-2b89f5f9-1544-44b3-8c95-5e0c9003fda4.png)

This also indicates that any submodule by default is not materialized in the parent directory remote branch, even though the submodule is not added to the .gitignore file.

path: /Technology & Software/5. GIT/5.3 Guidelines/5.3.3 Restore Deleted Repository
content:
#Introduction
---

## 1. Create or reuse PAT token
Reuse or create new access token. Token only needs read access on Code to read repository information, and write access on Code to restore it.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-e876a0ee-1d8f-4606-9f56-22e52c449455.png)

## 2. Find all deleted repos
We need the ID of the given repo to restore it, so go ahead query all delete repos to find the relevant ID. 

NOTE: that all deleted repos are only retained for 30 days.

To list all deleted repos in our organization run this powershell command. It requires a PS module called 'AzureDevOps', which is trusted and installed on Dev environment:
```
Install-Module -Name AzureDevOps

# Replace with your personal access token (PAT)
$personalAccessToken = "<insert your personal access token (PAT)>"
$base64AuthInfo = [Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetBytes(":$personalAccessToken"))

# Replace with your organization and project details
$organization = "kmd-dima"
$project = "KMD.DIMA.LG"

# Define the REST API URL for deleted repositories
$url = "https://dev.azure.com/$organization/$project/_apis/git/recycleBin/repositories?api-version=6.0-preview.1"

# Make the REST API call
$response = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $url -Method Get -Headers @{Authorization=("Basic {0}" -f $base64AuthInfo)}

# Output the deleted repositories
$deletedRepos = $response.value
foreach ($repo in $deletedRepos) {
    Write-Host "Repository Name: $($repo.name)"
    Write-Host "Repository ID: $($repo.id)"
    Write-Host "Deleted By: $($repo.deletedBy.displayName)"
    Write-Host "Deleted Date: $($repo.deletedDate)"
    Write-Host "---------------------------------"
}
```

An example of the output and the repository ID can be seen here:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-dffb5c05-7c93-407f-aa2e-b5328dd9a885.png)
## 3. Restore deleted repo
Find the relevant ID for the repo you want to restore and insert it into the PowerShell script below. 

NOTE: Your PAT token needs write rights on Code to perform this action.

```
Install-Module -Name AzureDevOps

# Replace with your personal access token (PAT)
$personalAccessToken = "<insert your personal access token (PAT)>"
$base64AuthInfo = [Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetBytes(":$personalAccessToken"))

# Replace with your organization and project details
$organization = "kmd-dima"
$project = "KMD.DIMA.LG"

# Replace with the repository ID you want to restore
$repoIdToRestore = "<insert relevant repo ID>"
$restoreUrl = "https://dev.azure.com/$organization/$project/_apis/git/recycleBin/repositories/$repoIdToRestore`?api-version=7.1-preview.1"

# Change the body content to not not being deleted anymore
$body = @{
    deleted = $false
} | ConvertTo-Json

# Send the PATCH request to restore the repository
Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $restoreUrl -Method Patch -Headers @{Authorization=("Basic {0}" -f $base64AuthInfo)} -Body $body -ContentType "application/json"

Write-Host "Repository with ID $repoIdToRestore has been restored."
```

# Introduction

Sourcetree is a powerful Git repository management tool designed to simplify version control for beginners while providing advanced functionality for experienced users. It offers a more intuitive interface compared to TortoiseSVN, enhancing both presentation and functionality. For more details about the tool, visit [Sourcetree's official website](https://www.sourcetreeapp.com/).

Before diving into this guide, it’s recommended to first read [GIT-What-when-and-how](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.LG.wiki/5028/GIT-What-when-and-how-), which covers important Git terminology and explains key improvements over SVN.

This page provides an overview of how to navigate and use the basic features of Sourcetree, helping you manage your repositories efficiently with Git.

---

# Navigating Sourcetree
To open Sourcetee, find the shortcut on the desktop. It is recommended to pin this app to your Taskbar for easy access in the future. 

When opening Sourcetree you can either add an existing git repository from your workfolder or clone a new repository from remote.
![image.png](/.attachments/image-bf9f3823-6379-4cf8-b83f-b62a33afed82.png)
The **Local** view lets you view all your local repositories, here you can also add an already existing repository to Sourcetree. See [link](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.LG.wiki/5212/Adding-a-local-repository-to-Sourcetree) for a guide on how to do this.

The **Remote** view lets you view all the Dima LG repositories and chose which you want to clone (download) to your local workfolder. See [link](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.LG.wiki/5214/Adding-a-remote-repository-to-your-workfolder) for a guide on how to do this.

# Using the Workspace
To open the repository Workspace view, go to the **local** view and double click a repository.
![image.png](/.attachments/image-3da41893-121a-44b3-a3e5-a7cb0cf9de60.png)

###Open repositories
In the top of the windows, marked with a red box, all open repositories will be displayed as tabs. To open a new press the small plus button.

###Action buttons


### Manage branches
In the left most side, your local branches are listed along with tags and remote branches. To change between local branches, double click a branch name to make it the active branch, all physical files will change to reflect the branch. To checkout a remote branch, find it in the explorer and double click it to create a local branch, the branch will now be added to the list of local branches and be set as the active branch.

### Commit history
This center window shows the commits and branches in on a vertical timeline.

## Internal diff not displaying changes
![image.png](/.attachments/image-f9e83dfc-5700-4fd3-a421-c1003b907345.png)

If the internal diff cannot display changes then the problem might be because the tool cannot read the file encoding, it works UFT-8.

The following code converts all your files to UTF-8
1. Open powershell
2. First browse to your project folder 
3. Execute the following code
```
Get-ChildItem *  -recurse -Include *.sql | ForEach-Object {
$content = $_ | Get-Content
Set-Content -PassThru $_.Fullname $content -Encoding UTF8 -Force}
```
4. Commit all changes

# Naming convention
The general naming convention for code product modules in DIMA LG is:

<project>.<type>.<tenant>

All in lowercase letters.

- **project** reflects the name of the given solution.
- **type** reflects what kind/category of the module.
- **tenant** reflects the customer for which this module belongs to.



##Recognized Project
Solution name reflects the name of the given solution. Should be kept short but also understandable. This is the technical name of  the module. Note that all modules have a technical name and a alternative friendly name, which is name of the solution in a customer/sales perspective. This mapping can be maintained in the admin portal maybe? Otherwise it can be maintained in some text file in each module. This can minimize the gab of recognizing modules between developers and sales persons.

Some examples of customer facing project solutions are:
- KY
- NOE
- DUBU3

Due to modules used across project solutions, the different modul types are also a reserved project name, and can therefore not be used in individuel solutions. This therefore covers these project names:
- reuse
- template
- backend
- log
- common
- tool
- web

When having project specific reuse or tools, then it should ex. be named like dubu3.reuse.001 or dubu3.tools.001

##Recognized Tenant
TenantNames reflects the receiver/consumer/customer (customers) for this given component. These customers can be both internal, general customers, specific customers or shared tenant across many customers. Dedicated reuse components does not have a TenantName.
- Global - GLOBAL tenant and used across solutions, not tenant specific deployment. Can be deployed once pr. server or only on one server. 
- Internal - Tools or modules that is not used for customer facing modules, but mainly for internal use. Could be automations, surveillance, operation or other related areas.
- 001 - Universal module for deployed for each tenant, still a customer facing module.
- TenantID - can be three digit [Municipality code](https://danmarksadresser.dk/adressedata/kodelister/kommunekodeliste). Is only used if module is developed for a specific tenant and no later need for deploying this for other tenant. Also if a tenant specifik module is branched out of the common solution. Try to avoid these specific modules if possible. If it is a tenant that is not a municipality, then go to [this page](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.LG.wiki/4529/TenantID's) and find/create a new tenant id.
- General - Only used for included repos, where general code can be shared across repos.

##Recognized ModuleType
See current module types in admin portal. These types can be categorized into seven categories:
  - product (product types - share tenant project or dedicated tenant project)
    - DSA
    - DATAAREA
    - TOOL
    - CONFIG
  - reuse (external/secondary repos)
  - template (template modules used as base for creation of new product solutions)
  - general ms modules (shared component across product solutions)
    - log
    - common
  - backend ms modules (db projects for different operation and monitoring solutions)
  - general tool (general tools that is not product specific, but for general user across projects. It can be tools for assistance in development or other relevant component in the overall dataflow.)
  - web 

### Example of naming convention for different module types
We have slightly different naming conventions to template and reuse modules. The reason is to easily identify them, also they will newer be deployed as a standalone solution to production.
  - product (PDT owner)
      - <project>.<type>.<tenant>
      - ex.
        - dubu.dsa.001
        - dubu.dataarea.001
        - dubu.targit.001 
        - dubu.tool.global
        - dubu.config.001
  - reuse (AO owner):
      - <type>.<project>.<tenant>
      - ex:
        - reuse.dsa.001
        - reuse.general_ms.001
        - reuse.targit.001
  - template (AO owner):
       - <type>.<project>.<tenant>
       - ex:
         - template.dsa.001
         - template.tagit.001
         - template.pbi.001
         - In ideal world there should be a template for each module type.
  - general ms modules (AO owner):
      - <project>.<type>.<tenant>
      - ex:
        - ms.common.001
        - ms.log.001
  - backend ms modules (AO owner):
      - ex:
        - <project>.<type>.<tenant>
        - kmdbi.backend.global
  
  - general tool (AO owner)
      - ex:
        - <project>.<type>.<tenant>
        - datatransfer.tool.global
        - dima.tool.global

The general tools available and corresponding documentation will be added to DIMA LG Wiki.

The reasons for this naming convention is to easily identify owners, users and type of a given component from the repo name. Also the order of these elements in the module name is important, as is affects the order and grouping of how the repo is listed in Azure DevOps Repos.

[[_TOC_]]

# Basic Installation

The following subchapters are which KMD softwares there must be installed on all servers

# Network requirements **Prod servers only**
We must have whitelisted the servers ip for klgateway in our network:
SCO-Test source IP adresses: 10.6.32.0/20
SCO-Prod source IP adresses: 10.7.128.0/20
**There are missing a guide or document describing how we must do it**

# Basic framework modules
- Copy the source code for the following 5 modules from \\\kdipmssdb01\f$\kmd\install\modules to local path f:\kmd\install\modules

- make sure you only copy the newest version of each of the 5 modules
![image.png](/.attachments/image-70ab57bd-9163-46d4-b897-7353b80d782c.png)

Install 5 modules with the following 4 Power Shell scripts. They need to be run as administrator.
- run \\\kdipmssdb01\f$\KMD\Utils\InstallMSSQLNewServer\OffLine install.ps1 to set up the required folders and ENV variables

- run \\\kdipmssdb01\f$\KMD\Utils\InstallMSSQLNewServer\log_ms_Psinstall.ps1 to install the module (open script and verify version)

- run \\\kdipmssdb01\f$\KMD\Utils\InstallMSSQLNewServer\KMDBI_Psinstall.ps1 to install the module (open script and verify version)

- run \\\kdipmssdb01\f$\KMD\Utils\InstallMSSQLNewServer\Common_ms_Psinstall.ps1 to install the module (open script and verify version)

# User setup
Create a user in [Secret Server](https://passwords.kmd.dk/SecretServer/app/#/secrets/view/folder/4079) in the folder "Microsoft BI Admin" with the generic username/password24 template
Call it gdpr_prod_access <SERVERNAME> 
with username gdpr_prod_access
and generate password

Create the user on the new server with sysadmin rights by following the three next pictures:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-608533cc-f0c5-466c-b865-f12849a692aa.png)
![image.png](/.attachments/image-431658fb-e09d-42ac-9644-eb1394433cd2.png)
![image.png](/.attachments/image-1e53732f-11ab-4387-8de3-225c067d52c6.png)
then create a linked server on the KMDBISITE (KDIPMSSDB16\prod) server and add user: 

- KMDPFOSAP\service_gdpr to use gdpr_prod_access on the remote server 
i.e.
`EXEC master.dbo.sp_addlinkedsrvlogin @rmtsrvname=N'<SERVERNAME>',@useself=N'False',@locallogin=N'KMDPFOSAP\service_gdpr',@rmtuser=N'gdpr_prod_access',@rmtpassword='PASSWORD FROM SECRETSERVER'`
- Create link server for user gdpr_prod_access: [Linkserver gdpr_prod_access.sql](/.attachments/Linkserver%20gdpr_prod_access-cd2e00b7-a190-44da-99bd-117197c06d52.sql). Remember to change to the relevant server name. The template is for server KDIPMSSDB13

- Execute the following script on the server that you are installing:

```
USE [master] 
GO 

CREATE CREDENTIAL [service_sqlagent] WITH IDENTITY = quotename( @@servername+ N'\service_sqlfilreader'), SECRET = N'@@@@@@@@@@' -- se secret server take password from the pfofil user. 
GO 

CREATE CREDENTIAL [CubeProcessorCrossServer] WITH IDENTITY = N'kmdpfosap\service_sqlagent', SECRET = N'@@@@@@@@@@' -- se secret server take password from the identity user. 
GO 

CREATE LOGIN [KMDPFOSAP\SQLDevelop_as_im] FROM WINDOWS WITH DEFAULT_DATABASE=[master], DEFAULT_LANGUAGE=[us_english] 
GO 

CREATE LOGIN [KMDPFOSAP\SQLReader_as_im] FROM WINDOWS WITH DEFAULT_DATABASE=[master], DEFAULT_LANGUAGE=[us_english] 
GO 

USE [msdb] 
GO 

/****** Object:  ProxyAccount [service_sqlagent]    Script Date: 5/9/2017 10:19:44 AM ******/ 
EXEC msdb.dbo.sp_add_proxy @proxy_name=N'service_sqlagent',@credential_name=N'service_sqlagent',  
@enabled=1,  
@description=N'Bruges til indlæsning af file fra pfofil share' 
GO 

/****** Operation System (CmdExec) *****/ 
EXEC msdb.dbo.sp_grant_proxy_to_subsystem @proxy_name=N'service_sqlagent', @subsystem_id=3 
GO 

/****** SSIS Package Execution *****/ 
EXEC msdb.dbo.sp_grant_proxy_to_subsystem @proxy_name=N'service_sqlagent', @subsystem_id=11 
GO 

/****** PowerShell *****/ 
EXEC msdb.dbo.sp_grant_proxy_to_subsystem @proxy_name=N'service_sqlagent', @subsystem_id=12 
GO
```
- Remember that you need to find the password for [pfofil1\service_sqlfilreader](https://passwords.kmd.dk/SecretServer/app/#/secrets/68883/general) in the first commandline and the password for [service_sqlagent](https://passwords.kmd.dk/SecretServer/app/#/secrets/34987/general) for the second line
- Add ad-group SQLFlis_as_im to Remote Desktop Users 
- Add full control to H: drive for ad group SQLFlis_as_im
- Add read control to folder f:\kmd\config\keyfiles for ad group SQLFlis_as_im
- Give SQLFlis_as_im these 3 rights on all flis2 and flis3 databases on the server
![image.png](/.attachments/image-1dac1d4b-771e-4c47-91a8-2cc50acbde0a.png)

# Install Core Tool module

# Installation of Coretool Sync 
Sync modules must only be installed on servers that need to update KMDBISITE with new releases
Sync modules on Azure DevOps with AdminPortal.
### Generate a PAT (Personal Access Token)
If you doesn't already have a PAT you caqn use.
https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.KIP/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.KIP.wiki/1416/Personal-Access-Token-setup
When you generate the PAT you get a code that looks like this prbjdtbhp6pp7ucu7v4p42vsvs5b6g6urcvu53w2cwd5cw7r6hpb **it is important that you save this code. It is needed when you Install core tool**
### Add PAT to kmdpfosap\service_sqlagent
Login at the server you want to install Sync tool on
Start a CMD as service_sqlagent, credentials can be found at [Secret server](https://passwords.kmd.dk/SecretServer/app/#/secrets/34987/general)
In CMD run the commands from this [link](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.KIP/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.KIP.wiki/1565/Azure-cli-login)
 Only run the commands under "If you are on the kmdpfosap domain use the following way"



###Configure Coretool Sync
Run the Powershell script SetUpSync.ps1 from this [link](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.KIP/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.KIP.wiki/1283/Coretool.Sync) (we are using Task Scheduler and trigger of 5 minuts)

- ServiceUser is kmdpfosap\service_sqlagent
- ServicePassword can be found on [secret server](https://passwords.kmd.dk/SecretServer/app/#/secrets/34987/general) 
- PAT is the code you got back when you made the PAT

### Test that sync is working
Before test check that adminportal has a releaseFeedInfo

#Installation of Orchestrator
Orchestrator will check if there is new installation order from adminportal, and execute the installation of the new release.

If you doesn't already have a PAT you can use same method as [above](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/9161/6.3.1-Installation-and-configuration-of-KMD-software?anchor=generate-a-pat-(personal-access-token)&_a=edit#generate-a-pat-(personal-access-token))

goto tab Actions

in Program/scrip type in pwsh

##  Running multiple SSAS instances on a single windows server


When running multiple SSAS instances on a single windows server it can be done in two different ways. 
Dynamic port assignment, and fixed port assignment.

When we are going _against customers_ we are using cap ip network and some natting occurs thus making it very difficult to handle dynamic port assignment though the network unless allow openings to a lot of ports.

Internally in KMD we have used Dynamic port assigment for out instances as all ports are alllowed for communication in KMD

### Different ways of port handling. 

**Dynamic Port Assignment**

When SSAS Starts:
Each SSAS instance (Multidimensional or Tabular) dynamically selects a free port unless configured to use a fixed port.
When SQL Server Browser Receives a Request on Port 2382,
The client sends a connection request on TCP port 2382 for SSAS.
SQL Server Browser looks up the actual port currently being used by the requested SSAS instance.
It then redirects the client to that dynamic port.
Dynamic Ports Are Chosen at Startup:
If no fixed port is set, each SSAS instance will select a random port on every restart.




**Fixed Port Assignment**

Make sure that the SQL SERVER Browser service is not started and it is set to disabled in the configuration.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-5eb400df-9fc2-4ff4-8933-4a425524eb26.png)



Steps to Assign a Fixed Port
Locate the msmdsrv.ini configuration file for the SSAS instance:

Default path:
C:\Program Files\Microsoft SQL Server\MSASXX.INSTANCE_NAME\OLAP\Config\msmdsrv.ini
Replace XX with your version (e.g., MSAS15 for SQL Server 2019).
Edit the file:

Find or add the <Port> element inside <ConfigurationSettings>.
Assign a fixed port (e.g., 2382):

<Port>2382</Port>

![image.png](/.attachments/image-0b0ae975-8ebf-42a3-8e0d-17e63e4533d0.png)

Save the file and then restart the SSAS instance.




How do i check it: 

RUN the following in a commandprompt

netstat -ano | findstr 2382

Verify that the SPID listning on the port are the SQL Server instance server you expect.

# Introduction

The Modulebuilder is a tool for managing database patches and version control. It helps compare database scripts with working databases or released versions, making it easier to identify differences and generate schema patches. With features like a compare wizard, it supports both DDL and DML operations during patch creation. While originally built for SVN, it now supports Git with some manual adjustments required for patch management.
In this section you can read about how to create a new patch.

# About patches
We generally use schema patches for out releases on database modules. A schema patch for a database refers to a set of changes applied to the database schema, which defines the structure of the database, including tables, columns, indexes, constraints, and other elements. Schema patches are often used to update the database schema to support new application features, fix structural issues, or improve performance.

We generally use patches when we have to do DDL changes to a solution in production that requires  dropping or altering a database schema, often tables. We can apply complex patches between release versions, applies DDL and DML operations where:
- Temp tables is created (DDL)
- Data is moved to temp tables (DML/Backup)
- Base tables is altered/dropped and recreated (DDL)
- Data is moved back into new tables that fits new schema (DML)

## Modulebuilder Compare Scripts
We can use the Modulebuilder tool for assisting on these patch operations. The compare wizard in the Modulebuilder have two general features:
1. Compare scripts to database working database
2. Compare Scripts against released version (for creating patches)

In general the compare wizard utilize the SVN client on the server for these operations. 

### Compare scripts to database working database
The compare scripts to database working database can be used to compare a working database with the scripts inside the module, from where the compare wizard is initiated. It then allows you to:
1. Compare working database with working scripts files.
2. Browse specific files and see detailed differences between source (DB) and target (Scripts).
3. Save any differences on the working database to your script folder. 


All features in 'Compare scripts to database working database' is supported after modules is migrated to GIT. The browse scripts are only functioning due to the SVN installation on the server, as it utilize the SVN client. This might be deprecated at some point, but if so relevant developers will be notified.

### Compare Scripts against released version (for creating patches)
The compare scripts against released version can be used for creating patches. It does so by comparing a given release with the scripts inside the module from where the compare wizard is initiated. It allows you to:
1. Compare working scripts with given release version.
2. Browse specific files and see detailed differences between source (given release) and target (Scripts).
3. Create patches on database objects where schema differs between source and target. All patches is saved to working script inside .\src\sql\02_EDW\Patches. This file is called From_(given previous release version)_To_Scripts and contain at patch template that can be manipulated and optimized for the given purpose.

All features in 'Compare Scripts against released version' is supported after modules is migrated to GIT. The browse scripts are only functioning due to the SVN installation on the server, as it utilize the SVN client. This might be deprecated at some point, but if so relevant developers will be notified.

Further the patch creation is still functioning, but it does course some warnings. The warnings is caused the removal of .svn inside the module. Therefor a GIT module is not anymore recognized as a SVN module, which causes this warning. Here is an example of these warnings:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-f580b63e-8c0a-4155-81da-6e87a8e4c2c6.png)

The SVN client is therefor also used for this operation, and might be deprecated at some point as well. If so relevant developers will be notified.

All the compare features is done by deploying either scripts or specific release to an test server (for now 172.31.112.142\test).

## Release patches
When releasing a module containing a patch, the Modulebuilder overwrites the name of the newly created patch folder. I automatically changes the name of the folder from From_(given previous release version)_To_(new release version). This functionality does not work anymore after the migration to GIT, as the Modulebuilder gets a hard error when doing this operation. This also caused by the SVN client not recognizing this module as an SVN module anymore. See an example here:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-26d9d946-fc64-4f16-b701-03893689c96e.png)

To overcome this issue, the patch folder have to be renamed manually before creating the release. There the 'new release version' part in folder name 'From_(given previous release version)_To_(new release version)' has to be set by the developer manually.

An example of manually changing the patch folder name before creating release could be as follow, where we have created a patch folder from release version 0.0.1 to a new release 0.0.2. The name of the patch folder just before creating the release should therefore be changed from 'From_0.0.1_To_Scripts' to 'From_0.0.1_To_0.0.2'. Ex:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-89243b0a-6652-4207-ba51-c88e849c23f2.png)

## Family Universe

Family Universe allows to analyze informations about current state of families in the municipality. Definitions come from Danish Statistics. Custom entities in this universe are:

- fact FamilyAndHousehol
- dimension Family
- dimension FamilyType
- dimension Household
- dimension HouseholdType

Information about families are not included in the source data, they have to be calculated basing on various avalaible information: age, sex, civil state, kinship and address. All this calculations are done in the procedure stage.Insert_WorkFamiy, results are stored in table stage.WorkFamily. This table is later a source for fact.FamilyAndHousehol, dimension.Family and dimension.Household.

Dimensions FamilyType and HouseholdType are based on hardcoded information sotred in config.FamilyType and config.HouseholdType.

Detailed design informations are avalaible at share point [Family_Household designsepc](https://kmddk.sharepoint.com/:x:/s/Dima-365/EYQ5UvCUtMhHt5lP-pkBP_gBtRHGOZtJqMzt9nywgF8VlQ?e=HAHMLa). All rules are gathered togetger in sheet Person-FamType-HouseType. It is possible to follow relations between family and household type and the rules which has to be fullfilled for each of them. 

### Flow of stage.Insert_WorkFamily

This procedure contains complex logic, to simplify it id divided into 8 steps described here and marked in the code. 

#### Step 1

In the first step basic informations about people are gathered in one temporary table #citizens to simplify further calclations. Cpr, sex, Age, address uuid, Civielstate, Status and, if present, same informations for spouse are collected for people with active Status (Status < 30), living in customer's municipality

In furhter steps all people from the #citizens will be inserted into stage.WorkFamily together with calcaluated FamilyType, address id and Cprs of two main people in the family, these are usually 1 or 2 adults. If there is only one adult in the family second Cpr, FamilyIdPNR2, is set to '0000000000'. We take womens Cpr as FamilyIdPNR1 and men's as FamilyIdNR2. If bot people have the same gender we take bigger Cpr as FamilyIdPNR1 and smaller as FamilyIdPNR2.


#### Step 2

This step covers Case 1, 2 and 3 from [Family_Household designsepc](https://kmddk.sharepoint.com/:x:/s/Dima-365/EYQ5UvCUtMhHt5lP-pkBP_gBtRHGOZtJqMzt9nywgF8VlQ?e=HAHMLa). We search #citiznes table for people who are married or in the registrated partnerships and living toether. We also check status of the spouse to ensure that person is alive with valid Cpr. FamilyType GF is assigned for marridges of different gender  and GS for same gender of both people. For partnership FamilyType is P.


#### Step 3

This step covers Case 4 from the excel sheet. We search for cohabitating parents - people who live under one address and have a child together. Following conditions must be satisfied:
- Civilstate of both people is not Married or in the Partnership (CivilState not in ('P', 'G'))
- People hava at least one child together registered in the CPR.
- People lve together

There are two select statements in this step, first one is for biological children and second for foster children. Foster children have same status as biological in this case.

FamilyType SLP is assigned to people inserted in this step.

#### Step 4

This step covers Case 5 from the excel sheet. We search for cohabitating couple, they must cover conditions:
- Two people of opposite sex
- Age difference under 15 years
- Not close relatives (parent-child or siblings)
- No shared children
- Only two adults in the household

There complex rules are checked in substeps:
- **Step 4.1**: We gather all combinations of child and parent Cprs. Two sources are utilized, table 015, where in each row we have child Cpr, mother's Cpr and father's Cpr and table 014 where we have Child Cpr and parent Cpr. This informations will be used to identify siblings.
- **Step 4.2**: We find all siblings combinations (paris), using data from Step 4.1. If two people have only one shared parents they are considered siblings. 
- **Step 4.3**: We transfrom table 014 to have information about child and two parenst in each row. It will be used to filter out not married couple who have children together.
- **Step 4.4**: We find households where exactly 2 adults live.
- **Step 4.5**: In housholds with two adults we search for marridges to exclude them later.
- **Step 4.6**: Using all previous steps we find cohabitating couples, from households with two people we filter out close relatives, couples with shared children and marridges from step 4.5. All filter are described in the code.

FamilyType SBP is assigned to people inserted in this step.

#### Step 5

In this step single adults having children are inserted, so it cover part of Cases 7 and 8 from excel sheet. We search for adults having at least one child (biological or foster) who were not yet inserted to stage.WorkFamily. 

In the next step we assign home living children, who can have up to 25 years, but cannot have their own children. To not confuse them with single adults, single adults with children are inserted in this step and single adults without children in Step 7.

FamilyType EK is assigned to women and EM to man.

#### Step 6

This step coever Case 6 from the excel sheet, all home living children are inserted. Home living children:
- Lives at the same address as at least one parent
- Is under 25 years old
- Has never been married or in a registered partnership
- Does not have any children (registered in CPR)
- Is not part of a cohabiting couple

There are three substeps, parents infotmation are taken from stage.WorkFamily:
- ***Step 6.1***: Filtering for children living with mother (so with only mother or both parent)
- ***Step 6.2***: Filtering for children living with father but not with mother - not included in 6.1. 
- ***Step 6.3***: Foster children

FamilyType is inherited from parents.

#### Step 7

This step covers rest of single adults from Case 7 and 8 from excel sheet. All adults from #citizens who are not yet present in stage.WorkFamily are inserted.

FamilyType EK is assigned to women and EM to man.

#### Step 8

This steo covers Case 9 from excel.It inserts all children (Age < 18) from #citizens who are not yet present in stage.WorkFamily and satisfy the rules:
- Does not live with either parent
- Is under 18 years old
- Has never been married or in a registered partnership
- Does not have children (registered in CPR)
- Is not part of a cohabiting couple

FamilyType EU is assigned.


### Flow of dimensions

After running all 8 steps everone from #citizens should have assigned FamilyType and Cprs of two main adults in the family.

Dimension.Family and dimension.Household are based on stage.WorkFamily and follow standars framework flow. 

Source key for dim Family are distict combinations of FamilyIdPNR1 and FamilyIdPNR2. Stage.WorkFamily is aggreagted to calcualte NumberOfKidsInFamily, NumberOfPersonsInFamily and NumberOfAdultsInFamily. Adults are over 18 and are not home living children. So 22-year old living with parents is considered a child.

Source key for dim Houselhold are distinct address uuids. Stage.WorkFamily is aggreagted to calcualte NumberOfKidsInHusstandHousehold, NumberOfPersonsInHusstandHousehold, NumberOfAdultsInHusstandHousehold and NumberOfFamiliesInHoushold. Adult rules are same as above.

FamilyType and HouseholdType dimensions have source in config tables inserted in PostScripts in dataarea.

### Flow of fact

Fact.FamilyAndHousehold is built directly on stage.WorkFamily. Household type are usually same as FamilyType but if more than one family lives in the househol then type AH is assigned. 

Keys in the fact:
- [DW_SK_Family]
- [DW_SK_HusstandHousehold]
- [DW_SK_PersonOplCoreinfo]
- [DW_SK_PersonAddresse]
- [DW_SK_PersonNavnName]
- [DW_SK_FamilyType]
- [DW_SK_HusstandHouseholdType]
- [DW_SK_Aldersinterval]
- [DW_SK_Dato]

Flags in the fact, values 0 or 1:
- [IsAnAdultByAge] - calculated using same rules as in dimensions.     
- [IsAChildByAge] - calculated using same rules as in dimensions.              
- [IsAChildByHomeLiving] - from stage.WorkFamily

 - Remade the logic beheind boligstatus 
 - Added stage.WorkRessource as work table for mapping.resource, stage.dimension.ressource and stage.factressource
 - Fixed a bug in IF_Skemasvar_tag where dw_archive and @audit was swapped. 
 - Added BoligId to Dimension.Ressource

1.4
 - Fixed missing patch in prev version.
 - New fields "AktuelIndsats" and "AktuelIkrafttraedelsesdato" i dimension IndsatsDetaljer
 - Fixed deltaload for indsatsInstandMaaned
 - Added type 2 history to the field [Aktiv] in dimension.ressource
 - Added type 2 history to the field [BoligensAnvendelighed] in dimension.ressource
 - Streamline the Priskatalog views

1.3
 - Fixed error in Priskatalog views
 - Fixed error in Priskatalog views
 - Fixed error in Priskatalog views
 - Added five fields to EOP Tema dimension
 - Added three more root nodes to the Hierarchy "ICS,FFB,Opholdsplan" 
 - Added "kladder" to be included in the EOP udredning fact
 - Changed the date calculation in EOP udredning to be based on activated date instead of created date.
 - Added "seneste udredning" flag to dimension UdredningDetaljer
 - Added try_cast and isnull to "numerisk svar" colunm in  fact Skemaspørgsmål svar
 - Added Views for Targit customers that replace logic in the ETL, the logic is now materialized in the transfer to dataout.
 - Fixed bug in BorgerTilhoerForhold where DW_EK_Borger was null insted of -2 
 - Fixed bug where skemaspørgsmålsvar data had wrong dw_sk_forløb = -2 and dw_sk_skemaskabalon = -2

1.2
 - Fix a overflow in skemaspørgsmålsvar
 - Continued changed all decimal and numeric to be less or equals to (29,18), no patch inforce this change
 - Alter precision on all decimal fields be less then 18
 - added view v_IF_Medicinadministration_Registrering that fixes the miss spelled fact IF_Medicinadminstration_Registrering
 - Planlagt_Returdato added to fact Udlån
 - Added FoersteGangPlanlagtVentetidTag to fact ydelsesbaseretTraening
 - Added fact Udredning
 - Modified DimensionTemaHierarki to included subthemes
 - DST L402, TilbudProduktionsEnhedsNummer and AFDELINGS_UUID added
 - Tilføjet tre tabeller til IQ Samarbejde Martinfo, Dato og Periodefilter
 - Tilføjet Leverandørønsker tabeller og koblinger på bolig og Indsatstilstand

# Data Source - Files delivery


### 📁 01 Files – Weekly Deliveries  
These files are delivered weekly and contain data from the beginning of the year up to the current delivery. They include calculated outputs.  
**Examples:**  
- `01KSD_LIS_0810_20241127062127.csv`  
- `01KSD_LIS_0810_20241127062127.csv.metadata`

---

### 📁 02 Files – Yearly Deliveries  
These files cover specific statuses not included in the weekly files. They are delivered during the **third week of the year** and refer to the **previous year**.  
**Examples:**  
- `02KSD_LIS_sidste_ar_0810_20230115123652.csv`  
- `02KSD_LIS_sidste_ar_0810_20230115123652.csv.metadata`

---

### 📁 03 Files – Custom/Historic Deliveries  
These are custom-generated files not supported by standard scripts. They are typically:  
- Created on request  
- Delivered for new customers as historic data  

⚠️ **Note:**  
Custom generated files not supported by the scripts, they can be generated on request or are generated for new customer as historic files. 
Unfortunately, they do not have proper dates in name. As a consequence, they should be deliver together with information what time they contain and the date in its name should be changed accordingly, to be read in proper sequence. Only then prefix 03 can be changed to 02 or 01 to be read by standard process.

# KMD OPUS Det Specialiserede Socialområde (DSS) - Dataarea
Dataarea til KMD Opus Det Specialiserede Socialområde (DSS).

## Introduktion
Datakilden til dette dataarea er BW DSO'erne `ZD5SLxxx` og `ZD1PSPRT`, som danner grundlag for de to facts `Forbrug` og `Takst`. Desuden er dette dataarea afhængig af at kunden er tilsluttet Økonomi, da positionsteksten kommer fra `ZD1SLxxx` DSO'en som er en del af datagrundlaget til KMD OPUS Økonomi universerne.

Der findes yderligere dokumentation for data leverancen fra BW i teamet "OPUS BW" -> "Finance" kanalen -> "Finance notes" under "D_Product Documentation". Kæderne vil følge navnestandarden `ZFIR_PW1xxx_TD_MS_DSS_PUSH` og de er samlet i visningskomponentet `FIR – EDW Det Specialiserede Socialområde (DSS)`. ILDER filer til løsning bliver afleveret på `/IM-P/ILDER/INTERN/OPUS-IMPORT/xxx/DSS`.

## Bemærkninger
I dette afsnit er der noteret forskellige bemærkninger omkring valg der er foretaget i modelleringen.

### Profitcenter i Takst
DSO'en `ZD1PSPRT`, som ligger til grund for `Takst` fact'en, holder ikke kendetegnet `0PROFIT_CTR`, så denne joines på fra PSP-elementets attributer (`0WBS_ELEMT_ATTR`). Det betyder at vi ikke har historik på denne og altid viser det aktive Profitcenter som er tilknyttet et PSP-element, skulle kunden skifte profitcentret der er tilknyttet et PSP-element vil det opdateres også tilbage i tid.

### Håndter dato i Forbrug
I forbrug fact'en sætter vi rækker med `FISCPER` `0000000` til `00000101`, vi har kun set rækker med 0 i forbrug kolonnen for denne værdi af `FISCPER`. Se note i `stage.Insert_FactForbrug.StoredProcedure.sql`.

### Bevillingsansvarssted i Takst
Fact Takst holder ikke Bevillingsansvarssted som hierarki, da denne ikke er udfyldt for nogen rækker.

### Omkostningssted i Forbrug
Fact Forbrug holder ikke Omkostningssted som hierarki, da denne ikke er udfyldt for nogen rækker.

path: /Technology & Software/13. Wiki Automation Scripts/13.1 Wiki pipeline notifications
content:
# Introduction
Azure DevOps provides a robust notification system to keep you informed about activities and updates in your projects. These notifications can be customized at the personal level to suit your preferences, ensuring you only receive relevant updates. On the KMDBI DevOps organization we have some default notifications which is inherited to personal level. One of these default notifications is a Build notification, that as default creates email notifications for all executions of Azure DevOps Pipelines. And due to our automation scripts being orchestrated by these pipelines and triggered once modifications is done, you will by default receive en notification email about the completion of the pipeline.

## How to disable notifications
To disable notifications on the automation pipelines related to wiki, you will have to disable the default notification and create a new, so you maintain the current default behavior around notifications. Only difference is blacklisting of the wiki pipeline.

This can be done as follow:

#### Step 1: Navigate to Your Notification Settings

1.  **Sign in** to your Azure DevOps account.
    
2.  Click on your **profile picture** or initials in the top-right corner of the Azure DevOps interface.
    
3.  Select **Notifications** from the dropdown menu.

#### Step 2: Review Your Current Notification Subscriptions

*   You will see a list of your current subscriptions under the **Personal Notifications** tab. These include notifications for work items, pull requests, pipelines, and more.
    
*   Go disable the default [Build completes] notification.

#### Step 3: Add New Notifications

1.  Click on **New Subscription** at the top of the page.
    
2.  Select 'Build' category and the 'A build completes' template
    
3.  Use the default configuration and add two filter criteria:
    1. Definition name:
    *   Set Field = 'Definition name'
    *   Set Operator = '<>'
    *   Set Value = 'KMDBI.wiki' (Scroll to find)

    2. Requested by:
    *   Set Field = 'Requested by'
    *   Set Operator = 'contains'
    *   Set Value = '[me]' (default)

4.  Click **Finish** to activate the notification subscription.


![Notificationsettings.png](/.attachments/Notificationsettings-883bf2b3-e282-40e5-ae49-ca0ff605760a.png)

#Introduction
This page describes how to get access to our admin portals.

##Authentication layers
There are two layers of authentication in the admin portal. One which is a default part of the portal and then a layer that can be enabled through configurations directly in the portal.

### Default Authentication layer
In the reuse part of the portal logic there are a table (system.PortalUserADGroupList) contains all ad users on the kmdpfosap domain. This table is maintained by this stored procedure system.UpdateADGroupListFromActiveDirectory.StoredProcedure.

When you login to the portal the user is validated by a lookup in the system.PortalUserADGroupList. This table also contains information about which ad groups the user is linked to. The ad groups is relevant when working with the authentication layer that can be configured in the portal it self.

For the portal to validate your user in the system.PortalUserADGroupList, it is a minimum requirement that you have an account in the kmdpfosap domain. To get a kmdpfosap account please do as follow:

1. Go to https://servicenow.kmd.dk/myportal/
2. Go to IT-Support:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-0c852e56-c2c6-46b4-870a-f96681fd1a52.png)
3. Go to Access Management
![image.png](/.attachments/image-d3d93a5a-2df6-4c4c-9beb-3634cb82b9d0.png)
4. Choose other access management
![image.png](/.attachments/image-09e129b1-2899-47ea-8d25-868d7af9ef78.png)
5. Fill out form..
 - Reguested for: The user to get access.
 - Subject: Creation of kmdpfosap user
 - Please enter database, server name, system or group to which you need to have access to: Access to kmdpfosap domain, and add user to one of the following ad groups:
     - SQLreader_as_im*
     - SQLDevelop_as_im**
 - Business justification for requested access: Add the reason why you need access. Ex. access to KMD Insight data...

* Used for read access in portals like access portal, so is minimum requirement
** Used if you are a developer and need access to various dev resources.

NOTE: In the admin portals that only utilize the default authentication layer, there is in practice no need to be part of any of the above mentioned ad groups. But the Authentication in the Access Management portals is based on the ad groups, and often having access to this is a requirement.


# Application authentication layer.
Based on configurations in the pages:
- User Groups
- User Rights

See the admin portal documentation about how to configure this.

content:
# Learnings

## Self hosted agents
We need to utilize self hosted agents for os to connect the pipelines hosted and orchestrated from Azure DevOps to our on-prem environment where all operations is handled.

A self hosted agent is a 1-1 reference to a on prem server/host. So for each server you want the pipelines to interferer with, you need a self hosted agent. You could have only on self hosted agent in the Azure DevOps portal, but then you will experience bottlenecks in your CI/CD actions, as the tasks will queue up, as only one pipeline on the agent can be executed at once.

A agent is used for each job in a pipeline. If a agent is not selected for the job, then it just uses a default Microsoft hosted agent and spins up a vm-image to execute the logic on.

On training ask if it is best to use multiple agens or the same all the way through? Bestto define the agent, when you just want a microsoft agent or just use default?

##  Parallel job
TODO...
Look into how we can run pipelines in parallel and what does it require. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/licensing/concurrent-jobs?view=azure-devops&tabs=ms-hosted.

Not only jobs but also whole pipelines. 

## AgentPools
All your agents is listed in the agentpool on project level. Here we need a agent for each on-prem environment we want to connect to. We need to find a flexible way to define the agentpoolname in our yaml files, as the pipelines should be able to operate across different environment. For now it is defined as input parameters for the pipeline. Issue with this approach that the list of agents is hardcoded as values in the parameter. Could be nice to maintain this list somewhere else.

## System access token
JAQ will make some docu on this. But this is an alternative to PAT tokens. It will be placed under https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/5851/3.-Secrets-Management.

We already use it in some other pipelines.

## Hierarchy in pipeline

### Azure DevOps Pipeline Hierarchy in Summary

| **Level**      | **Description**                                                       | **Example**                     |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| **Pipeline**    | The entire workflow, including triggers, variables, and stages.      | `trigger: main`                 |
| **Stages**      | Logical phases or sections of the pipeline.                          | `stage: Build`                  |
| **Jobs**        | Units of work within a stage, executed on a single agent.            | `job: BuildJob`                 |
| **Steps**       | Individual tasks or actions performed within a job.                 | `script: echo "Building..."`    |
| **Tasks**       | Predefined or custom actions used in a step to perform specific operations. | `task: PublishBuildArtifacts@1` |


### Key Features of Each Level in Azure DevOps Pipelines

| **Feature**             | **Pipeline**               | **Stage**         | **Job**          | **Step**            | **Task**           |
|--------------------------|----------------------------|-------------------|------------------|---------------------|--------------------|
| **Scope**                | Entire CI/CD workflow      | High-level phases | Units of work    | Individual tasks    | Predefined operations |
| **Parallel Execution**   | No                        | Yes               | Yes              | No                  | No                 |
| **Agent Usage**          | No                        | No                | Yes (one per job)| No (uses job's agent)| No (uses step's agent) |
| **Dependency Control**   | Between stages            | Yes               | Yes              | No                  | No                 |
| **Manual Approvals**     | Yes                       | Yes               | No               | No                  | No                 |
| **Reusable**             | N/A                       | N/A               | Limited          | No                  | Yes                |


```
Pipeline
├── Stage
│   ├── Job
│   │   ├── Step
│   │   │   ├── Task

```
It is important to have some structure on how to utilize the levels in relation to what you want to accomplish. Note that for each Job the git repo is reloaded. Also Stages brings some UI separation in the DevOps portal.

### **General Terminology**

*   **Inputs**: Specific to tasks and define task behavior (e.g., `command`, `version`). See inputs for PowerShell@2 tasks here: [PowerShell@2 - PowerShell v2 task | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/tasks/reference/powershell-v2?view=azure-pipelines)
*   **Properties**: General settings for components like stages, jobs, or steps (e.g., `displayName`, `pool`).
*   **Attributes**: Broader term that can refer to both properties and inputs.

## Compile vs runtime
1.  **Compile-Time Decisions:**
    *   Use parameters (`${{ parameters.<name> }}`) for defining high-level pipeline structures.
    *   Ideal for template expressions and static conditions.
2.  **Runtime Decisions:**
    *   Use variables (`$(<variable>)`) or runtime conditions for dynamic behavior during pipeline execution.
    *   Useful for tasks that depend on previous steps, environment state, or outputs.
By leveraging both compile-time and runtime capabilities effectively, you can build flexible and efficient Azure DevOps pipelines tailored to your requirements.

### Key Differences Between Compile-Time and Runtime in Azure DevOps Pipelines

| **Feature**          | **Compile-Time**                                    | **Runtime**                                     |
|-----------------------|----------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| **When Evaluated**    | Before pipeline execution.                         | During pipeline execution.                     |
| **Expressions Used**  | `${{ }}` template expressions.                     | `$( )` or `variables['']`.                     |
| **Scope**             | Pipeline structure and templates.                  | Job, step, and task logic.                     |
| **Dependencies**      | Parameters, hardcoded values.                      | Runtime variables, task outputs, environment.  |
| **Use Cases**         | Defining pipeline structure, defaults, and logic.  | Adapting to dynamic execution data.            |
| **Flexibility**       | Static and predefined.                             | Dynamic and reactive to execution context.     |
| **Common Elements**   | Parameters, stages, and jobs.                      | Variables, outputs, and conditional logic.     |
| **Error Detection**   | Errors occur before execution starts.              | Errors occur during execution.                 |
| **Examples**          | Template inclusion, conditional jobs/stages.       | Task-specific conditions, runtime variables.   |

##Variables
Pipeline variables can be defined at all levels until step/task level. At task level inline, env or logging values.

### Key Points:

1.  **Inline Script Variables**:
    *   Local to the script.
    *   Best for temporary, transient values within a step.
2.  **Environment Variables (`env`)**:
    *   Scope is limited to the step where they are defined.
    *   Can be accessed by any command or tool in the step.
3.  **Azure DevOps Logging Commands (`##vso[task.setvariable]`)**:
    *   Allows defining or updating variables dynamically.
    *   Variables set with this command can persist beyond the step and be used in subsequent steps.
The readability is better if things is defined on higher level. So we have choosen that no parameters is defined (except constant values) is defined at task level. Parameters is defined on job level and above.

### Connect to Azure KeyVault
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/release/azure-key-vault?view=azure-devops&tabs=managedidentity%2Cyaml

Should we use system or user assigned managed identity???? For now user assigned.

Azure DevOps does not directly support **system-assigned managed identities** for the DevOps organization itself (as it is a cloud service). However, you can still use managed identities within Azure DevOps, particularly when you’re running **self-hosted agents** on Azure Virtual Machines (VMs), **Azure Pipelines**, or **Azure Resources** that need to authenticate to Azure resources like **Azure Key Vault**, **Azure Storage**, or other Azure services.

If you're using a **Microsoft-hosted agent** in Azure DevOps (rather than a self-hosted agent), you don't have access to a **system-assigned managed identity** because these agents are not tied to any specific Azure resource (like a VM) that has a managed identity. Microsoft-hosted agents are ephemeral, meaning they are created and destroyed dynamically by Azure DevOps.

However, even without a **system-assigned managed identity**, you can still authenticate to Azure resources using a **service principal** with Azure Active Directory (AAD) credentials or by using **Azure Key Vault** to securely access secrets.

*   **Direct Managed Identity**: Not available for on-prem servers, but you can authenticate using Azure AD.
*   **Hybrid Identity**: Using Azure AD Connect and Azure AD Join for on-prem servers allows integration with Azure AD and can leverage Azure AD authentication.
*   **Service Principal**: You can use an Azure AD Service Principal to authenticate from on-prem servers to Azure services, mimicking the behavior of Managed Identities.
*   **Azure Arc**: Enables Azure services, including Managed Identity capabilities, to extend to on-prem infrastructure.

path: /Technology & Software/16. Azure Devops/16.4 Security/16.4.1 Personal Access Token (PAT)
content:
# Introduction

A PAT token is a secure, token-based authentication method used to access services and APIs. It acts as an alternative to using a password, providing more control and security. PATs are typically used for automated processes or integrating with third-party tools, and can be configured with specific permissions to limit access to necessary resources.

---

[[_TOC_]]

## Creating a PAT token
In Azure DevOps, PAT tokens can be generated by clicking the cogwheel in the top right corner and choosing Personal access tokens: 

![Skærmbillede 2025-01-15 105301.png](/.attachments/Skærmbillede%202025-01-15%20105301-1089eb0d-4229-4a2e-af53-f619ae1a9d8b.png)

On the next page, click **New token** to customize your token's permissions and expiration date. The maximum lifetime of a PAT token is one year from creation. Be cautious when assigning permissions to your PAT token. While the security of a PAT token is moderate, the risk of exposure is higher than with alternative methods. Full access should never be required. Once created, make sure to save your token in a secure location, as you will not be able to recover it once the page is reloaded. Remember, having a token with access to company data can pose a significant security risk if exposed.
![Skærmbillede 2025-01-15 105348.png](/.attachments/Skærmbillede%202025-01-15%20105348-1f24f76d-69e6-485e-a71d-6d25cd1b3c36.png)

## Securing your PAT
When using a Personal Access Token (PAT) in a script, pipeline, or similar context, avoid pasting the token directly into your code. Doing so exposes the token and compromises its security. A more secure approach is to create a variable within your library, store the token as its value, and then reference the variable in your code. This ensures that your token remains protected.
**Be aware that your token can still be exposed by printing the value of the variable**


![image.png](/.attachments/image-27bc0ddc-0bde-41fe-a171-774c31011321.png)

# Introduction

The System.AccessToken in Azure DevOps is a special, automatically generated token used to authenticate and authorize requests made by build and release pipelines. It is a predefined variable that provides access to the Azure DevOps REST API during pipeline execution. This token is automatically included in the pipeline and grants permissions based on the identity running the pipeline, ensuring secure access to resources like repositories, work items, and builds.

---

[[_TOC_]]

## How to use
The System.AccessToken is automatically available in Azure DevOps and can be accessed as an environment variable. To use it directly in your code, define a variable like this:

`$systemAccesstoken = $env:SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN`

## Security & permission management

The System.AccessToken is automatically generated and scoped to the pipeline in Azure DevOps, meaning its permissions are tied to the identity running the pipeline and are limited to the scope of the current pipeline run. This ensures that the token only grants access to resources that the pipeline has permission to interact with, reducing the risk of over-permissioned access.
the token is automatically managed by Azure DevOps, eliminating the need for users to handle or store the token themselves, which further reduces the chances of accidental leakage or misuse.

While you cannot directly change the permissions of the System.AccessToken, you can control its access by managing the permissions of the user or service account running the pipeline. When a pipeline is triggered (for example, by a commit or manual trigger), the System.AccessToken inherits the permissions of the identity that initiated the pipeline. This means that the System.AccessToken will have access to the resources the triggering user or service account is authorized to access, such as repositories, build definitions, and artifacts.
For automated pipelines, the service account used **(e.g., Project Collection Build Service)** is automatically assigned the necessary permissions to execute build and release tasks. This account operates under the principle of least privilege, ensuring it has just enough access to execute builds and releases, with its scope limited to the build environment and related resources.

The permissions of the **Project Collection Build Service** user can be viewed and managed under **Project Settings** > **Permissions**. To locate the specific service user, click **Users** at the top of the page and search for the account.

**You need to expand search to find the user**

![Skærmbillede 2025-01-15 130521.png](/.attachments/Skærmbillede%202025-01-15%20130521-200594e1-164b-4202-b6a1-700ad2eeeaf1.png)

path: /Technology & Software/16. Azure Devops/16.4 Security/16.4.3 Azure Pipeline Permissions
content:
# Introduction

Pipeline Permissions in Azure DevOps provide a powerful mechanism to control and secure access to your build and release pipelines. These permissions define who can trigger, modify, and view pipeline runs, as well as which resources (such as repositories, environments, and artifacts) a pipeline can access during its execution.
By configuring Pipeline Permissions, you can enforce role-based access control (RBAC), implement approval workflows, and ensure that only authorized users or service accounts can interact with sensitive environments or resources. This fine-grained approach enhances security and governance across your CI/CD workflows while maintaining flexibility for your development and operations teams.

---

[[_TOC_]]

## How Pipeline Permissions work

Pipeline permissions in Azure DevOps provide multiple layers of control to secure your workflows. At the user level, permissions determine what actions individuals or groups can take, such as viewing, editing, or running pipelines. These permissions are complemented by resource access controls, which specify the repositories, environments, and artifacts a pipeline can interact with during its execution.
Azure DevOps supports role-based access control (RBAC) through built-in roles like Contributor, Reader, and Administrator. This simplifies permission management while allowing fine-grained control over individual pipelines and associated resources. This multi-level structure ensures that administrators can maintain both flexibility and security when managing CI/CD workflows.

## Managing Pipeline Permissions

Pipeline permissions can be managed at several levels within Azure DevOps. Individual user permissions control access to actions like triggering or editing a pipeline. For example, the "Run Pipeline" permission determines whether a user can start a specific pipeline, while "Edit Pipeline" permissions allow modifications to its configuration. You can also manage these permissions for groups, simplifying administration for teams.
In addition to user permissions, pipelines require explicit authorization to interact with resources. For example, you can configure access to repositories, specify environments with approval gates, and control access to build artifacts. These resource authorizations ensure that pipelines only interact with the resources they are explicitly allowed to use.
Pipeline permissions can also be managed at the folder level, enabling hierarchical control of grouped pipelines. This approach allows administrators to apply consistent security settings across multiple pipelines efficiently.

In Azure DevOps, managing a Pipelines Permissions is done by clicking Pipelines in the left menu bar, then clicking on the three dots on the chosen pipeline:

![Skærmbillede 2025-01-15 142240.png](/.attachments/Skærmbillede%202025-01-15%20142240-0a400fef-06ec-48dd-ad08-d53ffe9ead9b.png)

And then click **Manage Security**

![image.png](/.attachments/image-27eda559-db0b-43b1-a103-6c1bbe48993d.png)

Afterwards you have the possibility to manage the permissions for users and groups interacting with the chosen pipeline. 

## Pipeline Permissions and Access Tokens

In Azure DevOps, pipeline permissions and access tokens work in tandem to ensure secure and controlled access to resources during pipeline execution. While pipeline permissions determine what actions and resources a pipeline is allowed to access, access tokens provide the mechanism for authenticating and executing those actions.
Pipeline permissions alone will not handle the interaction because they are not an authentication mechanism. Instead, they define which resources the token (eg. PAT or System.AccessToken) is authorized to access.

Read more about [Personal Access Token (PAT)](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10123/3.1-Personal-Access-Token-(PAT)) and [System.AccessToken](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10125/3.2-System-Access-Token).

## Best Practices for Pipeline Permissions
When managing pipeline permissions, it is crucial to follow the principle of least privilege. Always grant the minimum permissions necessary for the pipeline to function. Overly permissive roles or unrestricted access should be avoided, as they introduce unnecessary risks.
For sensitive operations, consider implementing approval workflows, particularly when pipelines interact with critical environments. Regularly reviewing permissions is another essential practice to ensure that only required access is granted. For authentication, always use an access token, rather than embedding credentials directly in scripts or configurations.
Finally, enforce organizational policies, such as branch protection rules and artifact retention settings, to complement pipeline permissions. These policies add another layer of security and governance to your DevOps processes.

path: /Technology & Software/5. GIT/5.3 Guidelines/5.3.2 Global Git Credential Setup
content:
# Introduction
This guide will help you set up your Git credentials globally on a Windows machine using PowerShell. This is a requirement first time you access new  environment, and want to start interacting with GIT.

---

## 1. Open PowerShell

1. Open **Windows PowerShell** in dedicated terminal or inside VS code.
2. Confirm the PowerShell window is open and ready for commands.

---

## 2. Configure Global Git Credentials

In PowerShell, enter the following commands to set up your name, email, and credential storage.

### Set Global Username
```powershell
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
```
- Replace `"Your Name"` with the name you want associated with your Git commits.

### Set Global Email
```powershell
git config --global user.email "you@example.com"
```
- Replace `"you@kmd.dk"` with the email address you want to associate with your commits.

### Enable Windows Credential Manager
```powershell
git config --global credential.helper wincred
```
- This stores your credentials securely in the Windows Credential Manager, so you don’t need to re-enter your username and password every time you push to a remote repository.

All commands can also be executed simultaneously
```powershell
git config --global credential.helper wincred
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@kmd.dk"
```
---

## 3. Verify Configuration

To confirm that your global settings are saved, use the following command:

```powershell
git config --list
```

This will display a list of all global Git configurations, including your username, email, and credential helper settings. 

---

## 4. Updating or Removing Credentials

If you need to update or remove your global credentials in the future, use these commands:

- **Update**: Simply re-run the `git config` commands with the new details.
- **Remove Global Setting**:
   ```powershell
   git config --global --unset user.name
   git config --global --unset user.email
   ```

This guideline provides a simple, one-time setup for Git global credentials using PowerShell, ideal for a consistent Git identity across all repositories.
