content:
[[_TOC_]] #config.PortalGetValue _Purpose_ Retrieve a value from a valuestring from a specific column. Be aware that you have to take care of datatype conversion and NULL values. _Example_ ``` set @StringVariable = (select config.PortalGetValue(@Columns,@Values,'') set @IntVariable = cast((select config.PortalGetValue(@Columns,@Values,'') as int); set @DateVariable = cast((select config.PortalGetValue(@Columns,@Values,'') as date); ``` #config.PortalSetValue _Purpose_ Set a value into a valustring on a specific column _Example_ ``` set @Values = (select config.PortalSetValue('',''@Columns,@Values)) -- Set NULL value set @Values = (select config.PortalSetValue('','$NULL$',@Columns,@Values)) ``` #config.PortalGetTableFieldTranslation _Purpose_ This function is normally used for creating and returning a proper message or errormessage to the UI related on a specific field. That could for example be related to a validation when something went wrong. It is not best practice to hardcode the name of a column and return that because it should work together with translation from the language layer module. This function returns the correct translated name. _Example_ ``` declare @FriendlyName as nvarchar(max); set @FriendlyName = (select config.PortalGetTableFieldTranslation('','','')); ``` Remark - the and and in some cases the will often already exists as local variables and therefore a more common example will be like this: ``` declare @FriendlyName as nvarchar(max); set @FriendlyName = (select config.PortalGetTableFieldTranslation(@Language,@Columnname,@ConfigtableName)); ``` #config.PortalGetLabelTranslation _Purpose_ We have several different objecttypes in the translation module such as 'Columns', 'Tables', 'Button' and 'Lookupvalues' but the 'Label' translation is a more general translation tag that can be used if none of the other fits to make sure that no text that will pop-up in the UI is hardcodet. The way to do it is to create a translation in the translation module with a 'LanguageCode', 'Objectname' and the 'Objecttype' = 'Label' (8) and then it can be used in the code as showed in this example. _Example_ ``` declare @Label as nvarchar(max); declare @Language as nvarchar(20) = (select config.PortalGetLanguage()); set @Label = (select config.PortalGetLabelTranslation(@Language,'')); ``` #config.PortalGetMessageTranslation _Purpose_ This function handles to create a message to the end-user that is dynamic related to the users language and also handles parameters (placeholder %1, %2 etc.). To work with this you have to create at 'Message' (Objecttype = 10) record with a unique 'Objectname' in the PortalTranslation for each language that you will support. Example: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-f85a96ba-8aaf-41fe-a2ae-62248708d4ca.png) This message is called 'PortalGeneral_OnDelete_ReferenceConstraint' and is translated into two languges and have also two variables that also will be dynamic depending on the language this user has choosen. Parameter to config.PortalGetMessageTranslation |No|Name  |Content  | |--|--|--| | 1 |Language  |Language code. Hardcoded or use the function (select config.PortalGetLanguage())  | | 2 |MessageName  |Refers to the nametag of the message created in Portaltranslation  | | 3 |Values  |Values that dynamically replace placeholders %1, %2 etc with static or dynamic values.
Remark placeholders are concatenated with '#¤#'  | _Example_ Remark - this example also use other dynamic translation function that are described on this wiki page. ``` declare @Message as nvarchar(max); declare @Language as nvarchar(20) = (select config.PortalGetLanguage()); set @Message = (select config.PortalGetMessageTranslation(@Language, -- Language code                        'PortalGeneral_OnDelete_ReferenceConstraint', -- MessageName                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               (select config.PortalGetTableTranslation(@Language,'')) + -- Placeholder 1                        '#¤#' +                                                                  (select config.PortalGetTableFieldTranslation(@Language,'','')) -- Placeholder 2                                                           )); ``` #config.PortalGeneral_ModifyOneColumn _Purpose_ This function is very effectly in a scenario where one column value need to be updated. Let say a situation where updating Table A you need to update a status column in Table B and want to execute the business logic and logging on table B as well. _Example_ ``` DECLARE @ReturnMsg nvarchar(max) EXECUTE  [config].[PortalModifyOneColumn]    @ConfigTable = ''   ,@RecordID = 99 -- RecordID (DW_ArchiveID)   ,@Columnname = ''   ,@Value = ''   ,@ReturnMsg = @ReturnMsg OUTPUT IF @ReturnMsg <> ''   RAISERROR (@ReturnMsg,16,1); ``` The same issue can be solved without using this function and instead use 3 steps: 1. config.PortalRecordToColumnValue 2. config.PortalSetValue 3. config.PortalGeneral_OnModify #config.PortalGeneral_CascadeDelete _Purpose_ This is as general function that can delete related records in a 'child' table and will normally be placed in a 'OnBeforeDelete' trigger to perform cascading delete to be sure that all business logic and changelog are executed during delete and by implementing this logic in a datamodel where a table delete the underlying data that again cascade delete underlying data means that a Cascade delete must only be aware of the first data level below the record and do not have to know anything about related tables from there. Remark - in a huge datamodel with a lot of data this approach can cost time to execute and it will then be nessesary to consider a normal T-SQL DELETE statement instead. _Example_ This example delete records in a table with a filter. ``` DECLARE @ReturnMsg nvarchar(max) EXECUTE  [config].[PortalGeneral_CascadeDelete]    @ConfigTable = 'CodelistValue'   ,@ColumnFilter = '[CodelistID] = ''31E0C151-F9D7-4C79-A840-43451C5E6D8A'''   ,@CheckUserRights = 1   ,@ReturnMsg = @ReturnMsg OUTPUT ``` #config.PortalRecordToColumnValue _Purpose_ When the Portal UI send and retrieve data with the database through standard stored procedures it is always formatted in the portal proprietary format which is 'Columns' and 'Values' separated with '#¤#'. Let’s says we during execution of some business logic want to modify existing data in another table or insert a new record by using the portal way of doing it so we need to convert the data into this propriatary format. _Example_ ``` declare @RecordID as bigint = (select DW_ArchiveID from config. where = ''); declare @Columns as nvarchar(max); declare @Values as nvarchar(max) declare @ReturnMsg nvarchar(max) EXECUTE  [config].[PortalRecordToColumnValue]    @ConfigTable = N''   ,@RecordID = @RecordID   ,@Columns = @Columns OUTPUT   ,@Values = @Values OUTPUT   ,@ReturnMsg = @ReturnMsg OUTPUT ``` If the execution goes wrong the @ReturnMsg will return an error message. #config.PortalGetLookupvalue _Purpose_ In case of a lookup column the data in the code will always be the KeyValue - so if you insert/modify/validate the data, the lookup value is always the KeyValue. Sometimes it is useful to be able to show the DisplayName instead of the KeyValue. That could be in custom views or messages send to the user. In that case the function is used because it not only converts the KeyValue to a DisplayName, but it also handles PortalTranslation if that exists. _Example_ ``` declare @Language as nvarchar(20) = (select config.PortalGetLanguage()); declare @DisplayName as nvarchar(max); set @DisplayName = (select config.PortalGetLookupValue(@Language,'','','')); ``` #config.PortalRefreshMetadata _Purpose_ This is a stored procedure that is called several times during installation, and it can be used during development but it is **NOT** allowed to use during execution of business logic, because it refresh all meta data in the solution like 1. PortalFieldList 1. PortalActionList 1. PortalLookupFieldValue 1. Views _Example_ ``` exec config.PortalRefreshMetadata ``` But during development it can always be called to make sure everything is refreshed if for example changes in an 'UpdateFieldlist' stored procedure has been made. #config.PortalGeneral_OnInsert _Purpose_ This stored procedure is used by the UI every time a user inserts a new record in a config table. The stored procedure starts a transaction and will call all other business logic related such as before and after custom code, validation code, logging etc. The stored procedure is also used in custom business logic to insert data in other tables. Let’s say we have a Table A that in 'OnAfterInsert' custom code have to insert some records in Table B. This should be done by using this stored procedure instead of T-SQL functions like INSERT INTO etc. to make sure, that business logic is executed on Table B as well. The use of this stored procedure will often be in combination with other tools like 'config.PortalGeneral_GetEmptyRecord', 'config.PortalRecordToColumnValue', 'config.PortalGetValue' and 'config.PortalSetValue'. _Example_ ``` DECLARE @ConfigTable nvarchar(250) = 'Table B' DECLARE @Columns nvarchar(max) DECLARE @Values nvarchar(max) DECLARE @RecordID bigint DECLARE @ReturnMsg nvarchar(max) -- Start with a empty record of Table B EXECUTE [config].[PortalGeneral_GetEmptyRecord]    @ConfigTable = @ConfigTable   ,@Columns = @Columns OUTPUT   ,@Values = @Values OUTPUT -- Set values in that new empty record set @Values = (select config.PortalSetValue('','',@Columns,@Values)) set @Values = (select config.PortalSetValue('','',@Columns,@Values)) -- Insert the new record in Table B EXECUTE [config].[PortalGeneral_OnInsert]    @ConfigTable = @ConfigTable   ,@Columns = @Columns   ,@Values = @Values   ,@RecordID = @RecordID OUTPUT   ,@ReturnMsg = @ReturnMsg OUTPUT   ,@CheckUserRights = 1 -- Validate user rights   ,@RunValidation = 1 -- run validation   ,@DisableLogging = 0 -- add to changelog -- Fail on error IF @ReturnMsg <> ''   RAISERROR (@ReturnMsg,16,1); ``` #config.PortalGeneral_OnModify _Purpose_ This stored procedure has the same common use as 'PortalGeneral_OnInsert' despite it expect the record to already exists and can then modify one or more columns. Consider to use the stored procedure 'config.PortalGeneral_ModifyOneColumn' in case only 1 or 2 columns has to change - then this is easier to work with. This example shows how to modify a column. _Example_ ``` DECLARE @ConfigTable nvarchar(250) = 'Table B' DECLARE @Columns nvarchar(max) -- Let’s assume that Columns, OldValues and NewValues comes with values into this code DECLARE @OldValues nvarchar(max) DECLARE @NewValues nvarchar(max) DECLARE @ReturnMsg nvarchar(max) -- Change values in the variable @NewValues set @NewValues = (select config.PortalSetValue('','',@Columns,@NewValues)) set @NewValues = (select config.PortalSetValue('','',@Columns,@NewValues)) -- Modify the new record in Table B EXECUTE [config].[PortalGeneral_OnModify]    @ConfigTable = @ConfigTable   ,@Columns = @Columns   ,@OldValues = @OldValues   ,@NewValues = @NewValues    ,@ReturnMsg = @ReturnMsg OUTPUT   ,@CheckUserRights = 1 -- Validate user rights   ,@RunValidation = 1 -- run validation   ,@DisableLogging = 0 -- add to changelog -- Fail on error IF @ReturnMsg <> ''   RAISERROR (@ReturnMsg,16,1); ``` #config.PortalGeneral_OnDelete _Purpose_ This stored procedure is used for deleting a specific record and at the same time execute delete business logic related to that configtable. It is recommended always to delete records using this stored procedure instead of just writing a DELETE statement to ensure handling of rules, cascading delete and logging. _Example_ ``` DECLARE @ConfigTable nvarchar(250) DECLARE @Columns nvarchar(max) DECLARE @Values nvarchar(max) DECLARE @ReturnMsg nvarchar(max) EXECUTE [config].[PortalGeneral_OnDelete]    @ConfigTable = @ConfigTable   ,@Columns = @Columns   ,@Values = @Values   ,@ReturnMsg = @ReturnMsg OUTPUT   ,@CheckUserRights = 1 -- Fail on error IF @ReturnMsg <> ''   RAISERROR (@ReturnMsg,16,1); ``` #config.PortalDebugStart [See how-to use the Debugger](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10163/Use-the-Debugger) #config.PortalDebugStop [See how-to use the Debugger](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10163/Use-the-Debugger) #config.PortalDebugExplore [See how-to use the Debugger](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10163/Use-the-Debugger) #config.PortalGetLanguage _Purpose_ Return the language code that the current user has chosen in the UI. It can be used in different situations but will often be used in relation to calls with other translation functions. _Example_ ``` select config.PortalGetLanguage() ``` #config.PortalGetUsername _Purpose_ Return the name of the current user logged into the portal UI. It will often be used related to logging and if the code is executed directly or without an UI the username is 'system'. _Example_ ``` select config.PortalGetUsername() ``` #config.PortalCloneFieldList _Purpose_ This is a rare used function, and the purpose is to create a field list based on an existing field list. That will often be in a situation where a temporary table is used in an ActionForm or a view. _Example_ ``` exec config.PortalCloneFieldList @FromConfigTable = N'Codelist', @ToConfigTable = N'CodelistTemp'; ``` _Result_ ``` select * from config.PortalFieldList where ConfigTable = N'CodelistTemp' ``` ![image.png](/.attachments/image-e5d1b811-503a-4452-ba5c-4fa230e8c8b2.png) #config.PortalGeneral_GetEmptyRecord _Purpose_ This function is a nice help function when creating a new record from scratch to be inserted with the stored procedure 'PortalGeneral_OnInsert' with @Columns and @Values as parameters. The function can return @Columns with all columns names and $NULL$ values in the @Values return value, so you only need to insert values with the function 'config.PortalSetValue'. _Example_ ``` DECLARE @RC int DECLARE @ConfigTable nvarchar(250) = 'Configtablename' DECLARE @Columns nvarchar(max) DECLARE @Values nvarchar(max) EXECUTE @RC = [config].[PortalGeneral_GetEmptyRecord]    @ConfigTable   ,@Columns OUTPUT   ,@Values OUTPUT ``` #config.PortalUpdateConfigtableValueList _Purpose_ This function is normally used internal in the platform, but it is nice to know. In some situations when inserting new data in several tables that are related with lookups and when the data is validated it can be necessary manually to update the lookup values in the transaction that is running. Let’s say we have a 'TableA' with lookup values from 'TableB' and in a transaction we insert new lookup values in 'TableB' and afterwards insert new records in 'TableA' with relation to the new lookupvalues. Then we have to force an update of valid lookupvalues for data from 'TableB' that are valid to use in 'TableA'. _Example_ ``` -- Insert data into 'TableB' (lookup values) -- Be sure that lookup values for 'TableA' are updated exec config.PortalUpdateConfigtableValueLists @ConfigTable = N'TableA' -- Insert data in 'TableA' ``` #dbo.Splitstring _Purpose_ Since the portal platform Columns and Values format is string based with '#¤#' as separator the splitstring function is often used and nice to know about. It is a standard function in the framework and basicly it works like the build-in-function 'string_split' but with two extra features that is not possible in the standard t-sql function: 1. Separator can be more than 1 char 2. The result set return both a value (item) and a record no (num) _Example_ ``` select * from string_split('a,b,c',',') select * from dbo.SplitString('a,b,c',',') ``` Result: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-f83778c8-d7b4-4b5e-b095-ddffcb8f2cd4.png) #config.PortalBrowserSessionID _Purpose_ The function returns a unique GUID (but declared as a nvarchar) per browser session so it is more unique than the username because an user can open more than one session at a time. The function is used internally in the portal platform but can be used in situations where it is needed to store some stat data on the specific browser session that should be used elsewhere in the business logic. Remark - the function can only return a unique value when the code is executed during a browser session. Otherwise, it will return the value 'system'. _Example_ ``` declare @BrowserSessionID as nvarchar(50) = (select config.PortalBrowserSessionID()); ``` #config.PortalGetDateStr _Purpose_ This function take a 'date' as a parameter and return a string formatted date with format 'yyyy-mm-dd' that can be used for several situations, but often it is used in combination with the 'config.PortalSetvalue' where a date is inserted into Columns and Values to be sure it is formatted correctly. _Example_ ``` declare @DateStr as nvarchar(50) = (select config.PortalGetDateStr(@Date); or set @Values = (select config.PortalSetValue('DateColumn',(select config.PortalGetDateStr(@Date),@Columns,@Values)) ``` #config.PortalGetDateTime _Purpose_ This function return by default always the 'getdate()' and instead of calling the 'getdate()' in the custom code it is recommended always to use this function because it will then be must easier to change it from 'getdate()' to ex 'getUTCdate()' _Example_ ``` select config.PortalGetDateTime() -- instead of select getdate() select getutcdate() ``` #config.PortalGetDateTime2Str _Purpose_ This function take a 'datetime2' as a parameter and return a string formatted date with format 'yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sssssss' that can be used for several things, but often it is used in combination with the 'config.PortalSetvalue' where a datetime2 is inserted into Columns and values to be sure it is formatted correctly. _Example_ ``` declare @DateTime2Str as nvarchar(50) = (select config.PortalGetDateTime2Str(@DateTime2); or set @Values = (select config.PortalSetValue('DateTime2Column',(select config.PortalGetDateTime2Str(@DateTime2),@Columns,@Values)) ``` #config.PortalGetDateTimeStr _Purpose_ This function take a 'datetime' as a parameter and return a string formatted date with format 'yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss'. It is used in combination with the 'config.PortalSetvalue' where a datetime is inserted into Columns and values to be sure it is formatted correctly. _Example_ ``` declare @DateTimeStr as nvarchar(50) = (select config.PortalGetDateTimeStr(@DateTime); or set @Values = (select config.PortalSetValue('DateTimeColumn',(select config.PortalGetDateTimeStr(@DateTime),@Columns,@Values)) ``` #config.PortalGetParentConfigTable _Purpose_ This function can be used in situations where a configtable is called as a linkedtable from different parent tables and the functionality changes based on the parent table. It will return the name of the parent table where the user navigates from in this specific moment in the specific browser session. _Example_ ``` if (select config.PortalGetParentConfigTable('MyTable')) = 'ParentTable1' then.... ``` #config.PortalGetParentId _Purpose_ This function is uses like the function above with the different that it return the RecordId of the parent table record. _Example_ ``` declare @ParentRecordId as bigint; set @ParentRecordId = (select config.PortalGetParentId('MyTable')); ``` #config.PortalGetCurrentSessionFilter _Purpose_ This store procedure can return the current sessionfilter when it is called in terms of what is the current configtable, the parent of the configtable and the recordid of the parent configtable. _Example_ ``` DECLARE        @return_value int,                                                           @ConfigTable nvarchar(250),                                                           @ParentConfigTable nvarchar(250),                                                           @ParentRecordId bigint EXEC                  @return_value = [config].[PortalGetCurrentSessionFilter]                                                           @ConfigTable = @ConfigTable OUTPUT,                                                           @ParentConfigTable = @ParentConfigTable OUTPUT,                                                           @ParentRecordId = @ParentRecordId OUTPUT ``` Remark - this will only work when the code is executed from the Portal UI where both the username and the BrowserID is known.

path: /Technology & Software/7. Admin Portal/7.1 Dev guide/7.1.3 Database development/PortalFieldList
content:
The 'PortalFieldList' is the most essential and used table in the platform and it contains all the information about a config-table that the UI need to build the list form and the card form. The data in 'PortalFieldList' is automatically created during installation and can always be refresh again on all tables by calling the stored procedure. ``` exec [config].[PortalRefreshMetaData] ``` This stored procedure will truncate the config.PortalFieldList table and recreate it with default values. After that it will call the 'UpdateFieldList' stored procedure related to one and every config table. As a developer you can change the behavior of the PortalFieldlist by updating existing records or even create new records when you want to change the settings on columns. Example of how to refresh portalfieldlist on a single table after the stored procedure '[config].[_UpdateFieldlist]' has been changed. ``` EXECUTE [config].[PortalGeneral_CreateFieldList] @ConfigTable = ''; ``` |Columnname|Description  | |--|--| | Configtable | Name of the Configtable this is related to | | ColumnId | Autogenerated as columnid from the table. Best practice is to create custom columns with Columnid >= 1000 | | SortOrder | The order of how the columns will appear in list and forms. By default, it will follow the columnid | | ListEnabled |0=No, 1=Column will be visible in the list form  | | ListLineBreak | 0 = The data will not have a line break and no tooltip. Used on smaller columns and on columns with a lot of data the user will have to expand the column to see all the data.

1= The UI will try to make a line break if not all data I visible inside the box. The user can still resize the column to avoid line break.

2 = The same as ‘0’ but on mouse-over the UI will show a tooltip with all the data. | | ColumnName | The physical from the table that name will be referred to from code when accessing data in the model | | DataType |nvarchar, *text, decimal, int, bit, Datetime2, Datetime, Date, Time, Uniqueidentifier (GUID).
Remark - datatype = 'text' is used for data that need a "Word" textbox-object.  | | DataSize | Only used for nvarhar columns. Datasize > 500 will get a larger textbox than datasize <= 500. | Precision | NOT USED | | Scale | NOT USED | | IsNullable | NOT USED | | FriendlyName | The displayname in the UI. I can be overwritten by language layer. | | IsPrimaryKey | 0=No, 1=Primary key or part of primary key. This is the logical primary key and by default the same as the physical primary key, but it can differ from that. This is the primary key from a user’s perspective and can often be the same as a secondary unique key. It is used to tell the user that a record with that key already exist.| | DerivedKeyColumnName | This is a more advanced option and related to IsPrimaryKey. Let’s say a column is part of a primary-key and the value is less user friendly - maybe a GUID, but we have another column with a more useful value- maybe a name. In this case that value will be shown to the user in case a message with primary-key error occurs. | | IsInsertField | 0=No, 1=The column is shown and active in an Insert mode. By default, all columns are insert fields. If the value = 0 the column is not visiable. If the columns should be visible but not active then set the value = 1 and IsProtectedOnInsert = 1  | | IsModifyFIeld | 0=No, 1=The column is shown and active in Modify mode. By default, is a PrimaryKey column not active on modify but that can be changed by setting the value = 1. If the column should be visible but not active in modify mode set the value = 1 and IsProtectedOnModify = 1 | | IsLookUpField |0=No, 1= Yes
The value '1' is automatically set during deployment (refreshmetadata) when it detects that lookupvalues are defined in a 'GetValue' stored procedure. See DevGuide for how to create lookup value stored procedure.   | | LookupInputType |0=None, 2=Single select, 3=Multi select. Default = 0 but when IsLookupField =1 then it is set to value = 2.  | | LookupRelatedColumn | This can be a comma separated list of other columns that have a lookup relation to this column. This column does not have to be a lookup column, but the other columns mention here are all lookup columns and the values in their lookup list depends on the value in this column. See DevGuide about building a related lookup column. | | IsHidden | 0=No,1=Yes. This is a legacy property and has the same result as saying IsInsertField = 0 and IsModifyField = 0. Avoid to used it in the future and use the other two instead  | | IsRequired |0=No,1=Yes. Auto set depending on the 'Allow Nulls' setting on the table column but can be changed here to set a column as Required even this is not required in the table design, but the other way around be aware about the 'NULL2Value' property so that a required column will get a default value if it is empty.  | | IsUserStamp | 0=No, 1= The reuse code will set the value to current user on insert and modify | | IsTimeStamp | 0=No, 1= The reuse code will set the value to current time on insert and modify | | IsUserstampInsert | 0=No, 1= The reuse code will set the value to current user on insert only | | IsTimestampInsert | 0=No, 1= The reuse code will set the value to current time on insert only | | IsUserstampModify | 0=No, 1= The reuse code will set the value to current user on modify only  | | IsTimestampModify | 0=No, 1= The reuse code will set the value to current time on modify only | | HelpText | The value will be used as a tooltip on mouseover on the column. Best practice is to use the PortalTranslation instead | | NULL2Value | This is the value that will be stored in the table when the user blanks the column.
'' = Blank
'NULL' = SQL NULL
'0' value zero
etc. | | IsCellEdit |0 = No, 1=Activate CellEdit functionality. This is an advanced feature that is documented inside the DevGuide. | | CellEditConfigTable | Related to IsCellEdit. See Devguide | | IsProtectedOnInsert | 0=No, 1= The column is protected in Insert mode. Requires that the IsInsertField = 1. | | IsProtectedOnModify | 0=No, 1= The column is protected in Modify mode. Requires that the IsModifyField = 1. | | IsComputed | This is a system setting that is set automatic if the column is defined as a computed column on the table. 0=No, 1=Yes and it means that the engine is not trying to change the column on insert and modify. | | IsDataRightsFilterEnabled | 0=No record level security is enabled, 1=The column will be enabled in the standard module to set up record-level security | | IsExportField | 0=No,1=Yes meaning that the column will be visible in the export to Excel dialog. By default, DW_ArchiveID and all custom field (not physical columns) will be disabled but that can be changed with this property | **Template** The 'config.ConfigTable_UpdateFieldList.StoredProcedure' stored procedure template can be found in the folder 'include\reuse_config\sql\00_CFG\Template\Mandatory\05_Procedures'.

path: /Technology & Software/7. Admin Portal/7.1 Dev guide/7.1.3 Database development/PortalActionList
content:
The 'PortalActionList' table is like the 'PortalFieldList' table an essential metadata table in the platform, and it contains all the information about actions related to a config-table. It is used for the UI to add action button into the UI. The list contains custom action and more general actions. The data in 'PortalActionList' is automatically created during installation and can always be refresh again on all tables by calling the stored procedure. ``` exec [config].[PortalRefreshMetaData] ``` This stored procedure will truncate the config.PortalActionList table and recreate it with default values. After that it will call the 'UpdateActionList' stored procedure related to one and every config table. As a developer you can change the behavior of the PortalActionlist by updating existing records or even delete actions that is not needed on a configtable. That could be general standard actions like 'Changelog', 'Datazoom' and 'InlineEdit' etc. Example of how to refresh portalactionlist on a single table after the stored procedure '[config].[_UpdateActionlist]' has been changed. ``` EXECUTE  [config].[PortalGetActionList] @ConfigTable = '',@RefreshActionList = 1 ``` |Columnname|Description  | |--|--| | Configtable | Name of the Configtable this is related to | | ActionName | Inserted by the system and may not be changed | | IconName | Name of the icon that will be shown in the action bottom. Valid icons can be found here https://fontawesome.com/search?q=excel&o=r&m=free | | FriendlyName | The name that will be shown in a tooltip to the user. By default, it is the same as the Actionname. | | HelpText |Not implemented  | | ConfirmMsg | If this column has a value, the yes/no dialog will appear with that current text. This the legacy implementation that is still supported but it is recommended to use ‘OnConfirmation’ stored procedure instead which is more advanced and supports language translation | | SortOrder | Set the order of actions in every type of 'Placement' | | RunAsync | Can be 0 (false) or 1 (true). It means that the action is running is parallel (background). That is used when processing heavy operations to avoid timeouts. The disadvantage is that the user will not get any return message when the action is done. Be aware not to lock any tables and be sure to create a begin transaction and commit transaction when inserting the startlog statement.  | | Placement |The value indicated where to place the action and can have 5 values:
0 = Visible directly on each line
1 = Moved to the drop-down menu
-1 = Not visible. This value is used for system actions
2 = This is an action that can run on selected lines and placed in the top of the screen
3 = Same as 2 but the action is placed in a dropdown menu. | **Systemaction** The platform will automatically add some standard action to every configtable and they are mentions in the following table. This action can be removed in the 'UpdateActionList' stored procedure if they are not needed in a specific table, or they can be disabled with user-rights configuration. |ActionName|Description  | |--|--| | ColumnCustomize | ![image.png](/.attachments/image-c0191942-8d84-443a-8e0d-936059e74646.png) Give the user the possibility to change order of columns and hide columns. This setting is stored per user. | | CreateCopy | If this action exist the ![image.png](/.attachments/image-814bbb23-7f67-40f8-b83b-e09bf7e15252.png) button will apear on every line and the feature is to create a new record based on information from the current line. As standard it will keep all columns and set the DW_ArchiveID = $NULL$ but sometime more code must be added to the OnInit stored procedure in order to handle more complex functionallity.   | | ExcelExport |Open a dialog to export selected data to clipboard | | InlineEdit | The inlinedit add these buttons on every line![image.png](/.attachments/image-a25c2187-fa3b-4505-88f0-ab77017e6117.png) to delete and change data directly on the line instead of open the card form | | MultiSelect | The MultiSelect action add standard functionality for mark lines and use that as a filter and remove that filter again. It will add the following buttons on the UI ![image.png](/.attachments/image-47b76c04-545e-4d77-b4b6-2bf6aefdc3ba.png) | | Changelog | This action is anly for showing changelog. It will not disable logging on the table. The changelog can look like this example: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-261af8ad-3a92-4755-9798-0faffe0f46ac.png) | | Datazoom | Datazoom is a function more used for developers or administrators and may be hidden for normal users. If the action is deleted in the 'PortalActionList' it will be gone for every user. Therefore, this action will often be hidden by usinf user-rigths for specific user-groups. The DataZoom gives a lot of technical information on the table like the psycical record, information about primary keys and Columns Values information that can be used for debugging or problem solving. ![image.png](/.attachments/image-66e08869-d501-4dce-9f76-8ad87e4e3378.png) | **Template** The 'config.ConfigTable_UpdateActionList.StoredProcedure' stored procedure template can be found in the folder 'include\reuse_config\sql\00_CFG\Template\Mandatory\05_Procedures'.

path: /Technology & Software/7. Admin Portal/7.1 Dev guide/7.1.3 Database development/Flows
content:
[[_TOC_]]

#Insert record flow

A new record can be inserted in several ways.

- By a user working within the UI

- By calling the PortalGeneral_OnInsert stored procedure from T-SQL

- Importing data through one of the build-in import features or T-SQL import stored procedures.

- Some trigger code on a table that trigger to insert data in another table. That could be 'OnAfterInsert' on table A that inserts data in table B.

All these ways to insert data goes through the same flow starting from the horizontal line. When the user insert data by using the portal UI there is a step before that, where columns can be initiated with values to help the user. This requires custom code for that and 'OnInit' is never called when data is inserted one of the other ways mentioned in the list above. In this scenario the init of values must be set in 'Values' by code before calling the 'PortalGeneral_OnInsert'

![image.png](/.attachments/image-674de0b9-0c8e-4d86-bd5c-9b21e7102050.png)

#Modify record flow

A record can be modified by a user from the UI and directly by calling T-SQL 'PortalGeneral_OnModify' and the flow is the same in both scenarios. The modify flow is also similar to the insert flow except from that modify has to value parameters.

- OldValues

- NewValues

Remark - the OnModify flow will only be executed when 'NewValues' differs from 'OldValues'!!!

![image.png](/.attachments/image-c9894392-64dd-41cf-a2f7-2196eb0d7af1.png)

#Delete record flow

Delete records works the same from UI and directly from T-SQL.

Remark - the custom code 'OnBeforeDelete' can be used to execute cascading delete. Otherwise, it will fail if the record has related records in other tables.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-e23cdc2f-ff3f-4dd1-8a27-7333d435e695.png)

#Tableimport flow

The tableimport function is a stored procedure that is called when data is imported.

- Through the UI module 'ExportImport'

- Running an import script that is generated by the module 'ExportToScripts'

In both scenarios the stored procedure 'config.PortalTableImport' is called with several parameters and one of them is 'Data' which is a NVARCHAR(MAX) that contains all the columns and values in one string (BLOB). The string must be formed in the portal proprietary format.


![image.png](/.attachments/image-be8f6859-855e-44b3-ac25-4e747a24a6eb.png)

The 'PortalTableImport' convert the 'Data' into lines (records) and loop through these lines. First it checks if the user has the needed rights to insert and modify data in the table and then the loop starts, and everything is running as one transaction which means that if something fails the hole transaction is rolling back and nothing has happened.


The function uses standard functionality except from the 'OnBeforeImport', that is a custom possibility to control the import flow. This custom procedure is called if it exists, and it is called on each record with 'Columns' and 'Values'. That custom code can skip the record and continue to the next and it can change both 'Columns' and 'Values'. That is extremely useful in scenarios where the code needs to take care of ex primary keys. Let us say that some of the primary key columns is not included in the data but it can be found or generated and then send that result back to the flow before the flow check data and decide to insert or modify.

Since this flow is not calling an 'OnInit' procedure the 'OnBeforeImport' can also be used to set default values on columns or maybe some columns does not exists in the 'Data' stream and in that case the 'OnBeforeImport' can both add the column to the 'Columns' list and set the value to $NULL$ or blank.

#JSON Send flow

JSON Send is a core function that is used to insert and modify and running actions on one record (PUT) or on several records (BATCH). It is **important** to notice that there are deviations between JSON Send and the Tableimport because Tableimport is more an import functionality where JSON is an API approach to modify data without using the UI.

That deviations will be changed in the future but for now the main difference is that 'JSON Send Flow' is not calling the 'OnBeforeImport' trigger since it is not an import functionality.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-78c69032-f9b1-40c5-9a25-29aebfc54b73.png)

Remark also that the flow is calling 'OnInit' and that behavior will be considered and maybe removed in a future version because it can cause some problems depending in the code written in 'OnInit' because 'OnInit' is normally used in relation to the UI.

/Technology & Software/7. Admin Portal/7.1 Dev guide/7.1.3 Database development/How-to/Enable Generic Import on a table
content:
This feature enables Import of data to a table directly as an action on the table. Otherwise, the user must leave the table and use the module 'Export/Import (Basic)'.

The feature adds a new action called "GenericImportData" and everything from naming, icon and tooltip are managed by the reuse but can be overwritten.

The action afterwards be disabled with user rights for specific users or user groups just like all other action can.

The result of an implementation will add a new button to the table like this:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-88f51890-cc00-4c0f-bd1b-ae5d9558aa53.png)

And the dialog will then look like this.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-82a971e6-75dd-4a28-a927-e4117f6789bb.png)

**How-to**

The only thing to do is to copy the template stored procedure from reuse called.
"include\reuse_config\sql\00_CFG\Template\Optional\config.ConfigTable_Action_GenericImportData.StoredProcedure.sql" and just like all other templates just rename 'ConfigTable' to your tablename and inside the stored procedure replace #ConfigTableName# with the new name as well. After deploying the solution, the action will be implemented to the configtable.

path: /Technology & Software/7. Admin Portal/7.1 Dev guide/7.1.3 Database development/How-to/Enable MultiDelete action on a table
content:
'MultiDelete' is a reuse function that manages to delete more records at a time in a table. The function can be enabled on a table simply be adding a standard action called 'GenericMultiDelete' and after a PortalRefresh the action will appear in the upper right menu on the table:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-ed883abf-81a7-4598-8f2a-3bca6f43deda.png)

The action is called 'GenericMultiDelete' and related to user-rights configuration it will work just like all the other action do.

**How-to**
The only thing to do is to copy the template stored procedure from reuse called.
"include\reuse_config\sql\00_CFG\Template\Optional\config.ConfigTable_Action_GenericMultiDelete.StoredProcedure.sql" and just like all other templates just rename 'ConfigTable' to your tablename and inside the stored procedure replace #ConfigTableName# with the new name as well. After deploying the solution, the action will be implemented to the configtable.

path: /Technology & Software/7. Admin Portal/7.1 Dev guide/7.1.3 Database development/How-to/Implement Cell-edit
content:
Cell-edit is an advanced feature in the Portal platform that can enhance the functionality of a specific cell in a normal table list. Normally a table list shows only one table with columns. But let us say we have a table where some columns are normally columns and then other columns are with more information underneath. I could be a design where we have a 1:1 relation from the main table to an underlying table with more information depending on which cell they click or additional fields in the cell differs depending on a status column from the main table.

Let’s bring in a few examples:

Eks 1)
In the application 'Dynamic Dimension' we have implemented a cell edit in the mapping part of the application where we have a matrix with data vertical and dynamic number of columns horizontal. These columns horizontal differs in underlying behavior and each cell is a record in another table.

The vertical table is called 'config.CodelistMappingCodelist' and the cell table is 'config.CodelistMappingRule.'

In the first picture below the main table is from 'Value' to 'Description (rule)' and the column '[Var1]' and '[Var2]' has further information as shown in picture two. This example is even more advanced in cell-edit implementation because the number of horizontal columns is also dynamically and that is not a part of the Cell-edit implementation.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-0a65bfeb-eed4-408e-ad8b-b55fc0833244.png)

![image.png](/.attachments/image-b286a616-c350-47de-8cfe-e03d8e58fc3d.png)

Eks 2)     
Another example is the 'Leveranceportal' where we have a table called 'Package' and a column called 'Schedule'. By clicking in that cell, a new cell-edit form opens with information from another table called 'PackageSchedule' whit one record to set up a schedule on that specific package.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-4a83566f-847b-4f27-a340-df604bb32206.png)

![image.png](/.attachments/image-6e76c5e2-bef4-424e-928f-fc81fabe51a9.png)

That example could suddenly be designed in other ways. All schedule information could be on the 'Package' table but since it is not possibly to group information on a card form it would be less user-friendly to just put all columns on the same page. This design also gives the possibility to have different user permissions on the schedule part in case not all users are allowed to set-up schedule.

**REMARK**
The implementation of Cell-edit was released before the 'Action-form' feature and therefore the 'Action-form' will in some cases be a better choice than the 'Cell-edit'. This example two would properly today be implemented as an 'Action-form' with an action button on the right side of each line instead of using a cell for it.

Check the implementation for an 'Action-form' here [Build an ActionForm](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10158/Build-an-ActionForm).

**Implementation**
In this description we use the example no 2 above with a main table called 'Package' and a cell-edit table called 'PackageSchedule'.

_1) Create a derived column for the cell-edit in the main-table (parent)._

Since the cell-edit column is not a physical column in the 'Package' table we need to create a derived column in the stored procedure 'config.Package_UpdateFieldList' like this

```
INSERT INTO [config].[PortalFieldList]
           ([ConfigTable]
           ,[ColumnId]
           ,[SortOrder]
           ,[ListEnabled]
           ,[ColumnName]
           ,[DataType]
           ,[DataSize]
           ,[Precision]
           ,[Scale]
           ,[IsNullable]
           ,[FriendlyName]
           ,[IsPrimaryKey]
           ,[IsInsertField]
           ,[IsModifyField]
           ,[IsLookupField]
           ,[LookupInputType]
           ,[LookupRelatedColumn]
           ,[IsHidden]
           ,[IsRequired]
           ,[IsUserstamp]
           ,[IsTimestamp]
           ,[HelpText]
           ,[NULL2Value]
           ,[IsCellEdit]
           ,[CellEditConfigTable]
           ,[IsProtectedOnInsert]
           ,[IsProtectedOnModify])
SELECT
            @ConfigTable as [ConfigTable]
           ,1000 as [ColumnId]
           ,120 as [SortOrder]
           ,1 as [ListEnabled]
           ,'Schedule' as [ColumnName]
           ,'nvarchar' as [DataType]
           ,250 as [DataSize]
           ,0 as [Precision]
           ,0 as [Scale]
           ,'Yes' as [IsNullable]
           ,'Schedule' as [FriendlyName]
           ,0 as [IsPrimaryKey]
           ,0 AS [IsInsertField]
           ,0 AS [IsModifyField]
           ,0 AS [IsLookupField]
           ,0 AS [LookupInputType]
           ,'' AS [LookupRelatedColumn]
           ,0 AS [IsHidden]
           ,0 AS [IsRequired]
           ,0 AS [IsUserstamp]
           ,0 AS [IsTimestamp]
           ,'' AS [HelpText]
           ,'' AS [NULL2Value]
           ,1 AS [IsCellEdit]
           ,'PackageSchedule' AS [CellEditConfigTable]
           ,0 AS [IsProtectedOnInsert]
           ,0 AS [IsProtectedOnModify]
```
Notice that the column 'IsCellEdit' is set to 1 and the column 'CellEditConfigTable' is set to 'PackageSchedule' which is the name of the configtable that will be used in the cell-edit.

_2) Create a configtable_

Define the configtable that is used in the cell-edit. It is done just like all other configtables with a stored procedure 'UpdateFieldList', maybe some lookup value stored procedure, and OnValidate stored procedure and in some situations also a OnBeforeModify / OnAfterModify stored procedure.

_3) Create a 'OnloadCellData' stored procedure_

The next step is to create a stored procedure that the UI call when the user dobble-click in a cell that is marked as a cell-edit column.

**Template**
The 'config.ConfigTable_OnLoadCelldata.StoredProcedure' stored procedure template can be found in the folder 'include\reuse_config\sql\00_CFG\Template\Optional\05_Procedures'.

The job for this stored procedure is more things:
- Insert the record in table 'PackageSchedule' if does not exist since the cell-edit always work in 'modify' mode so the record has to exists.
- Return columns and values for the card form that will open when the UI return from this stored procedure.
- Return the name of the configtable to be edit in cell-edit mode. (Note 1)

**Note 1**
This is important! In this example described above we know that that name of the configtable to be edited in cell-edit is always the same on each row. In that case we can set the property 'CellEditConfigtable' to 'PackageSchedule' and the cell-edit functionality will call a stored procedure named 'config.PackageSchedule_OnLoadCelldata'.

Let´s say we have a situation where the cell-edit configtable change on each line depending on a value in one of the other columns. That could be a status or record type column. In that situation we can’t tell the name of the cell-edit configtable a design time so we will leave the column 'CellEditConfigtable' blank. If this is blank and the user click the cell the UI will instead call a stored procedure named 'config.Package_OnLoadCelldata' which is the name of the main table. Then this can return the columns and values **and** the name of the configtable that is used in the celledit.

_Example of a stored procedure_

The interface of such a stored procedure is like this:

```
@Columnname nvarchar(max),

@Columns nvarchar(max),
@Values nvarchar(max),                                     

@CellEditConfigTable nvarchar(max) OUTPUT,
@CellEditColumns nvarchar(max) OUTPUT,
@CellEditValues nvarchar(max) OUTPUT,
@ReturnMsg nvarchar(max) OUTPUT
```

|Parameter|Description  |
|--|--|
| Columnname |The name of the cell-edit column. Is only useful in case we have more than one cell-edit column in a table  |
| Columns | Columns of the calling table (parent) |
| Values | Record values on calling table (parent) |
| CellEditConfigTabe | Check Note 1 - this value is by default the name from PortalFieldList (CellEditConfigtable) but it can also be empty and mut be set in this stored procedure. REMARK - if the value is returned with blank the cell-edit will abort without an error |
| CellEditColumns | Return the columnlist of the configtable that will be edited in the modify card form |
| CellEditValues | Return the valuelist of the configtable that will be edited on the modify card form |
| ReturnMsg | Return and errormessage |

_How to write the OnLoadCelldata_

Here is an example of how to write the stored procedure for cell-edit. It receives Columns and Values from the parent table and create the cell-edit record if is not existing. After that, it builds the CellEditColumns and CellEditValues that will be used on the modify card form.

```
ALTER PROCEDURE [config].[PackageSchedule_OnLoadCellData]
      (-- Standard system variables

                               @Columnname nvarchar(max),

                               @Columns nvarchar(max),
                               @Values nvarchar(max),                                   

                               @CellEditConfigTable nvarchar(max) OUTPUT,
                               @CellEditColumns nvarchar(max) OUTPUT,
                               @CellEditValues nvarchar(max) OUTPUT,
                               @ReturnMsg nvarchar(max) OUTPUT
                               ) 
AS

DECLARE @Language nvarchar(20) = (SELECT [config].[PortalGetLanguage]());
DECLARE @Username nvarchar(50) = (SELECT [config].[PortalGetUsername]());
DECLARE @ConfigTable as nvarchar(250) = (select Item from dbo.SplitString((SELECT OBJECT_NAME(@@PROCID)),'_') where Num = 1);

set @Values = replace(@Values,'''','''''');

set @ReturnMsg = '';

BEGIN TRY

  -- create schedule if not exists
  declare @PackageScheduleID as uniqueidentifier; 
  set @PackageScheduleID  = (select [config].[PortalGetValue](@Columns,@Values,'ID'));
  declare @ScheduleRecordId as bigint;

  declare @PackageName as nvarchar(250) = (select [config].[PortalGetValue](@Columns,@Values,'PackageName'));

  set @ScheduleRecordId = (select DW_ArchiveID from config.PackageSchedule where ID = @PackageScheduleID);

  if @ScheduleRecordId is null
  begin
    declare @CreateColumn as nvarchar(max);
                             declare @CreateValues as nvarchar(max);

                             set @CreateColumn = 'ID#¤#EffectiveFrom#¤#ProcessTime#¤#MonthFilter#¤#DaysInMonthFilter#¤#ReverseDaysInMonthFilter#¤#DaysInWeekFilter#¤#ScheduleWithStatus#¤#ScheduleWithTasks#¤#PublishDayAfter'
                             set @CreateValues =  cast(upper(@PackageScheduleID) as nvarchar(50)) + '#¤#' + cast(CAST(convert(varchar,getdate(),121) AS DATE) as nvarchar(50)) + '#¤#' + cast(CAST(convert(varchar,getdate(),121) AS TIME) as nvarchar(50)) + '#¤#' + '#¤#' + '#¤#0' + '#¤#' + '#¤#0#¤#1,4,5#¤#$NULL$'

                             EXECUTE [config].[PortalGeneral_OnInsert]
                                @ConfigTable = @ConfigTable
                               ,@Columns = @CreateColumn
                               ,@Values = @CreateValues
                               ,@RecordID = @ScheduleRecordId OUTPUT
                               ,@ReturnMsg = @ReturnMsg OUTPUT
                               ,@CheckUserRights = 1
                               ,@RunValidation = 0
                               ,@DisableLogging = 0  

  end;

  EXECUTE [config].[PortalRecordToColumnValue]
    @ConfigTable = @ConfigTable
   ,@RecordID = @ScheduleRecordId
   ,@Columns = @CellEditColumns OUTPUT
   ,@Values = @CellEditValues OUTPUT
   ,@ReturnMsg = @ReturnMsg OUTPUT

   set @CellEditColumns = @CellEditColumns + '#¤#PackageName';
   set @CellEditValues = @CellEditValues + '#¤#' + @PackageName

END TRY
BEGIN CATCH
  SET @ReturnMsg = ERROR_MESSAGE(); 
  RETURN 1;
END CATCH

RETURN 0;

```

path: /Technology & Software/7. Admin Portal/7.1 Dev guide/7.1.3 Database development/How-to/Implement Record-level security
content:
Security on tables is a standard feature in the portal reuse that enables to gain or deny access on table level and configure CRUD rights and access to actions per user or user-groups.

In this example with the table 'Codelist' all users have access to 'read' data and execute standard actions. The members of user group 'Administrator' will also get these standard rights and furthermore get create, modify, delete and some more actions.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-0fb0f135-d84c-4dee-b21b-7dcec1ce08e0.png)

This setup has nothing to do with record-level security but will gain or deny access to all records in a table. The next level is to setup security on records by defining filter on columns.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-777bad50-d5e9-40ee-a3f3-960c388eaa20.png)

This is just an example, but the user rights here define that it will filter on the column 'Name' and only show records that contains the word *test' or 'Land'. It will also not be possible for det user to change the data or insert new data outside this filter.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-1460e6c0-1ef7-47d0-ba19-06d4101dd299.png)

It is possible to define several lines but only one line per Columnname and the 'LogicalOperator' cannot change so it must be 'AND' or 'OR' on all lines.

**Enable columns for record-level security**

It is important to notice that by default no columns are enabled for record-level security. To enable a column to set the property 'IsDataRightsFilterEnabled' = 1 in the PortalFieldList by adding update code in the stored procedure 'UpdateFileList'.

**How does it work**

The magic is placed in standard reuse stored procedure like 'PortalGeneral_GetRecordList', 'PortalGeneral_OnInsert', 'PortalGeneral_OnModify' so be default it will work without any changes besides to set the 'IsDataRightsFilterEnabled' property on columns and defining rights in the portal.

_GetRecordList_

It is important to notice here that often we create a custom 'GetRecordList' stored procedure and here it is important always to base that on a template because in that stored procedure we need some code to filter on data like in this example.

The '+  **(select config.PortalGetDataUserRightsWhereClause(@ConfigTable))**' part is the logic that set a dynamic filter on the data based on record-level security configuration.

```
CREATE PROCEDURE [config].[#ConfigTableName#_GetRecordList]
  (@TableFilter nvarchar(max) = '')  -- EX FromTableName#DW_ArchiveID

AS

DECLARE @Language nvarchar(20) = (SELECT [config].[PortalGetLanguage]());
DECLARE @Username nvarchar(250) = (SELECT [config].[PortalGetUsername]());
declare @ConfigTable as nvarchar(250) = (select Item from dbo.SplitString((SELECT OBJECT_NAME(@@PROCID)),'_') where Num = 1);

BEGIN TRY
                             DECLARE @SQLStatement AS nvarchar(max) = ''; 

                             SET @SQLStatement = N'
                               select
                                  sub.*
                              FROM
                                 ( select PT.* from [config].[#ConfigTableName#_GetRecordListView] PT [WhereClause]) sub        '
                                                          +  (select config.PortalGetDataUserRightsWhereClause(@ConfigTable))  + ' order by sub.DW_ArchiveID desc'

                             IF @TableFilter <> ''
                             BEGIN
                               -- General TableFilter
                               if replace(@TableFilter ,'MenuTableFilter','') != @TableFilter
                               begin
                                  declare @Filter as nvarchar(max) = (select FilterExpression from config.PortalTableFilter where DW_ArchiveID = (select item from dbo.SplitString(@TableFilter,'#') where num = 2))
                                                           set @SQLStatement = replace(@SQLStatement,'[WhereClause]',' ' + replace(@Filter,'@User','''' + @Username + ''''));                                               
                               end else
                               begin
                                                            -- LinkFrom table
                                                            DECLARE @FromTableName as nvarchar(150) = (select Item from dbo.SplitString(@TableFilter,'#') where num = 1);
                                                            IF @FromTableName <> ''
                                                            BEGIN
                                                                                       DECLARE @FromRecordId as bigint = isnull(cast((select Item from dbo.SplitString(@TableFilter,'#') where num = 2) as bigint),-1);

                                                                                       -- Build the WHERE statement with information from FromTableName and the RecordId
                                                                                       -- Lookup columns from the calling table and create a dynamic WHERE clause
                                                                                       SET @SQLStatement = replace(@SQLStatement,'[WhereClause]',' WHERE 1=2'); -- change the where clause
                                                            END;
                               END;
                             END ELSE
                               set @SQLStatement = REPLACE(@SQLStatement,'[WhereClause]','');

                             EXECUTE sp_executesql @SQLStatement;                          

END TRY
BEGIN CATCH
  THROW;
  RETURN 1;
END CATCH

```
So always be sure to have that logic in a custom 'GetRecordList' if the table is enabled for record-level security.

**Lookupcolumns**

If a table is uses as lookup on a column in another table it is necessary to define the same security filter again on that table / column so that only allowed records will be populated when the user open that lookup.

path: /Technology & Software/7. Admin Portal/7.1 Dev guide/7.1.3 Database development/How-to/Use the Debugger
content:
The debugger in this platform is not a traditional debugger as we know from development environment like C# etc., but it is a tool that can trace the communication between front-end and back-end to discover what happens and which columns and values are send and retrieved during the execution.

It can´t handles errors so it will not log errors, and the debug record will not be inserted if an error occurs. In that case the Portallog will be a better place to look. So, the debugger is more a tool to use if something logic is not working as attended.

The debugger can both be used from the UI and from T-SQL. The way it works is to start de debugger and then work in the portal UI in the specific area with an issue and afterwards open the PortalDebug table and investigate what has happened.

**UI**
In a standard application the 'Debugger' can be found in the menu.
![image.png](/.attachments/image-aa2e568b-874c-49a5-a854-f4266df0c90d.png)

And the page looks like this.
![image.png](/.attachments/image-eab709bd-744e-4320-9e1c-a98f634ea4ec.png)

The debugger can then be started with pushing the ![image.png](/.attachments/image-3a2fae83-c142-4eaf-b834-862d3ccaa499.png) button and then go to the part in the application where the logging should come from or open another page with the portal so you have one session with the debugger and one session with the application.

After that go back to the debugger and hit the ![image.png](/.attachments/image-f76af7a8-d191-4b7b-8ea6-2566de6a0d6f.png) button and the debugger will stop.

Lines will then appear in the debug windows and from top to bottom it will tell what stored procedure has been called - both standard stored procedure and custom stored procedures.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-60bc6780-4c6e-4060-9288-894f1967fea8.png)

Often the debugger is used to clarify if values in columns are as expected and on every stored procedure where we have columns and values that will also be logged here. To get a better view of columns and values the button ![image.png](/.attachments/image-dc7cd769-da0b-4c24-84af-609bf174501a.png) on each line is useful to get a better picture like in the example here where the line with triggername "OnModify" is explored:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-f3a625f9-f774-48aa-bedd-5181fd4fd90d.png)

And it tells that the column 'Description' has changed.

That is what the debugger in the portal can be used for and it is very useful in situations where custom columns are added to the model and changed during the flow to track is that happens as expected.

This functionality can also be used through T-SQL instead if using the portal UI.

**T-SQL**
To work with the debugger from T-SQL are few functions and a table is nice to know about.

Start the debugger.
```
exec config.PortalDebugStart;
```

Stop the debugger.
```
exec config.PortalDebugStop;
```

Select the debugger.
```
select * from config.PortalDebug;
```

Eks:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-a8b70d60-cccd-47a2-8f9f-0d6c339774c7.png)

Explore one line with columns and values.
```
exec config.PortalDebugExplore 1124;
```

Result:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-f19982c8-5f7e-40e1-ae05-3279319771be.png)

[[_TOSP_]]

path: /Technology & Software/7. Admin Portal/7.1 Dev guide/7.1.3 Database development/How-to/Use the Debugger/Debug T-SQL from Visual Studio
content:
As mentions in the above section the debugger inside the Portal UI is more a logger than a debugger. It is not possible to debug code, but the logger can be useful in order to get more information about which stored procedures are called and which columns and values are send as parameters.
With that information it will be possible to do further debugging in T-SQL using Visual Studio.

It is also important to know that the UI only call a few entry points in the reuse T-SQL code (see list below) and with that knowledge and the Columns / Values from the logger the debugging in Visual Studio can begin.

| Stored procedure (Entry point) |Description  |
|--|--|
| PortalGeneral_GetRecordList |Retrive data or call a custom GetRecordList to retrive data  |
| PortalGeneral_GetValueList |Call the custom stored procedure that return a lookuplist for a given Configtable and Columnname  |
| PortalGeneral_GetRelationList |Call the custom stored procedure that return relation data between two columns  |
| PortalGeneral_OnInsert | Insert new record  |
| PortalGeneral_OnModify | Modify an existing record |
| PortalGeneral_Delete | Delete a record |
| PortalGeneral_RunAction | Run a custom action  |
| PortalGeneral_OnLoadActionForm | The ui calls this to return information about the actionform to build  |

**Example**
Let’s says we have a problem with modifying a record in the portal and we want to debug that. By using the Debug (logger) we have detected that the portal calls the 'OnModify' on the table 'PortalADGroup' with Columns and OldValues/NewValues.

With that information it is possible in Visual Studio to connect to the database and start a debugging session with code like this. Must of the code can be generated by scription the stored procedure as execute and then just put in the missing values.

```
DECLARE @RC int
DECLARE @ConfigTable nvarchar(250) = 'PortalADGroup'
DECLARE @Columns nvarchar(max) = 'ADGroupName#¤#Description#¤#MemberOf#¤#DW_ArchiveID'
DECLARE @NewValues nvarchar(max) = 'DN\KMD2-xxx#¤#Kirsten Knudsen#¤##¤#5'
DECLARE @OldValues nvarchar(max) = 'DN\KMD2-xxx#¤#Kirsten Knudsen Jensen#¤##¤#5'
DECLARE @ReturnMsg nvarchar(max)
DECLARE @CheckUserRights bit = 1
DECLARE @RunValidation bit = 1
DECLARE @DisableLogging bit = 0

-- TODO: Set parameter values here.

EXECUTE @RC = [config].[PortalGeneral_OnModify]
   @ConfigTable
  ,@Columns
  ,@NewValues
  ,@OldValues
  ,@ReturnMsg OUTPUT
  ,@CheckUserRights
  ,@RunValidation
  ,@DisableLogging

```

By setting a breakpoint at the 'EXECUTE' line it is possible to debug the code and investigate variables etc.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-f052e1a4-d472-4780-b366-119c82e1322f.png)

Stepped into the config.PortalGeneral_OnModify and looking at some variables.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-84293b09-5220-48aa-bf20-ef844f003e98.png)

path: /Technology & Software/7. Admin Portal/7.1 Dev guide/7.1.3 Database development/How-to/Work with JSON API
content:
#**HOW TO USE JSON TO GET AND PUT DATA**

In the AdminPortal framework there are different ways to CRUD data directly with T-SQL code by calling stored procedures from the reuse library. If the user/developer has access to data it is of course possible to access data directly with INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE statements but we recommend always to use "API" stored procedure to ensure that business logic, validation rules and logging are executed.

The framework exposes three stored procedure that make it possible to retrieve and send data in JSON format to the data model just the same way as the UI does it.

##_config.PortalSendJSON_

This stored procedure can be used to send records to the database. The call will be managed as one transaction and if something fails the hole transaction will be rolling back. In this example only the table "OrganisationStructure" is used, but you can have different tables in the same script.

```
declare @JSON as nvarchar(max) = N'
{
                             "OrganisationStructure": [
                             {
                                                          "Level": "1",
                                                          "Description": "Operator"
                             },
                             {
                                                          "Level": "2",
                                                          "Description": "Indirect Reseller"
                             }
 ]
}'
set nocount on;
DECLARE @ReturnMsg nvarchar(max)
DECLARE @RC as int
EXECUTE @RC = [config].[PortalSendJSON]
  @JSON = @JSON,
  @ReturnMsg = @ReturnMsg OUTPUT,
  @ThrowException = false,
  @ValidationOnly = false,
  @UpdateIfExists = true,
  @IgnoreIfExists = true,
  @DisplayDataResult = false,
  @MessageLevel    = 1,
  @CheckUserRights = 0
```

|Parameter|Description  |
|--|--|
| JSON | A valid JSON expression |
| ReturnMsg | If something went wrong a message will be returned here |
| ThrowException | 0=No, 1=Yes - when an error occurs the code will throw an expression |
| ValidationOnly | 0=No, 1=Yes meaning that the transaction is rolling back. That can be used to check the JSON |
| UpdateIfExists | 0=No, 1=Yes meaning that the record will be updated - but only with columns that are included in the JSON |
| IgnoreIfExists | 0=No - if the record exists an error will return. 1=Yes - existing records will be ignored and can then be updated be setting UpdateIfExists = 1  |
| DisplayDataResult | 0=No, 1=Yes - at the end the SP will return the data that was changed during the update |
| MessageLevel | 0 = None, 1 = HighInfo, 2=LowInfo |
| CheckUserRights | 0=No, 1=Yes meaning that the user running the code must have user rights to do so. (1) is best practice but (0) can be used if the script is used for deployment |

##_config.PortalGeneral_JSONGet_

This stored procedure is used for getting data out of a data model in a JSON format. It will retrieve data the same way as the UI does and the result will include both physical columns from the table and derived columns generated in the portal logic.

Here is an example of how to do it. This ex get data from the 'CodelistName' table. All columns but with a filter on 'Name' and ordered by column 'Description'.

```
DECLARE @JSON nvarchar(max)
DECLARE @ReturnMsg nvarchar(max)

EXECUTE [config].[PortalGeneral_JSONGet]
   @ConfigTable = 'Codelistname'
  ,@ColumnList = '*'
  ,@ColumnFilter = '[Name] like ''%test%'''
  ,@ColumnOrder = 'Description'
  ,@ExcludeDerivedColumns = 1
  ,@ReturnNULLColumns = 0
  ,@ReturnWithROOT = 0
  ,@JSON = @JSON OUTPUT
  ,@ReturnMsg = @ReturnMsg OUTPUT

```
This result is lige this:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-f4b4688e-44ef-4c95-802a-52f29441c25d.png)

|Parameter  |Description  |
|--|--|
| Configtable | Name of the table to get data from |
| ColumnList | Not required but can be a list of columns. It is also possible to create derived columns with T-SQL expressions |
| ColumnFilter | Can filter on data as done i T-SQL. Without the WHERE clause but AND / OR etc is supported |
| ColumnOrder | Blank or a list of columns that the data should be sorted by |
| ExcludeDerivedColumns | 0 (default) = All columns define in PortalFieldlist will be included in data. 1 = Only physical columns in the table will be included  |
| ReturnNULLColumns | 0 (default) = Columns with NULL is not included. 1=NULL columns are included with the value 'null' |
| ReturnWithROOT | 0 (default) = Record is returned as a array without a ROOT name. 1= Data is returned with a ROOT name. |
| JSON | The result formed as JSON |
| ReturnMsg | ReturnMsg if something went wrong. Blank if the statement succeeds |

##_config.PortalGeneral_JSONPut_

The PUT stored procedure can be used to INSERT/MODIFY/DELETE or/and run ACTION for one record per call. It can be used everywhere in a solution code to modify data instead of using config.PortalGeneral_OnInsert, config.PortalGeneral_OnModify ect and it can be used under deployment to modify data. The function was developed in a project where specific operations in the solution was implemented in a special developed UI application than the standard AdminPortal UI and by using the Put and Get function the new portal UI execute the same functionality and business logic as with the AdminPortal UI.

Eks 1: Insert or Update a customer.
```
DECLARE @JSONResult nvarchar(max)
DECLARE @ReturnMsg nvarchar(max)

DECLARE @JSON nvarchar(max) = N'
  {
    "Number":"10000",
    "Name":"Test customer 1000",
    "Active":true
  }'

EXECUTE @RC = [config].[PortalGeneral_JSONPut]
   @ConfigTable = 'Customer'
  ,@JSON = @JSON
  ,@Action = ''
  ,@JSONResult = @JSONResult OUTPUT
  ,@IgnoreIfExists = 1
  ,@UpdateIfExists = 1
  ,@ReturnMsg = @ReturnMsg OUTPUT

```

Eks 2: Delete a customer.
```
DECLARE @JSONResult nvarchar(max)
DECLARE @ReturnMsg nvarchar(max)

DECLARE @JSON nvarchar(max) = N'
  {
    "Number":"10000"
  }'

EXECUTE @RC = [config].[PortalGeneral_JSONPut]
   @ConfigTable = 'Customer'
  ,@JSON = @JSON
  ,@Action = 'DELETE'
  ,@JSONResult = @JSONResult OUTPUT
  ,@IgnoreIfExists = 1
  ,@UpdateIfExists = 1
  ,@ReturnMsg = @ReturnMsg OUTPUT

```

| Parameter |Description  |
|--|--|
| ConfigTable |Name of the configtable to Put data  |
| JSON | Valid JSON input  |
| Action | Run a action on that record. DELETE is a build-action but it can also be specific actions related to that table except call to Linked Tables.  |
| JSONResult | The inserted/updated record is returned as a JSON object  |
| UpdateIfExists | 0=No, 1=Yes meaning that the record will be updated - but only with columns that are included in the JSON |
| IgnoreIfExists | 0=No - if the record exists an error will return. 1=Yes - existing records will be ignored and can then be updated be setting UpdateIfExists = 1  |
| ReturnMsg | ReturnMsg if something went wrong. Blank if the statement succeeds |

##_api.PortalGeneral_JSONGet_
