path: /Technology & Software/7. Admin Portal/7.1 Dev guide/7.1.3 Database development/How-to/Work with TaskQueue
content:
The 'TaskQueue' module in reuse_config is a set of tables and stored procedures that implement a setup for communication with external components that are asynchronously execute by one or more services. The UI cannot communicate with external API´s because it is a generic UI application and that would mean that specific code must be implemented in the UI and that is not the concept or architecture of the UI application.

The 'TaskQueue' implementation is a generic implementation of tasks landing in a queue with agreed information and services that read these task - execute them and call back with a success or an error. When the service calls back the task can be setup to call a stored procedure that can handle the return value and update some status information in the portal and start new tasks in case it is a part of a workflow.

Let start with some of the objects in the module.

**queue.TaskQueue (Table)**

Data will be inserted in this table by calling **[queue].[AddTask]**

|Columnname|Description  ||
|--|--|--|
| EntityID | GUID that is a reference to a record in the application. There can be several records with the same EntityID. When the service calls back it is calling with the 'TaskID'. With that 'TaskID' we can get the 'EntityID' that again can find and update the referred record in the application.  | |
| TaskType | The tasktype that a service can execute. The service will ask for tasks with that specific 'Tasktype' | |
| TaskSubType | A 'TaskType' can be split into several subtypes - ex 'Add', 'Update', 'Delete'. It is not mandatory to use 'TaskSubType' | |
| TaskStatus | NEW, PROCESSING, FAILED, SUCCEEDED | |
| TaskID | A unique sequence (primary key) of the TaskQueue. It is ID that the services use when the service call back | |
| SubStatus | In a scenario where a task runs in a longer period it can temporarily update with a substatus and a PctDone. It requires that the service call the stored procedure [queue].[UpdateTaskSubStatus] | |
| PctDone |Ditto as 'SubStatus'  | |
| TaskWorkerID | The ID of the service that is executing the task.  | |
| TsLastStatusChange | Timestamp when the status last changed. Automatic updated   | |
| DurationMs | Duration in milliseconds the task runs. Automatic updated ||
| TaskErrorCode | Error coded returned from the service if it fails ||
| ErrorMessage | ErrorMessage returned from the service if it fails ||
| OnCompletedProc | When the service returns the logic can then call a stored procedure with the status (see below). This can help updating the Entity with some status or start a new task if it is a Workflow that is running  ||
| JSONTask | The information in a JSON structure that the service needs. This is an agreement with the service what the content is formed.  ||
| JSONResult |This is not a mandatory field but in some scenarios a service can send information back to the backend that can be stored in the databasen or used to create the next task in the workflow.  ||
| CreatedTs | Datetime when the task is created. Automatic updated.  ||
| CreatedByUserName | The name of the user in the Portal that has created the task. ||

**queue.TaskWorker (Table)**

Data in this table is auto inserted and updated when the service ask for new tasks by calling **[queue].[GetNewTask]** and **[queue].[GetNewTasks]**.

|Columnname|Description  |
|--|--|
| ID | The ID of the service |
| Description |  |
| HeartBeat | Datetime when the service requested new tasks |

**[queue].[AddTask] (procedure)**

_Purpose_

With this stored procedure the portal application can add a new task to the queue asking one of the services to handle that task depending on the Task Type.

The @entityId will reference to a record in the portal that trigger this task so it will be possible to find back to that record when the service return and call the @onCompleteProc. (see below how to implement the @onCompleteProc). There can be several tasks with the same @entityID because the 'TaskId' columns is the primary key on table queue.TaskQueue.

_Example_

```
EXEC [queue].[AddTask]
                                                          @entityID = '4E2A8655-A1F1-4173-BBF5-F47BCFF863FE',
                                                          @taskType = N'ServiceName',
                                                          @taskSubType = N'Add',
                                                          @subStatus = N'',
                                                          @onCompleteProc = N'dbo.MyCompleteProc',
                                                          @jsonTask = N'{"VariableName":"A","Value":10}',
                                                          @createdByUsername = N'username',
                                                          @taskID = @taskID OUTPUT

```

**[queue].[GetNewTask] (procedure)**

_Purpose_

A service will call this stored procedure with a taskworkerid and a task type and it will return the next task to execute with the following columns. Empty if no tasks where found. The tasks that are returned to the service will automatically change TaskStatus to 'PROCESSING'.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-357dab38-55f9-444b-b1cd-4466f9565742.png)

_Example_

```
EXECUTE [queue].[GetNewTask]
   @taskWorkerID = N'NameOfWorker'
  ,@taskType = 'NameOfService'

```

**[queue].[GetNewTasks] (procedure)**

_Purpose_

The stored procedure **[queue].[GetNewTask]** call this stored procedure with @numTasks = 1, so this is the stored procedure that returns x numbers of tasks and change TaskStatus to 'PROCESSING'.

_Example_

```
EXECUTE [queue].[GetNewTasks]
   @taskWorkerID = N'NameOfWorker'
  ,@taskType = 'NameOService'
  ,@numTasks = 10

```

**[queue].[SetTaskSucceded] (procedure)**

_Purpose_

When a service executes a task with success it will call this stored procedure and the stored procedure will update the task and call the @onCompleteProc if that is defined on the task.

_Example_

```
EXECUTE [queue].[SetTaskSucceeded]
   @taskID = ??
  ,@taskType = 'NameOfService'
  ,@subStatus = ''
  ,@durationMS = ??
  ,@jsonResult = N'' -- If some information needs to be send back it can be built into a JSON object string

```

**[queue].[SetTaskFailed] (procedure)**

_Purpose_

When a task fails this stored procedure must be called and it requires a few more information than the succeeded store procedure such a taskerrorcode and errormessage. It will update the task with this information and call the @onCompleteProc so that necessary action can be done in the backend in order to update some status and/or creating a changelog about the error that has occurred.

_Example_

```
EXECUTE  [queue].[SetTaskFailed]
   @taskID = ??
  ,@taskType = 'NameOfService'
  ,@subStatus = ''
  ,@durationMS = ??
  ,@taskErrorCode = ??
  ,@errorMessage = 'ErrorMessage'
  ,@jsonResult  = N'' -- If some information needs to be send back it can be built into a JSON object string

```

**[queue].[UpdateTaskSubStatus] (procedure)**

_Purpose_

This stored procedure can be used in case where a task runs minutes or even hours. It can then frequently call the backend and update the task with a process status in percent and a substatus.

_Example_

```
EXECUTE  [queue].[UpdateTaskSubStatus]
   @taskID = ??
  ,@taskType = 'NameOfService'
  ,@subStatus = 'Doing something'
  ,@pctDone = 56

```

**[queue].[ReleaseTask] (procedure)**

_Purpose_

It will require some logic implemented in the service to work with this stored procedure but the use of it is in case a service is shutting down to ensure that the tasks are released again by changing the taskstatus from 'PROCESSING' to 'NEW'.

_Example_

```
EXECUTE [queue].[ReleaseTask]
   @taskWorkerID = 'NameOfWorker'
  ,@taskID = ??
  ,@taskType = 'NameOfService'

```

**[config].[OnCompleteProc] (procedure)**

_Purpose_

The name of this stored procedure is just an example, and it can be named anything depending of the functionality it is handling. The stored procedure will be executed when the task change status to 'SUCCEEDED' or 'FAILED' and give the business logic the possibility to act on that and maybe update a status columns, adding some logging or even add some new tasks to be run if this task type is a part of a workflow.

The stored procedure must be implemented like this example.

_Example_

```
create procedure dbo.Complete(@taskID bigint,@taskStatus nvarchar(20))
as

declare @EntityID as uniqueidentifier = (select top 1 EntityID from queue.TaskQueue where TaskID = @taskID); tabellen.

-- find the referred record in the portal and do something
```

**[config].[TaskQueue_UpdateFieldlist] (procedure)**

_Purpose_

By default the **queue.TaskQueue** table is not enabled as a portal config table but that is possible because the table is prepared to be a config table so the first thing to do is to add a 'UpdateFieldList' stored procedure and add the table to the PortalMenu. In the following example the table is made not editable but it would be possible to change that, so it is possible to update and even add records from the portal UI.

Remark - that the table is placed in another schema than 'config' and therefore last line is needed to tell the portal backend where the table is placed physical.

_Example_

```
CREATE PROCEDURE [config].[TaskQueue_UpdateFieldList]
AS

set nocount on;

declare @ConfigTable as nvarchar(250) =  replace(replace(replace(OBJECT_NAME(@@PROCID),'[',''),']',''),'_UpdateFieldList','');

UPDATE config.PortalFieldList
  set IsModifyField = 0, IsInsertField = 0
WHERE
  ConfigTable = @ConfigTable

GO -- IMPORTANT To HAVE A GO HERE
EXEC sys.sp_addextendedproperty @name=N'PhysSchemaName', @value=N'queue' , @level0type=N'SCHEMA',@level0name=N'config',
                                level1type=N'PROCEDURE',@level1name=N'TaskQueue_UpdateFieldList'

```

/Technology & Software/7. Admin Portal/7.1 Dev guide/7.1.3 Database development/How-to/Work with tables in another schema than config
content:
Normally and by default all config tables are places in the 'config' schema, but it is possible to work with config tables that are placed in another database schema or even tables with different table name that the name used physical.

So let’s say we have a table called **[system].[IncommingCustomers]** and we want to access that table through the portal UI and all other entry points and work with that table just as a normal config table. Furthermore, we want to name it **Customer**.

Before we can do that, we must make sure, that the table contains all the mandatory fields like other config tables.

```
...
[DW_ArchiveID] BIGINT (assigned to a sequence)
[DW_Audit_Insert] INT
[DW_Audit_Update] INT
[DW_Audit]
...
```

The next step is to create the **Updatefieldlist** stored procedure and be aware in the bottom of the template we have two lines that are not active by default but when we activate them, we can change the name of the schema and the table name like this:

```
...
/* Here you can change the physical name of both schema and table name

GO -- GO MUST BE EXECUTED BEFORE NEXT COMMAND

EXEC sys.sp_addextendedproperty @name=N'PhysSchemaName', @value=N'InsertPhysSchemaNameHere*' , @level0type=N'SCHEMA',@level0name=N'config', @level1type=N'PROCEDURE',@level1name=N'#ConfigTableName#_UpdateFieldList'

EXEC sys.sp_addextendedproperty @name=N'PhysTableName', @value=N'InsertPhysTableNameHere' , @level0type=N'SCHEMA',@level0name=N'config', @level1type=N'PROCEDURE',@level1name=N'#ConfigTableName#_UpdateFieldList'

*/
...
```
The **GO** command is important to keep because this line is only part of the deployment of the stored procedure and not that has to be part of the stored procedure on every execute.

Change the value of 'InsertPhysSchemaNameHerre' to the ex 'system' and 'InsertPhysTableNameHere' to 'IncommingCustomers'. Be sure to change the #ConfigTableName# also to the logical table name.

After deploy we will have at logical config table called 'config.Customer'.

**Remark**
This feature is also very useful in case we want to work with read-only data placed in views.

path: /Technology & Software/7. Admin Portal/7.1 Dev guide/7.1.3 Database development/Templates/Mandatory
content:
To build a config-table some minor objects are needed.

All mandatory templates can be found in the folder.

`include\reuse_config\sql\00_CFG\Template\Mandatory`

**config.ID_ConfigTable.Sequence**

All tables must have the column 'DW_ArchvieID' assigned with a sequence. The UI uses that as a unique RecordID and can also be referred to that column in the business logic.

**config.ConfigTable.Table**

The layout/design of a table is free, but it must include at least these 4 columns.

```
...
[DW_ArchiveID] BIGINT (assigned to a sequence)
[DW_Audit_Insert] INT
[DW_Audit_Update] INT
[DW_Audit]
...
```
**config.ConfigTable_UpdateFieldList.StoredProcedure**

This stored procedure has two purposes:
1. If it exists the table can be added to the PortalMenu
1. The developer can change the PortalFieldList properties during deployment and add more derived columns to the model.

Two examples of how to change properties:

```
update config.PortalFieldList
  set IsRequired = 0
where
  ConfigTable = @ConfigTable and ColumnName in ('HelpText','ConfirmMsg','IconName')

update config.PortalFieldList
  set IsModifyField = 1, IsProtectedOnModify = 1
where
  ConfigTable = @ConfigTable and ColumnName in ('ConfigTable','ActionName')
```

One example to insert a new column that is not in the table but only a derived column in the application. Best practices are to use ColumnId from 1000.

```
INSERT INTO [config].[PortalFieldList]
           ([ConfigTable]
           ,[ColumnId]
           ,[SortOrder]
           ,[ListEnabled]
           ,[ColumnName]
           ,[DataType]
           ,[DataSize]
           ,[Precision]
           ,[Scale]
           ,[IsNullable]
           ,[FriendlyName]
           ,[IsPrimaryKey]
           ,[IsInsertField]
           ,[IsModifyField]
           ,[IsLookupField]
           ,[LookupInputType]
           ,[LookupRelatedColumn]
           ,[IsHidden]
           ,[IsRequired]
           ,[IsUserstamp]
           ,[IsTimestamp]
           ,[HelpText]
           ,[NULL2Value]
           ,[IsCellEdit]
           ,[CellEditConfigTable]
           ,[IsProtectedOnInsert]
           ,[IsProtectedOnModify]
                                ,[IsDataRightsFilterEnabled]
                                ,[IsExportField])
SELECT
            @ConfigTable as [ConfigTable]
           ,1000 as [ColumnId]
           ,1000 as [SortOrder]
           ,1 as [ListEnabled]
           ,'ColumnName' as [ColumnName]
           ,'nvarchar' as [DataType]
           ,50 as [DataSize]
           ,0 as [Precision]
           ,0 as [Scale]
           ,'Yes' as [IsNullable]
           ,'ColumnName' as [FriendlyName]
           ,0 as [IsPrimaryKey]
           ,1 AS [IsInsertField]
           ,1 AS [IsModifyField]
           ,0 AS [IsLookupField]
           ,0 AS [LookupInputType]
           ,'' AS [LookupRelatedColumn]
           ,0 AS [IsHidden]
           ,0 AS [IsRequired]
           ,0 AS [IsUserstamp]
           ,0 AS [IsTimestamp]
           ,'' AS [HelpText]
           ,'' AS [NULL2Value]
           ,0 AS [IsCellEdit]
           ,'' AS [CellEditConfigTable]
           ,0 AS [IsProtectedOnInsert]
           ,0 AS [IsProtectedOnModify]
                                ,0 as [IsDataRightsFilterEnabled]
                                ,0 as [IsExportField]

```

path: /Technology & Software/7. Admin Portal/7.1 Dev guide/7.1.3 Database development/Templates/Optional
content:
All optional templates can be found in the folder.

`include\reuse_config\sql\00_CFG\Template\Optional`

[[_TOC_]]

#config.ConfigTable_UpdateActionList.StoredProcedure

This stored procedure is used for customizing properties of actions such as placement, order, and icon-name. It can also be used to delete standard action that do not make sense on a specific table. The stored procedure is only called during deployment or when the stored procedure 'config.PortalRefreshMeatadata' is called.

```
UPDATE config.PortalActionList
  set IconName = 'fa-undo', ConfirmMsg = 'Undo publish?', FriendlyName = 'Undo Publish',SortOrder = 31,Placement = 1
WHERE
  ConfigTable = @ConfigTable  and ActionName = 'PublishUndo'

UPDATE config.PortalActionList
  set SortOrder = 100, IconName = 'fa-comment',Placement = 1
WHERE
  ConfigTable = @ConfigTable  and ActionName = 'ChangeComment'

delete from config.PortalActionList WHERE ConfigTable = @ConfigTable  and ActionName = 'CreateCopy';
```

**Important**
The icon names that can be used can be found here [Find Icons with the Perfect Look & Feel | Font Awesome](https://fontawesome.com/search?m=free&o=r)

#config.ConfigTable_GetRecordlist.StoredProcedure

By default the platform can handle to select data from a table with the stored procedure 'config.PortalGeneral_GetRecordList' but it is possible to overwrite this by using this template for a more specific select of data.

This is often actual in scenarios like:
- Custom columns that must be computed
- Adding colors on lines or cells
- Managing link table where a filter on the table must be set based on the calling table

**Remark**

The column 'DW_ArchiveID' must always be included and returned to the portal because that column is the internal primary-key and record-id and the portal will nok work properly without that information.

#config.ConfigTable_GetRecordListView.View

This template will often be used in combination with the stored procedure above 'config.ConfigTable_GetRecordlist.StoredProcedure' because instead of building an advanced select statement inside the stored procedure in an embedded SQL variable it is easier to use and change if this select statement is created in a view and then called from the stored procedure.

It can though be used without the 'config.ConfigTable_GetRecordlist.StoredProcedure' and if the view exists the standard stored procedure 'config.PortalGeneral_GetRecordlist' will call and use that view. Otherwise, it will select from the table.

**Remark**

The column 'DW_ArchiveID' must always be included and returned to the portal because that column is the internal primary-key and record-id and the portal will nok work properly without that information.


#config.ConfigTable_GetValueList.StoredProcedure

This template must be used when we work with lookup-columns. In earlier version we used a stored procedure per column. That will still work backwards but it is recommend using this template going forward.

It means that this manages all lookup columns in one and therefore the stored procedure has 'ColumnName' as a parameter. The implementation of lookup can differ a lot but it will always ends with creating and returning data in the table 'config.PortalLookupFieldValueTemp' and from there the standard functionality takes over.

For each column that need a lookup a section like this ex below is created and the generation of 'ValueKey' and 'ValueString' is written inside a CTE section like in this example.

```
IF @ColumnName = 'xyz'
BEGIN
                             set @ColumnHasLookup = 1;

                             With LookupDS(ValueKey,ValueString) AS
                             (
                               -- Change here
                               SELECT '0','value0'
                               UNION
                               SELECT '1','value1' 
                               UNION
                               SELECT '2','value2' 

                               -- Change here
                             )

                             INSERT INTO [config].[PortalLookupFieldValueTemp]
                                                                                          ([ID]
                                                                                          ,[ValueKey]
                                                                                          ,[ValueString]
                                                                                          ,[IsEnum])

                             SELECT
                               @id,
                               DS.ValueKey,
                               DS.ValueString,
                               0 -- 1 = Enum, 0 = TableData
                             FROM LookupDS DS

                             -- CHANGE ORDER HERE
                             ORDER BY DS.ValueKey
                             -- CHANGE ORDER HERE
END;
```

Another example where the generation of values is more advanced and comes from another table:

```
With LookupDS(ValueKey,ValueString) AS
(
  -- Change here
    select 
     '' as ValueKey
                             ,'' as ValueString
  from config.Codelist
  union
  select 
     cast(upper([ID]) as nvarchar(50)) as ValueKey
                             ,[Name] + ' (' + cast(ValidFrom as nvarchar(20)) + ', v' + cast([Version] as nvarchar(10)) + ')' as ValueString
  from config.Codelist

  -- Change here
)
```

**@ColumnHasLookup**
This parameter is returned to the flow and it is important to notice the use of that because when the portal metadata is refreshed during deployment or when running the stored procedure 'config.PortalRefreshMetadata' the platform regenerates lookupvalues on every column. So, it calls this stored procedure for each column even if the property 'IsLookupField' is '0' and if it gets a '1' in return it will set the property 'IsLookupField' = '1' in the 'PortalFieldList'. That means it is only necessary to write a section in this stored procedure to create a lookupfield and the platform will set the property 'IsLookupField' automatically.

**SortOrder**
By default, the returned lookup values are sorted by 'ValueString' but that sort order can and will often also be changed here in the last line of the template.

In this example it is sorted by 'ValueKey' that is represented as an 'INT' value but since the 'ValueKey' is a string it has be casted before sorting to get the correct order.

```
INSERT INTO [config].[PortalLookupFieldValueTemp]
           ([ID]
                                ,[ValueKey]
           ,[ValueString])

SELECT
  @id,
  DS.ValueKey,
  DS.ValueString
FROM LookupDS DS

-- CHANGE ORDER HERE
ORDER BY CAST(DS.ValueKey as INT) ASC
-- CHANGE ORDER HERE
```

**Performance**
To gain performance when creating a lookuplist it is important to know if the list can change or if it is static until the next version. If the list is static it is recommended to activate the statement below that is commented out in the template, so that lookup values are not created every time.

```
IF exists(select top 1 * from config.PortalLookupFieldValue where ConfigTable = @ConfigTable and ColumnName = @Columnname)
  return;
```

**Multi language translation**
Translations can be implemented in different ways. It always depends. Sometimes the translated value is part of the data that is selected and in that case the variable @Language can be used in the CTE section to retrieve translated data.

Another scenario is to use the 'PortalTranslation' module and to translate lookup values into different languages. That is a standard functionality, and the platform will always try to search for translations on lookup 'ValueKeys'.

Translation can be a huge effort to do and maintain and to get track of which columns must be translated and "normally" best-practice is - as a minimum - to translate static Enum lookup values and therefore there is a column 'IsEnum' (0,1) where the developer can tell the translator that this is a Enum value that has to be translated.

```
INSERT INTO [config].[PortalLookupFieldValueTemp]
                                                                                          ([ID]
                                                                                          ,[ValueKey]
                                                                                          ,[ValueString]
                                                                                          ,[IsEnum])

                             SELECT
                               @id,
                               DS.ValueKey,
                               DS.ValueString,
                               1 -- 1 = Enum, 0 = TableData
                             FROM LookupDS DS

                             -- CHANGE ORDER HERE
                             ORDER BY DS.ValueKey
                             -- CHANGE ORDER HERE
```

That means the translator can create a select statement that can help to get the overview and to insert missing translations into the table 'PortalTranslation'.
```
select * from config.PortalLookupFieldValue where  IsEnum = 1
```

#config.ConfigTable_GetRelationList_PrimaryColumn_RelatedColumn.StoredProcedure

The relation between columns is a feature that is often used in an application. It can be a scenario where the outcome of one lookup column is depending on the value or values chosen in another column. That is called a "parent-child" relation. That relation can involve more columns than just two because more than one column (child) can be related to the same parent, and it can also be a chain where "Column C" is related to "Column B" that is related to "Column A".

Most of the scenarios all columns involved in the relations are lookup columns but it can also be a non-lookup column typically the "parent" that can be hidden or non-editable, but it will work like a filter on the "child" valuelist.

The first thing is to define the relation between columns. That is done by update code in the stored procedure "UpdateFieldlist" prefixed with the name of the table. It will be stored as a property in the fieldlist ([PortalFieldlist](/AdminPortal/Documentation-for-Developers/PortalFieldList) in the column 'LookupRelatedColumn'. Remark that this is defined on the "parent" column and can be a comma-separated list of "children" columns related to that "parent".

Now the UI can see that a relation is defined between "ParentColumn" and "ChildColumn" and will now expect a stored procedure to exist that returns relation data between these two columns.

These relation data come in different ways - it can be more or less hard-coded for example in a case where it is a relation between enum-columns, or it can be data from one or more tables or a combination. The stored procedure must always return two columns "PrimaryValueKey" and "RelationValueKey" and always CAST these values into NVARCHAR and be aware of upper/lower case. Always return the relation data with same upper/lowercase than the data to which it is related.

Here is an example where "ColumnB" is related to "ColumnA"

Stored procedure "config.<ConfigTable>.UpdateFieldList"
```
UPDATE config.PortalFieldList
  set LookupRelatedColumn = 'ColumnB'
WHERE
  ConfigTable = @ConfigTable  and ColumnName  IN ('ColumnA')
```

Create a stored procedure named "<Configtable>.GetRelationList_ColumnA_ColumnB"
```
ALTER OR CREATE PROCEDURE [config].[<ConfigTable>_GetRelationList_ColumnA_ColumnB] 
as

DECLARE @Language nvarchar(20) = (SELECT [config].[PortalGetLanguage]());
DECLARE @Username nvarchar(50) = (SELECT [config].[PortalGetUsername]());

    select
                             '' as PrimaryValueKey
                             ,'' as RelationValueKey

```
This select can be built in many ways but must return the possible combinations. If it is ok to choose a 'blank' value that combination should also be returned by the stored procedure.

#config.ConfigTable_OnInit.StoredProcedure

The OnInit stored procedure has the purpose to initiate values when the user hit the ![image.png](/.attachments/image-5c654d83-d77d-4cd5-ac67-19a2507fe380.png) or the ![image.png](/.attachments/image-34aa31f3-7525-4dd7-a7e9-5f5b10a74b3d.png) button. It gives the developer a trigger to put values into the record before it is shown in the UI and it can be different scenarios where this feature is useful:
- To set standard values hardcoded or stored in a setup table to help the user in creating new records faster.
- To manage the "CreateCopy" or to change the behavior of that.
- To set primary key values in situations where the table is a link table (child table) called from a parent table.

It is important to notice that the stored procedure should in some tables be able to handle all 3 scenarios and therefore it will be a good idea to check whether the OnInit is called from the "Create" button or the "CreateCopy" button by for example checking if some of the primary-key columns already has a value in @Values. If that is the case the OnInit is called from a "CreateCopy" and with that knowledge the logic that set standard values should not always be executed on every column. It always depends.

The third scenario where the table is a linked table (child table) the OnInit must manage this and set values on related columns between the linked table (child) and the calling table (parent).

Here is an example:
```
-- Get the parent ArchiveID (RecordID)
declare @LinktableParentArchiveID as bigint = (select config.PortalGetSessionFilter(@Username,@ConfigTable));

-- Get the value of the related column between parent and child table
declare @CodelistID as nvarchar(250) = (select cast([ID] as nvarchar(50)) from config.Codelist where DW_ArchiveID = @LinktableParentArchiveID);

-- Set that value on the new record
SET @Values = (Select [config].[PortalSetValue]('CodelistID',@CodelistID,@Columns,@Values));

```

#config.ConfigTable_OnValidate.StoredProcedure

This stored procedure is where to write business logic that can validate and stop the flow of inserting or modifying data and return a proper message to the user.

Check the [Flowchart](/AdminPortal/Documentation-for-Developers/Flows) to see where it is called. The OnVaidate is called on every column and collect an error message and then continue to the next column so it can show all error at one time, but the transaction will not finish on an error. The OnValidate will only be called if something has changed.

The parameters to work with are "ColumName", "OldValues" and "NewValues".

Remark - it is of course possible in a validation to use values from other columns than the one that is validated, but always get the values from the string '@NewValues' and not from '@OldValues' or by selecting values from the database because that will always be old values.

"OldValues" is useful to check against "NewValues" to see if the column has changed and it is not allowed to change the column from one specific value to another.

It is important to give the user a well-formed message that the user can understand with lot of information and to consider use of multi-language functionality and object names etc.

Here is an example of creating return messages:

```
IF isnull(@RangeFrom,'') <> '' and isnull(@ListOfValues,'') <> ''
begin
  if @Language = 'da-DK'
    set @ReturnMsg = quotename((select [config].[PortalGetTableFieldTranslation](@Language,'RangeFrom',@ConfigTable))) +
                  ' kan ikke bruges sammen med ' + quotename((select [config].[PortalGetTableFieldTranslation](@Language,'ListOfValues',@ConfigTable)))
  else
    set @ReturnMsg = quotename((select [config].[PortalGetTableFieldTranslation](@Language,'RangeFrom',@ConfigTable))) +
                                                                             ' cant´t be used together with ' + quotename((select [config].[PortalGetTableFieldTranslation](@Language,'ListOfValues',@ConfigTable)))
end;
```
This example can be improved by using the PortalTranslation module and create a message tag for each language that is used.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-89158607-087d-4756-93a5-fa884065b1a2.png)

Now the message tag is "ConfigTable_OnValidate_Example". That tag is free text, but best-practice is to name is so that it will be easy to figure out where it is used in the code.

Now the same code that generate error message can be changed to this. Check out the function "PortalGetMessage" on further information.

```
set @ReturnMsg = (select config.PortalGetMessageTranslation(@Language,'ConfigTable_OnValidate_Example',
                   quotename((select [config].[PortalGetTableFieldTranslation](@Language,'RangeFrom',@ConfigTable))) + '#¤#' +
                                                             quotename((select [config].[PortalGetTableFieldTranslation](@Language,'ListOfValues',@ConfigTable)))
                     ))

```

#config.ConfigTable_OnBeforeInsert.StoredProcedure

OnBeforeInsert is called just before the new record is inserted. This is the last chance to change data that will be inserted or to validate something and then return an error message that will stop the hole transaction.

Here is an example where some data is washed before inserting and it also check if data already exists and that is an example where the primary key definition is not enough to check for duplicated records.

```
ALTER PROCEDURE [config].[CodelistHierarchy_OnBeforeInsert]
      (-- Standard system variables
                               @Columns nvarchar(max),
                               @Values nvarchar(max) OUTPUT,                

                               -- ReturnMsg
                               @ReturnMsg nvarchar(max) OUTPUT) 
AS

DECLARE @Language nvarchar(20) = (SELECT [config].[PortalGetLanguage]());
DECLARE @Username nvarchar(50) = (SELECT [config].[PortalGetUsername]());

declare @ConfigTable as nvarchar(250) = (select Item from dbo.SplitString((SELECT OBJECT_NAME(@@PROCID)),'_') where Num = 1);

set @ReturnMsg = '';

BEGIN TRY
                             set @Values = (select config.PortalRemoveChar1013('Name',@Columns,@Values));
                             set @Values = (select config.PortalRemoveChar1013('Description',@Columns,@Values));
                             set @Values = (select config.PortalRemoveChar1013('Description UK',@Columns,@Values));

                             declare @CodelistID as uniqueidentifier = cast((select config.PortalGetValue(@Columns,@Values,'CodelistID')) as uniqueidentifier);
                             declare @Name as nvarchar(max) = cast((select config.PortalGetValue(@Columns,@Values,'Name')) as nvarchar(max));

                             if exists(select * from config.CodelistHierarchy where CodelistID = @CodelistID and Name = @Name)
                             begin
                               if @Language = 'da-DK'
                                 set @ReturnMsg = quotename((select [config].[PortalGetTableTranslation](@Language,@ConfigTable))) + ' = ''' + @Name + ''' findes allerede.'
      else
                                 set @ReturnMsg = quotename((select [config].[PortalGetTableTranslation](@Language,@ConfigTable))) + ' = ''' + @Name + ''' already exists.';

                               return 1;
                             end;

END TRY
BEGIN CATCH
  SET @ReturnMsg = ERROR_MESSAGE();
  RETURN 1;
END CATCH

RETURN 0;

```
#config.ConfigTable_OnInsert.StoredProcedure

The 'OnInsert' is not recommended to use and is only still possible for backwards compatibility for solutions that were built before triggers like 'OnBeforeInsert' and 'OnAfterInsert' and the standard 'OnInsert' where implemented. These new triggers together with the generic 'PortalGeneral_OnInsert' will be able to fulfill all needs related to insert of data and standard logging is also handeled.

Remark - if this trigger is used changelog must be implemented and be aware that 'OnBeforeInsert' and 'OnAfterInsert' will be executed if they exist even if the 'OnInsert' trigger is used.

#config.ConfigTable_OnAfterInsert.StoredProcedure

'OnAfterInsert' is useful the run some code after the record is inserted and before the transaction is committed. That could ex be insert of related data in other tables or update of a status in a parent table etc.

Remark - the parameters are @Columns and @Values and @RecordID and @RecordID is the same as 'DW_ArchiveID' that this record will be stored with when the transaction commit, but the 'DW_ArchiveID' is not at this point persistent in @Values - so therefor use the @RecordID.

#config.ConfigTable_OnBeforeModify.StoredProcedure

The stored procedure is called just before the record is updated into the database table and it is still time to update/change some of the columns by setting new values into @NewValues and even wash and validate data and if necessary, return an error in @ReturnMsg that will roll back the hole transaction.

#config.ConfigTable_OnModify.StoredProcedure

Just as the 'OnInsert' trigger it is not recommended to use this trigger anymore. Instead use the 'OnBeforeModify' and 'OnAfterModify' and then let the platform take care of modifying the data and do the change logging and checking for user rights etc.

#config.ConfigTable_OnAfterModify.StoredProcedure

The trigger is called just after the record is modified but before the transaction is committed. So, the updated data is in the table and this trigger can be used to make updates in related tables such as status columns in parent tables etc.

Remark - it is NOT possible the change data in @NewValues and therefore updated to the current record must be done in 'OnBeforeModify'. If it is done here, just by executing a standard T-SQL 'UPDATE' it will not be reflected in the changelog.

#config.ConfigTable_OnBeforeDelete.StoredProcedure

This trigger is useful for cascading delete where other records are related to the record that is just to be deleted. To avoid and foreign-key-relation error related records must be deleted in this section just as the example below.
```
DECLARE @CodelistID as uniqueidentifier = cast((select config.PortalGetValue(@Columns,@Values,'CodelistID')) as uniqueidentifier);

delete from config.CodelistHierarchyLine where CodelistHierarchyID in (select ID from config.CodelistHierarchy where CodelistID = @CodelistID);
delete from config.CodelistHierarchy where CodelistID = @CodelistID;
delete from config.CodelistValue where CodelistID = @CodelistID;
delete from config.CodelistValueValidation where CodelistID = @CodelistID;
delete from config.CodelistComment where ParentID = @CodelistID;
```

Remark - consider to do the delete by calling the 'PortalGeneral_CascadeDelete' function described in the section [Portal Dev tools](/AdminPortal/Documentation-for-Developers/Portal-Dev%2Dtools)

#config.ConfigTable_OnDelete.StoredProcedure

This trigger is not recommended to use anymore and is only for backwards compatibility. It will - if it exists - overrule the standard 'OnDelete' functionality including logging.

Since the platform has gotten implemented both the 'OnBeforeDelete' and the 'OnAfterDelete' trigger it will often be better to let the platform handle the delete of the record.

#config.ConfigTable_OnAfterDelete.StoredProcedure

The trigger is called after the record is delete and before the transaction is committed so it is still possible to perform a rollback. Otherwise, this trigger can be used for cleaning up or change of status in related tables.

#config.ConfigTable_OnConfirmation.StoredProcedure

The 'OnConfirmation' trigger is only used in the UI and is called when the user pushes an action. That can be a single-record action or a multi-action.

The trigger sends the name of the action with columns and both old and new values and that can be used for any kind of confirmation to send back and then let the user choose to continue or abort.

Actionname can be build-in-action buttons like 'Create', 'Delete', 'Save' and 'Cancel' and the table specific actions as well.

So, when the user hit the button, the stored procedure is called and can return a 'ConfirmMsg' and a 'ConfirmMsgType'. The 'ConfirmMsg' is the message or question that will be shown in the dialog box and the 'ConfirmMsgType' if the type of dialog box.

|ConfirmMsgType|Buttons  |Actions  |
|--|--|--|
| 1 |OK  | The UI will cancel afterwards |
| 2 |OK/Cancel  | The UI will cancel when the user hit 'Cancel' |
| 3 |Ignore/Cancel  | The UI will cancel when the user hit 'Cancel' |
| 4 |Yes/No  | The UI will cancel when the user hit 'No' |
| 5 |Cancel  | Tre UI will cancel afterwards  |

```
if @ActionName = 'MyAction'
begin
  set @ConfirmMsg = 'Ask for some confirmation?';
  set @ConfirmMsgType = 3; -- Ignore/Cancel
  return 0;
end;

--or--

if @ActionName = 'Save'
begin
  set @ConfirmMsg = 'Are you sure that you want to save?';
  set @ConfirmMsgType = 4; -- Yes/No
  return 0;
end;

```

#config.ConfigTable_OnBeforeImport.StoredProcedure

This trigger is useful when importing data into a table either with a script that is generated from the 'ExportToScript' module or when importing data that has been pasted from Excel.

In some situations, it is necessary to check the data and skip the record or to do some data washing or even add more information to the data stream before it is inserted or updated. All of that is possible within this trigger.

@Columns and @Values - Does only include those columns that are in the import data so maybe something is missing and need to be added before the data can be inserted properly.

An example of that here where a key-column is added.
```

IF REPLACE(@Columns,'CodelistName','') = @Columns -- It does´t exists
 SET @Columns = @Columns + '#¤#CodelistName'

SET @Values = (SELECT config.PortalSetValue('CodelistName',(select top 1 [Name] from config.Codelist where ID = @CodelistID),@Columns,@Values));

```

@SkipRecord is a way to skip a single record and then continue with importing without getting an error.
```
SET @CodelistID = cast((select [config].[PortalGetValue](@Columns,@Values,'CodelistID')) as uniqueidentifier);
if not exists(select top 1 * from config.Codelist where ID = @CodelistID)
  set @SkipRecord = 1;
```
**Important**

It is important to notice that this trigger is NOT called when importing JSON data even if that data is scripted from the 'ExportToScript' module and that is because the JSON format was originally designed for API integration and not import of data. Since that has changed over time and the JSON now also can be used as data scripting it will be changed in the future that this trigger somehow should be called with JSON import as well.

#config.ConfigTable_OnChangelog.StoredProcedure

This trigger is a rare feature to use but it has the purpose to combine changelogs from several tables / records in one changelog view. When the user open the 'Changelog' on a record it will by default show all logs from that table with that current 'DW_ArchiveID' (RecordID), but let’s says we have one or more related tables like a 'parent-child' design and it will be user friendly to show change-logs from that 'child' table in the same window as the 'parent' or the other way around when opening the changelog on the 'child' table to show changes from the 'parent' table as well.

The stored procedure receive a @RecordID from the current record and can then return two parameters @AssociatedConfigTable and @AssociatedRecordId and that is the name of the 'child' table and the 'RecordID' related to that like in this example:

```
set @AssociatedConfigTable = 'ConfigDetailTable_1_Name'; -- the name of the table
set @AssociatedRecordId = '17'; -- The record id of the record.
```

Or it can even be more tables like in this example just by separating with #¤#.
```
set @AssociatedConfigTable = 'ConfigDetailTable_1_Name#¤#ConfigDetailTable_2_Name'; -- the name of the tables
set @AssociatedRecordId = '17#¤#42'; -- The record id of the records.
```

#config.ConfigTable_OnLoadActionForm.StoredProcedure

See [Build an ActionForm](/AdminPortal/Documentation-for-Developers/How%2Dto/Build-an-ActionForm)

#config.ConfigTable_OnLoadCellData.StoredProcedure

See [Implement Cell edit](/AdminPortal/Documentation-for-Developers/How%2Dto/Implement-Cell%2Dedit)

#config.ConfigTable_Action_NameOfAction.StoredProcedure

The template can be used on both a single-record action or a multi-action and if it is a single-record the @Columns and @Values will be information about the record that can be used for validation, lookup etc. If this is a multi-action @Columns and @Values will look different.

| Columns |Values  |
|--|--|
| DW_ArchiveID |Comma separated list of recordid  |
| NoOfRows | Number of total rows  |
| NoOfSelectedRows | Number if selected rows. Will the same count from the list in 'DW_ArchiveID' |

To start with rename '#ConfigTablename#' with the name of the table and replace 'NameOfAction' with the system name for the action. After refresh metadata the action will be added and then use the [Optional](/AdminPortal/Documentation-for-Developers/Templates/Optional) 'config.UpdateActionList' to put information as icon name and placement on the action.

As default the template is implemented with changelog functionality so it will be logged when the user run this action. If this logging is not wanted just to remove these three sections of code:

```
-- Standard code
IF @DW_ArchiveID > 0
BEGIN
  DECLARE @Project as nvarchar(50);
  DECLARE @TaskName as nvarchar(50);
  SET @Project = (select config.PortalGetProjectname());
  SET @TaskName = (SELECT OBJECT_NAME(@@PROCID)) + '_' + cast(@DW_ArchiveID as nvarchar(10));

  -- Log start
  EXEC [config].[PortalChangeLog_Start]
                                                                                                                    @Project = @Project,                                         
                                                                                                                    @TaskName = @TaskName,
                                                                                                                    @Username = @Username,
                                                                                                                    @Columns = N'',
                                                                                                                    @NewValues = N'',
                                                                                                                    @OldValues = N'',
                                                                                                                    @Audit_ID = @DW_Audit OUTPUT
  -- Log start
END;

-- and --

-- Log end OK
IF @DW_ArchiveID > 0 EXEC [config].[PortalChangeLog_Ok] @Audit_ID = @DW_Audit,@Changes = 0;
-- Log end OK 

-- and --

-- Log end Error
  IF @DW_Audit > 0 AND @DW_ArchiveID > 0
    EXEC [config].[PortalChangeLog_Error] @RecordID = @DW_ArchiveID, @Audit_ID = @DW_Audit,@Message = @ReturnMsg;
  -- Log end Error 

```

Logging is often useful when the action is running code like updating data, but an action can also be a call to a link table or opening an ActionForm.

This example shows to have an action that will open a linked table.

```
ALTER PROCEDURE [config].[Codelist_Action_Hierarchies]
     (-- Standard system variables
                               @Columns nvarchar(max),
                               @Values nvarchar(max),

                              -- ReturnMsg
                               @ReturnMsg nvarchar(max) OUTPUT)
AS

DECLARE @DW_Audit as int = -1;

DECLARE @Language nvarchar(20) = (SELECT [config].[PortalGetLanguage]());
DECLARE @Username nvarchar(50) = (SELECT [config].[PortalGetUsername]());

declare @ConfigTable as nvarchar(250) = (select Item from dbo.SplitString((SELECT OBJECT_NAME(@@PROCID)),'_') where Num = 1);

SET @ReturnMsg = '';

BEGIN TRY   
                             DECLARE @DW_ArchiveID as bigint = cast((select config.PortalGetValue(@Columns,@Values,'DW_ArchiveID')) as bigint)
                             set @ReturnMsg = '#Linktable#CodelistHierarchy';   
                             RETURN 0;
END TRY
BEGIN CATCH
  SET @ReturnMsg = ERROR_MESSAGE();
  RETURN 1;
END CATCH

RETURN 0;
```

In case nothing else as T-SQL should be executed as validations etc. the code can be minimized into this:
```
ALTER PROCEDURE [config].[Codelist_Action_Hierarchies]
     (-- Standard system variables
                               @Columns nvarchar(max),
                               @Values nvarchar(max),

                              -- ReturnMsg
                               @ReturnMsg nvarchar(max) OUTPUT)
AS

set @ReturnMsg = '#Linktable#CodelistHierarchy';
RETURN 0;
```

An action can also be an 'ActionForm' and that is similar to the 'LinkTable' and should just be like this:
```
ALTER PROCEDURE [config].[Codelist_Action_Hierarchies]
     (-- Standard system variables
                               @Columns nvarchar(max),
                               @Values nvarchar(max),

                              -- ReturnMsg
                               @ReturnMsg nvarchar(max) OUTPUT)
AS

set @ReturnMsg = '#ActionForm#';
RETURN 0;
```

#config.ConfigTable_Action_NameOfActionWithTransaction.StoredProcedure

This stored procedure template can be used when the action is only T-SQL code, and it must run in a transaction that can be rolled back in case of an error. The default entry point 'PortalGeneral_RunAction' does not start a new transaction because it can be - as described above - used for different kind of actions that for example starts a new dialog or it can call one of the standard procedures for 'Insert', 'Modify' and 'Delete' and these stored procedures will handle transactions.

That is why this template is used to ensure that the transaction can roll back. Just as the normal transaction the template is implemented with standard logging but that can be removed if it is not needed.

#config.ConfigTable_Action_GenericImportData.StoredProcedure

See [Enable Generic Import on a table](/AdminPortal/Documentation-for-Developers/How%2Dto/Enable-Generic-Import-on-a-table)

#config.ConfigTable_Action_GenericMultiDelete.StoredProcedure

See [Enable MultiDelete action on a table](/AdminPortal/Documentation-for-Developers/How%2Dto/Enable-Generic-Import-on-a-table)

[[_TOC_]]


In this series of wiki articles I will try to describe the UI development process alongside how to make use of the build pipelines and finally deployment and configuration.

# Introduction
So first of, the Administration Portal should be considered an SQL Database GUI. The frontend serves as an empty shell, where the actual business logic is developed in the database. It consists of an Angular Frontend, C# Middle Layer and SQL Backend. In this series I will focus solely on the frontend (Angular) & middle layer (C#) as this should be the primary responsibility of an application developer, where as an sql developer will take care of the database development.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-5e11b9d7-5604-4026-bd2a-139010678216.png)

_Above visual representation is stolen from [here](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10141/7.7.1-Overview)._

# Good Practices
* Use the DevOps tools to keep track of assignments. Like create User Stories with tasks or bugs so you have something to register time on and use for PR's. 

* Always use branching when developing. Currently the main branches are Develop & Production. Whenever I develop I like to create a new branch (from the develop branch) called something like: us/12312(id) or bug/2312(id) so I know which task / bug is associated with the branch.

* Always use PR's, even though you might be the only developer on the project it is always good practice to use PR's before merging stuff into the main branches (Develop & Production).

* Readability over everything else. You might not be the only one that have to look into the code, so focus on readability and maybe even write a short comment if its complex like so:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-25865f29-1315-4bcd-86d1-df349afe095c.png)

# Running the Application locally
* For running the application locally for dev purposes find more information [here](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10180/Running-the-application-locally).

# Frontend (Angular) & Middle layer (C#) development
* The UI of the Admin Portal is based on the WebApp Sample from the DIMA Platform team. It's a web application consisting of a C# api and an Angular frontend. For more information on how to work with the code check out these articles: [Frontend Development (Angular)](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10177/Frontend-Development-(Angular)) or [Middle Layer Development (CSharp)](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10179/Middle-Layer-Development-(CSharp))

# Internal dev environment
* For testing changes internally between the developer and LHN we have established a DEV environment for LHN to be able to test UI changes. Find more information [here](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10178/Internal-DEV-Environment).

# Build pipelines
* For build pipelines we use the azure pipelines, more information can be found [here](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10173/Build-Pipelines).

# Configuration
* To learn more about the configuration needed for the Administration Portal to run, please read [here](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10174/Configuration).

# Deployment of Portal UI
* As previously stated we have two build pipelines which enables for Portal UI deployment via either [docker / Kubernetes](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10176/Deployment-of-Portal-UI-to-Kubernetes) or old-school [IIS](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10175/Deployment-of-Portal-UI-to-IIS).

[[_TOSP_]]

[[_TOC_]]


# Intro
The Administration portal project has one build pipeline which runs automatically every time code is pushed to either the development and / or the production branch. Below is a short introduction:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-91bf3eed-ab75-424d-b8f4-f8ad3825db7c.png)

# AdminPortal.ZIP.Release
The ZIP release pipeline packs the Admin Portal application into a zip file which can then be downloaded as an artifact and deployed on a server with IIS. Note that the zip file does not contain the appsettings.json file which is needed for configuration, so it does not accidently gets overwritten.

**To download the latest zip file from the pipeline navigate to:**
Pipelines => AdminPortal.ZIP.Release => Latest Successfull Run => Published:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-f1bd98c1-6194-48f6-9092-f42ba05c6df5.png)

Click the three dots on the right and just select download:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-7be34383-7250-4fdf-9420-84f6b16968a9.png)

This zip file contains everything needed to either upgrade to a newer version of the new Admin Portal or deploy a new one (excluding the configuration file).

[[_TOC_]]


# Introduction
In this article I will briefly explain the configuration needed to run the Administration Portal. Configuration can be done either through environment variables or in an appsettings.json file, where the first is usually used in a Docker / Kubernetes setup and the latter when hosting on a windows server through ex. IIS. As the Admin Portal is based on the WebApp sample project from DIMA, it has loads of configuration parameters, I will however only list the ones required to run the Admin Portal here. But first, an example of an AppSettings.json

# AppSettings.json example:

```
{
  "GeneralSettings": {
    "ProductName": "adminportal",
    "APIVersion": "",
    "EnableStaticFiles": true,
    "EnableAuditLogging": true,
  },
  "WebPageSettings": {
    "WebPageTitle": "DIMA Sample Web Application",
    "IdleIntervalCheckInSeconds": 10,
    "IdleMaxTimeBeforeLogOutInSeconds": 1800
  },
  "DatabaseSettings": {
    "StandardCommandTimeout": 30,
    "ConnectionStrings": {
      "source": "CONNECTION STRING"
    },
    "CustomCommandTimeouts": {
      "action_commandtimeout_portalexporttoscript_createimportscript": 10
    }
  },
  "LoggerSettings": {  
     "ApplicationID": "",
     "AuditSettings": [],
     "ActivitySettings": [],
     "MetricSettings": []
  },
  "SecuritySettings": {
    SEEE BELOW!
  }
}
```

# Environemnt Variables Example
* This is how it would look like in a kubernetes helm chart. Please note that this is the absolute minimum ish, and no logging is configured.
```
 GeneralSettings__ProductName: "adminportal"
 WebPageSettings__WebPageTitle: "Admin Portal DEV"
 "SecuritySettings__AuthenticationMode": "OpenIdConnect"
 "SecuritySettings__OpenIdConnectSettings__ClientId": "f26de9f3-b8b0-4d21..."
 "SecuritySettings__OpenIdConnectSettings__Scope": "openid urn:DIMA-admin-portal-api.dev/user_impersonation"
 "SecuritySettings__OpenIdConnectSettings__ValidAudiences": "urn:DIMA-admin-portal-api.dev"
 "SecuritySettings__OpenIdConnectSettings__MetadataAdress": "https://identity.kmd.dk/adfs/.well-known/openid-configuration"
 "SecuritySettings__OpenIdConnectSettings__ValidIssuer": "https://identity.kmd.dk/adfs/services/trust"

 DatabaseSettings__CustomCommandTimeouts__action_commandtimeout_portalexporttoscript_createimportscript: "3600"
 DatabaseSettings__CustomCommandTimeouts__action_commandtimeout_portalexportimport_importdata: "3600"

 KeyVaultSecrets:
 - env_name: DatabaseSettings__ConnectionStrings__source
 secret_name: KMDBISITECON
```

# General Settings
* Should be quite self explanatory
* EnableStaticFiles & EnableAuditLogging are required for the app to run

# Web Page Settings
* Should be quite self explanatory

# Database Settings
* _"Standard Command Timeout"_ - Is used to set the time in seconds before database calls times out
* _"Connection strings"_ - Though this is an array, it should only contain one single connectionstring named "source" which points to a database containing the Admin Portal Modules. If you need one, ask Lars Høj (LHN) for more info on this.
* _"Custom Command Timeouts"_ - This is used for setting a custom command timeout on single "Actions" that are expected to take longer than normal, without setting a global command timeout. Ask Lars Høj (LHN) for more info on this.

# Logger Settings
* The Admin portal makes use of the DIMA Logger on which configuration info can be found [here](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.KIP/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.KIP.wiki/703/KMD.DIMA.Logger). Ex.

```
"LoggerSettings": {
  "ApplicationID": "KMD.DIMA.KIP.WebApp.AdminPortal",
  "AuditSettings": [],
  "ActivitySettings": [
    {
      "Type": "MSSQLServer",
      "Level": "All",
      "MSSQLServerSettings": {
        "ConnectionString": "CONNECTION STRING",
        "Schema": "app_log",
        "TableName": "logActivity"
      }
    }
  ],
  "MetricSettings": []
},
```

# Security Settings
* Security settings controls which type of authorization shoul be used and currently supports either "AD" or "Open Id" 

### AD Auth
* For using AD its as simple as:

```
"SecuritySettings": {
     "AuthenticationMode": "AD"
}
```

_If you're using "AD" as authentication scheme remeber to navigate to IIS manager -> Authentication for the site.
Here you should set "Anonymous Authentication" to "Disabled" and "Windows Authentication" to "Enabled"._

![image.png](/.attachments/image-aea28439-b1c7-4ea5-b0a2-a4913ceb2577.png)

### Open Id Connect
* Open ID requires a bit more. If you've not requested a new application entry in KMD Identity, a guide for this can be found [here](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.KIP/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.KIP.wiki/2389/Ordering-a-new-application-registration).
* After aquiring the required info input it like this:

```
"SecuritySettings": {
    "AuthenticationMode": "OpenIdConnect",
    "OpenIdConnectSettings": {
      "MetadataAdress": "https://identity.kmd.dk/adfs/.well-known/openid-configuration",
      "ValidIssuer": "https://identity.kmd.dk/adfs/services/trust",
      "ValidAudiences": "urn:DIMA-admin-portal-api.dev",
      "ClientId": "f26de9f3-b8b0-...",
      "Scope": "openid urn:DIMA-admin-portal-api.dev/user_impersonation"
    },
}
```

content: [[_TOC_]] # Introduction In this article we'll look into deploying / upgrading the Administration Portal on an IIS server. As we're currently in the process of figuring out whether or not to use automatic tools for this, this will be a manual process for the time being. Please also note that due to me not being able to test this 100% you might encounter a quirk or two, so if you manage to fix these encounters feel free to reach out to me (CKT) so I can update the article. # Upgrading from the "Old" Portal to the "New" If you're upgrading from the old .net framework version of the Portal to the newer .net 6 version, note that this still acts a new deployment. However you should have most of the configuration and prerequisites at hand which should make the process smoother. # Prerequisites First ensure that at the minimum these dependencies are present on the target server. * Access to database with Admin Portal sql backend (ask LHN for this) * Service accounts (kmdbisite db admin & local admin on server that hosts the IIS) * .net 6 hosting bundle installed. Download [here](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet/6.0). (Be sure to pick the hosting bundle and not just the regular runtime) ![image.png](/.attachments/image-7bf7c6bb-bec4-4056-b6be-26338cc7b198.png) * IIS Manager * Certificate for the server (if needed) * Wildcard certificate for the domain # Step 1: Acquire the code and copy it to the server * To acquire a .zip containing the latest working version of the admin portal please refer to the [build pipelines article](https://dev.azure.com/kmddk/CTDataPlatform.OnPremises/_wiki/wikis/AdminPortal/31368/Build-Pipelines?anchor=adminportal.zip.release) and check the section "AdminPortal.ZIP.Release". * Once downloaded, copy the .zip file to the target server. # Step 2: Unpack the zip * Now find a suitable directory to unzip the contents of the .zip file. Usually this will be in the c://inetpub//wwwroot//NAME OF PORTAL FOLDER. # Step 3 A: Configuration app.settings.json (Only for new deployments) * If this is the initial deploy you'll need to create a configuration file called appsettings.json in the above directory like so: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-1faa7a94-3ff7-423c-9cff-03c6cf71c3b3.png) * To find an example of this please check this article: [Configuration](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10174/Configuration). Typically if this is an upgrade from the "Old" Portal to the New Portal you'll have the connection strings at hand already, so just input them in file. Otherwise reach out to the DB owner. * **REMEMBER** that it should not be saved as a txt file but json. Otherwise the file cant be detected, and the application will not inject the appsettings. # Step 3 B: Configuration web.config (Only for new deployments) * If this is the initial deploy you'll need to create a configuration file called web.config in the above directory like so: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-1ea8d560-8f8d-477b-b404-c8bc6c18251e.png) * This should contain the following code: ``` ``` * **REMEMBER** that it should not be saved as a txt file but config. Otherwise the file can't be detected, and the application will not start, as there is no index/default file to read. From here it also gets instructions on which dll to launch. # Step 4: Create site in IIS Manager * Now that the code is ready and configured next task is to create a new site in ISS Manager, so open the application. * Right click "Sites" and click "Add Website" ![image.png](/.attachments/image-d286a19f-40ae-430c-be3d-b769733c05ce.png) * Next fill in the blanks in the window that pops up: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-de7d423b-5fbc-452b-80db-fb47735ee0a5.png) * Give it a descriptive name and set physical path to the directory created in step 2. * In terms of binding you'll of cause need a domain and preferably an SSL certificate for HTTPS. (I'm currently unsure if it works with just HTTP in terms of authentication) # Step 5: Required changes for the app pool * Next navigate to "Application Pools" where a new one should have been created when you created the site in step 4, named what ever name the site got. Right click it and select "Basic settings" and change .NET CLR version to "No Managed Code": ![image.png](/.attachments/image-d5dc3986-ff33-49d0-9188-a6a8cb6b76f5.png) # Step 6: Set service account on the application pool * Navigate to Application Pools and right click the one created earlier * Select "Advanced Settings" * Click the three dots next to "Identity" * Set the service account and click "ok" * ![image.png](/.attachments/image-a6b82443-e2ef-4571-b20f-d347f936ede7.png) * Remember to ensure that the service account has full access to the folder where the application code is placed, ex. "C:\inetpub\wwwroot\AdminPortalV2": ![image.png](/.attachments/image-4f91b738-3eec-4797-a1e6-566bd57e91d8.png) # Step 7: Do an iss reset * Final step is to open a CMD terminal with admin rights and run the command "iisreset" to restart the iis server. * You should now a fully working admin portal running on the domain which you specified in the bindings section. # Issues & fixes ## Getting a 500 Http Error upon launch of the Portal If you're using "AD" as authentication scheme remeber to navigate to IIS manager -> Authentication for the site. Here you should set "Anonymous Authentication" to "Disabled" and "Windows Authentication" to "Enabled". ![image.png](/.attachments/image-aea28439-b1c7-4ea5-b0a2-a4913ceb2577.png) ## Login box loop If you experience the "infinite login box loop" bug, you'll need to disable loopback check: * ”Search windows” * write ”regedit” and open * choose: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa * right click on “Lsa” * choose: “New” → DWORD (32-Bit) value * write "DisableLoopbackCheck" * Right click under data (Value data) and set to 1. ## Windows auth login prompt not required As standard the Portal will ask for credentials whenever one navigate to it in a new browser session. If this is not required for your usecase you can deactivate the behavior like so: * Open iismanager * Click your site * Click "Authentication" * Right click "WindowsAuthentication" and select "Advanced Settings" * Deselect "Enable Kernel-mode authentication" & click "ok" ![image.png](/.attachments/image-082dcd9e-33fa-48f5-8464-88a126cc45c2.png)

content:
[[_TOC_]]


# Introduction
In this article I will explain some of the quirks to be aware of while developing the Angular frontend code on the Admin Portal. I do expect you have some experience working with angular and JavaScript so I won't go into coding details, just more what you need to be aware of. If you haven't read the guide on how to run the app locally please read it first [here](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10180/Running-the-application-locally).

# Package.json
First take a look into the package.json file. Here you'll be able to see the different shortcut commands that you can write "npm run" in front of in the terminal, like "npm run start" etc. The two most important here, besides the build commands, is "UpdateApi" & "UpdateTable".

## UpdateAPI
* Whenever changes to the C# api has been made locally, one needs to run a bat file that creates a new npm package which gets pushed to a registry somewhere. More on this in the api specific article. However the frontend angular code uses this openApi spec to create the services required for interacting with the api which is quite nice. So TL;DR; run this command whenever new changes has been made locally on the C# api for the angular frontend to pickup these changes.

## UpdateTable
* "Unfortunately" the table used is based on another internal product called the Dima Table and because of this, most table related changes is required to be made there. Currently Mads Illemann (LKF) is responsible for this project. If any changes are required reach out to him and once he's done implementing and have run the NPM Build pipeline ask for the version number and just change that in the command: "npm install @dima/table-library@0.1.432 --force" <---

* Please note that since the angular version in the portal is 14 the changes for the Dima Table & NPM build pipeline has to be made and run on the DIMATable-14 branch, remember to tell LKF so he's aware as well.

* Also Please note that it is very important that the version number is hardcoded, else it will download the latest version which includes loads of breaking changes because the Dima Table angular version has since been updated to 16 ish.

# Services
Hopefully you know that in Angular services are an important part of development when interacting with Web Api's. Fortunately one does not need to create a new one or update existing ones when making changes in the api as every time you run the "npm run updateAPI" command, the openAPI stuff updates all services and creates new ones if needed. So it's just a matter of importing the automatically created service and then refer to the required function ex.:

Api:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-c5afaed0-c4d5-4e4d-89c0-debc3968e4a7.png)

Angular:
Import the service (note that the service name is always the given c# controller name following "service")
![image.png](/.attachments/image-68c995d9-b5e0-4703-abd5-61d4f75aa001.png)

Then in code
![image.png](/.attachments/image-68587869-aa06-431a-a157-54d99c23483a.png)
Notice the function name is "api" following a concatenation of the url and request type.

# Google Material
For third-party components we decided to use Material unless they didn't provide a useable component for the use case required, like Datetime selector where another third-party component was used.

# Upgrading to a newer Angular version
Currently the frontend Angular version is 14.x. We have tried upgrading it to a newer version but it made so many breaking changes that we didn't have time to upgrade it. So I wouldn't recommend doing this unless you have time for it and know what you're doing.

# Deployment of changes
Whenever changes are merged into either the Develop- and/or production branch a couple build pipelines run which you can read more about [here](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10173/Build-Pipelines). 

Once they are done the code is ready to be deployed. Now this can either be your task or some devops dude from another project. Typically when you've made changes that you'll want LHN to test, you'll have to deploy these changes to his DEV environment. Fortunately this is quite easy, check this article: [Deployment to internal dev environment](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10178/Internal-DEV-Environment)

[[_TOC_]]


# Introduction
The C# Middle Layer acts like a proxy between the database and frontend, more than being a business heavy backend, as almost all business logic is contained in the database. Though it is a typical Web Api, it does nothing more than just forwarding request & responses between the frontend and database with the exception of a few functionalities. This means that development is seldom needed hence why there are only a couple things to look out for when you eventually have to change some code or implement new.

# Make code changes visible in angular
Whenever you make code changes I would recommend that you test them locally before you push it to the development branch and further into the world. 

To make the changes visible for use in the local Angular project navigate to and run the .bat file named "BuildApi.bat" in the projects "web" folder. I prefer to do it in a PowerShell window so it doesn't close afterwards so you have the opportunity to read the error message if ones come up.

This will then pack the application into an npm package and push it to some DIMA registry. Now you just run "npm run updateApi" in your angular console and it'll update the corresponding services or create new ones if needed with your changes. 

For it to be able to run you'll need .NET 6 SDK install but you should have that anyway for the C# code to work. Also you might have to run a "az login" command in the PowerShell window to login to azure for it to download stuff.

# Deployment of changes
Whenever changes are merged into either the Develop- and/or production branch a couple build pipelines run which you can read more about [here](/Technology-&-Software/7.-Admin-Portal/7.1-Dev-guide/7.1.2-UI-Development/Intro-%2D-Start-Here/Build-Pipelines). 

Once they are done the code is ready to be deployed. Now this can either be your task or some devops dude from another project. Typically when you've made changes that you'll want LHN to test, you'll have to deploy these changes to his DEV environment. Fortunately this is quite easy, check this article: [Deployment to internal dev environment](/Technology-&-Software/7.-Admin-Portal/7.1-Dev-guide/7.1.2-UI-Development/Intro-%2D-Start-Here/Internal-DEV-Environment)

# Introduction
In this article I will explain how to get started in terms of developing the Administration Portal UI. By now I you should know that the technologies involved are Angular (Frontend) & C# (Middle layer) so I do expect you have some experience here as I won't go into details on how to write code, more how to get it running and where to edit.

# Getting started
Start of by cloning the project from [here](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/_git/KMD.DIMA.AdminPortal) to a local folder on your computer. Notice that both the Angular and C# part's of the project are contained in the same repository.

Inside this cloned folder is a lot of files and folders. The two which are most important are **"api"** & **"web"**. The first contains the C# api code and the latter angular.

# Running the application locally
* Step 1:
Fire up your favorite IDE's, I prefer Visual Studio for C# & Visual Studio Code for Angular and load up the projects. Be sure to have a appsettings.development.json file in the C# project like below:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-1923d4a0-9e74-44fc-8e12-c508ed343b7a.png)
If you're unsure what this should contain, please refer to the configuration wiki article [here](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10174/Configuration). 

* Step 2:
Once configuration is done start the api by hitting IIS Express in Visual Studio:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-0c97c215-9952-4b42-82a5-4133c659fd09.png)
If its runs succesfully it should open a new browser window with a swagger endpoint overveiw:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-f6c64d06-1d6f-4078-acd7-3173da89ca3d.png =500x)

* Step 3:
Now that the api is running, next up is the frontend. Open a terminal in Visual Studio Code (while the project path is set to the "Web" folder containing the angular code), and enter Npm Run Start:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-e5149e0a-354c-4fea-bebe-e7bd7a3a47ae.png)
Which should result in:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-26165cf2-719f-4b28-ab78-5cc5c78290b2.png)

* Step 4:
Now that both the API and Frontend is running navigate to localhost:4200 in any browser and you should see either a login screen or something like this depending on what database you're connected to:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-1f85370c-0954-42b7-ac67-bd4da4655e40.png)

* Step 5:
You're now ready to begin making changes to the code. For more on information on this check out these articles: [Frontend Development (Angular)](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10177/Frontend-Development-(Angular)) or [Middle Layer Development (CSharp)](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10179/Middle-Layer-Development-(CSharp))

# Errors
If you encounter any errors or 500's when trying to load the portal on the localhost address it is usually a bad connectionstring or something to do with your account not having the right DB rights for the database which you're trying to connect to. Contact the DB admin to fix that, or ask LHN for guidance.

# Introduction

On this page, you will learn how to use Draw.io in Visual Studio Code, and how to add it to a `README.md` file. 

---

## How to get and use Draw.io in VS Code

Open up VS Code, click extensions as shown on the picture below. Search for Draw.io integration or hit [this link](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=hediet.vscode-drawio), which will redirect you to the extension marketplace. 

![image.png](/.attachments/image-651ca356-a8a1-456b-bf97-ad25c2fb63c2.png)

Create a new file in your project folder and ensure its name extension is `.drawio.png`. This allows the file to be displayed in Azure DevOps while keeping it editable without the need for manual updates to the displayed image.
Now you have the same benefits as using draw.io in your browser!

![image.png](/.attachments/image-37568724-5071-4f71-a44b-4d35e39f62ea.png)
## Adding your diagram to a README.md file

Now you have your diagram saved as a `.drawio.png` file. To inject it into your `README.md` file, navigate to your README and reference the image in the `README.md` file using Markdown syntax. You have the option to give your diagram a description, and afterwards, you must enter the file path. 
In the example below, the diagram is lying in the root folder, which results in the path just being `test.png`. Use the Markdown Preview Ctrl+Shift+V to ensure the diagram displays correctly. Make sure to keep the `.drawio.png` file for future editing.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-6fd24b0f-577f-488b-a2cc-de17f77fbfcb.png)

Now your diagram is visible in your repository!

![image.png](/.attachments/image-3b75b406-e867-42a8-b34a-ba7df6ee363f.png)
