path: /Processes/5. Maintenance Sharepoint docs/5.2 Guides/5.2.1 ServiceNow & CMDB
content:
# Introduction

---

## ServiceNow 
In ServiceNow, you have the option to extract information about servers, contracts, profit centers, business services, service requests, and server events. It is possible to create custom setups in ServiceNow that match your specific information needs.

### CMDB in ServiceNow
CMDB stands for Configuration Management Database and contains essential information about your servers and IT environment. The entities included in the CMDB are referred to as Configuration Items (CIs). CIs consist of the following elements: hardware, software, documentation, governance, and the services delivered to the business. Additionally, it includes information about how the individual entities, solutions, and services are interconnected. The CMDB can also provide details about who in the organization is responsible for the respective systems.

The picture below illustrates the elements of the CMDB at an overarching level.
![==image_0==.png](/.attachments/==image_0==-a88a32db-9fe9-4f76-aa97-4d224214d6ef.png) 

### Configuration Items (CI) in ServiceNow
If you need information about a specific server, such as the OS on the server, you can find these details by searching for the server via Configuration Items. A wide range of information about the server is available—for example, profit center, license type, server description, etc. Below are some specific details that can be found in a Configuration Item.

[Link to configuration items](https://servicenow.kmd.dk/nav_to.do?uri=%2Fcmdb_ci_list.do%3Fsysparm_query%3D%26sysparm_first_row%3D1%26sysparm_view%3D)
Write the name on the server and push Enter.
![==image_0==.png](/.attachments/==image_0==-de3e3588-05d4-4907-985d-4cb08b4adb1d.png) 

#### CI | Local or nearshore
Under Consumed Resource Units in the Configuration Item, it is possible to see whether the server is managed locally or nearshore under Service Location.

#### CI | Service Level
Under Service Level in the Configuration Item, it is possible to see which SLA agreement the server is covered by, such as the KMD standard SLA.

#### CI | Domain
Information about which domain the server belongs to can be found under Additional Attributes in the Configuration Item.

#### Corrections to CIs in ServiceNow
If any corrections need to be made to CIs in the CMDB, a case must be created via the 3101 portal – select CMDB – General CI Correction.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-3a7fc41d-749d-4ae9-bf6f-11866ec720e7.png)

## ServiceNow | Contracts & Profit Centers
All servers are set up with a profit center and contract. Each area in DIMA – for example, Cognito – is associated with a profit center and a contract number. It is important that the following profit centers and contract numbers are used for each area when ordering servers. Similarly, it is crucial that already existing servers are correctly registered with respect to profit center and contract.

### Overview of DIMA areas and their associated profit centers and contracts.
| **Area**                          | **Profit Center**         | **Contract**   |
|-----------------------------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| **Procurement Analysis**          | Business Solutions – IA   | 50101012       | CNTR0412370 |
| **EasyEconomy**                   | Business Solutions – NØ   | 50200105       | CNTR0412501 |
| **Central Government**            | CG - Central Government   | 50201850       | CNTR0411877 |
| **Cognito**                       | Cognito                   | 50172001       | CNTR0412226 |
| **InControl**                     | Health Solutions          | 50771004       | CNTR0414407 |
| **Local Government (Primary)**    | LG - Local Government     | 50162630       | CNTR0414289 |
| **Local Government**              | LG - Local Government*    | 5030400230     | CNTR0213833 |

## ServiceNow | Ordering & follow-up on Service Requests

### Follow-up on open Service Requests
In ServiceNow, you can view DIMA's open service requests. The overview shows all open service requests linked to the contract selected in the setup. Remember, you can adjust the setup and save it as a favorite.

### Ordering of Service Requests
There are 2 portals for ordering service requests. Most service requests should be ordered through the IBM Service Request Catalog in ServiceNow. A few requests must be ordered by DIMA's SDM through the PaaS portal.

Be particularly aware that an order/service request should only contain one order/service request. For example, if you have 3 port openings, 3 separate orders/service requests must be created. If the order contains multiple requests, it will always be charged as T/M (time and materials), which means that the benefit of having many services included in ongoing operational costs is not utilized, and DIMA will incur higher costs with IBM than necessary.
Templates have been created for the most common service requests ordered in ServiceNow: [Link to templates](https://teams.microsoft.com/_#/files/General?threadId=19%3Ae68860e43a5e4c3eb788f031361fcdf7%40thread.skype&ctx=channel&context=05%2520Maintenance&rootfolder=%252Fsites%252FDima-365%252FDelte%2520dokumenter%252FGeneral%252F12%2520DIMA%2520Highway%2520-%2520Process%2520Instructions%252F05%2520Maintenance)

## Reporting of Major Incididents
For Major Incidents during working hours, contact DIMA's Service Delivery Manager, who will create a P1 Incident:
Lene (LVF)
If Lene is unavailable, contact Leszek Wielonek (LEW) instead.
For Major Incidents outside working hours, contact the Service Desk both by phone and email:

Local Operations  
* [2650@kmd.dk](mailto:2650@kmd.dk)  
* 44602650

Nearshore Operations  
* [helpdesk@kmd.dk](mailto:helpdesk@kmd.dk)  
* 44602600

Remember, it should be written in English!

### Template for Major Incidents 

* Priority
P1 INC: Business critical service: Service unavailable. Impact on all user

* Business Impact description
SAP IQ is one of the prod servers unavailable - server went down before the data refresh has been finalized - no new data has been delivered to the customers - 23 000 users.

* System/server/application 
PFOSAP0021
    
* When did the issue start, time in CET

* Error description

### Categorizing of Incidents

|------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| **P1 INC**                                     |                                               |
| Business critical service: large parts of the service unavailable or very long response times | Many users                                    |

content:
# Introduction

This instruction describes the roles and responsibilities related to the use of the WEB01 user. The WEB01 user must be used for all batch updates of reports, updating of dashboard data, and email sending.
The WEB01 user may only be used for batch updating of reports, updating of dashboard data, and email sending, and not for development, testing, or troubleshooting!

---

## General information about the WEB01 user
The WEB01 user is a system user created by KMD for all municipalities. The user's password never expires.

The WEB01 user must be used for all batch updates of reports, updating of dashboard data, and email sending.

The WEB01 user must, of course, have data access to the knowledge areas from which data needs to be updated.

- In MSSQL solutions, data access is granted through a connection to a knowledge area in the CMC. This can be done with just a few minutes' notice, depending on when the CMC operator has time and is available.
- In SAP solutions, this is done by creating a POB case through 3101. This may take up to a couple of days.
- In DB2 solutions, the municipality's security officer links a role profile to the user. This may take up to 14 days.

Since the WEB01 user is a system user and thus accesses the municipality's data anonymously, no physical person should be "looking over the shoulder" of the anonymous user and accessing the municipality's data without it being logged. Therefore, the WEB01 user's password should only be known to a very limited group—those who set up the operational jobs.

## Use of the WEB01 user in new areas.
As mentioned above, the WEB01 user does not automatically work on knowledge areas it has not been used for before.
It is therefore important to provide notice in advance. This applies, for example, both when launching a new corporate management solution and when existing solutions are linked to new knowledge areas.
Consultants have access to knowledge areas so they can create reports that pull data from new knowledge areas. The issue arises when the reports are moved to full production, and the permissions for the WEB01 user have not been obtained, and the data accesses have not been linked.
So the message is – remember to notify about the desired operational setup for new knowledge areas as early as possible. The notice should be sent to the OPUSLIS mailbox, preferably with a copy to FSH.

## Data removal calendar
To ensure coordination, management, and risk assessment of data deletion in DIMA's production environment, it is planned in a data removal calendar, which can be found on SharePoint.

The calendar contains all scheduled data deletions. The data removal calendar is updated by the management.

## Notification of intended data deletion
A notification must be sent at least 7 days before the intended data deletion. It is recommended to send the notification earlier than 7 days if possible. The notification is made by submitting a ServiceNow case containing:
*   Desired time for data deletion

The management ensures the subsequent deletion of data in DIMA's production environment. This applies to both MS Backend, MS Frontend/Dataout, and IQ.

sequenceDiagram  
participant MGMT as Management

content:
# Introduction

This instruction describes roles, responsibilities, and prerequisites for the use of the SAP Business Objects development environment for customer-facing testing. That is, testing where the municipal user temporarily gains access to the SAP Business Objects development environment in connection with a development project.

---

## Conditions

The user should only be created for the period during which they are testing the development of a new solution/universe. After this, the user must be deleted! It should be aimed to create as few users as possible, meaning only those who need to test the solution (1-2 users) should be created. The user is only allowed to save reports in their own favorites folder. Reports are generally not moved between environments. This means that the test reports created in the development environment are deleted after the development is completed.
Regarding the use of the development environment, this must always be cleared with either Brian Freiheit or Jacob Jensen. This means that usage requires approval from either Brian Freiheit or Jacob Jensen.
Be aware that we do not make any commitments regarding performance or uptime of the environment, as it is also used for other purposes. This means that there may be downtime during certain periods. As a general rule, the environment should not be down for extended periods. The environment points to the development database on SAP IQ, meaning we do not need to release changes for customers to test it.

## Licenses

It is essential to comply with the licensing rules for SAP Business Objects and SAP IQ! This means that municipal users should only be temporarily created in the development environment. Access to the environment should be as short as possible, with a maximum duration of 2 months.

## Users and Access
Municipal users are created by contacting the SAP Business Objects responsible persons, namely (JFD or BFL). The following information must be provided:
-   Username
-   Name
-   Email

The user must log in via this link:
[https://kmd-opus-ledelsesinformation-test.kmd.dk/BOE/BI](https://kmd-opus-ledelsesinformation-test.kmd.dk/BOE/BI)

# Instruction

This instruction describes the roles, responsibilities, and tasks related to communication of operational disruptions on the customer network.

---

## Use of Kundenet and communities

- Kundenet is used as a communication platform for operational information, notifications, and updates, including patches, for KMD Opus LIS.

- BO Platform, Operations & Maintenance is responsible for operational information for all products handed over from the project phase to maintenance to BO Platform, Operations & Maintenance.

- Communities on [www.learn.kmd.dk](http://www.learn.kmd.dk/) are used as a communication platform for domain-specific and technical news and information.

- Product Owners are responsible for technical information related to all products, such as LIS Aktiv, LIS Momentum, etc., on Communities.

## Guidelines for Operational Information
- Operational information regarding missing data updates must be placed on the customer network by 10:00 AM on all weekdays. Responsible: BO Platform, Operations & Maintenance.
- Operational information regarding outages (major incidents) must be placed on the customer network as soon as possible. Responsible: BO Platform, Operations & Maintenance.

Additionally, a text must be placed on the customer network when the issue is normalized/resolved.

## Templates – texts for Kundenet
Here are the template texts for communication to the customer network. The yellow highlight indicates that the text is a template that should be adjusted based on the specific operational disturbance.

### Template Text No. 1
**Missing Data Delivery from External Supplier**  

Data for LIS XXX has not been updated today due to the lack of data delivery from the data supplier. It is expected that the data will be delivered and updated by XX-XX-XXXX. We apologize for any inconvenience caused by the missing data update.

### Template Text No. 2
**Missing Data Update**  

Due to issues with data update execution last night, data for LIS XXX has not been updated with fresh data today. A new status will be sent once the data is updated. We apologize for any inconvenience caused by the missing data update.

### Template Text No. 3
**System Outage**  

It is currently not possible to access KMD Opus LIS. A solution is being worked on. Status will be updated continuously.

**Note:** Be cautious when mentioning "delayed" in updates, as contracts related to data updates do not specify a fixed time for data updates. Instead of "delayed," consider using "not fully updated." Customers with specific SLA agreements in their contracts should be handled accordingly.

## Responsible for Operational Information
Below is an overview of those responsible for communication on the customer network in the event of operational disruptions. The actual communication is coordinated with the operations manager.

| AREA          | RESPONSIBLE         |
|---------------|---------------------|
| SAP BW        | MHA, NRP, or JA     |
| SAP BO OPERATION | MHA, NRP, or JA     |
| MS            | MHA, NRP, or JA     |
| DB2           | MHA, NRP, or JA     |


## Information on Kundenet
On Kundenet, operational information can be placed under:
-   **KMD Opus Data** – targeted at data-out customers (select "Opret" at the bottom of the page)
-   **KMD Opus LIS** – targeted at LIS customers (select "Opret nyhed" at the bottom of the page)

When selecting "Opret" or "Opret nyhed," the following dialog box will appear where you need to fill out the Title and Content. Be aware that you can choose the start and end dates for the time period.

![==image_0==.png](/.attachments/==image_0==-7c3f774e-fdc6-4d6c-a6f4-f9d26ede9d32.png) 

## Proportionality criterion
Communication of operational disruptions on Kundenet must always be assessed according to a proportionality criterion. The proportionality criterion involves weighing the number of affected customers and the impact of the disruption. The assessment of whether an operational disruption should be communicated on Kundenet is therefore always an individual evaluation.
Operational information must be placed on Kundenet in cases where all or many customers are affected by the disruption and the disruption lasts for an extended period (+ 15 minutes). For longer operational disruptions affecting a smaller number of customers, the customers should be contacted directly via email.

### Communication of operational disruptions on Kundenet
|                           | Extended operational disruption (+15 minutes) | Short-term operational disruption (less than 15 minutes) |

path: /Processes/5. Maintenance Sharepoint docs/5.1 Instructions/5.1.7 Reopening universes after notification of shutdown
content:
# Introduction

This instruction describes roles, responsibilities, and tasks related to reopening universes. The instruction is aimed at the process where one or more universes are shut down, such as in a situation where a universe is phased out or replaced by a new universe.

---

## Instruction

::: mermaid  
sequenceDiagram  
participant PM as Product Manager  
participant SD as Service Desk  
participant MR as Maintenance Responsible
%% Customer Notification and Information to Service Desk
PM->>PM: Decide if reopening is possible (yes/no)
PM->>SD: Inform Service Desk of reopening decision (yes/no), CC nyledelse@kmd.dk
PM->>SD: Send shutdown notifications (Notice 1: ≥6m, Notice 2: ≥3m, Notice 3: ≥14d before shutdown)
PM->>SD: In Notice 3, inform reopening will be subject to payment if possible

%% Handling customer inquiries about reopening universes
SD->>PM: Contact Product Manager for price if customer requests reopening
PM->>PM: Calculate price (list price + 30%, for 1 month)
SD->>Customer: Inform customer of price if reopening is possible
SD->>PM: If customer wants reopening, provide contact person + EAN number
PM->>Billing: Ensure billing via billing team

%% Reopening process
SD->>MR: Contact Maintenance Responsible for reopening
MR->>MR: Handle reopening and possible shutdown of universe
:::

content:
# Introduction

In connection with releases of products in DIMA below schema must be filled out. All questions must be answered.

---

## Release request document

All developers who wants a release must fill out the release request document which must describe the release in overall terms and state what version to be deployed in production. 

All dependencies and pre-steps must be described. 

Document: Template - Release Request.docx 

[Dima-365_General_12DIMAHighway-ProcessInstructions_5Maintenance](https://teams.microsoft.com/_#/files/General?threadId=19%3Ae68860e43a5e4c3eb788f031361fcdf7%40thread.skype&ctx=channel&context=05%2520Maintenance&rootfolder=%252Fsites%252FDima-365%252FDelte%2520dokumenter%252FGeneral%252F12%2520DIMA%2520Highway%2520-%2520Process%2520Instructions%252F05%2520Maintenance) 

The release request must be mailed to [OPUS-LIS@kmd.dk](mailto:OPUS-LIS@kmd.dk), [PEY@kmd.dk](mailto:PEY@kmd.dk) and [TNH@kmd.dk](mailto:TNH@kmd.dk)

## Release consideration and impact on the daily jobs

✓ Do you introduce new tool
✓ Do you introduce changed jobs, including changed schedules and dependencies
✓ Do you have all port openings ordered before the release
✓ Do you introduce new service account user or the service account now is to be used on all production servers, like DB2 user
✓ Have you considered the impact on the customers, like truncate of tables on IQ
✓ Do you truncate any tables during installation of new release
✓ Should the release be done during a weekend to avoid performance issues during first run

## Checklist 
Below to be used to follow up on the steps during a release 

*   DONE / V-sign: Task solved

| Status | Task | Who | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | Release date to be decided and confirmed by maintenance team | PDT Team |  |
|  | If Data-Out customer informs about new release | PDT Team |  |
|  | Evaluate impact of release in relation to size, more customers etc. in due time (5-10 days) | PDT Team |  |
|  | Release request sent in due time (5 days) | PDT Team |  |
|  | Release available in SVN on release date morning | PDT Team |  |
|  | Release meeting if necessary | PDT Team/TNH/PEY |  |
|  | Create a release plan with all tasks and order for release if necessary | PDT Team/TNH/PEY |  |
|  | Decide if the release should be in a weekend | TNH/PEY |  |
|  | Decide what customers to be the first ones if not all in one go | PDT Team |  |
|  | Decide if jobs must be disabled | TNH/PEY |  |
|  | Decide if schedule should be moved | TNH/PEY |  |
|  | Decide when to release for all customers | PDT Team |  |
|  | If many patches after the release, then pack a new version and deploy like a week after the original release | PDT Team/TNH/PEY |  |

## Gate Planning

Below gate plan can be used during the release for modules with many customers. 
Steps from Gate 3 handles the deployment for the first 1-5 selected customers. 
Steps from Gate 4 handles the possible deployment for the next 5-10 selected customers. 
If gate 3 and 4 releases are running successfully, the rest of the customers will be deployed.
![==image_0==.png](/.attachments/==image_0==-b23c8b94-6c9f-44cb-8c80-f37f1b0ccdf6.png)

# Introduction

This instruction describes roles, responsibilities, and tasks related to release notifications in DIMA's production environment.

---

## Release Calendar
To ensure coordination, management, and risk assessment of releases in DIMA's production environment, all releases are planned in a release calendar, which is available on SharePoint.
The calendar contains all scheduled releases as well as frozen zones. The release calendar is updated by the Release Manager. Major incidents and necessary bug fixes are handled ASAP.

| FROZEN ZONE | RELEASE |
| --- | --- |
| Period during which no releases are deployed to the production environment – e.g., during holiday periods | Release of a product to the production environment – either a new product or a new version of an existing product, resulting from changes in EDW or the universe. |

## Notification of planned releases
A notification must be sent at least 7 days before the planned release. It is encouraged to send the notification earlier than 7 days if possible. The notification is sent via email to [Opus-lis@kmd.dk](mailto:Opus-lis@kmd.dk) containing:
*   Desired release time
*   Completed “Template release request” LINK

The Release Manager conducts a risk assessment of the requested release and provides feedback to the requester. The Release Manager ensures the subsequent release on DIMA’s production environment.

content:
# Introduction

This instruction describes the roles, responsibilities, and tasks related to the review of the logical data model and the review of universes in a development project.

---

## Iterative development process
The development process is iterative and includes several phases. In the following figure, the different process phases are shown, along with the person responsible for each phase in the development of new universes. The process steps related to the review of the logical data model and universes are highlighted in the figure.

Figure 1: Iterative Development Process (Universes)
_Responsible_
![image.png](/.attachments/image-a7db860b-d3f5-4cfc-ae7d-6f8acc5cd2c5.png)

The logical data model outlines the organization of data and the relationships within the data. In the logical data model, various questions have been addressed, such as:
-   Use of aggregate tables vs. detail tables
-   Use of history (type 1 or type 2 history)
-   Clarification of the need for shared dimensions
-   Use of authorizations (row-based security)
-   Hierarchies
-   Use of user-defined dimensions, etc.

## Instruction
Tasks are described below.

::: mermaid

sequenceDiagram
    participant PO as Product Owner
    participant R as Reviewer
    participant RB as Review Board

    PO->>PO: Ensure review of data model based on:
    PO->>PO: 1. Solution description (template – BI universe)
    PO->>PO: 2. Data model (template – data model review)
    PO->>PO: 3. Star model (IDT)
    
    PO->>R: Notify Reviewer early to allow time for potential model changes

    R->>R: Conduct data model review based on:
    R->>R: 1. Solution description
    R->>R: 2. Data model
    R->>R: 3. Star model

    PO->>R: Joint review of the result

    PO->>PO: Implement adjustments to the data model if needed

    PO->>R: Contact Reviewer to review the final version of the universe
    PO->>R: Reminder: Reviewer may have other (non-movable) tasks

    alt Disagreement on the data model
        PO->>RB: Contact Review Board
        RB->>PO: Review Board makes the final decision
    end


:::

content:
#Testing new releases on .29 server

##Purpose
Discover changes in files between Targit version - so that we are able to implement changes if necessary.

##Test
Quick Checklist
1. Backup of existing version
2. Install new version
3. Save and deploy IMPD files
4. Save datamodels
5. Save Analysis files
6. Run comparescript
7. Check any of the relevant affected files
8. Report changes to Targit Group

###Backup
First we need to take a backup of the existing version of Targit.

This is done from 
```
D:\KMD\backup
```
Here you will run the powershell script
``` 
Backup Testserver.ps1
```

This will create a folder named [YYYYMMDD] (eg. "20250207")

Inside this there will be another folder named after the Targit version that the backup was taken from.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-989ffe46-8772-4e3b-8367-137be00456c8.png)

The backup script backs up the following:

C:\ProgramData\Targit
Which contains all Targit Settings and analysis files.

D:\KMD\Targit\Schedules
Which contains all impd packages.

###Install new Targit version.
Found at portal.targit.com

Just do a normal upgrade like done for customers.

###Update files to new versions.

When Targit is updated, it doesn't change datamodel, impd or analysis files until they have been saved anew.


####Datamodel
Right click on the two connections "Opus Løn og Personale" and "Opus Økonomi" click edit datamodel and then save them.
![image.png](/.attachments/image-15765c65-ff62-4ec7-b8ec-8fd4977428f3.png)

####IMPD
Opus the improj solutions at "D:\KMD\install\Solutions\Test Versionsændinger" and deploy them.
![image.png](/.attachments/image-d384dbf3-e8b8-4202-b42b-bf376d7d3d78.png)
Select yes to this prompt:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-cd13ec43-7384-4af2-b16e-4caf6a4f53bf.png)
And click deploy again.

-- THIS NEEDS SOME SIMPLER ANALYSIS FILES  TO MAKE IT LESS TIME CONSUMING --

####Analysis files

Open the targit client and navigate to Global\KMD Insight and just open the analyses and save them.


## Run compare script
When all files have been updated to the new Targit version it is time to run the comparison script to see which files have changed.

The script is called 
```
Sammenlign backup med installeret.ps1
```
and is located at
```
D:\KMD\backup
```

You will be prompted to select the backup you wish to compare the current version with. Default is the latest modified so you can usually just press "enter".
###Compare files

You will receive a summary of the results:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-14c0703f-01fd-4c9d-9dd7-5ba2f160aa3d.png)

You will then have to navigate to the backup folder to check the following files:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-ed7eaa29-96f1-4e2a-a706-ed6a9f466e74.png)

Located at eg. D:\KMD\backup\20250207\Build 25.1.21002

If you then open the TargitPublishedFolders-Comparison.csv

You will get an overview of the changes.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-7276b70a-8f0e-4a08-909c-f342822eeef1.png)
Here you need to know that only the .impd files are relevant.
An unfortunately (for this exercise) impd files will change their build number every time they are deployed so will always show up here.

But you need to compare the old and new files to spot if there are any material changes:

This can be done in visual studio code or notepad++

In visual studio code you need to right click the files in the Explorer and select "Select for compare" on the old file and then "Compare with selected" on the new File

![image.png](/.attachments/image-157e23ac-8689-42f3-8fc2-f5a87a1b776d.png)
This will give the following overview:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-9e17e659-7f75-43ea-9e32-e33b00204941.png)
Here we see that some additional lines have been added which are candidates for breaking compatability with previous versions.

In this case the new impd file needs to be moved over to .87 server and run there to see if it will fail.
dump the file to your own folder at  
```
D:\KMD\Targit\Schedules\PublishedFolders
```
and run it from the scheduler if it completes then there should be no issues.

You then need to do the same for the 
```
TargitSettings-Comparison.csv
```
and 
```
TargitVFS-Comparison.csv
```

Only check differences in files that are actually relevant.
So from this settings comparison you should only check the highlighted:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-e207cf90-17d6-456c-80d7-72f4a67e6454.png)

Datamodel example:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-2c25b692-fe8f-4b21-bad2-5c4aa7af6662.png)

This needs to be checked on the .87 server.

When comparing VFS files you can skip stuff like this:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-17a8b190-74ae-4378-9dda-8edddbbbe193.png)


But things like this should mean that the VFS files have indeed changed in the new Targit Version and that we can't deploy to older versions:

![image.png](/.attachments/image-48bedffe-1056-40d8-90dd-1e79cf230759.png)
No need to check on .87 server

###Report changes to Targit Group
```
Disclaimer: The comparisions in this guide are not from an actual Targit upgrade.
```

The changes in this comparison would lead me to report the following.
* impd files have changed but still function on old version (upgrade ok)
* datamodels have changed and do not function on old version (upgrade on .87 not ok)
* VFS files have changed. Can't push VFS files to customers on older versions. (Upgrade still ok)

Can not recommend upgrade until customers are upgraded due to datamodel changes.

content:
# Introduction

On this page, you can read about the importance of README files and how to use them effectively in software development. README files provide essential documentation directly within the project, helping developers and users understand the purpose, setup, and usage of a module without needing external references. A well-maintained README improves collaboration, ensures continuity, and enhances project usability.

---
[[_TOC_]]

## Purpose of README 

A README file serves as the entry point for understanding a project. It provides essential information about the purpose, setup, and usage of the module, ensuring that new users and developers can quickly get up to speed.

## Best Practices

### Documentation Close to the Module

*   Place the README file in the root directory of the module to ensure easy access.
    
*   Keep all documentation as close to the relevant code as possible to maintain clarity and consistency.
    

### Automation and Integration

*   Strive for automated documentation updates via pipelines to ensure that the README remains accurate as the codebase evolves.
    
*   Use tools like static site generators or documentation parsers to integrate README updates into the development workflow.
    

### Simplicity and Maintainability

*   Keep the README clear and concise—only include the most critical information.
    
*   Avoid excessive details that may become outdated quickly.
    
*   Structure the README in a logical way to facilitate quick comprehension and easy updates.

## Using Draw.io in README Files

Including diagrams in README files can greatly enhance clarity and understanding, especially for complex systems and workflows. Draw.io is a powerful tool for creating and embedding diagrams directly into your documentation. For more information on how to use Draw.io in README files, refer to this guide [Draw.io in VS Code](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10202/19.1-Draw.io-in-VS-Code).

## Creating Documentation

Writing effective documentation is key to ensuring your project is well understood and easy to maintain. Properly structured documentation helps onboard new developers and improves collaboration. For a detailed guide on best practices for creating documentation, refer to [Creating Documentation](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/8846/2.-Creating-Documentation).

content:
#Example based on KP dataarea implementation
## Step 1: find relation to FOLKEREG and procedures to be modified:

```
USE [615_KP_02_EDW]
GO

SELECT
    s.name AS SynonymName_ToBeRemoved,
    o.name AS StoredProcedureName_ToBeModyfied,
	'DROP SYNONYM IF EXISTS ' +schema_name(s.schema_id)+'.'+ s.name+';' Patch_for_Synonyms
FROM
    sys.synonyms AS s
INNER JOIN
    sys.objects AS o ON o.type = 'P' -- Filter for stored procedures
INNER JOIN
    sys.sql_modules AS m ON o.object_id = m.object_id
WHERE
    s.base_object_name LIKE '%FOLKEREG%'  -- Filter synonyms
    AND m.definition LIKE '%' + s.name + '%' -- Check stored procedure definition
    AND o.is_ms_shipped = 0  -- Exclude system stored procedures (optional)
ORDER BY
    s.name, o.name;
```
Exemplary result for KP:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-d6334038-6cb2-44d1-a610-2a5df426b112.png)

## Step2:New synonym to CM
Synonym is deliberately created in dbo schema not to transfer dimension to IQ.
```
CREATE SYNONYM [dbo].[dimensionMasterCitizen] FOR [615_CM_02_EDW].[dimension].[MasterCitizen]
```

## Step 3: Modification of stage procedures where needed
### Audit check
[dbo].[dimensionMasterCitizen] needs to be on the DW_Audit checklist for @Audit_Archive to guarantee that if anything changes there main part of stage procedure will be executed. 

```
declare @Audit_Archive int = isnull((select max([DW_Audit])
		from 
		(
			select max([DW_Audit]) DW_Audit from [archive].[KMF_POSTERING_T] UNION ALL
			select max([DW_Audit]) DW_Audit from [archive].[MAF_EFFEKTUERING_T]  UNION ALL
			select max([DW_Audit]) DW_Audit from [dbo].[dimensionMasterCitizen]  UNION ALL
			select max([DW_Audit]) DW_Audit from [archive].[PERSON_T]
		 ) a
	 ),-1) 		
```

### Main Query Part
It is important to know that not all citizens can be found in CitizenMaster. We can find only those that currently live in a given municipality. That is why it is crucial to calculate everything that can be extracted from CPR based on it instead of taking it from CM. These are:
- cpr - all formats
- birthday
- age 
- sex 

AI (copilot for instance) can be really helpful in matching fields (destination with new source), detecting where length of the field or types require attention. To do that DDL for Citizen Master as new source (Select into based on view), DDL of stage table as designation and select statement are needed in a prompt.

---

## Registering hours on SuccesFactor

Navigate to [SuccesFactor's front page](https://performancemanager5.successfactors.eu/) and click view my time sheet.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-02b1b731-cf8d-46cb-9f0b-63c3f074abed.png)

This will give you an overview of the the current week in days. You can click the calendar symbol, to get a larger overview. 
Choose the desired day, click **Apply Planned Time** and correct the start and end time to match your working hours for the day:

![qirkbolr.png](/.attachments/qirkbolr-e95fea76-1dce-442d-9120-28d6b94a99a5.png)

Afterwards click save in the bottom of the page. If you have more days to register, repeat the previous step, otherwise click submit.
Make sure when submitting your hours on **KMD Timesheet**, that they are matching the Recorded Working Time on SuccessFactor, which is your working duration minus the unpaid break of thirty minutes.

# Introduction

On this page you can read how to book vacation time and register your sick days.

---

[[_TOC_]]

## Booking vacation time

As soon as you know when you want to have vacation, you should book it in [SAP](https://sap.hec.kmd.dk/sap/bc/ui2/flp?sap-client=400&sap-language=EN#TimeEntry-manageTimesheet) and register it in the Vacation Overview Sheet. 

You can access it here: [Vacation Overview Sheet.xlsx](https://kmddk.sharepoint.com/:x:/s/DIMALG-365/EQZg0HHnz3RDuqPYnqU7iVABrH96iFFLLXn3qRdkgs7r8w?e=nib3H5)

If you do not have the days available yet, book them in Vacation Overview Sheet and then register them in SAP as soon as you have earned them. Finally, write it in your Outlook calendar so colleagues know not to book meetings with you. You need to book all three places.

You should always agree any vacation plans with your direct manager and any colleagues who might be affected. Each team can make their own specific guidelines on how you go about this. In most cases getting vacation approved will be trivial. 

**Note that:**

*   Use all vacation in the holiday period (before the 31st of December). 
    
*   Holiday left over from last holiday year, must be the first holiday taken (this is only relevant in the period where you can spend holiday from both holiday years). After that, Special Holiday hours must be used. 

*   At least 3 weeks of holiday must be taken during the period 1st of July to 15th of August. 

*   Register holiday before starting the holiday, if possible. Otherwise, they should be registered no later than the day you return from holiday. 

*   Only transfer holiday to next holiday period in exceptional cases. No more than 5 days can be transferred (and up to 5 days from the year before). This is dictated by law, so it is especially important that we observe this.

More details about vacation time booking can be found in the [D&D Handbook.docx](https://kmddk.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/DIMALG-365/ERaruzHB3CtKmg2y_y8-gRcBjQzR55Wk6kYCVSgA6lG8cQ?e=LC1pn7&CID=66ebc6e4-c12b-8b60-05d1-f53f13101551)

content:
This document describes the integration of DWH and Azure infrastructure blueprints: elements, dependencies and steps needed to configure DWH blueprint on Azure infrastructure.

_It is assumed that the reader has working knowledge of the Azure infrastructure blueprint.  
If not, it is highly recommended to get familiar with the following [documentation](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.KIP/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.KIP.wiki/607/Blueprint)._

**DevOps repository**  
The [Azure infrastructure blueprint](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.KIP/_git/KMD.DIMA.KIP.Blueprint?path=%2F&version=GBmaster&_a=contents) is ready to configure essential infrastructure required to install and run the DWH framework.  
The core link in this setup is the [DevOps repository](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.KIP/_git/KMD.DIMA.KIP.DWH.AppConfig) which holds configuration scripts (module) which can be divided in two groups:

*   Power Shell scripts – contain the code required to configure elements of the DWH blueprint.  
    Files’ names describe their roles which detailed explanation can be found in subpages in this Wiki  
    ![Picture1.png](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/671b3047-9a49-4a5c-b477-5986397a81a4/_apis/git/repositories/e7eb4961-f1bb-42a8-b884-b4d62c827131/Items?path=/.attachments/Picture1-1f792ef7-1090-4320-b454-af252c5bfc4e.png&download=false&resolveLfs=true&%24format=octetStream&api-version=5.0-preview.1&sanitize=true&versionDescriptor.version=wikiMaster)

*   Ansible scripts – which are wrappers for above scripts, enabling using them directly in the Azure infrastructure blueprint  
    ![Picture2.png](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/671b3047-9a49-4a5c-b477-5986397a81a4/_apis/git/repositories/e7eb4961-f1bb-42a8-b884-b4d62c827131/Items?path=/.attachments/Picture2-72a8755b-ed48-464b-93ca-467e84ab43ca.png&download=false&resolveLfs=true&%24format=octetStream&api-version=5.0-preview.1&sanitize=true&versionDescriptor.version=wikiMaster)  
    By organizing the code like presented above, it is possible run the same code either manually (for previous manually configured environments) or using the Azure blueprint.  

*   Those who are more familiar with Ansible can easily notice that it is a definition of an Ansible role.
The assignment of roles (files) to vms is presented below:  

![Capture.PNG](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/671b3047-9a49-4a5c-b477-5986397a81a4/_apis/git/repositories/e7eb4961-f1bb-42a8-b884-b4d62c827131/Items?path=/.attachments/Capture-16ecc834-352c-4dc6-98b3-0c6d66d52e2a.PNG&download=false&resolveLfs=true&%24format=octetStream&api-version=5.0-preview.1&sanitize=true&versionDescriptor.version=wikiMaster)  

The module (DWH blueprint) is installed in Azure Infrastructure blueprint by cloning its repository into Ansible roles’ folder (blueprint/ansible/roles/dwh-framework).  
Its version used in the configuration is set similar to other module references in the dependencies file (blueprint/ dependencies.tf.json).

**Key Azure components**
*   Virtual machines – these are the core services used to run DWH framework. 3 of them are run for different purposes:
    *   ETL1 – holds an instance of SQL Server (sql role)
    *   Portal – holds portals that are used to manage deployments and control the setup (portal role)
    *   Jumphost – it is used to get to an ETL1 instance and holds tools needed by developers (jump role)  
        _*Please make sure that you have added coresponding vm ad groups in settings/core/ad-groups!_
*   Application user – user used to build the context for all services used by the DWH framework and access
*   Configuration of other required Azure components (like discs or network) is done by the Azure blueprint and is transparent from the perspective of configuration of DWH framework.

**Terraform configuration**
1.  The very first step is to enable configuration of the DWH framework in the global settings:  

![Capture.PNG](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/671b3047-9a49-4a5c-b477-5986397a81a4/_apis/git/repositories/e7eb4961-f1bb-42a8-b884-b4d62c827131/Items?path=/.attachments/Capture-ff928519-c67a-42cd-8fec-0f0426c6bda4.PNG&download=false&resolveLfs=true&%24format=octetStream&api-version=5.0-preview.1&sanitize=true&versionDescriptor.version=wikiMaster)
  
This toggle activates creation and configuration of core (e.g. vms) and support (e.g. network, discs, users) infrastructure.

2.  The second important step is to create an application user (dwh-framework) in settings\core\service-accounts.tf:

    
```
locals {
    service_accounts = {      
            "powerbi-master": {
                 display_name = "PowerBI Masters Account"
                 usage_location = "DK"
             }
             "web-interface-test-user": {
                 display_name = "Web Interface Test User"
                 usage_location = "DK"
             }
             "dwh-framework": {
                 display_name = "Dwh Framework Automation Account"
                 usage_location = "DK"
             }
    }
}
```

This account is used to build the security context in vms (e.g. for running services) and also to get access to DevOps artifacts.  
_Since the only way to download DevOps artifacts is to login using PAT, one needs to create a proxy user for dwh-framework in a tenant which is used in DevOps and generate the access token which needs to be saved in a backend KV (e.g. SPA-Dev-DevOps-KV)._  
Steps to recreate a PAT token:

*    invite a user to a tenant 1e2ad6d6-274f-43e8-89ef-d36d65bb83b5
*    accept invitation to the tenant 1e2ad6d6-274f-43e8-89ef-d36d65bb83b5 (in Azure AD by resending the invitation)
*    ask DevOps admin (SOB or HMR) to assign the service user ({project_short_name}-dwh-framework-{env}@dima.kmd.dk) to KMD.DIMA.KIP.Feed.Readers in KMD.DIMA.KIP project
*    make sure that user is added at the organization level to users

![Capture.PNG](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/671b3047-9a49-4a5c-b477-5986397a81a4/_apis/git/repositories/e7eb4961-f1bb-42a8-b884-b4d62c827131/Items?path=/.attachments/Capture-d6c34c44-5a3e-48ad-9770-8194aa4fd868.PNG&download=false&resolveLfs=true&%24format=octetStream&api-version=5.0-preview.1&sanitize=true&versionDescriptor.version=wikiMaster)
*    login with newly created user (use different browser or incognito mode and choose KMD tenant 1e2ad6d6-274f-43e8-89ef-d36d65bb83b5) and create PAT (call it {project_short_name}-dwh-framework-{env}-artifacts-access) - grant only permission to **read packaging**  
    ** when assigning user to a given DevOps group make sure that it has proper privileges assigned - [more under the link](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.KIP/_wiki/wikis/KMD.DIMA.KIP.wiki/2861/Artifact-feeds)
*    save newly created PAT in {project_short_name}-Dev-DevOps-KV (e.g. SPA-Dev-DevOps-KV) as a secret named **dwh-framework-SERVICE-ACCOUNT-PAT**

This Tool is used to release a Module.\
It makes a nuget package and pushes it to azure dev ops

  

## Install Release

##Pre conditions for
Install coretool
[10. Module Core Tool - Overview](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/9084/10.-Module-Core-Tool)


## Call Release
Execute CoreTool.Release.exe from command line, with Json or reference to Json file as parameter

## Parameter description
If you write json directly (config=) use ' instead of "

file="C:\Temp\Download.json"
file1="C:\Temp\Download1.json"
file2="C:\Temp\Download2.json"
config={<json>}
config1={<json>}
config2={<json>}

Files and configs gets merged into a single config by tool.

###Placeholders in config
%MODULENAME% -> replaced with "id" (module name) value from config
%KMDHOME% -> replaced with KMDHOME system variable
%KMDNUGET% -> replaced with KMDNUGET system variable


## Json release file

### Parameters in file

* id -> the module name
* version -> the version number that you want to release  
* authors-> who made the module
* modulePath -> the path to the module
* description -> the description. Release note if up
* target -> up (Universal Package) or nuget
* up -> List of up specific variables
** organization -> devops organization
** project -> devops project, leave empty if organization scoped feed
** feed -> devops feed
* nuget -> List of nuget specific variables
** source-> the key of the dev ops feed
** NugetConfigPath -> the path to the nuget.config file
** releaseNotes -> the release note

## Example

Use ServerConfig and default file:
%KMDHOME%\Bin\CoreTool.Release.bat file="%KMDHOME%\Config\CoreTool\ServerConfig.json" file1="C:\Temp\release.json"

### Default file
```json
{
  "id": "001_dsa_mnttest",
  "version": "0.0.4",
  "authors": "Z6MNT",
  "modulePath": "C:\projects\KMDWORK\Z6MNT\001_dsa_mnttest",
  "description": "test",
  "target": "up",
  "up": {
    "organization": "kmd-dima",
        "project": "Test - MNT",
        "feed": "MNTTestFeed"
  }
}
```

### File with all parameters
```json
{
  "id": "001_dsa_mnttest",
  "version": "0.0.4",
  "authors": "Z6MNT",
  "modulePath": "C:\projects\KMDWORK\Z6MNT\001_dsa_mnttest",
  "description": "test",
  "target": "up",
  "up": {
    "organization": "kmd-dima",
        "project": "Test - MNT",
        "feed": "MNTTestFeed"
  },
  "nuget": {
    "source": "MNTTestFeed",
        "NugetConfigPath": "%KMDHOME%\config\CoreTool\nuget.config",
        "releaseNotes": "test"
  }
}

```

This Tool is used to build a Module.\
It creates a 'dist' folder in the module root folder. This folder is cleaned every time a build is done and recreated.

  

## What to build
In the root folder of the module, there is a build.proj file. In this file you can setup what you want to build. \
Look at module dev guide 'Link will be inserted here in the future'

Install coretool

* Copy 'config.targets' from ModuleAgent\CoreTool.Build to %KMDHOME%\Config\Bin
* Build project and copy content of ModuleAgent\CoreTool.Build\CoreTool.Build\bin\Debug\netcoreapp3.1 to somewhere on installation server.

  

## Run Build

If you write json directly (config=) use ' instead of "

file="C:\Temp\Download.json"
file1="C:\Temp\Download1.json"
file2="C:\Temp\Download2.json"
config={<json>}
config1={<json>}
config2={<json>}

Files and configs gets merged into a single config by tool.

###Placeholders in config
%MODULENAME% -> replaced with "id" (module name) value from config
%KMDHOME% -> replaced with KMDHOME system variable
%KMDNUGET% -> replaced with KMDNUGET system variable

  

## Json build file

### Parameters in file

* modulePath -> the path to the module you want to build
* msBuild -> the path to Msbuild.exe
* buildProjTarget -> The target in the build.targets file. Current targets GenericBuild,LimitedBuild default:GenericBuild

  

### Default file
```json
{
    "modulePath" : "C:\projects\KMDWORK\Z6MNT\001_dsa_mnttest",

}

```

### File with all parameters

```json
{
    "modulePath" : "C:\projects\KMDWORK\Z6MNT\001_dsa_mnttest",
    "msBuild" : "C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\2019\Professional\MSBuild\Current\Bin\MSBuild.exe",
    "buildProjTarget" : "LimitedBuild"

}
```

## Example

Use default file.
C:\test\CoreTool.Build.exe file="C:\Temp\Build.json"

# Introduction 

This page will guide you to get Local Admin Rights for your PC through a webservice. 

---

## What is LAPS?

Microsoft LAPS is a product that manages local administrator password storing them in Active Directory (AD). LAPS automatically randomizes and updates passwords, so that no users in KMD will have the same passwords and that passwords don’t become stale and more vulnerable to hacking.
In short, Microsoft LAPS ensures that all the devices and users throughout our systems have unique, strong passwords to prevent data breaches or unauthorized logins.

## How to use LAPS 

1. Visit [https://laps.kmd.dk/Computer/AccessRequest](https://laps.kmd.dk/Computer/AccessRequest)

2. Enter your Computer name (e.g. "A12345") and click 'next' 
![image.png](/.attachments/image-c0a21285-7b7c-44a7-8c28-58dce65599db.png)

**HINT** - Your computer name can be found beneath your PC on a barcode, or in File Explorer as in the picture below. 
![image.png](/.attachments/image-e54ad195-b403-45ac-90b8-e032d4660a5b.png)


3. Click on the 'Request Access' on the site
![image.png](/.attachments/image-3e7babfc-b925-4388-bd66-5d9ec678806c.png)

4. Click 'Copy Password' and use it together with .\administrator as admin username 
![image.png](/.attachments/image-bb2d1b57-2526-4f2d-8da3-1b3e24d357c9.png)

Example of User Account Control pop-up, where you can use LAPS
![image.png](/.attachments/image-316dfed9-bd1b-4942-8cc3-7d497d8dda82.png)

When opening the project on the KMDPFOSAP domain, you might experience some issue with the sln file in Visual Studio. The issue is related to loading Intelisense. # Introduction

Through a visionary data warehouse strategy, KMD has created a shared municipal standard platform based on the latest Microsoft standard software components in the form of database technology. This platform combines a structured methodology and framework with great flexibility and cost-effective development—without compromising on quality or stability. The full solution description can be found in [this SharePoint document](https://kmddk.sharepoint.com/:w:/r/sites/DIMALGSalesandCustomerRelations-365/_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7BE5513332-C099-4473-BEAA-3FF95E603C6F%7D&file=KMD%20INSIGHT%20Enterprise%20Data%20Warehouse.docx&action=default&mobileredirect=true).

---

## Solution Description

The solution architecture follows a layered approach, consisting of the staging, EDW, data mart, and presentation layers. As data moves through these layers, it is utilized for historical tracking, cleansing, validation, structuring, conversion, and the application of business rules—ensuring optimal reporting capabilities for the customer across the organization.

KMD applies Kimball’s recognized and proven principles and methods, focusing primarily on supporting the customer's business processes. This means that the foundation of the solution is developed according to "Best Practice" within the field, ensuring that maintenance and further development of the data warehouse solution remain as cost-effective as possible. This approach provides the customer with full flexibility to scale and expand within the new solution.

# Introduction

TARGIT Solution - Multi-Supplier Setup is a solution where KMD provides the TARGIT BI platform, including data marts and services, running on a dedicated InMemory server. KMD manages data delivery and maintenance, while the customer handles the installation and operation of the TARGIT Client server. The full solution description can be found in [this SharePoint document](https://kmddk.sharepoint.com/:w:/r/sites/DIMALGSalesandCustomerRelations-365/_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7B293EBE70-477C-45E5-BB65-92165B541403%7D&file=Teknisk%20driftsmodel%20til%20TARGIT%20l%C3%B8sning%20%E2%80%93%20flerleverand%C3%B8r%20setup.docx&action=default&mobileredirect=true).

---

## Solution Description

This solution is based on TARGIT as the BI application, with KMD as the supplier of data marts and the associated TARGIT solutions, as well as services related to the TARGIT installation on a dedicated KMD InMemory server.  
All operations and production of refined data up to and including the data mart are managed by KMD on the described source systems. This includes maintenance and service of the municipal data warehouse.

A dedicated InMemory server is set up at the customer’s site, where KMD installs the necessary TARGIT services and manages the ongoing data updates and delivery. Additionally, the related TARGIT datamodel.xml file is maintained and delivered to the customer, who is responsible for installing the data model on the TARGIT Client server.

Operations, monitoring, maintenance, and services related to data deliveries and TARGIT services on the TARGIT InMemory server are managed by KMD. The customer is responsible for the operation, monitoring, and maintenance of physical servers and operating systems. Furthermore, the customer has full responsibility for installations and operations on the TARGIT server, from which data models and data are made available to end users.

# Introduction

TARGIT Solution - Local Hosted leverages TARGIT as the business intelligence (BI) platform, where KMD provides the data marts, TARGIT solutions, and related services. The customer is responsible for server operations, while KMD handles the management of data processing, system monitoring, and platform maintenance. The setup involves dedicated servers for TARGIT InMemory and Client, allowing seamless integration with third-party solutions as needed. The full solution description can be found in [this SharePoint document](https://kmddk.sharepoint.com/:w:/r/sites/DIMALGSalesandCustomerRelations-365/_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7B19EC51F6-C345-4DDA-A50F-67FA9D4A1790%7D&file=Teknisk%20driftsmodel%20til%20TARGIT%20l%C3%B8sning%20%E2%80%93%20Lokal%20Hostet.docx&action=default&mobileredirect=true).

## Solution Description 

This solution is based on TARGIT as a BI application, with the customer responsible for server operations, and KMD as the provider of data marts and the associated TARGIT solutions and services related to the TARGIT installation.  

All operations and production of refined data up to and including the data mart are managed by KMD on the described source systems.  
At the customer's site, at least two independent servers are established, one handling TARGIT InMemory and the other the TARGIT Client. # Introduction
Inside the param files like IQ.param there is a parameter reference for the ODBC driver used to transfer data to the IQ destination. The parameter that point towards this is /IqDestDsnName:IQ_Udvikling. For that a ODBC DSN is needed.

## **What is an ODBC DSN?**

ODBC **DSN (Data Source Name)** is a configuration that stores **database connection settings** for an ODBC (Open Database Connectivity) driver. It allows applications to connect to a database **without needing to specify connection details** (like server name, username, password, etc.) in the application code.

## What is needed for the ODBC DSN?
The attributes needed to make a connection to IQ are:
- Driver
- Host
- Integrated
- PWD
- UID

Here is an example from odbc driver to IQ dev:
![image.png](/.attachments/image-c20ce8a0-0b7e-42f6-a75c-9cc4d04135ed.png)

The ODBC DSN can be found in the Registry Editor, from where a new entry can be added as well.

# Introduction
Purpose of the document is to highlight the security measures on our platform. We will cover various aspects across all our platforms and technologies, and go into depth on what exact has done to comply with security measures within the given area.

WORKING PROGRESS!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!


## Scope
The different platforms in scope for this security overview are:
- MSSQL: Storage engine serving ETL loads in our multitenant data warehouse.
- IQ: Storage engine serving analytics queries initiated from the SAP BO platform.
- SAP BO: Multitenant analytics platform containing semantic models and web application supporting analytics workloads and hosting of shared and individuel data reports.
- TARGIT: Internal on-prem environment used for development of Targit relevant components like Datamodel, In-memory database, ETL load and reports creation. On the Targit platform we have a decentralized environments, where all production components are hosted within individuel customers domains.
- Azure DevOps: A cloud-based platform by Microsoft that provides DevOps toolchain for developing and deploying applications. Azure Repos is used for source control of all our modules. Azure Pipelines are used for Continuous Integration (CI) and Continuous Deployment (CD) on some specefic module types like Tabular models. Azure Artifacts used for package versionering representing releases of all our modules. Azure Boards for planning and tracking work using Kanban boards, Scrum boards, and dashboards.
- Microsoft Azure (cloud platform): Microsoft Azure is a cloud computing platform used for infrastructure, platform, and software services over the internet. This platform is mainly used for hosting web based applications and services supporting our CI/CD workloads like ex. Keyvault and secret management. 
- Also address security regarding connection and internal/external traffic.

## General Security Principles
The current general security protection is handled through network security, meaning platforms and data stored and moved within a secured network. Within this secured network access is further restricted by access control and role-based security.

## Authentication and Authorization
I general all internal users are identified and verified through Windows authentication. All on-prem platforms and related components are hosted within specific domain (KMDPFOSAP). This applies for internal endpoints of our MSSSQL, IQ, SAP BO and internal Targit platform. Windows authentication is used for authenticating users to these platforms, further the authorization is governed by ad groups.

# Introduction

This page will describe how to create a new subscription in the Cloudrunners tenant. 

---

## Creating a New Subscription

To create an Azure Subscription in the Cloudrunners tenant, please use the template below and send it to azuresub@kmd.dk

Subscription Name:  
Cost Center ID:  
Subscription Owner Email:  
Asset Owner Email:  
Environment Type:

### Description

**Subscription Name** is just a name for identifying the subscription in Azure  
**Cost Center ID** must be a valid ID from SAP  
**Subscription Owner** is the person who owns the subscription and who is able to give permission to others  
**Asset Owner** is a person who has the authority to change anything in aspect to an azure subscription. The ideal asset owner seen from the Cloudrunners perspective - in short, is a person who has the authority to change the developers backlog.  
**Environment Type** must be one of the following values:
*   "[Sandbox (Playground)](https://dev.azure.com/kmddk/KMD%20Shared%20WIKI/_wiki/wikis/KMD-Shared-WIKI.wiki?wikiVersion=GBwikiMaster&pagePath=/KMD%20Shared%20WIKI/CCoE%2C%20Cloud%20Management%20%26%20Compliance%20%252D%20Cloudrunners/Landing%20Zones/New%20Subscriptions/Sandbox%20(Playground)%20landing%20zone)"
*   "Development"
*   "Test (QA / UAT)"
*   "Staging"
*   "Pre-production"
*   "Production"
*   "Education"
*   "Demo (Pilot)"

When a subscription is ordered in Cloudrunners, the subscription is subject to an automated incubation process that configures the following security related components.
*   Required tags set on subscription
*   Service providers registered:
    *   Microsoft.PolicyInsights
    *   Microsoft.Security
*   Qualys installation/onboarding
*   Microsoft Defender for Cloud connector to Sentinel (for CDC)
*   Defender for Cloud plans enabled:
    *   Servers plan 2 with agentless scanning.
        *   Exclusion tag is set to: AgentlessScan = Off - (if set on VMs they are excluded)
    *   App Service
    *   Databases
        *   Azure SQL Databases
        *   SQL servers on machines
        *   Open-source relational databases
        *   Azure Cosmos DB
    *   Storage (Classic)
    *   Key Vault
    *   Resource Manager

After this process, the subscription is moved to the target management group, the default is **KMD Plus** where a number of [security guardrails](https://dev.azure.com/kmddk/KMD%20Shared%20WIKI/_wiki/wikis/KMD-Shared-WIKI.wiki?wikiVersion=GBwikiMaster&pagePath=/KMD%20Shared%20WIKI/CCoE%2C%20Cloud%20Management%20%26%20Compliance%20%252D%20Cloudrunners/Guardrails) are implemented.

# Introduction
This page describes how and who you can invite into Cloudrunners. 

---

## Who can I invite into the Cloudrunners tenant?
All users employed in KMD Group are welcome as users in the Cloudrunners Entra ID tenant.

Users need to have an identity in one of these domains:
*   kmd.dk
*   kmdpoland.pl
*   charlietango.dk
*   [banqsoft.com](http://banqsoft.com/) 
*   banqsoft.se
*   banqsoft.no
*   banqsoft.pl

Employees from these domain will be invited as guests, but shortly after the invite they will be converted into the user type "Member" in Cloudrunners.

## How to Invite an User to Cloudrunners
As a KMD member you can invite employees. Simply invite the user via Azure Entra ID, in the portal.
This will trigger cross-tenant sync. The user will be available immediately, and within 1 hour the sync will add metadata to the user

![image.png](https://dev.azure.com/kmddk/3e95d692-683b-439a-8e57-6f20520d3e30/_apis/git/repositories/dab98b43-cf04-4e3e-a916-43273977310f/Items?path=/.attachments/image-2af7e6cb-bba0-49cf-a4d0-9696c990ea89.png&download=false&resolveLfs=true&%24format=octetStream&api-version=5.0-preview.1&sanitize=true&versionDescriptor.version=wikiMaster)

## Guest Users in Cloudrunners

In the Cloudrunners tenant, at guest user is defined as a person who is not employed in KMD Group. A guest is typically an external consultant that needs access to specific resources in a subscription for **a limited amount of time**.
A guest is NOT a KMD customer with permanent access to resources.
A guest is a personal account. You cannot invite a shared account into the Cloudrunners tenant.

### How do I invite a guest user?

Please write to azuresub@kmd.dk to get in touch with the Cloud Management and Compliance team. You cannot invite a guest user yourself.
State the following about the guest:
*   Name
*   Email
*   Reason for inviting the guest
*   For how long should the account exist? (max 3 month)
*   Who is responsible for this guest?

Responsible employees...

Changing roles and access...

# Processes & Activities

An illustration of AO's processes and activities, each step is described below.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-6c617e74-df5c-4fcd-ad4a-270ced42eedf.png)

## [AO Dashboard](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_dashboards/dashboard/b117211d-459d-4fc9-8823-39992996fd1b)

### Purpose

The purpose of this ticket system is to provide all employees within DIMA LG and other relevant internal stakeholders with a central place to report relevant topics related to the data platform.
This single point of reference makes it easier for DIMA LG to prioritize both operational and strategic enhancements of the data platform. It supports the needs of current and future customers while reducing friction and improving business processes across DIMA LG.

### Role of the Architecture Office (AO)

AO is responsible for facilitating and assessing incoming requests. AO does not make independent decisions but ensures the involvement of all relevant stakeholders for informed decision-making and prioritization. All tickets, prioritization, and decisions are open and available within the organization.

### Process and Flow for Reported Tickets

When a ticket is created, AO (MMP) assesses it. Once assessed, the ticket moves to the AO Board and transitions through various states:
*   **Assessment** – Ticket is under evaluation.
*   **Backlog Assessment** – Decision pending: rejection or backlog inclusion.
*   **Backlog** – Tickets closely related to the current data platform.
*   **Backlog Vision** – Visionary tickets related to the data platform.
*   **Backlog Prioritized** – High-priority tickets nearing active development.
*   **Active** – Tickets currently in development/implementation.
*   **Backlog - Rejected** – Rejected tickets with a documented rationale.
*   **Backlog Vision - Rejected** – Rejected visionary tickets with justification.
*   **Closed** – Completed and finalized tickets.

## [AO Pre-Backlog](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_boards/board/t/Architecture%20Office%20-%20Pre-backlog/Features)

The Pre-Backlog serves as an initial filtering mechanism before tickets move into the AO backlog for further processing.

## [AO Backlog](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_boards/board/t/Architecture%20Office%20-%20Projects/Features)
Key considerations for backlog items include:
*   **Artifact Mapping**
*   **Effort Estimation**
*   **Acceptance Criteria**
*   **Task Type**

### Backlog Projects

The AO is actively involved in multiple phases of projects:
*   **Assessment**
*   **Design**
*   **Development**
*   **Implementation**
Upon project completion, the AO ensures:
*   **Evaluation**
*   **Adoption Review**
*   **Project Evaluation**

## [Roadmap](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_boards/board/t/Architecture%20Office%20-%20Roadmap/Epics)

The AO roadmap outlines how technology supports strategy and ensures alignment with long-term business goals:
*   Ensures **long-term technology decisions** align with strategic plans.
*   Defines the **direction** for platform, tools, and technologies.
*   Guides **competency development and career growth** for colleagues.
*   Helps maintain an **attractive work environment** for current and future employees.
*   Aligns **commercial and technical strategies** for sustained business growth.
*   Supports **sales and business management** in customer dialogues.
*   Keeps the organization **up-to-date** with relevant technological trends.
*   Ensures compliance with **rules, regulations, security requirements, and standards**.

path: /Technology & Software/1. SAPBO/1.3 IDT (Information Design Tool)/1.3.6 Multiunivers
content:
# Use of Multiple Business Layer Views in Universes.
      
The purpose of multi-universes is to improve performance, for example, by using subqueries, to simplify complexity by consolidating solutions, and to ensure user-friendliness, for example, by reusing queries and auto-merge

Business Layer Views allow for grouping the content of the universe in different contexts.

It is not possible to set fixed rules for when it makes sense to use business layer views for a given area, but some of the points below may be considered to determine if it makes sense to use them in a specific situation.     

**Scenarios where SAP Business Layer Views can be used**
*   Multiple facts in the solution: Complexity can be high, and it can improve the user experience by making it easier to understand the relationships between fact and dimension tables.
*   **Reuse of dimensions**: When multiple facts draw on the same dimensions, reusing them is advantageous. Maintenance of mouseover texts is also simplified as it only needs to be reported in one place.
*   For example, with an aggregate table with the dimensions that work there and a detailed table/view (master table) with all dimensions.
*   MU student: division of master data and regular school data.
*   **Same data source provider**: For example, AS2007 and Silkeborgdata, where the same provider delivers data sources with many common dimensions and business overlaps.
*   Business areas where users extensively use Query on Query: An example could be the collection of Momentum Target Groups and Momentum Placements.
*   Different **usage scenarios**: When there are different usage scenarios, the individual views can be tailored.
    *   Division of finance into budget and consumption parts.
    *   "Quickstart": A very simplified view with the most used dimensions and metrics. It should give the new user easy access to the solution. The default view will then contain all dimensions and metrics.
*   Migration situation: If facing a version change where new universes need to be developed, it can be a good time to introduce different business layer views.

      

## Scenarios where the use of multiple Business Layer Views is not appropriate
*   Time dimension: Business layer views on time should not be used if that is the only purpose. Time can be linked to Aggregate awareness and does not require separate views.
*   **High complexity**: If the data area is very extensive, for example, FLIS or OPUS in general, the entire area should not be consolidated into one universe with many business layer views.
*   Release frequency: If there are frequent releases on different parts of the view, it may argue against consolidating them.
*   **Row-based security**: If there is different row-based security on the individual facts.
*   Authorization management: If there is separate authorization management related to the individual sub-universes, this argues against consolidating these universes into one with multiple different views.
*   Technology combination: It is not possible to combine Tabular/Bex with IQ in the same business layer view.
*   Sales considerations: There may be sales considerations that prevent consolidation into too large solutions.
*   Municipal special considerations, where it is desired to differentiate within the municipality which users may see which universes and/or update reports.

## Attention points
**Master view**: The master view must be available to convert from the old universe to a new "Multi-universe" with multiple Business Layer Views.

**Deadline**: It is important that a fixed deadline is set for the closure of the old universes in connection with the conversion to a universe with multiple business layer views. This must be communicated to customers with at least 3 months' notice.

## Review and Approval of Multi-universe
Introduction and use of multi-universe for both new and existing universes must be reviewed and approved by BFL to ensure consistent use.

## Documentation

The Powershell script: MakeDocFromBL.ps1 supports multiple business layer views
It is recommended to use the version where each dimension has one row per view:
![2025-03-31_13-47-38.jpg](/.attachments/2025-03-31_13-47-38-e8330b5b-555c-4386-af25-f67e3614068d.jpg)

      
##Guideline for multiviews

Choose names for the business layer views which are logical for the end user and use the same name for the contexts and views in IDT. Consistent naming conventions for views, contexts, and business views are required to ensure clarity and coherence as the universes are getting more complex. The name of the facts might correspond to the name of the contexts, IDT view name and det business layer views but it is not required.

An example of naming could be like this:

Fact name: OvergangFolkepension
Context name: Overgang til folkepension
IDT view name: Overgang til folkepension
Business layer view: Overgang til folkepension

      
###Creating views in data foundation
It is recommended to create views in the data foundation to make it easier to survey the relations between tables when working with several facts. Name the views so it corresponds to the name of the facts as shown below if it makes sense.

![Skærmbillede 2025-03-31 154222.png](/.attachments/Skærmbillede%202025-03-31%20154222-a98bedb8-9653-4b48-998e-584cc9059781.png)

###Contexts
The contexts should correspond to the views.

      
TIP: You can change the name of the context by changing the name in the properties folder.

![Skærmbillede 2025-03-31 154339.png](/.attachments/Skærmbillede%202025-03-31%20154339-96764307-4b11-4db3-8325-e16f6fa762c2.png)

      
###Business layer view
To make it easy for the enduser to see how measures can be combined to dimensions, you should create folders for the dimensions that match the folders of the measures eg. **Dimensioner (Måltal - OF)** and **Måltal - Overgang til folkepension (OF**).  For each view and context, make a business view with legitimate dimensions and measures.

![Skærmbillede 2025-03-31 154627.png](/.attachments/Skærmbillede%202025-03-31%20154627-da70368d-999a-4da0-917d-910a6572cce0.png)

path: /Technology & Software/16. Azure Devops/16.1 DevOps Pipelines/16.1.1 Pipeline Security in Azure DevOps
content:
# Introduction

Securing pipelines in Azure DevOps is crucial to protecting code, infrastructure, and deployment environments. This document outlines best practices for improving pipeline security, including the use of YAML-based pipelines, agent security, variable management, and permissions.

[[_TOC_]]

---

## Use YAML Instead of Classic Pipelines
YAML pipelines are stored in the repository, making it easier to track changes, review security updates and enforce policies. YAML templates allow reuse of pipeline definitions across projects, reducing the risk of configuration drift. If you use classic UI-based pipelines, they will be stored separately from the code repository, making them harder to audit and version-control effectively. 

## Security in Agent Pools
Ensuring the security of agent pools in Azure DevOps is critical to maintaining the integrity of your CI/CD pipelines. Properly securing agent pools helps protect sensitive data, prevent unauthorized access, and mitigate potential threats. This section outlines best practices for securing both Microsoft-hosted and self-hosted agent pools.
Microsoft-hosted agents are generally more secure, but cannot be used to access KMD servers.

### Microsoft-Hosted Agents

-   **Pros**:
    -   Managed and updated by Microsoft, ensuring the latest security patches.     
    -   No need to maintain infrastructure, reducing attack surface.
    - Runs in an isolated environment for each pipeline run.
        
-   **Cons**:
    -   Limited customization.
    -   No persistent storage between jobs.
        

### Self-Hosted Agents

-   **Pros**:
    -   More control over agent configuration and dependencies.    
    -   Can cache dependencies for faster builds.
        
-   **Cons**:
    -   Higher security risk if not properly maintained (e.g., outdated software, exposed credentials). 
    -   Requires continuous monitoring and patching.

If your pipeline does not need access to KMD servers, Microsoft-hosted agents are the more secure choice, but in some cases wont be a possibility. In case you need to use a Self-Hosted agent, best practices are listed below:

- Run agents in an isolated environment.
- Restrict access to agent pool.
- Regularly update and patch agents. 
- Use dedicated agent pools for different security levels. 

## Use Variables and Parameters Securely

When creating pipelines on Azure DevOps, credentials are often needed. This can be a Personal Access Token (PAT) or other secrets. These type of secrets should **always** be stored in Azure DevOps Variable Groups or Azure Key Vault, instead of hardcoded into the YAML. Parameters should be defined at the top level of the pipeline, to make it configurable without modifying code. Least privilege principle should be enforced, to limit who can read or modify sensitive variables. 

A new variable group can be created by hovering the pipeline symbol and choosing library.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-28ef5287-e4cb-44a9-a47c-d65c822817be.png)

Click on "+ Variable group"
![image.png](/.attachments/image-826a90d6-ddcb-4331-bb74-2bb5c0d0871c.png)

Now you have created a new variable group. Here you have the possibility to link secrets from an Azure key vault or add variables directly. After you have given your variable a name and a value, the value will be hidden and the variable can be used in pipelines without hardcoding sensitive information. 

![image.png](/.attachments/image-dca08afb-7daf-4759-bcf5-25ee3dd94863.png)

Best Practices:
-   Store secrets directly in a variable group or in Azure Key Vault and link them to the variable group.
-   Use variable groups to centrally manage values shared across multiple pipelines.
-   Use runtime parameters to control pipeline behavior dynamically while ensuring validation of user inputs.

## Permissions and Access Control

### Pipeline Permissions

To enhance security, access to pipelines should be restricted to authorized users or service accounts. Editing rights should be limited to a select group to prevent unauthorized modifications, while execution permissions for critical pipelines should be carefully controlled. Approval workflows should be enforced for deployments to production to minimize risks.

### Repository and Environment Security

Branch protection rules should be implemented to require approvals for merging changes that impact pipelines, ensuring that modifications are reviewed before being applied. Additionally, securing deployment environments through approval workflows and access controls helps prevent unauthorized deployments.
By enforcing strict permissions and approval processes, organizations can reduce the risk of unauthorized changes and maintain the integrity of their DevOps pipelines.

## Additional Security Considerations 
A few additional best practices for pipelines security involves the following:

- **Monitor Pipeline Runs**: Enable auditing and logging of pipeline executions.
- **Use Conditional Checks**: Prevent unauthorized execution of scripts and deployment steps.  
- **Scan for Vulnerabilities**: Integrate security scanning tools (e.g., SAST, DAST) into the pipeline.
- **Enforce MFA and Conditional Access**: Strengthen authentication for pipeline contributors.

# Customers with SLA terms
