# Standard SLA terms

## Servicemål: driftseffektivitet

Målet for driftseffektivitet er 99% indenfor aftalt driftstid.
Der måles løbende på, om kunderne har adgang til KMD Insight platformen.
Driftseffektivitetsmålingerne foretages for leverance ved Kundens Access Point på Leverandørens lokation.

Driftseffektiviteten opgøres hver måned.
Rapportering gøres tilgængelig overfor Kunden 1 gang pr. måned senest den 10. hverdag i efterfølgende måned.

Såfremt kunden forlanger bod / ønsker at drøfte driftseffektivitet i samarbejdsorganisationen, gennemgås de automatiserede målinger for at øge præcisionen af tidsrummet for udfald, samt varslede servicevinduer og lignende. Varsling sker pt. via learn.dk.

Driftseffektiviteten opgøres således:
100 * Tilgængelig Driftstid / Aftalt Driftstid
Tilgængelig driftstid omfatter Aftalt Driftstid minus den tid, hvor KMD Insight ikke er tilgængelig.

Driftsafbrydelser regnes fra det tidspunkt inden for Aftalt åbningstid, hvor Leverandøren har konstateret fejl/manglende tilgængelighed og indtil leverandøren konstaterer, at tilgængeligheden er genoprettet.

I disse tilfælde medfører driftsafbrydelser ikke nogen reduktion af den tilgængelige driftstid, når denne skal beregnes:
*   I tilfælde af at driftsafvikling ikke kan opretholdes som følge af en driftshindring, som Kunden er ansvarlig for, eksempelvis fejl i Kundens eksisterende it-miljø, eller udefra kommende forstyrrelser som f. eks fejl i offentlige datanet, fratrækkes den omfattede tid ikke Aftalt Driftstid ved beregning af tilgængelig driftstid. Bemærk at el-afbrydelser ikke er omfattet af nærværende undtagelse.
*   Forhold hvor KMD ikke selv har mulighed for at foretage fejlrettelser: SAP BO og Sybase/SAP IQ som er 3. parts leverandører af bagvedliggende software.
*   For tid medgået til varslede servicevinduer, opdateringer mv. jf. ovenfor.
*   Servicevinduer mv. placeres kun undtagelsesvist/ekstraordinært indenfor aftalt åbningstid.

KMD vurderer og iværksætter relevant tiltag, når driftseffektiviteten falder under grænseværdierne. Dette indgår som emne på møderne i samarbejdsorganisationen.

Endelig rapporteringsform er under afklaring og første måling af driftseffektivitet leveres senest primo september 2025.

## Servicemål: Svartider

Der måles svartider på en SAP BO rapport fra forespørgsel påbegyndes til rapportens data er opdateret. Målingen foregår indenfor KMD’s KMD Insight miljø.
Der måles på en repræsentativ rapport svarende til dette: Rapporten henter samme datasæt hver gang, der bestående af minimum 100.000 rækker med mindst 3 måltal fra et univers til en rapport med grafer og tabeller.

Den gennemsnitlige svartid er maksimalt 20 sekunder.
Svartider angives som gennemsnit af 90% fraktilen. Fraktilen fremkommer ved at fjerne de 5% dårligste samt de 5% bedste svartidsmålinger fra måleresultatet.
Der måles mindst 1 gang pr. time indenfor aftalt driftstid. Leverandøren tilstræber at måle hyppigere, hvis dette ikke påvirker performance.

Svartid opgøres hver måned.  
Der måles ikke svartider i tilfælde af, at KMD Insight platformen ikke er tilgængelig.
Svartidsproblemer som er forårsaget af forhold, hvor KMD ikke selv har mulighed for at foretage fejlrettelser er undtaget: SAP BO og Sybase/SAP IQ som er 3. parts leverandører af bagvedliggende software.

Rapporteringsform er standardiseret rapport, som indeholder opgørelsesperiodens opnåede mål i henhold til tærskelværdierne.
Rapportering gøres tilgængelig overfor Kunden 1 gang pr. måned senest den 10. hverdag i efterfølgende måned.

KMD vurderer og iværksætter relevant tiltag når svartiderne falder udenfor grænseværdierne.  Dette indgår som emne på møderne i samarbejdsorganisationen.

Såfremt kunden forlanger bod / ønsker at drøfte svartider i samarbejdsorganisationen, gennemgås de automatiserede målinger og der korrigeres for manglende tilgængelighed og svartidsproblemer, der ikke er forårsaget af forhold, som KMD er i kontrol med jf. ovenfor  

Endelig rapporteringsform er under afklaring og første måling af svartider leveres senest primo september 2025.

##Servicemål: dataleverancer (ikke bodsbelagt servicemål)

Målet for opdatering af KMD Insight modulerne er inden kl. 8 jf. opdateringsfrekvensen (månedlig / ugentlig / daglig). Der kan dog være aftalt senere opdateringstidspunkt for enkelte moduler med kunden, eller dataleverancerne fra kundens fagløsninger ankommer så sent, at det ikke er muligt at opnå.

Der måles på om 95 % af alle load og data-ud job er gennemført inden klokken 08.00.
Det opgøres som en samlet procentsats for hele måneden for alle jobs for den samlede leverance til kunden og beregnes således:

Dataleverancen opgøres pt. således:
100 * Antal afsluttede jobs / antal startede jobs inden kl. 08.00.

Startede jobs opfylder følgende krav:
*   Er et load-job eller data-ud job.
*   Er planlagt til kørsel.
*   Har tidligste starttidspunkt mellem batchstart og kl. 08.00 om morgenen.
*   Jobs, der kører flere gange før og efter kl. 08.00, tælles ikke med.

Afsluttede jobs opfylder følgende krav:
*   Alle kravene for startede jobs.
*   Afsluttet succesfuldt før kl. 08.00 om morgenen.
*   Hvis det kører flere gange (eksempelvis ved genkørsel), skal den endelige succesfulde kørsel være afsluttet før kl. 08.00 om morgenen.
*   Jobs, der fejler og ikke køres igen før kl. 08.00, tælles ikke som succesfulde.

Rapportering gøres tilgængelig overfor Kunden 1 gang pr. måned senest den 10. hverdag i efterfølgende måned. Endelig rapporteringsform er under afklaring og første rapportering leveres senest primo september 2025.

KMD vurderer og iværksætter relevante tiltag når opdateringstidspunkterne falder udenfor grænseværdierne. Dette indgår som emne på møderne i samarbejdsorganisationen.

Opmærksomheden henledes på, at der ikke er faste leveringstidspunkter for dataleverancerne fra kundens bagvedliggende fagsystemer. Dette betyder at KMD ikke kan garantere at data er opdateret inden kl. 8 på opdateringsdage. Dette inkluderes i målingerne der da tages udgangspunkt i et kunde-centrisk perspektiv, men det er vigtigt at klarificere, at der er en betydelig kilde til usikkerhed udenfor KMDs indflydelse og kontrol.

This page includes information regarding the operation of the IQ servers.

# Servers

There is a total of three servers; one orchestrator note (writer note) and two reader notes.
The writer notes takes input from MSSQL servers in the nightly jobs. The reader notes deliver data to SAP BO.

# Backup

The nightly backup of the IQ database follows the following timings:
(Updated 17.07.25)

| **Start Time** | **End time** | **Activity** |
|--|--|--|
| 08.00 | Before 09.00 | Backup of IQ DB to files. A number of files are created of around 32 GB each and placed on the backup drive of the server (Y:). |
| 19.30 | Appr. 00.30 | Comvault backup of files. Files are copied from C:, D: and Y: to external location. Duration varies depending on load|
| 07.30 | Appr. 07.50 | Files on backup drive (Y:) are deleted. |

All backups are full. The backup taken on Fridays is kept for a month, the others are kept for 15 days.

# Alerts and Monitoring

We have four specific monitoring scripts for IQ.
      
* IQ_ping.ps1: Verifies if the server is running and pingable. If this fails it means nothing is listening on the port, hence it should probably only happen if IQ / server crashed.
(Uses the dbping utility to verify if the server is up)
* IQ_version.ps1: Verifies if the IQ server is responding. If this fails it indicates that IQ is not responding (correctly). This would normally require further investigation.
(Connects to IQ and checks whether the version string contains “SAP IQ”)
* IQ_check_mpx_status.ps1: Verifies if the multiplex is working. If this fails it probably means that a reader node needs a refresh.
(Connects to IQ and checks the status of the multiplex setup)
* Storage space: Monitors the space on the IQ database raw disks. If more than 85 % usage it raises a P2 incident, if more than 95 % it raises a P1 incident. This check is made every 5 minutes. This will either happen if we have an organic increase over time but more likely - if it happens over a short period - it is caused by a problem with a user that didn't log out and hence caused a table to be replicated over and over. 

We are (17.07.25) considering the following not yet implemented:

* Backup delay: Monitors if the backup is delayed and raises

::: mermaid  flowchart TD     A[Write code] --> B(Code review)     B --> |Feedback| A     B --> |Accepted| E[Pack release candidate]     E --> F[Cold test]     F --> G[Warm test]     G --> H[Release]     subgraph test [ ]         F         G     end     subgraph release [ ]         E         test     end :::
1. Write code Actor: Developer * Create a branch Before starting to implement a feature or resolve a bug, create a git branch. Go to the relevant userstory/bug and press "create a branch", in the tile in the right middle side of the window. ![Create a branche.png](/.attachments/Create%20a%20branche-5b9196df-6ed0-4956-9785-f277cd769aad.png) * Commit code When you finish part of your solution, make a git commit. More commits makes it easier for other to understand your process and follow the evolution of the code. * Test code Test your code before making a pull request, it is your responsibility. * Pull request When coding is done and it has been tested, it is time to create a pull request. A pull request is a request to merge the feature/bug branch with the master branch. The request is send to one or more developers for review of the code. A pull request should have a title, description, be linked to a userstory and a have one or more reviewers. The **description** should describe what the codes does, why it is designed as it is and how it has been tested. The linked user story describes the purpose of the code change. When the pull request have been created, press "set auto-complete". The settings should be as follows. ![image.png](/.attachments/image-620ca6ec-6ba6-4f7e-94e7-853d7cacd305.png )
2. Code review Actor: Reviewer The purpose of the code review is as follows: - Find and eliminate potential bugs - Spread knowledge of the code to make the developer team more robust - Discuss the code design in order to spread good code practices The review process has the following steps: 1. A developer receives a review, informs the author that they wish to review the code, then they proceed to read the code. The Reviewer marks themself as mandatory Reviewer . 2. The Reviewer informs the author that they are ready to receive a presentation of the code, this presentation becomes a discussion of the code. The Reviewer provides feedback to the code and the author makes code changes as they think is best. 3. When the Reviewer and Developer agree that the code is ready for release, the Reviewer press Accept Here are some topics that the reviewer bring up during the review: - [ ] How has the code been tested - [ ] Has the change been added to the release notes - [ ] Why has the code been designed in the way it is - [ ] Is there any performance concerns to be aware of
3. Pack release candidate Actor: Release Responsible In this step the Release Responsible prepares the code and pack a release, this release will be tested in the next step. * Rename patch Before packing the release, the Release Responsible needs to prepare the patch folders by renaming them using the following schema: `From_X_To_Y`. X is the original version and Y is the new version number that will be assigned the release. It may be necessary to create multiple patch folders if the solution instances installed in production is not on the same version. This can be seen on this page https://prodsiteportal.intranet.kmdhub.net/table/CustomLatestInstallModuleLicenseCICD Remember to commit the patch folder. * Check release notes Some solutions contain release notes. If so, remember to check that all features and bugs have been added to the release notes. The release notes can be found in the README file in the root of the solution folder. Example of release notes https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_git/nexus2.targit.001 and the syntax in the README file https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_git/nexus2.targit.001?path=/README.md * Packing a release (candidate) Before packing a release ensure that you have done the following: - Commit all changes to git - Don't have any unstaged files, all files located in the solution directory will be part of the release - Ensure that correct patch folders exist - Build and commit solution (to ensure script(00_Scripts) are updated) To pack a release, open the Modulebuilder, go to the Release tab ![image.png](/.attachments/image-26831068-1e29-4b7d-9ee6-be8c9f4127bc.png) New version number: Enter a version number of the release. The naming convention is as follows: Major.Minor.Build. **Major** should be increased when a large edition has been made to the code, such a new module or non-backwards compatible change. **Minor** should be increased when a feature has been added to the solution, a feature is something that the customers can see, such as new fields to a dimension or a new measure. **Build** should be increased when bugfixes or optimizations has been added. Comment: Write an internal comment that is only visible for other developers. Dependencies and "Can be installed to a new customer or a customer with one of these release:" are not used. Press Ok to create the release If you get the following error in the Module Builder, then you need to gain acces to the az login. ![image.png](/.attachments/image-a249a042-680b-4ff9-9968-6e2457506150.png) Firstly, find the commando prompt on your own computer, not the KDIDRDPAP01 server, type in _az login --tenant 1e2ad6d6-274f-43e8-89ef-d36d65bb83b5 --allow-no-subscriptions --use-device-code_ and press _ENTER_. Then, You'll see the following: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-a2875e70-d72d-4602-a634-2c8646490524.png) Copy the code and go to the link --> https://microsoft.com/devicelogin Here, you'll paste the code and press _ENTER_. Then, you will get a new message in the commando prompt. ![image.png](/.attachments/image-dc6069fd-ffe8-410b-8181-b743a3f85797.png) Press _ENTER_ in the commando prompt. Now you have access and should be able to create the release again without errors. * Release tag To make it easier to see when a release candidate has been created, we added tags to the specific commit 1. Go to Sourcetree, open your repository, history view 2. Right click the commit where the release was created, and press Tag... 3. Enter the Tag name (Release[Major].[Minor].[Build]), check the "Push tag" checkmark box, and press Add Tag ![image.png](/.attachments/image-b05816e3-b982-49fb-bd51-444a3e358ad5.png) ![image.png](/.attachments/image-07efb583-c24b-46a6-bd3c-53db625fb38d.png)
4. Cold test Actor: Release Responsible A cold test is a test without data. The purpose of this test is to test: 1. the release can be installed on a new customer, ensuring that there are no dependency errors. 2. the release can be installed on a customer that already have the previous version of the module. We test if the patch works as intended. To make this process easy, we created the preprodTest.ps1 script, which can be found in the powershell directory under src. It always works*. Remember to: 1. change the variables defined in the top. 2. Seek access to the customers involved. `$customersNewRelease`, are the customer(s) that will have the release candidate installed. (case 1) `$customersUpgradeRelease`, are the customer(s) that will first have production version installed then the release candidate on top of that. (case 2) _*It assumes that Common, Dato, and other modules, which it depends on, have already been installed._ Nedenstående viser koden fra powershell scriptet _PreProdTest.ps1_ ``` $module = '001_dataarea_nexus2' $area = 'Nexus2' $releaseVersion = "1.11.13" $previousReleaseVersion = "1.11.9" $zuser = "z6hdh" $downloadFolder = "D:\KMDWORK\$($zuser)\download\" $customersNewRelease = @("219") $customersUpgradeRelease = @("316","607") $server = "KDIDMSSDB01" $ConnectionString = "Data Source=$server; " + "Integrated Security=SSPI; " + "Initial Catalog=KMDBI; " + "Connection Timeout = 0"; Import-Module kmdbips.etl.global foreach ($customer in ($customersNewRelease+$customersUpgradeRelease)) { Write-Host "Deleting all database objects in "$customer $database = "[$($customer)_NEXUS2_02_EDW]" $clearDatabase = " DECLARE @RC int EXECUTE @RC = [system].[CleanDatabase] $($database) " Invoke-SQL -connectionString $ConnectionString -sqlCommand $clearDatabase } <# az login --allow-no-subscriptions #> #Download the Requested versions $versionsToDownload = @($previousReleaseVersion,$releaseVersion) $downloadDirectory = $($downloadFolder) mkdir $downloadDirectory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue foreach ($version in $versionsToDownload) { $downloadDirectoryVersion = "$downloadDirectory\$version" mkdir $downloadDirectoryVersion -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Remove-Item -Path "$downloadDirectoryVersion\*" -Recurse -Force az artifacts universal download --organization https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/ --project="KMD.DIMA.LG" --scope project --feed KMD.DIMA.LG --name 001_dataarea_nexus2 --version $version --path $downloadDirectoryVersion } # Deploy the old version of the solution and patch foreach ($customer in $customersUpgradeRelease) { $directory = "$downloadDirectory\$previousReleaseVersion\$module" Set-Location "$directory\bin" sqlcmd -b -SKDIDMSSDB01 -vIMPORTCUSTOMERID="$($customer)" -vCUSTOMERNAME="$($customer)" -vAREANAME="$($area)" -vUSERNAME=$($zuser) -vDistPath="..\.." -i"..\sql\00_MasterScript.sql" Set-Location "$downloadDirectory\$releaseVersion\$module\bin" sqlcmd -b -SKDIDMSSDB01 -vCUSTOMERNAME="$($customer)" -vAREANAME="$($area)" -vFROMVERSION="$($previousReleaseVersion)" -vTOVERSION="$($releaseVersion)" -vDistPath="..\.." -i"..\sql\02_EDW\Patches\From_$($previousReleaseVersion)_To_$($releaseVersion)\00_Scripts.sql" } # Deploy the new version of the solution foreach ($customer in ($customersNewRelease+$customersUpgradeRelease)) { $directory = "$downloadDirectory\$releaseVersion\$module" #& $directory\bin\deploy_sql.bat $server $customer $area $customer $($zuser) "$directory" "$directory\sql\00_MasterScript.sql" Set-Location "$directory\bin" sqlcmd -b -SKDIDMSSDB01 -vIMPORTCUSTOMERID="$($customer)" -vCUSTOMERNAME="$($customer)" -vAREANAME="$($area)" -vUSERNAME=$($zuser) -vDistPath="..\.." -i"..\sql\00_MasterScript.sql" } ``` Denne powershell fil kan køres ved at blive trukket over i din powershell commando promt og derefter trykke _ENTER_.
5. Warm test Actor: Release Responsible A warm test is a test with data. By running Extract, Transform, and Load, we test the entire flow of the solution with the new changes. Often it is also necessary to do other kinds of tests depending of the nature of the features/bugs released.
6. Release Actor: Release Responsible * Release request An email describing the release should be send to MQH@kmd.dk and TNH@kmd.dk | **Release request** | **Description** | |-- |-- | | Expected release date | As soon as possible | | Customers involved | All | | Initial step | None | | Modules involved | 001_datarea_nexus2 1.11.13 | | Upgrades from | 001_datarea_nexus2 1.11.11
001_datarea_nexus2 1.11.13| | Test Run | 230,159,330,846,210, 350 | | Changes comparing to previous release | Small bugfixes | ###Release verification To check that the release has been installed on all the relevant customers go to [https://prodsiteportal.intranet.kmdhub.net/](https://prodsiteportal.intranet.kmdhub.net/) -> Installation -> latest module installed Filter on the version just installed "LatestVersion" , "ModuleName", "ActiveServer"=1 and "ActiveLicense"=1. Check that all customers are on the correct version. Note the number of customers on the new version. ![image.png](/.attachments/image-6ecb8281-f5ca-4129-9ac5-9e43149575ef.png) In the Queue view you can see the different types of installs (SQL,IQSQL,SSIS….) and the version they are on. To see if the SQL part is installed to the correct version go to [https://prodsiteportal.intranet.kmdhub.net/](https://prodsiteportal.intranet.kmdhub.net/) -> CI/CD -> Queue Filter on InstallationModule, InstallationType = SQL, InstallationVersion ![image.png](/.attachments/image-8c96a420-9e38-4353-abd4-223e546e6a2c.png) Note that the number of rows is 88 in latest module but 87 in Queue view. The reason for that is that Lyngby-Taarbæk (173) is only running Fælles depot (IQSQL) and therefore, not counted in the SQL installationType.

# FLIS 3 Overview
FLIS 3 aims to release datapackages at different times with different frequency.
Currently this is in POC stage using KP and KP Benchmark as example.

Differences for us is that
- Each dataarea must be able to load/process individually 
- Data is only processed to Tabular cubes

# Overview and changes from FLIS 2
In FLIS 3 the data packages are made available individually pr. area at different times with different frequency. This is different from FLIS 2 that delivers all data monthly.

The way we will support this is to split up the "FLIS database" into a number of "FLIS area databases".

NetCompany is developing this separated architecture on prototype using the area "KP" (Kommunernes Pensionssystem) with corresponding Tabular cubes "KP" and "KP Benchmark".

# Dataflow
![image.png](/.attachments/image-60257a65-059a-45b0-9fb6-a2a002b878ed.png)
Data for each area is delivered in 3 separate data packages.

NOTE: 
Currently 2 - Benchmark is contained in municipality zip.
Since Benchmark must be processed only once pr. delivery, we are handling that manually.

## SFTP/Unzip
Powershell scripts: 
FLIS3_Download_Download <customer> <area>
FLIS3_Download_Unzip <customer> <area>

Files are downloaded from Kombit SFTP into area specific folder below
H:\FLIS3\<customer>\Sourcedata

A file with latest download timestamp is added to folder.
Files are unzipped into area specific folder below:
H:\FLIS3\<customer>\Extract

Notice that for Global data there are the following subfolders before the area specific folder:
Tvaerkommunale dimensioner
Tvaerkommunale facts

## Extract
Extract loads each csv file into corresponding table.
File must be UTF-8 in order to be able to contain correct danish characters.
There must be a header with field names at the top of the file.
Fields must be contained in " and be separated using ; - like this: "asdf";"ghjk"

## Process/Deploy Tabular
For Targit customers the data is processed into Tabular cubes.
After processing the cubers are made available on data out server.

## Load to IQ
For SAP BO customers the data is loaded onto the IQ platform.
Global data is loaded into the role000
Customer data is loaded into the roleXXX with views pulling data from role000

[[_TOC_]]

# Overview
The jobs are found in the corresponding database module.
All the jobs are calling powershell scripts.
Jobs are called in the order
DOWNLOAD → EXTRACT → LOAD

# Job params
The jobs are found in the corresponding database module and called using
| Parameter | Type | Detail |
|--|--|--|
|customer | int    | customer number or 999 for Global |
|area     | string | area name like KP                 |

_Examples_
F:\KMD\Config\Powershell\FLIS3_Download_Download Global KP
F:\KMD\Config\Powershell\FLIS3_Download_Download 480 KP


# Powershell scripts
The jobs are responsible for calling the appropriate Powershell script with the proper parameters.
In FLIS 3 the powershell scripts have been unified into the following scripts:

| Powershell | Purpose |
|--|--|
| FLIS3_Download_Download | Connects to SFTP and download new data packages if any    |
| FLIS3_Download_Unzip    | Unzips downloaded files if any                            |
| FLIS3_Extract_Bulk      | Load extracted data into DSA database using bulk insert   |
| FLIS3_Load              | Load data from EDW to IQ platform using datatansfer tool  |

# Description
Databases are organized into Global and Area databases, each with corresponding DSA and EDW.

This makes it possible to set up jobs that can process each area individually and without dependency to other areas.

# Global
The netcompany term for Global is Generel.
In KMD we use this for storing shared data across the areas.
This database needs only to be updated once pr. area, which optimizes disk space and processing time.

## DSA
DSA contains globally shared tables (Generel), area specific dimensions and benchmark data.
 
#### Global dimension tables
DimAlder
DimAlder10
DimJaNej
DimKommune
DimKøn
DimProcent
DimTidMåned
DimVarighedMåned

#### KP dimension tables
DimPensionstype
DimSagstilstand
DimSagstype
DimUdbetalingstype
DimYdelsestype

#### KP Benchmark facts
FactPensionBenchmark
FactSagBenchmark
FactUdbetalingBenchmark
FactYdelseBenchmark

## EDW

### synonyms
Synonyms are created using code in \02_Synonyms\CreateMultipleSynonymsToDSA
It creates synonyms to archive tables in DSA.

### views
Views are made with one base view in schema "dimension" or "fact".
These are loaded to IQ using param files.
The following schemas are used by Tabular:
Benchmark
Generel


# KP
The municipality area KP contains data relevant for Kommunernes Pensionssystem

## DSA
### dimension tables
DimPerson

### fact tables
FactOvergangFolkepension
FactPension
FactSag
FactUdbetaling
FactYdelse

## EDW

### synonyms
Synonyms are created using code in \02_Synonyms\CreateMultipleSynonymsToDSA
It creates synonyms to archive tables in DSA.

### views
Views are made with one base view in schema "dimension" or "fact".
These are loaded to IQ using param files.
The following schemas are used by Tabular:
Dimension
Kommune

# Overview
The purpose of the database is to control the dataflow with proper process conditions.
This is a major change from FLIS 2 that made use of trigger files to control the dataflow.
Also information for SFTP login is now stored in database and not in the download jobs.

# Tables
config tables contain base information for each area and each customer respectively.
process.tabular is the main table that joins customers/areas with process and load states.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-eed6d490-4f59-4601-9663-4c5fafed7f07.png)

## ProcessState
| value | description |
|-|-|
| 1 | Data downloaded |
| 2 | Ready for extract |
| 3 | Ready to process |
| 4 | Database processed |
| 5 | Ready to copy database |
| 6 | Database copied to dataout |

## LoadState
| value | description |
|-|-|
| 0 | Data not ready |
| 1 | Data ready |

# Procedures
Interaction is done through stored procedures.
They provide a layer of abstraction on top of the actual database fields.
This method helps the user by having to interact with only a few procedures instead of knowing the details of the underlying tables.

## Config procedure

| Schema  | Procedure | Purpose | Notes |
|-|-|-|-|
| config| UpdateCustomerAreas | Insert missing customer/area combinations into process.tabular using default values | param @customer=0 (all), @deleteFirst=0 (keep entries) |


## Tabular cube processing

| Schema  | Procedure | Purpose | Notes |
|-|-|-|-|
| process | GetProcessList | Retrieve list of Tabular cubes ready to be processed | param @optional_server, return @tabulardatabases   |
| process | ProcessStart | Sets flag that database processing has started | param @tabulardatabase |
| process | ProcessOK | Processing has finished with success | param @tabulardatabase |
| process | ProcessError | Processing has finished with error | param @tabulardatabase |

## Process/Load state getters

| Schema  | Procedure | Purpose | Notes |
|-|-|-|-|
| process | GetIsReadyForExtract | Check that customer/area is ready for extract | return @Isready boolean |
| process | GetIsReadyToLoad | Check that customer/area is ready for to IQ | return @Isready boolean |
| process | GetIsReadyToProcess | Check that customer/area is ready to process | return @Isready boolean |
| process | GetIsReadyToCopy | Check that customer/area is ready to be copied | return @Isready boolean |
| process | GetProcessState | Return state for customer/area (shouldnt be used directly) | return @State int |

## Process/Load state setters

| Schema  | Procedure | Purpose | Notes |
|-|-|-|-|
| process | SetIsProcessing | Set processing flag for customer/area | params @customer, @area, @processing |
| process | SetIsProcessingFromTabularDatabase | Set processing flag for customer/area | param @tabularDatabase |
| process | SetLoadState | Set load flag for customer/area | params @customer, @area, @state |
| process | SetProcessState | Set process state for customer/area (used by other ProcessState setters) | params @customer, @area, @state |
| process | SetProcessStateFromFolder | Set state for customer/area using ftpFolder | params @customer, @folder, @state |
| process | SetProcessStateFromTabularDatabase | Set state for customer/area using tabular database | params @tabulardatabase, @state |
| process | SetProcessStateDownloadReady | Set download is ready for customer/area | params @customer, @area |
| process | SetProcessStateExtractReady | Set extract is ready for customer/area | params @customer, @area |
| process | SetProcessStateProcessReady | Set process and load is ready for customer/area | params @customer, @area |
| process | SetProcessStateCopyReady | Set copy is ready for customer/area | params @customer, @area |
| process | SetProcessStateDatabaseCopied | Set copy is complete for customer/area | params @customer, @area |

# What is FLIS

**FLIS - Det fælleskommunale ledelsesinformationssystem
FLIS er den fælleskommunale løsning til ledelsesinformation, der samler data fra kommunernes fagløsninger og hver måned sender opdaterede, validerede data til kommunerne, som de kan bruge til benchmarking og ledelsesinformation.**

# FLIS data areas
_Tværgående dataområder_
Borger
Økonomi
Personale & Fravær
  
_Skole & Daginstitution_
Skole
Dagtilbud
  
_Social & Sundhed_
Voksenhandicap
Udsatte børn og unge
Fælles Sprog III (indsatsområder på social og sundhedsområde for enkelte borgere)
Ældre
  
_Arbejdsmarked & Beskæftigelse_
Kommunernes Ydelsessystem (KY)  
Ydelsesrefusion (YR)
DREAM (effekt af indsats på beskæftigelse)
DFDG (kvalitet på jobindsats - får ikke data pt)
Kommunernes Pensionssystem (KP - nyt område)

# Other players
NetCompany: supplier - collects and publish data and cubes
Kombit: supplier of solutions to municipalities
Lifa: competitor
Fujitsu: competitor ?

# FLIS Insight purpose
Gather, process and publish cubes to customers.
48 customers, split into 39 SAP BO and 9 Targit


[[_TOSP_]]

# Introduction
There is create a local drive where files of all format can be dumped for storage. This is a local onprem storage.

## Use cases
This share is for storing files that later can be used for deferent things. It could be extracted metrics from different API's, like pipeline logs or wiki usage. Currently the lake contain a backup of the old SVN server. It is opitmal for data that is not jet in use, but the history want to be preserved for later use.

## Relevant paths
The datalake can be found on KDIDMSSDB01 on the o: drive.
- link to SVN backup: O:\KMDBIDataLake\SVN

Please reach out to CDO or MMP if you need access to this share, or have a relevant use cases.

path: /Technology & Software/2. Targit/2.12 Tips and Tricks/2.12.5 Oprettelse af Benchmark kuber
content:
Formålet med Benchmark kuber er at skjule/anonymisere relevante dimensioner, i dette eksempel fx alle personhenførbare data. Dette gøres således at alle har mulighed for at tilgå data og sammenligne på tværs af fx afdelinger eller hierarkier, uden at kunne slå op på den enkelte borger - da kuben er renset for personhenførbare data.

### **Fremgangsmåde:**  
Anbefalingen fra KMD er, at:
-  KMD laver en forbindelse som ligner 1:1 den oprindelige forbindelse – i dette eksempel en ny SD forbindelse, som er en 1:1 kopi af den oprindelige SD kube.
- Derefter gøres databasen per default utilgængelig for alle, således der som udgangspunkt ikke er nogle brugere, som har adgang til kuben.
-  Derefter oprettes der én rolle, som skal styre adgangen til Benchmark kuben. På denne rolle sættes 'Tilladelse' til 'Ingen i denne rolle' på alle andre kuber, således den ikke fejlagtigt giver adgang til data, som 'Benchmark rollen' IKKE skal have adgang til. 

![image.png](/.attachments/image-b3622c76-d510-47f5-ad33-709c83c47fe1.png)

- I 'Benchmark rollen' findes de relevante personhenførbare dimensioner i Benchmark kuberne, og 'Tilladelse' sættes til 'Ingen i denne rolle' - fx som 'Adresse' markeret med gult i skærmbilledet herunder.
Denne 'Benchmark rolle' skal alle TARGIT brugere som udgangspunkt have adgang til.
    - Ideen med denne rolle er derfor, at ALLE TARGIT brugere har adgang til Benchmark kuberne uden personhenførbare data vha. denne rolle, men de har ikke mulighed for at kigge i de "normale" kuber.

    -  Personhenførbare dimensioner kan fx være 'Navn', 'CPR', 'Adresse', 'Personnummer' (**HUSK** selv at tage stilling til, om der er andre dimensioner i kuben, som kan klassificeres som personhenførbare - KMD har ikke ansvar for opsætningen af disse)
- **Obs:** der er naturligvis også andre måder at styre dette på - det vigtigste er, at få lavet en rollesammensætning, som sikrer, at personhenførbare data er utilgængelige for alle.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-5aef1146-b876-4fae-bcac-1423073f3a03.png)

Herefter er ’Adresse’ dimensionen ikke at finde i kuben:

![==image_1==.png](/.attachments/==image_1==-8915108e-1b41-462b-b2e4-c994195e82eb.png) 

Dette gøres på alle relevante dimensioner.

### **_VIGTIGT:_**
Det er vigtigt at pointere, at KMD ikke har ansvar for at sikre at personhenførbare data skjules i benchmark kuben. Kommunen har selv ansvar for at personhenførbare data ikke er tilgængelige, så ovenstående skal ses som eksempler og vejledning, men det er vigtigt at kommunen selv tager stilling til, om der er andre dimensioner, som kan klassificeres som personhenførbare.

# Introduction
In KMD we have security policy about authentication towards our KMD Entra Tenant. As default all authentication towards KMD Entra Tenant requires device based login.

## Device based login
**Device-based login** refers to an authentication method where access to a system or application is granted **based on the identity and trust level of the device** being used — not just the user credentials. Currently there are a long list of requirements for devices used for Device-based login, on of these requirements is that the device have to be added to the KMD domain. This requirement cannot be met by our current development environment, as all our on-prem VM's are stored in the KMDPFOSAP domain. Therefore individual users cannot use device based login from our Dev and Prod environments. Currently we need to authenticate towards our KMD Entra Tenant, when we authenticate to Azure DevOps, which are something we do in relation to versioning of source code in repos or publishing releases to artifacts. Therefor having a need to authenticate towards KMD Entra tenant from either KMDPFOSAP or other Azure Cloud services requires a work around or a bypass of this default policy. 

## Bypass this policy though CA-Persona-Developers group
To bypass this default you can be added to a blacklist, where this policy is not forced upon your kmd account. This is done though https://myaccess.microsoft.com, which is Microsoft **self-service portal for managing access** to applications, groups, and resources within an organization. Within this self service portal you can request access to the CA-Persona-Developers. Remember to add a reason that states the need to authenticate through the KMDPFOSAP domain.

The access is given for a fixed time period, to pay attention to notifications in you inbox when the access needs to be extended.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-5f4816bb-91c4-46ff-b6ec-d6778fccd93f.png)

For underlying questions about this group and how it is managed, then please reach out to KRK, who is the owner of this access group/packages.

# Introduction
The **Azure CLI** (Command-Line Interface) is a cross-platform tool used for managing **Azure resources** and performing administrative tasks from the command line. It provides a set of commands for interacting with Azure services, making it easier for developers, system administrators, and DevOps professionals to automate and manage their Azure infrastructure.

## Usage in KMD DIMA
We use the azure cli mainly to interact with Azure Devops. Currently it is used by the modulecoretool to interact with Azure Artifacts. It uses it for publishing and downloging artifats.

## Extensions
We use the devops extension for the Azure CLI, in this extension the artifattool is placed, which is used for interacting with Azure DevOps Artifacts. The artifact tool accessible through a exe fil on this file path after installation:  C:\Users\<user>\.azure\azuredevops\cli\tools\artifacttool\ArtifactTool_win-x64_0.2.394. This extension is installed togehther with the initial installation of the modulecore tool: https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_git/KMD.DIMA.KIP.DWH.AppConfig?path=/files/install-core-tool.ps1

## Debugging
If there are any issues with execution of any az commands, then used the --debug parameter on the command, and it will return a full log of the actions it performs.

```
missing...
```

**Solution:**
Instead of just running Az login, then try to run_
```
az devops login
```
It then prompt you for a token, where you paste the newly created PAT token and then run (enter).

**Root cause:**

*   Azure DevOps uses a different auth token system.
*   When you use `az login`, you get an Azure access token scoped for ARM.
*   Azure DevOps CLI does not automatically use this token because Azure DevOps REST APIs require a Personal Access Token (PAT) or OAuth token scoped for Azure DevOps.
    
What happens when you run `az devops login`?
*   It securely stores your PAT token in your local Azure CLI context.
*   `az devops` commands use that stored PAT to authenticate requests.
*   This allows Azure DevOps CLI commands to run without error.

Just try to clear cache and then sign in again.
```
az account clear
az logout
az login --allow-no-subscriptions --use-device-code
```
It now should link you to alle the azure subscriptions you account relates to.

### Root cause:
The error is caused by some wrong credentials cached on the host, this is why az account clear might solve the issue.

path: /Processes/2. Creating Documentation/2.1 Dataout Documentation/2.1.2 Extracting Datamodel references DBML
content:
# Introduction The `GetDBMLDatamodel` stored procedure is used to generate DBML (Database Markup Language) code from a database. This code is intended for use in tools like [dbdiagram.io](https://dbdiagram.io) and DBML ER Diagram visualizers in Visual Studio Code. This procedure extracts metadata from tables and columns, applies transformations and filtering, and generates a textual representation of the database schema, including relationships and references. This allows developers and analysts to visualize and understand the database schema quickly and clearly. Also this output is part of the documentation we going forward will provide our dataout customers. [[_TOC_]] --- ## How to use The stored procedure highlighted in the screenshot below is part of the reuse layer and is shared across all dataarea modules. This centralized approach promotes consistency and reduces code duplication when working with common functionality. Start by locating the stored procedure shown in the screenshot below. This procedure is maintained in the shared reuse schema and can be called from any dataarea module. ![image.png](/.attachments/image-db8e79ec-7d24-4c06-b35d-09826000e0fb.png) ### Input Parameters A number of input parameters can be set before running the procedure, e.g. excluding an object or blacklisting a table, this will exclude the listed value in the datamodel without interfering with the data itself. The same goes for including objects. Below is a description of the different input parameters. | Parameter | Description | |----------------------|-------------| | `@AreaName` | *(Optional)* Area/schema name for filtering tables, e.g., `'sdloen'`. Defaults to `'$(AREANAME)'`. | | `@TableBlackList` | *(Optional)* Semicolon-separated list of fully qualified table names (e.g., `'dimension.vcd_Table1;fact.vcd_Table2'`) to exclude. | | `@PatternMapCustom` | *(Optional)* Custom column name mappings, formatted as `'Pattern:ResultSuffix;...'`. It is used to overwrite naming of attributes, so the code can detect references between table objects. An example of a pattern is: `'DW\_[ES]K%Dato%:Dato;'`, which looks for attributes named `dw_ek` or `dw_sk` and containing `dato` in the name, and renames them to `dw_ek_dato` or `dw_sk_dato`. By default, the following patterns are added:

- `'DW\_[ES]K%Dato%:Dato;'` – Maps column names with date pattern (e.g., DW_ESK%Dato%)
- `'DW\_[ES]K%valid%:Dato;'` – Maps valid column patterns to Dato type
- `'DW\_[ES]K%AldersInterval%:AldersInterval;'` – Maps age interval column patterns
- `'DW\_[ES]k%tid%:Tid;'` – Maps time-related column patterns to 'Tid' type
- `'DW\_[ES]k%MartInfo%:MartInfo;'` – Maps MartInfo-related columns | | `@ObjectToExclude` | *(Optional)* Object-level exclusions in DBML syntax, e.g., `TABLE MyTable { "MyColumn" int };`. | | `@ObjectToInclude` | *(Optional)* Object-level inclusion in DBML syntax, e.g., `TABLE FWSALE_FACT_SALE2 { "DW_SK_Customer" int "DW_SK_Product" int "DW_SK_Dato" int "SalesPrice" numeric(28, 10) "Qty" numeric(28, 10) "SalesAmount" numeric(28, 10) "DW_ValidDate" date "DW_ArchiveID" bigint "DW_Audit" int "DW_Audit_Insert" int "DW_Audit_Update" int };ref: FWSALE_FACT_SALE2."DW_SK_Customer" > FWSALE_DIMENSION_CUSTOMER."DW_SK_Customer" `. | Example of usage: ![image.png](/.attachments/image-5daec649-a967-4246-ae5a-fe479cb72dd1.png) You can also call the procedure in your module by using a standard SQL 'EXEC' statement within your dataarea module with the required parameters. For example: `EXEC [doc].[GetDBMLDatamodel] @ObjectToExclude = N'ref: FWSALE_FACT_SALE."DW_SK_Product" > FWSALE_DIMENSION_PRODUCT."DW_SK_Product" ', @ObjectToInclude = N'TABLE FWSALE_FACT_SALE2 { "DW_SK_Customer" int "DW_SK_Product" int "DW_SK_Dato" int "SalesPrice" numeric(28, 10) "Qty" numeric(28, 10) "SalesAmount" numeric(28, 10) "DW_ValidDate" date "DW_ArchiveID" bigint "DW_Audit" int "DW_Audit_Insert" int "DW_Audit_Update" int };ref: FWSALE_FACT_SALE2."DW_SK_Customer" > FWSALE_DIMENSION_CUSTOMER."DW_SK_Customer" '` ### Save the Executed Query for Reuse After running the procedure, save the executed SQL statement in the doc folder of your module. Note that it is only referenced dimensions that is part of dimension objects. Facts contains all attributes. As part of the dataout documentation a separat [excel document is provided](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_wiki/wikis/KMDBI.wiki/10507/Dataout-Description). Used example: [createDBMLcode.storedprocedure.sql - Repos](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_git/demoframework.tool.global?path=/001_dataarea_fwsale/doc/createDBMLcode.storedprocedure.sql&version=GBmaster) ### Validate the Output Before using the DBML file or sharing it for documentation purposes, make sure to **review and validate the output**. Check that: * All expected **tables** are included * **References** between tables are correct * **Column definitions** (data types, primary/foreign keys) are accurate * There are no **unintended warnings or missing elements** This step ensures the visual representation and documentation are reliable and reflect the actual data structure. ### General business logic for populating DBML script Here are an overview of the logic that DBML output script assumes: - vcd views is used over v vies, and v views is used over the underlying materialized table. These are lined on the base name of the object. - References are only made based on attributes starting with dw_ek_ or dw_sk_ . - References to dimensions tables are limited to only include dw_ek_ or dw_sk_ keys where equals tablename. - Snowflaking from one dimension to another is based on the third part of the attribut name separated by _. Ex. dw_sk_kommune_belliggenhed, dw_sk_kommune is used to find the reference to dw_sk_kommune on dimension.kommune table. - References between fact tables is only made, if one of the tables starts with IF in the tablename. If your datamodel does not follow this preferred logic, then you need to utilize the '@ObjectToExclude or '@ObjectToInclude to bypass the default logic and make some customer adjustments. ## Insert in a Visual Tool After executing the stored procedure, the result is printed in the **Messages** tab of your SQL editor as shown in the screenshot below. This output can be copied and used to visualize or further analyze the data structure in external tools. ![image.png](/.attachments/image-31f9796e-3e98-4cd6-b66e-7e0263bc50a4.png) **Important:** When copying, make sure to exclude the Warning message at the top and also the completion message at the bottom. Open your preferred visual tool that supports .dbml or SQL structure imports. Paste the cleaned output into the editor to generate a visual model of your procedure’s result. This makes it easier to review, share, or document the structure. Save the visual representation or the raw .dbml in the doc folder of your module using the naming convention: `[AreaName]_[ddMMyyyy].dbml` Used example: [demoframework_08052004.dbml - Repos](https://dev.azure.com/kmd-dima/KMD.DIMA.LG/_git/demoframework.tool.global?path=/001_dataarea_fwsale/doc/demoframework_08052004.dbml&version=GBmaster) ## External Documentation We have created a guide for external use, that shows how to use free tools like **dbdiagram.io** and a **Visual Studio Code extension** to convert DBML into a star schema visualization. The guide includes a description of DBML, step-by-step instructions and example output, mainly used for customers. The external documentation in danish can be found here: [Anvendelse Af DBML Kode](https://kmddk.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/DIMALG-365/EY_9yp8TFdpJjjwaGdklCcUBXxLLEwxIBsdIzet4WaVKfw?wdOrigin=TEAMS-MAGLEV.p2p_ns.rwc&wdExp=TEAMS-TREATMENT&wdhostclicktime=1746690074219&web=1") If guidance in english is needed, please refer to [Introduction | dbdiagram Docs](https://docs.dbdiagram.io/). If you wish to use the Visual Studio extension to visualize the dbdiagram, it can be found here: [DBML Entity-Relationship Diagrams visualizer - Visual Studio Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=bocovo.dbml-erd-visualizer). ## Notes - Only the top-ranked view or table is selected if duplicates exist (based on name length and schema). - When excluding fact tables, remember to exclude the VCD views (not the base fact tables). - Currently supports filtering across multiple databases via sys.databases and synonyms.

content:
#Introduction
This page contains a guideline on how to make dataout documentation on our MS DM layer.



1. Go to dataout documentation application: 
   - Login to https://prodkmdlgconfig.adminportal.intranet.kmdhub.net/text/Overview (dev has this url: https://devkmdlgconfig.adminportal.intranet.kmdhub.net/text/Overview but should not be used, only in case of testing and development).
   - login using you kmdpfosap/z<something> username and password. Any issue on connection, please reach out to CDO.
2. Retrieve data for given solution:
   - Go to 'Documentation' (left side menu) -> 'Update database'
   - Here you can update all schemas in the documentations solution, based on what which objects a given customers database contains. You can extract column schema's for only a specific solutions or all solutions within a given database. It is therefore a requirement for this to work, that the target db is accessible through a linked server from the server where the kmdlgconfig module is installed. Also the user MDMDocumentationDDL needs DDL acces to that particular database. In doupt then ask TNH:
     - DatawarehouseServer: The name of the server on which the database you would like to document is located. In reality this is the name of the linked server pointing to the server where the given database is located.
     - DatawarehouseDatabase: The name of the database on which the objects to be described are located
     - DatawarehouseSchema: The name of the schema for the given solution you would like to describe. It only takes on schema as input, and if you like to create documentation you will have to create a entry for each - this will eventually result in a dataout documentation file per schema. <s>(leave this value empty to collect objects across all solutions in given database)</s>

      ![image.png](/.attachments/image-93977e09-dd70-4c28-8680-d11b816912f8.png)

   - Once info on given solution is filled out, you can then retrieve all object data for given solution. Hit the second button on the right side of the table.
![image.png](/.attachments/image-1f0a2074-09f0-4d1f-bc61-71459fc9ed51.png)
To validate that data is extracted go to 'Update column description' page, and filter for the expected schema. Note that only explicit schema's in DatawarehouseSchema column in 'Update database' is listed on 'Update column description' to limit the data amount. Documentation is still preserved on the KMDLGMDM database.
3. Submit existing descriptions/documentation from SAP BO
   - Login (RDP) to 172.31.55.81 using you kmdpfo/z<something> username and password. Any connection issues, please reach out to CDO.
   - Login into IDT and export univers meta data.
![image.png](/.attachments/image-d6588087-4d66-4158-920a-b01025b0f814.png)
   - Save univers meta data on network drive '\\\KDIDCLIAP00\DocExchange' as TXT file. If you cannot navigate to this drive, then please just enter it in the file explore path object.
![Skærmbillede 2023-08-28 123305.png](/.attachments/Skærmbillede%202023-08-28%20123305-cde4e07f-2514-4673-9402-1701cafc1bd8.png)
Every 5 minutes files is read by the application and transferred to the application. After completion the file is deleted.

4. Fill out missing descriptions
   - Go to 'Documentation' (left side menu) -> 'Update column description'
   - Here you can filter for missing descriptions on the given solution, and fill out the blanks. Currently only 'DescriptionDK' and 'AltDescriptionDK' is supporterted and applied by the application. If need for additional attributes like 'Name', 'AltNameDK', 'AltNameUK', 'DescriptionUK' and 'AltDescriptionUK', please reach out to MMP, and we can asses how to support these objects in the final documentation.

      ![image.png](/.attachments/image-864debe6-b5bb-4560-a814-6e2f3d258795.png)
'DescriptionDK' are only maintained by the descriptions coming from SAP BO. And if 'AltDescriptionDK' are only maintained through the application interface. If 'AltDescriptionDK' is not blank, then this text will always be favored over the input in 'DescriptionDK' field.

5. Deploy documentation to given customer database
   - Once the documentation is filled out, then the final discriptions can be deployed to the given customer database as Extended Properties on each column object. This extended property object, is the on used and fetched by the final documentation document.The upload button can be found here: 

      ![image.png](/.attachments/image-43494b8a-9adc-4ecf-9fac-339434fef122.png)
 If You want generate excel file You can skip that step and go to the next one. 'GenerateExcelDocumentation' button includes update documenation functionality.
6. Save new dataout document
Once you are ready to create a final document to hand out to the customers, then follow these steps:
   - Hit the 'GenerateExcelDocumentation' button. It will then create a excel output which is first queued and in iterations of every 5 min materialized. The document is materialized in the corresponding dataarea git repository, in the folder 'doc/dataout' on the dafault branch. Here all versions of the documentation is stored with this naming convension '<SolutionName>_DataoutDocumentation_yyyymmddhhmmss.xlsx. The 'GenerateExcelDocumentation' button looks like this:

      ![image.png](/.attachments/image-d038e658-dc0b-4d19-8cb7-a23db3eaa6a5.png)

   -    If module repository name is non-standard for example: opusfravaermaaltal.dataarea.101, You need to fill 'RepoName' parameter on edit row. For standard repos no action needed for that parameter.

         ![image.png](/.attachments/image-59194767-c10c-48f9-aa62-34ecfad77a5b.png)

      - To download the latest version of a given generated documentation, please open the entry and copy the url and pass it in you browser and then it will automatic be downloaded to your PC.

         
         ![image.png](/.attachments/image-1caa6ba1-4775-4879-8dea-ff05313151d2.png)

path: /Technology & Software/14. KMDBIFW - BI Framework/14.1 Modules/14.1.7 Use of SSIS and T-SQL
content:
# Introduction

In this framework, a clear distinction is defined between the use of SSIS and T-SQL. In the literature, this is referred to as a "hybrid" approach to the use of SSIS and T-SQL – meaning that tools are used for what they each do best. This approach is based on experience from other projects and from the consultants working with this framework. 

[[_TOC_]]

---

Generally, the two tools are used as follows within the framework:

# ETL (SSIS) "FLOW"
*   Move data A->B from various sources
    
*   Visual flow control
    
*   Error handling
    
*   Logging
    
*   Parameter control
    
*   Execution (parallel)
    
# T-SQL "OPERATIONS"
*   Performance (sorting, join, merge, lookup, conditional lookup)
    
*   Merge (insert-update-delete) performs well
    
*   Complex problems are better solved in SQL (e.g., chart of accounts structure)
    
*   Source control (database projects) works much better with T-SQL than with SSIS
    
*   Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD) are better handled with a SQL template. Alternatively, a third-party SSIS module can be used
    
*   Checkpoint / Rollback is more easily implemented and stable in SQL via our templates
    
The line between the two tools is very clear: SSIS is used to load data from the source into the first layer of the DSA (staging) – namely the extract layer. From there, SSIS is used solely to execute the flow – including logging and error handling. All transactions are handled using T-SQL.

# Documentation in SQL

All SQL code must be documented in a way that provides the next developer with a solid foundation for understanding the intent and background of the given code.
To avoid unnecessary maintenance of redundant documentation, it is assumed that the developer is familiar with the development framework, including its functionality, data flow, and naming conventions. Therefore, nothing should be documented within a procedure that can already be inferred from the procedure’s name and its position in the flow.
The same principle applies to the Microsoft SQL Server platform, meaning that common T-SQL expressions do not require documentation. It is assumed that the reader has a working knowledge of T-SQL.

All stored procedures and functions must include the following header. If the purpose and content are not immediately apparent from the procedure’s name and location in the flow, they must be described explicitly:

```
/*
 Description : ??

 ==============================================================================================

 Date       ID   Init  Comment

 yyyymmdd   #1   xxx   

 (Insert #? in the code to enable searchability)

 ==============================================================================================
*/
```

At the top, the stored procedure’s purpose is described. The ID is sequential for each object and allows for the insertion of, e.g., `#1` in the code to support searchability, as shown below:

```
#1 – START
  "Insert new or modified code here"
#1 – END
```

path: /Technology & Software/14. KMDBIFW - BI Framework/14.1 Modules/14.1.1 DSA/DSA Development Guidelines
content:
# Introduction

On this page, you can find an overview of the Stage layer components and processes. It covers key topics such as the architecture, data flow, naming conventions, table structures, SSIS packages, validation, and integration into the main package, providing a comprehensive guide to staging in the data warehouse framework.

[[_TOC_]]

---
# Stage (DSA) 
The Stage layer is the first step in the process, where data is read from the source system into the EDW. This layer is the least defined in the framework, as source systems can vary greatly in how they are accessed, and it will typically be handled differently from project to project. However, the end result must be that data is stored in the _archive_ area of the staging database, and the tables must reflect the source system in terms of naming, data types, and primary keys, and must contain the full data load from the source. This ensures that the EDW layer can be regenerated as needed with complete data.

![image.png](/.attachments/image-8e03f1f7-5e18-4e06-8881-f698f0ffef94.png)

The logic in this flow is built using templates in the form of SSIS packages and a standardized approach to building stored procedures, ensuring that staging is carried out in a consistent manner.
The **Extract** layer acts as a kind of draft area, where data is initially loaded. If the load is successful, the data is moved to the **Archive**. Whether this data transfer is a full load or a delta load depends on the situation, but the movement is handled by a stored procedure using either **DELETE/INSERT** or **MERGE**. Note that **MERGE** requires a unique key in the **Archive**.
It is also considered best practice in staging to load all fields from the source system, even if they are not currently needed.
The following components are included in the framework's **Stage** layer:

| **Type** | **Name** | **Function** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Schema** | `archive` | Archive tables and stored procedures are created in this schema. |
|  | `extract` | Extract tables reside in this schema. |
|  | `management` | This schema is used for synonyms to stored procedures for logging purposes. |
|  | `template` | This schema contains template stored procedures used to move data from `extract` to `archive`. |
|  | `system` | _(Not described in source text – can be clarified if needed)_ |
| **Synonyms** | `[management].[StartLog]` | Used to log the start of a job. Automatically used by the SSIS package flow. |
|  | `[management].[EndLogOK]` | Same as above. |
|  | `[management].[EndLogError]` | Same as above. |
|  | `[management].[EndLogOkDeleteIfNoChildren]` | Deletes the log entry for a given `MainID` if there are no logs referencing it via `ParentID`. |
| **Stored Procedure** | `[archive].[Insert_<SourceSystem>_<SourceTable>]` | Created to move data from `extract` to `archive` if needed. The SSIS package will call the stored procedure automatically. Must follow naming convention, where `xxx` is the table name (e.g., _Borger_) and `yyy` is the source system (e.g., _DB2_).Example template: `[template].[archive_Insert_Merge_xxxx_yyy_MergeEx]`.For a simple DELETE-INSERT, use the template `[template].[archive_Insert_xxxx_yyy_InsertEx]`. |
|  | `[archive].[Insert_extract2archive_FullLoad]` | A generic stored procedure used to move data from an extract table to archive. Primarily used when loading from text files where data is first moved to a buffer table and then to extract. If successful, this SP can be used to archive. Alternatively, a custom stored procedure can be written as described above. |
| **Helper Functions** | `[system].[TSQL_SimpleFieldList]` | Utility function to generate SQL code for `SELECT` statements. Helps optimize SQL development in stored procedures. |
|  | `[system].[TSQL_AssignFieldList]` | Utility function to generate SQL code for `SET` assignments. |
|  | `[system].[TSQL_CompareFieldList]` | Utility function to generate SQL code for comparing field values. |

# Stage: Naming Convention

It is important to follow a consistent naming convention for objects. The following standards are used in the **Stage** layer:

| **Object** | **Standard** | **Example** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Extract Table** | `[extract].[<SourceSystem>_<SourceTable>]` | `[extract].[PRISME_LEDGERTABLE]` |
| **Stored Procedure** | `[archive].[Insert_<SourceSystem>_<SourceTable>]` | `[archive].[Insert_PRISME_LEDGERTABLE]` |
| **Sequence** | `[archive].[ID_<SourceSystem>_<SourceTable>]` | `[archive].[ID_PRISME_LEDGERTABLE]` |
| **Archive Table** | `[archive].[<SourceSystem>_<SourceTable>]` | `[archive].[PRISME_LEDGERTABLE]` |
| **SSIS Project** | `DSA_SSIS_<SourceSystem>` | `DSA_SSIS_PRISME` |
| **SSIS Package** | `<SourceTable>.dtsx` | `Ledgertable.dtsx` |

**Note:**  
Fields in the staging layer must be named exactly as in the source system and must use the same data types as those in the source system.

# Stage: DW Fields

The following table summarizes the **DW fields** found in the `extract` and `archive` tables in the Stage layer:

| **Field** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `DW_ArchiveID` | This is a sequential number (sequence) automatically assigned to new records. If passed to the next layers, it allows tracing data from Datamart back to Stage. This field can be omitted if not meaningful—for example, if data is aggregated and only distinct values are passed on, making tracing impossible. |
| `DW_Audit` | A sequential number assigned when the job starts. All records affected in the same execution/batch get the same value. This field must be populated for both **Insert** and **Update** transactions. |
| `DW_Audit_Insert` | Should have the same value as `DW_Audit` when the record is inserted into the table. |
| `DW_Audit_Update` | Should be assigned the same value as `DW_Audit` **only** when the record is updated. |
| `DW_IsDeleted` | Present in `archive` tables and used when historical tracking of deleted records from the source is required. This requires a unique key on the archive table matching the source and a **full load** from the source into `extract` every time. A `MERGE` between `extract` and `archive` can then identify and flag deleted records using this field. |

**Note:**  
Updates to these `DW` fields are all handled in the stored procedure:  
`[archive].[Insert_<SourceSystem>_<SourceTable>]`

# Stage: Quick-Link

The table below lists the elements included in the Stage layer and their function or meaning:

| **Object** | **Example Name** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Extract Table** | `[extract].[PRISME_LEDGERTABLE]` | The extract table acts as an “inbox” or draft table. This is where SSIS loads data from the source—either full loads or deltas. |
| **Sequence** | `[archive].[ID_PRISME_LEDGERTABLE]` | A sequence is used on the archive table to assign a running ID (`DW_ArchiveID`). |
| **Archive Table** | `[archive].[PRISME_LEDGERTABLE]` | The archive table is the final table in Stage (DSA). It resembles the extract table, but includes additional DW fields. It always holds historical data from the source, ensuring that the EDW can be fully reconstructed. |
| **Stored Procedure** | `[archive].[Insert_PRISME_LEDGERTABLE]` | This stored procedure moves data from extract to archive. |
| **SSIS Package** | `Ledgertable.dtsx` | The SSIS package controls the flow from source to archive. |

# Stage: Extract Table

An `extract` table is created as a direct copy of the source—meaning that field names and data types must match the source exactly. This ensures optimal mapping and makes the data structure easier to understand for other developers. In addition to the source fields, an audit column is added. The table is placed in the `extract` schema and named using the convention `source_tablename`.

```
CREATE TABLE [extract].[<Source>_<Table>](
    [<Field from source>] [<Data type from source>] NOT NULL,
    [DW_Audit] [int] NULL
) ON [PRIMARY]
```
> It is always a good idea to use an existing extract table as a starting point.

**Tip:** An alternative approach, for more experienced developers, is to go directly to the SSIS package step. Begin by writing the SELECT statement against the source and let the DST component in the SSIS package generate the table with the correct field names and data types. Once created, return to this step to finalize the structure.

# Stage: Archive Table

The `archive` table stores the final dataset from the source, representing a full load. If the source is always loaded fully into the EDW, the extract layer may be skipped. However, if delta loads and deletion handling are required, both `extract` and `archive` layers must be used.
An archive table setup includes first creating a sequence, followed by the table definition.

```
CREATE SEQUENCE [archive].[ID_<Source>_<Table>]  
    AS [bigint]
    START WITH 1
    INCREMENT BY 1
    MINVALUE 1
    MAXVALUE 9223372036854775807
    CYCLE  
    CACHE 50000  
GO
```

```
CREATE TABLE [archive].[<Source>_<Table>](
    [<Field from source>] [<Data type from source>] NOT NULL,
    ...
    [DW_ArchiveID] [bigint] NOT NULL CONSTRAINT [DF_<Source>_<Table>_ArchiveID]  
        DEFAULT (NEXT VALUE FOR [archive].[ID_<Source>_<Table>]),

    [DW_Audit_Insert] [int] NOT NULL CONSTRAINT [DF_<Source>_<Table>_AuditInsert] DEFAULT ((0)),
    [DW_Audit_Update] [int] NOT NULL CONSTRAINT [DF_<Source>_<Table>_AuditUpdate] DEFAULT ((0)),
    [DW_Audit]        [int] NOT NULL CONSTRAINT [DF_<Source>_<Table>_Audit] DEFAULT ((0)),
    [DW_IsDeleted]    [tinyint] NOT NULL CONSTRAINT [DF_<Source>_<Table>_IsDeleted] DEFAULT ((0)),
    [DW_IsCurrent]    [tinyint] NOT NULL CONSTRAINT [DF_<Source>_<Table>_IsDeleted] DEFAULT ((1)),

    CONSTRAINT [PK_<Source>_<Table>] PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED (
        [<Key from Source>] ASC
        ...
    ) WITH (
        PAD_INDEX = OFF,
        STATISTICS_NORECOMPUTE = OFF,
        IGNORE_DUP_KEY = OFF,
        ALLOW_ROW_LOCKS = ON,
        ALLOW_PAGE_LOCKS = ON
    ) ON [PRIMARY]
) ON [PRIMARY]

```

> Always start with an existing table and use search/replace to adapt it with table-specific fields. These can often be reused from the corresponding extract table.

> Note: The archive table should share the same primary key as the source system (if available). This enables `MERGE` logic and simplifies later mapping in the EDW. If no key exists, omit the primary key.

# Stage: Archived Stored Procedure

A stored procedure must be created to handle the data transfer. If a simple `DELETE-INSERT` approach is sufficient, you can copy the template:

`[template].[archive_Insert_yyy_xxxx_InsertEx]`

...and rename it to:

`[archive].[Insert_<Source>_<Table>]`

However, it is generally recommended to use the `MERGE`-based template:

`[template].[archive_Insert_yyy_xxxx_MergeEx]`

...as a starting point—especially if a good primary key is available. Though this template requires more customization, it includes logic for handling deletions, preserving historical records in the `archive` table. This approach is more robust, particularly if inconsistencies may arise in the source (e.g., deleted dimensions with dependent transactions).
Make the necessary adjustments to match your specific table. A search-and-replace method will simplify much of the work, and you can script the `INSERT` and `SELECT` statements directly from the tables involved.

> **Note:** The template contains logic to check the `DW_Audit` values in both the `extract` and `archive` tables. Data will only be moved if the `max(DW_Audit)` in `extract` is greater than in `archive`. For large datasets, it may be necessary to add an index on the `DW_Audit` field.

# Stage: SSIS Package

In the SSIS staging project, start by making a copy of the SSIS package named `_Template.dtsx`. Rename the copied package to match the name of the new table—e.g., `Afdeling.dtsx`. Save the package and reopen it.
The package will appear as follows:

![==image_0==.png](/.attachments/==image_0==-839b0cb0-6822-4f91-a43c-d63dfcee9726.png) 

At first glance, nothing else needs to be done except opening **Variables**.

![==image_0==.png](/.attachments/==image_0==-f35cda41-2449-487d-954a-3f687f6f078c.png) 

Check that **SourceSystem** is correct. It is only used for information in logging. Otherwise, **DirectArchive** should be changed to **1** if the step from **extract** is to be skipped and data is to be loaded directly into the **archive** table.
Next, open **DFT SourceToExtractOrArchive** and adjust **SRC** and **DST**, where the select statement is written. For example:

![==image_0==.png](/.attachments/==image_0==-d69195c4-742d-4b40-8dde-4f2d53d866a2.png) 

**SRC:**
```
SELECT AFDNR, NAVN  
FROM Afdeling
```    

Note: No casting or similar is needed, as the data types are the same as in the source.

**DST:**
Adjust the mapping. The DST table is set automatically, and if the naming conventions are followed, SSIS will handle the mapping automatically.

![==image_0==.png](/.attachments/==image_0==-ef03d727-738e-4b53-9608-b089cbd2b4c7.png) 

# Stage: Validation
Run the SSIS package. It can, for example, be run stepwise by first executing ‘DFT SourceToExtractOrArchive’ and then running the stored procedure manually. If everything works, run the entire package.

Check the logging in the management schema to see if it looks reasonable.

Stage: Adding SSIS Package to Main Package
The SSIS package must be added to the Main package by opening the package `MainStage.dtsx`. Since the main package runs fully dynamically, a line must be added in the stored procedure `system.SSISpackagesInsertMaster`.
It could look like this:
```
IF UPPER(@Area) = 'STAGE_BORGER'
 BEGIN  
   EXECUTE [system].[SSISpackagesInsert] @Area, 'Borger.dtsx', 1
   EXECUTE [system].[SSISpackagesInsert] @Area, 'Afdeling.dtsx', 2
   EXECUTE [system].[SSISpackagesInsert] @Area, 'Flytninger.dtsx', 3
 END
```   

`@Area` is the name of the SSIS project to be referenced here. Specify the package name, and the number (e.g., `1`) indicates the partition in the parallel process that may be created. If no number is specified, the default is `1`. By default, the package runs with 4 parallel processors to optimize performance.
